articleTitle: Kirigami Inspired Inkjet-Printed Split Ring Resonator as a Disposable, Low Cost Strain Sensor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study presents a kirigami inspired split ring resonator (SRR) strain sensor. Since the SRR resonance frequency depends strongly on its split gap, one kirigami cut was designed to align with the SRR split gap, allowing SRR resonance frequency to be varied by applying uniaxial stress. The strain sensing mechanism is explained based upon the relationship between frequency and induced strain. A composite substrate comprised of two paper sheets bonded using epoxy is used as the dielectric. An SRR coupled with microstripline is inkjet-printed on the top paper using silver nanoparticle ink, and the ground plane on the bottom paper is realized using stretchable ink. Reflection coefficients for the fabricated prototype are measured at different strain levels. Resonance frequency increases from 4 to 4.64 GHz for 17.24% applied strain, with measured strain sensitivity = <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.2\times 10^{7}\ \text{Hz}/\%$</tex>, and minimum detectable strain level ≈ 0.84%. The proposed strain sensor is easy to manufacture, low cost, and disposable because it is inkjet-printed on paper. Thus, paper-based strain sensor can be considered a suitable substitute of polymer-based strain sensor.

articleTitle: A Study of Folded Monopole Antenna Close to Metal Object by Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two types of folded monopole antennas with different input impedance have been studied to achieve an antenna with robustness to metal objects for wireless communication in a space enclosed by metal objects. In this study, we analyze the change in the input impedance owing to the proximity of the metal plates to the antenna in terms of mode current and mode weighting coefficient calculated using the characteristic mode analysis.

articleTitle: A Compact Bird-Shaped Antenna Array for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact 1×2 millimeter wave (mm-Wave) antenna array for 5G communication is presented in this work. The antenna is impedance matched over frequency range of 24-28 GHz. The design employs a low-loss Rogers RT 5880 laminate having 0.508 mm thickness. The bird-shaped metallic patch is etched on the substrate top-layer and is accompanied by a partial ground plane at rear-side of the miniaturized laminate. The design has an overall size of 15 ×15.5×0.508 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna array reflection coefficient is below -10 dB and covers the whole mm-Wave band. The peak gain of 1×2 elements antenna array is 7 dBi. The antenna array configuration can be employed for the 5G mm-Wave communication.

articleTitle: A low-profile K-band phased array for airborne platform
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a 36-element K-band T/R phased array with height only 12.3mm. With only 36 elements in this array, the array can scan to ±50° in both H-plane and E-plane. Furthermore, by applying GaAs MMIC, the measured EIRP and G/T of the array are 51 dBm and G/T -12.5 dB/K respectively. The array with low-profile, small aperture and high performance is ideal for compact airborne platform applications such as unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Wearable Sensor for High Accuracy Tissue Imaging using Reciprocity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microwave imaging (MWI) is a desirable alternative for identifying anomalies (tumors) within the human body. Previous microwave imaging techniques have complex designs and large computational time for image reconstruction. In this paper, we present a simple and real-time imaging technique using inverse scattering. The proposed technique is demonstrated to detect anomalies using 4 different scenarios: a) separation between anomalies, b) anomalies sizes, c) permittivities of the anomalies, and d) frequency of the illuminated signal.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Modeling for Ocean Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Based on the motion model of ocean waves and internal waves, the electromagnetic field equations with ocean and internal waves as excitation sources are established. Three-dimensional vector finite element method is used to numerically model the electromagnetic field interaction with ocean and internal waves. The accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated by comparing with analytical results.

articleTitle: A Regularly 2-D Limited Scan Array with Low Grating Lobes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2-D limited scanning phased array antenna is proposed in this paper. The array antenna is composed two similar sub-arrays with equidistant rectangular grid. By arranging the sub-arrays randomly, the grating lobes of the phased array antenna are reduced. To prove the idea, a 98-sub arrays antenna operating at Ka-band is designed as an illustration. The grating lobes is below −13.7dB during the beam steering from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}\sim\pm 10^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: 3D Miniaturized GPS Antenna for Outdoor Sports Watch
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: One of the small wireless embedded systems issues is to gather low energy, small power consumption, small mechanical dimensions (related to frequency) and communication efficiency. In this paper we describe a way to improve the properties of a watch based GPS antenna for outdoor sports. If the key would be the study of microwave and mechanical watch properties? We try to answer with a 3D small LDS (Laser Direct Structuring) [1] antenna.

articleTitle: Beam-Steerable Antenna Composed of Metalines
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A beam-steerable array antenna composed of metalines is presented. The footprint occupied by the arrayed metalines is smaller than that for a corresponding array of patches. The height of the antenna is extremely small: on the order of 1/100 of the operating wavelength. A circularly polarized beam formed at a fixed frequency is steered over an angle range of approximately 70 degrees in the elevation plane. The antenna characteristics, including the radiation pattern, VSWR, and gain, are described.

articleTitle: Multiple Target Angular and Radial Velocity Association in Interferometric Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this article we present a method for extracting the radial and angular velocity of multiple targets using a two-element continuous-wave correlation interferometer. A filter-bank is used to spectrally isolate the individual target signals in the Doppler domain, then correlation processing is performed between the two antennas, between corresponding banks. With this method we are able to associate target-specific angular velocity and Doppler responses, while mitigating the intermodulation distortion which occurs when correlating a response with multiple scatterers. Simulated results are provided which show the individual target time-frequency responses from which angular velocity may be estimated.

articleTitle: Design of High-Selective FSR with a Single Layered FSS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A frequency-selective rasorber(FSR) with high frequency-selective property is proposed in this work. Dipoles with two series LC structures are presented on the resistive layer. In addition, a single layer FSS with loop structure is also designed. The equivalent circuits model (ECM) of the FSR is then analyzed. The simulation results demonstrate the high frequency-selectivity of the proposed FSR.

articleTitle: A Single Channel LCMV Beamformer Based on Time-Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-channel LCMV beamformer based on time-modulated array (TMA) is proposed and investigated. With time modulation technique, single channel receiving signal can be obtained and sampled. The essential concept of the proposed method is recovering the correlation matrix utilizing the sideband signals extracted in digital domain and adopting the LCMV criterion to get the weight vector. Compared to traditional uniform linear array (ULA), the proposed method offers several advantages such as low hardware complexity and low channel mismatch while it has the similar performance. Simulation results are provided to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Scattering from a Shifted-Hyperbolic Medium
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Hyperbolic media represent a fundamental concept in metamaterial science. Conventionally, such media have a completely symmetric dispersion diagram, but this symmetry may be broken by the introduction of nonreciprocity. We study here two equivalent shifted-hyperbolic media, a moving monoisotropic medium and a stationary bianisotropic medium. We demonstrate that these media support a double refraction with the two refractive waves symmetrically propagating with respect to the interface but with different velocities. This effect may lead to novel types of electromagnetic devices such as hybrid dividers - phase shifters, and trigger further opportunities in the realm of shifted dispersive media.

articleTitle: “Smart” 3D Electromagnetic Modeling
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Techniques for “smart” 3D EM modeling are briefly recollected and described. By applying these techniques to a 3-layer printed dipole antenna, which is coaxially fed through finite sized reflector, the number of unknowns in MoM/SIE approach is reduced for an order of magnitude with negligible loss of accuracy. Such minimalistic model enabled full wave simulation of array of 28 by 28 elements at PC computer.

articleTitle: SAR and Temperature Distributions in a Head Model Due to Electromagnetic Radiation with Frequencies up to 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A numerical study is conducted to investigate the SAR, temperature distribution and penetration depth of an electromagnetic plane wave incident on a human head model, for frequencies up to 100 GHz. A multi-layered, planar human head model is utilized for the analysis using the dispersive finite-difference time-domain formulation based on the auxiliary differential equation method along with the bio-heat equation. Numerical results show that penetration depths decrease exponentially with frequency, maximum SAR and resulting temperature rise values increase with frequency. The results obtained in this investigation are useful to evaluate the effect of the EM plane wave incident on the human head model up to 100 GHz.

articleTitle: Dehydration Approach for Enhancing Terahertz Detection of Cancer in Freshly Excised Breast Tumors
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work we demonstrate the use of 60% concentration of glycerol solution as an optical clearance agent in freshly excised breast tissues. The research aims at enhancing the differentiation between cancer and collagen tissues using terahertz imaging technique. The terahertz reflection mode imaging is utilized in this work. The preliminary results demonstrated a potential contrast enhancement in the terahertz image between cancer and collagen tissues.

articleTitle: A Dielectric Antenna with Rejection Mechanism for Full-Duplex Body Area Network Radios
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents design and implementation of a dielectric resonator antenna for body area network applications with full duplex operation at two adjacent ISM frequencies. The antenna design features a new parasitic radiator arrangement providing a switchable mechanism to reject communication at 2.45 GHz. Rejection level as high as 12 dB was achieved. In order to improve the antenna front-to-back ratio (FTBR), a mushroom-type electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure is placed underneath the antenna to eliminate parallel plate mode and spurious radiation of the aperture feed. Simulation results reveal that the antenna exhibits nearly unidirectional radiation with an FTBR of better than 15 dB and gain of 5.8 dBi.

articleTitle: Quantum Information Propagation Using Huygens' Principle
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new computational framework for quantum electromagnetics has recently been proposed (D.-Y. Na, J. Zhu, F. L. Teixeira, and W. C. Chew, arXiv 1911.00947, 2019). In this work, we demonstrate the use of Huygens' Principle for quantum information propagation. Instead of numerical eigenmodes, Fourier modes are used to quantize the field. Wave propagation and second-order correlation function calculated based on this scheme are shown.

articleTitle: Linear Broadside Array with Nonuniform Amplitude Distribution
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design and the fabrication of a planar antenna powering system are presented, ensuring a uniform phase distribution with non-uniform amplitudes based on the principle of binomial law. This distribution allows the suppression or a significant reduction of the secondary lobes of an antenna array. An interesting shape of this structure which is simple to carry out and well suited to antenna arrays placed on a circular profile is proposed. The basic element of the structure is the Wilkinson planar power divider. The measurements obtained using the vector network analyzer follow the binomial law of the amplitude distribution of the power supply outputs. Besides that, the evaluation of the effectiveness of these structures as a function of realization modes is achieved.

articleTitle: Interesting Behavior of Rectangular Microstrip Patch with Specific Perturbations on the Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A kind of metallic perturbation on the ground plane of a microstrip patch has been examined indicating some interesting as well as useful features. A strategic geometry, its location, and dimension can magically improve the pattern symmetry and also the cross-polarized (XP) level. A pair of metallic posts in an X-band rectangular patch demonstrates the same indicating about 20 dB improvement in the XP radiations. This design is free from fabrication tolerance and other high frequency related issues.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modeling of Stacked DRA using Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quantum particle swarm optimization (QPSO) approach is used to predict the equivalent circuit parameters of the stacked dielectric resonator antenna (DRA). This approach is a quantum-inspired version of PSO that follows quantum mechanics rules instead of classical Newtonian dynamics. This version helps to control only one parameter instead of two controlled parameters of the classical PSO. In this paper, coaxial-fed two dielectric resonator antennas are stacked on a perfect conductor (7.2-10.5 GHz). The desired antenna input impedance is evaluated using commercial software such as CST/HFSS and used in the QPSO optimization algorithm to find the parameters of antenna's equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Sub-wavelength Particle Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Precise characterization method for fine particles featuring sub-wavelength sizes is presented by implementing a deep neural network (DNN) for the first time. The proposed sub-wavelength particle detection method using the millimeter wave (mmWave), terahertz (THz) frequency band enables real-time measurement of the relative volume density of particles in a noncontact manner. The proposed method combined the machine learning technique with complex electromagnetic problems featuring nonlinear characteristics. Consequently, it is experimentally verified that the neural networks provide a correlation model for scattering coefficients of sub-wavelength particles and their corresponding relative volume density.

articleTitle: Wide-Bandwidth V-Band Circularly Polarized IPD Based Quarter-Mode Substrate-Integrated Waveguide Antenna Using Flip Chip Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wide-bandwidth V-band quarter-mode substrate-integrated waveguide (QM-SIW) antenna using integrated passive device (IPD) process and flip-chip technology is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna mainly comprises of four QM-SIW formed by flip-chip cavity structure surrounded a series-type power divider network to achieve circularly polarized radiation. The cavity size is of 3.2 × 3.2 × 0.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna is well suited for compact high-integrated millimeter-wave beam forming wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Unidirectional Radiation of Thin Slot Antenna on Single Substrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel deformed reflector very close to a narrow slot is proposed to realize unidirectional radiation. These reflectors consist of two large metal planes and are separated by one slot in order to accommodate the feed. The microstrip line feeding is adopted on a thin substrate of λeff/42 thickness at 5.8GHz.

articleTitle: A Circuit Model for Energy Synchronous Direct Antenna Modulation Using an Electrically Small Loop
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple circuit model for a broadband electrically small loop transmitter using energy synchronous direct antenna modulation (DAM) is presented. The concept of energy-synchronous DAM using a loop antenna is briefly described and compared to a conventional narrowband transmitter, via time domain simulations of the current on the loop. A brief analysis of the affect of ohmic loss on the stored current is presented. Initial results suggest that the dissipation in the loop is negligible over short symbol durations, but motivates a discussion about the need for a more comprehensive parametric study for this class of DAM transmitters.

articleTitle: Estimation and Compensation of Array Mutual Coupling Using the Sequential Loading Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates how a recently proposed network parameter method can be used to accurately predict and remove the mutual coupling effects of an antenna array. The method operates solely on a matrix of previously-calculated admittance parameters that defines a broad class of antennas. The sequential loading method (SLM) calculates the new admittance parameters, including mutual coupling, of a specific antenna of interest that is a subset of the class. The SLM is then used again in an iterative post-processing technique to find a set of terminal loads that minimizes the effects of the mutual coupling. The proposed method is demonstrated by using it to predict and eliminate the mutual coupling effects of a 6-element linear receiving array of dipoles which are a subset of the original 5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> linear wire antenna class. The method is validated by comparing its results to those obtained using a conventional full-wave simulator.

articleTitle: Azimuthal scattering of electromagnetic waves for radiating structures based on chiral metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the results of calculating the radiation characteristics of radiating structures based on biisotropic chiral metamaterials. It has been established that these radiating structures can provide radiation of electromagnetic waves of circular polarization in azimuthal directions. It is also shown that when these radiating structures are placed on metal surfaces, their radiation characteristics do not change significantly.

articleTitle: Overview on Combination of Numerical Modelling and Near-Field Measurements for Complex Electromagnetic Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Full wave simulations and Near-field (NF) antenna measurements are two different but widely accepted engineering techniques to characterize the radiating properties of antennas placed in complex electromagnetic systems. Simulations are attractive as they scale to problem size by varying the numerical method or simply by applying more computational power. However, the simulation accuracy depends on the accurate knowledge of material characteristics and/or an accurate description of the radiating source. Such information is not always available. Measurements are generally provided with estimates of uncertainty and can be performed on any antenna regardless of the material properties. Unfortunately, measurements scale less well to problems size as very large measurements systems tends to be expensive. The logical solution to this problem is to measure only the pertinent antenna part and use the numerical techniques to model the external scattering in a combination of measurements and simulations. This can be obtained through the use of equivalent current (EQC) to accurately represent the measured antenna and as measured source in numerical simulation. This approach has been validated in applications such as automotive, aerospace, EMC etc. In this paper we give a brief introduction to method and a discussion on achievable accuracies. The method is illustrated by a new application example.

articleTitle: An Optimization Driven Method for the Synthesis of Reconfigurable Parasitic Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an optimization driven method for the synthesis of pattern reconfigurable parasitic antenna arrays is presented. The proposed approach allows the design of antennas fulfilling different performance requirements. Two test cases, aimed at optimizing the antenna directivity and front-to-back ratio, respectively, are presented.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Model of a Loaded Inverted F Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A transmission line model of a capacitively loaded inverted F antenna (IFA) is presented in order to later study the loaded antenna performances and design an electrically small antenna. The tested model shows an error of 1.7% in frequency compared to electromagnetic simulations for different antenna heights and different values of the loading capacitance.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Corrugated Ground Planes for GNSS Multipath Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Accuracy and precision of positioning, navigation, and timing using the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is important for current and future applications such as autonomous vehicles and Internet of Things. A major threat to the accuracy and precision of GNSS is multipath interference from reflections around the antenna. To combat this issue, reference station antennas use corrugated ground planes to suppress multipath signals. In this paper, a comparative study of performance, size, and weight of six corrugated ground plane solutions is presented.

articleTitle: NRCS Backscatter Analysis at Low Grazing Angles with LATPROP Radar Data Collected During the CASPER West Research Campaign
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Variations of meteorological parameters within the marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) influence radar propagation at low grazing angles as well as the backscatter from the sea surface. The backscatter is predominately a function of the wind, radar frequency, polarization, and grazing angle. The grazing angle is a strong function of the refractive conditions present. Analytical models at low grazing angles fail, thus the five existing empirical models will be analyzed with data collected using the lower atmospheric propagation (LATPROP) radar during the Coupled Air-Sea Processes and EM Ducting Research (CASPER) West research campaign that took place from September-October 2017 off the coast of southern California.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Frequency Selective Surface for Antenna Applications in 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents the design of a dual-band frequency selective surface (FSS) which works as a bandpass filter in the 28 GHz and 38 GHz bands. The proposed FSS is a single layer, easy to fabricate structure and consists of non-uniform unit cells arranged in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> grid. Furthermore, the proposed FSS is compact and can be placed at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/21$</tex> distance from the antenna. The design of FSS is validated by using it as a superstrate for two microstrip patch antennas operating at 28 GHz and 39 GHz, and it is demonstrated that the antennas maintain their radiation characteristics, even with the FSS located at sub-wavelength heights over the antennas. With a slim design, the FSS can be employed as a cover for the antenna of 5G mobile terminals operating in the millimeter-wave bands.

articleTitle: Novel Low-Profile Circular-Polarized Antenna Based on Huygens Source
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new compact circular-polarized Huygens source antenna with low profile. A circular-ring that can generate electric and magnetic resonances is employed to complete this design. The operating principle of the Huygens source is introduced. The input power with 90° phased differences is provided by a coupled feeding system. A low profile with a thickness of 0.046 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>(λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength in free space at the center work-frequency) is achieved. The -10 dB operating bandwidth is 3.7%, which covers 1.57 GHz to 1.63 GHz. The fractional 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth is 2.75%. In addition, the maximum gain and the half-power beamwidth are 2.85 dBi and 128°, respectively. Finally, good simulated performances validate this concept.

articleTitle: Design of a 7 T Spiral Resonator-Based Filter for MRI Planar Array Coupling Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a filter for the decoupling of a 7 T RF MRI planar array by using miniaturized spiral resonators is presented. First, we introduce the filter design guidelines and, then, we perform full-wave simulations on an arrangement of three adjacent MRI RF rectangular loops. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution achieves excellent decoupling levels both between strictly adjacent and next-neighbors coils couples (better than -20 dB), while avoiding the use of additional lossy decoupling lumped elements connected into the coil array, hence accomplishing a mechanically robust and versatile design.

articleTitle: A Wideband Self-Decoupled Dual-Antenna Pair for 5G MIMO Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed a wideband self-decoupled dual-antenna pair for fifth-generation (5G) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) smartphone. The dual-antenna pair is composed of an ultra-wideband antenna element and another antenna element obtained by rotating former one by 180º.Two antenna elements are compactly printed on either side of the metal ground and a compact-field is appearing. The relative position of two antennas is chosen appropriately and good isolation can be obtained. The proposed dual-antenna pair is fabricated and measured. The isolation between two antenna elements is better than 11dB over 3.3-6.0 GHz, of which there are two decoupling frequencies. The measured efficiency is 38%-66% over the operating band.

articleTitle: Ultra Compact Implantable ISM Rectenna with 3-D Printed Biocompatible Packaging Considerations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a very compact 10×10×3.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> implantable rectenna as a receiver for wireless power transfer from an external transmitter towards an implantable device inside the body. The miniaturized rectenna involves the fabrication of an ultra-compact voltage doubler rectifier using lumped components. The implantable rectenna was packaged using conventional methods, while the use of 3-D printed external packages, fabricated using biocompatible resin material, is currently being experimentally explored. The approved dental biocompatible resin for the FormLab2 3-D printer is being used.

articleTitle: Analysis of Black Phosphorus Terahertz Photoconductive Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a parametric analysis of a photoconductive antenna that implements the 2-D material black phosphorus (BP). This material fills the gap between the electrodes of the antenna. The study involves modeling and simulation of the device using COMSOL Multiphysics at different bias voltages. We present the calculations of the photocurrent density versus time at the center of the gap in the BP layer, and the maximum photocurrent density value measured over time for multiple bias voltages. The results showed a saturation behavior versus bias voltage.

articleTitle: Characterization of Vehicle to Pedestrian Correlation Properties
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper analyzes the time correlation properties of vehicle-to-pedestrian (V2P) channels based on measurement campaign carried out at 3.8 GHz. Several propagation conditions and different mobility patterns were investigated. Subsequently, an analytical auto-correlation function (ACF) is proposed and successfully compared to the measurement data.

articleTitle: An Integrated Radar and Communication Antenna System for Single Mast Platforms
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design approach useful to integrate in the same mechanical structure two functionalities of the Electronic Warfare (EW) environment: Radar-Electronic Support Measurements (RESM) and Communication-Electronic Support Measurements (CESM). The interested architecture provides electro-magnetic and thermo-mechanical solutions to minimize the coupling between the installed antennas and to reduce the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of the whole structure. The proposed system can be installed on several platforms, especially when only a single mast is available for both CESM-RESM, such as new generation patrol vessels, submarines and frigates. Finally the main advantages of the integrated system are: lower costs, simplified installation and modularity.

articleTitle: Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance Systems with Extended Range
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel design for extending the range of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems is presented. The proposed system is based on a simple and planar loop resonator known as the U-loop. A 60 mm radius U-loop is placed between transmitting (TX) and receiving (RX) elements of a Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) system. The measured results show that a CSCMR system with U-loop is able to extend the range of optimal performance from 60 mm to 120 mm, which is equivalent to the diameter of the U-loop, while maintaining a Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) of 73% that is suitable for charging electronic devices.

articleTitle: Effect of Different Reflector Shapes on Sub 6-GHz 5G Dipole-Based Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the study of different reflector shapes for obtaining stable radiation pattern in the frequency of 1.4-2.7 GHz while maintaining good return losses values. Single and dual polarization dipole-like element have been used as feeders. Flat, parabolic, elliptical and ellipsoid based reflectors are presented in this paper with some measurements, to conclude with the significance of selecting the appropiate reflector shape.

articleTitle: High-Gain Low-Profile Platform-Embedded Endfire CPW-CTS Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high-gain low-profile embedded coplanar waveguide continuous transverse stub (CPW-CTS) antenna array is presented. The antenna is platform embedded to limit its effect on drag for high-speed applications such as on aircrafts. The depth of the antenna is less than 1/36 of a wavelength and is cavity backed. The endfire gain is 13.2 dBi, compared with endfire gains of 11.8 dBi reported in [3] and approx. 10 dBi reported in [6]. It has -1 dB and -3 dB endfire gain bandwidths of 6.3% and 11.0%, respectively. A -3 dB bandwidth of 8.4% was reported in [3]. The impedance bandwidth is 14.3%.

articleTitle: Frequency-Tunable Dual-Band and Polarization-Flexible CRLH SIW Resonant Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As communication systems demand compact size and multi-functionality, advanced antenna elements with radiative feature including frequency-tunability, multi-band functionality, and polarization-flexibility are highly sought after. This paper presents a novel antenna structure delivering abovementioned desirable features. The antenna is fabricated on a single printed circuit board and tuned using varactors. The simulated results correspond well with the measured results. The proposed antenna shows frequency tuning range from 1.54 GHz to 2 GHz at first radiation band. Second radiation appears at around 5.3 GHz. The antenna has a very compact size of around 0.1 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 0.7 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at first and second radiation frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: A Switchable A-T-A Rasorber with High Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A switchable rasorber with high selectivity is proposed. The rasorber is composed of a frequency selective surface (FSS) and a resistive layer. Both FSS and resistive layers are loaded with a PIN diode. When diodes are turned off, a low loss transmission band between two absorption bands is obtained. When diodes are turned on, the transmission band is closed, making the rasorber into an absorber. A Third-order FSS is adopted to enhance the selectivity of the transmission band. The proposed switchable rasorber can be used to design the smart radome.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing Simulations of mm-Wave Channels with FDTD-based Diffuse Scattering Models
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ray-tracing (RT) provides an accurate and cost-effective way to perform propagation modeling, assisting in the planning and optimization of wireless communication systems. To exploit its full potential in the challenging task of mm-wave channel modeling, it is important to include diffuse scattering. We use the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method to characterize rough surface scattering and derive diffuse scattering models that can be integrated with ray-tracing. This paper introduces this approach and presents simulation results for 5G indoor propagation scenarios.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Study on the VANET Topology Characteristics from Propagation-Aware Traffic Flows Extracted from Measured Data
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Understanding the dynamics of the network topology characteristics of vehicular networks (VANET) plays a key role to determine the feasibility of real-time safety and non-safety applications over VANET. Through the lenses of time-varying network metrics, including link duration, degree distribution, and number of connected components, this paper presents a preliminary analysis for VANET network topology characteristics for low and high traffic density. In our analysis, we integrate real-world buildings and obstacles along the propagation environments and measured data from the California Performance Measurement System (PeMS) database into a microscopic mobility model to obtain realistic traffic flows.

articleTitle: Artificial Magnetic Material for Array Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Artificial magnetic material (AMM) has attracted enormous interests as it provides high permeability in the microwave region which is not achievable in current natural magnetic materials. In this paper, we have investigated one three-dimensional artificial magnetic material (AMM) based on the octagonal spiral resonator. This AMM can achieve the same high effective permittivity and permeability of 4.85 at 1.014 GHz. By using this AMM substrate, the miniaturized patch array antenna has been realized with a stable radiation pattern and low reflection ( ) at the working frequency according to the CST simulation. Moreover, the dipole array antenna based on magnetic material has also been simulated. The simulated results validate that the magnetic substrate can be applied to reduce the scan blindness effect in an array antenna for reaching wide scanning range.

articleTitle: On Bandwidth Bounds for Array Elements above a Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Q-factor of an antenna has been used to evaluate the maximum achievable bandwidth in small antennas. This capability has been extended to resonant periodic structures as well, enabling the maximum achievable bandwidth of specific element shapes to be evaluated for narrowband antenna arrays. In this paper, the sensitivity of the bandwidth to perturbations in the array element is studied for infinite periodic arrays above a ground plane.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable and Foldable Monolithic Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel reconfigurable ReflectArray (RA) with multiple apertures for Cubesat applications. The design consists of a central RA with two or more folding panels connected using a surrogate hinge. Depending on the folding direction of these panels (forward or backward), a new RA aperture is formed. The proposed RA with the folding panels and corresponding hinges are printed on a single PCB board. A design of such an RA with two foldable panels is presented. This RA has two different single pencil beams pointing at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta=30^{o},\phi=0^{o})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta=-30^{o},\ \phi=0^{o})$</tex>, as well as a dual-beam pattern with beam peaks at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta=\pm 30^{o},\ \phi=0^{o})$</tex> operating in the Ku-band at 16 GHz. Key advantages of this RA for CubeSat applications include small stowed volume, low fabrication cost, and reduced complexity.

articleTitle: Delay Calibration in Software-Defined Radios for High-Accuracy Microwave Ranging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Localization is an important aspect in a number of sensing applications, including distributed antenna arrays where inter-node range accuracy on the order of λ/15 is required to support distributed beamforming. For microwave frequencies, this leads to range accuracies of cm or mm. When ranging is implemented in commercial hardware such as software-defined radios, the additional delays incurred within the system must be accurately characterized to ensure that delays proportional to λ/15 are accounted for. In this paper, we implement a calibration approach that uses internal crosstalk between channels in a commercial software-defined radio to determine systematic latencies. Using linear-frequency modulated pulses, we demonstrate the ability to estimate hardware-induced ranging errors with a standard deviation of 6.245 mm using 10 linear-frequency modulated pulses with a time-bandwidth product of 850 at various carrier frequencies. When used for distributed antenna arrays, this delay estimation error supports distributed beamforming at frequencies up to 3.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Self-restrained Decoupling Technique for Two Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel self-restrained (SR) decoupling technique (DT) is presented to increase the isolation between two antennas. The “self-restrained” feature means that the decoupling structure is only attached to the individual antenna itself without demanding any connection to other being coupled ones. The design parameters of the resultant decoupling structure can be precisely derived to achieve high isolations. A two-element monopole array is employed as a benchmark. Results show that good matching and high isolation are achieved simultaneously.

articleTitle: GSW Algorithm Based High-resolution Phase-only Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce two phase-only transmission-type metasurfaces to achieve multi-focus focusing based on weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (GSW) algorithm. One can achieve bifocal focusing with the same intensity, while the other can achieve multifocal focusing with different intensity. The focusing performance of two metasurfaces is analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Hinged Microstrip Quasi-FIR Filter for Physically Reconfigurable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Physically reconfigurable radio frequency (RF) front-ends are required for future 5G/millimeter-wave (mm-wave) systems to enable portability and/or integration on small platforms. In this paper, we present a novel preselection filter capable of physical reconfiguration and mechanical actuation utilizing quasi-finite-impulse response and flexible hinges. The filter is optimized for operation from 4.0 to 5.5 GHz. Parametric analysis of the hinging mechanism shows desirable results with negligible effects on the underlying filter performance. Unfolded and folded prototypes were fabricated and tested. Measurements showed that both topologies operate as designed within the 1.5 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Expression for Evaluating Directivity of Non-uniform Period Time Modulated Linear Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the expression for directivity of nonuniform period time-modulated linear antenna array is obtained and its variations with inter-element spacing is presented. In the case of uniform period time-modulated array (UTMA), due to the same time-modulation frequency to each antenna element, different harmonic signals from different time-modulated elements radiate at the same frequency and accumulate in space. In contrast to UTMA, the harmonic signals of different time modulated elements in the non-uniform period time-modulated array (NTMA), are spread in space because of different modulation frequencies for the different individual elements. Therefore, the sideband power calculation, as well as the directivity calculation in NTMA, is different from that of UTMA, and this is considered for the first time in this paper.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Dual-band Orbital Angular Momentum Generation Based on Trilayer Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurface has drawn much attention for its extraordinary ability of manipulating wavefronts at will. However, the wavelength-dependent behavior of the metasurface greatly hinders its design freedom. In this work, a novel highly efficient 2-bit dual-band metasurface unit cell is proposed, which is composed of three metallic layers separated by two spacers. As a proof of concept demonstration, a dual-band orbital angular momentum generator based on the proposed unit cells is designed and numerically verified.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of Low-Profile, Metal-only, Offset Parabolic Stepped Reflector Antenna for Emerging CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The needs for low-profile high gain antennas have significantly evolved in the recent past due to the possibilities of advanced space missions with CubeSats. In this paper, we describe the development of a low-profile, offset, metal-only stepped parabolic reflector antenna which can be integrated with the CubeSat form factor with minimal deployment complexity. The reflector surface consists of multiple parabolic sections that are confocal and thus provide a collimated beam in the far-field. As a representative example, an offset stepped reflector with a diameter of 20 cm and a profile height of 7.9 mm at 19 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured. The performance of this stepped reflector is comparable to that of an ideal parabolic reflector, however with a significant reduction in profile height.

articleTitle: Near-Field Sensor Based on SIW Microstrip Cavity Resonator with a Circular Aperture
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A near-field planar sensor fabricated from an SIW cavity resonator is explored. The sensor consists of a rectangular SIW cavity resonator operating in the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> mode, with a circular aperture on the top plate of the resonator acting as a sensing aperture. The performance of the sensor as a near-field sensing device and as near-field imager are explored.

articleTitle: Theoretical Modal Analysis of Square Waveguides filled with Effectively Skew Uniaxial Media
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The analytical solution procedure and exact form solutions for the modes of a square metallic waveguide filled with effectively skew uniaxial media are presented. The presented solution is useful because it provides the equations needed to design integrated polarization converters. Those converters can alter a certain guided mode to another mode with orthogonally polarized field. This type of mode converters is essential for the design of dually polarized integrated millimeter wave components. The paper results are validated by numerical simulations as well as prototype measurements in the millimeter wave band.

articleTitle: Tri-State Sequences Control of TMAs for Multibeam Reception
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A time-modulated array (TMA) is a multi-antenna system that offers the possibility of exploiting the sideband radiation patterns as steerable directional beams which can either serve a number of distributed users or exploit the multipath channel angular diversity. Unfortunately, as the number of exploited harmonic beams increases, both the antenna efficiency and the beam steering flexibility drastically decrease. In this paper, we present a novel TMA switching network based on single-pole triple throw switches controlled by tri-state sequences. The TMA allows for a flexible steering of the first positive harmonic beam and, at the same time -taking advantage of the time-multiplexed zero states of the pulses- it can additionally exploit the fundamental beam pattern, reaching an excellent total efficiency level.

articleTitle: Impact of Coupling on Beam Pattern vs. Frequency in an L-band Array-fed Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Array-fed reflector antennas are being considered for various synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites. Mutual coupling between the array elements, as well as with the reflector, impact the antenna performance significantly. The impact of this coupling is assessed for an L-band antenna. Two different feedings and two different element spacings are considered. The impact of the mutual coupling versus frequency is assessed through extensive full-wave simulations in HFSS. Two methods to reduce the impact of mutual coupling are analyzed.

articleTitle: Channel Frequency Domain Characteristic Analysis of LTE-R System under High-Speed Railway Scenario
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: LTE for Railway (LTE-R) system will be deployed at 460MHz frequency band to meet the user requirements of intelligent railways. To evaluate the coverage quality of LTE-R, a multi-carrier system operating over frequency selective channels, we investigate channel frequency domain correlation properties in a high-speed railway scenario at 460MHz. Based on the measurements, the received power of each subcarrier are modeled as Nakagami-m channel model which characterizes the small-scale fading distribution over time domain. Based on the modeling results, the correlation coefficients between different frequency bands are analyzed to explore statistical characteristic of different sub-carriers. Then the minimum required number of different sub-carriers for coverage quality evaluation and effective Signal to Interference and Noise Ratio (SINR) estimation of LTE-R system are suggested based on the analysis results.

articleTitle: Towards More Accurate Design Models for Electromagnetically-Coupled Microstrip Patch Antennas between 1 and 10 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents an analytical framework approach for electromagnetically-coupled microstrip patch antennas (EMCMPA) to more accurately predict the initial antenna dimensions between 1 - 10 GHz. The proposed EMCMPA design model is validated in simulation, where a coherent error is obtained between the desired and simulated resonant frequency. A minimum simulated antenna efficiency of 80% and initial resonance frequency errors smaller than 10% are achieved in all tested frequencies.

articleTitle: Design of Circular Polarization Unit-cell for Beam-shaping
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the design of a circularly polarized unit-cell for ku-band transmit array applications is presented. The designed unit-cell employs three layers of metallic structures which are printed on two substrates and there is no air gap or foam layer between them. The presented unit-cell has a compact structure while providing a full transmission phase rang of 360 degree through its rotation along its normal axes. The transmission coefficient is less than 0.1 dB for frequency range of 16-16.5 GHz. The proposed unit cell is utilized to form a transmit array which is capable of radiating vortex beam. The simulation results for designed transmit array verifies the fine performance of the presented unit-cell.

articleTitle: Microwave based Glucose Concentration Determination using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Non-invasive blood sugar measurement attracts more and more attention in recent years, given the increase in diabetes-related complications and inconvenience in the traditional ways using blood droplets. In this paper, we present a study on the use of machine learning algorithms to determine glucose concentration based on the microwave scattering parameters (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) measured on the glucose solution with various concentrations. Dielectric parameters were extracted appropriately based on the modified Debye dielectric dispersion model from the measured broadband S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, and utilized as the features to create a large dataset by adding various Gaussian noises. Machine learning algorithms were then used to classify glucose concentrations ranging from pure water to 1000 mg/dL. A perfect 100% glucose concentration classification accuracy has been achieved. The study suggests a proposing way to develop the non-invasive glucose detection method using big data machine learning.

articleTitle: Transistor-based Magnetless Faraday Metasurface and Spatial Isolator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report here a magnetless Faraday metasurface and its application as a spatial isolator. The nonreciprocity of this metasurface stems from time symmetry breaking by transistor-loaded conducting circular ring metaparticles. In contrast to previously reported transistor-ring structures, this metasurface operates in transmission mode rather than in reflection mode, which is more challenging in design and which enables the spatial isolator application. It is shown that this surface is electric-magnetic hybrid insofar as it involves both electric and magnetic rotating dipole moments.

articleTitle: A Parasitic Loaded Dual-Pin Circularly Polarized Antenna for Dual-Band WiFi Operation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we present a dual-band antenna designed for modern WiFi communication. The proposed antenna is composed of two disc-based patches arranged in a concentric structure. The external patch operates at 2.45 GHz while the internal one operates at 5.2 GHz, hence compatible with the operation dictated by the IEEE 802.11/n protocol in the S and C bands. The two channels are independent, since the antenna has two separate feeding points with coaxial connectors on the backing ground plane. The antenna operates in Circular Polarization and exhibit a gain exceeding 4 dB for both the frequencies, making the proposed device suitable for indoor operation.

articleTitle: A Compact MTM-EBG-Enabled Common-Mode Filter Without A Defected Ground
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A bandgap structure for common-mode suppression in conductor-backed coplanar stripline is presented, which achieves wideband performance in a fully-printed and single-layer topology. The bandgap structure is designed utilizing multiconductor transmission-line metamaterial techniques, does not require defects in the conductor backing, and may be directly embedded into the transmission line traces. Common-mode signals are rejected while differential-mode signals are passed with greater than 10 dB return loss over 2.3-4.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Coupled Line Unit Cell for Independent Control of Even and Odd Mode Phase Delays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Coupled lines are essential to numerous microwave components such as directional couplers, filters, and phase shifters. In this paper, we propose a topology for a tunable coupled line unit cell. In the design, the even and odd mode phase delays can be tuned independently of one another while maintaining an impedance match for both modes. An analytical description of the coupled line unit cell is presented in addition to experimental results for a fabricated structure designed to operate in the X-band. Such a unit cell could be used to simultaneously control the coupling coefficient and transmission phase of a directional coupler in real time.

articleTitle: Finite Element Boundary Element Hybrid via Direct Domain Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A hybrid Finite Element-Boundary Element Method (FE-BE) is presented which employs a Direct Domain Decomposition Method (D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>M) solver. The method is based on the `PECfication' idea, where all electric field unknowns are eliminated by forming the FE Schur complement.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Scanned Slotted Waveguide Antenna at Millimeter-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we describe the design and development of a novel traveling slow-wave antenna to substitute serpentine waveguides using a periodically loaded standard WR22 waveguide. When changing the frequency from 32.5 GHz to 37.4 GHz the beam steers from 12° to 72° while the gain of the antenna remains within 3-dB from the maximum gain of 17 dB. The antenna has an efficiency of over 60% and a linear change of angle vs. frequency. The antenna has a length of 26.6 cm and a beamwidth of 4°. Compared to a serpentine slot array, this antenna has a much narrower lateral profile which allows placing several of them side-by-side to either narrow or facilitate scanning the beam in the transverse plane. Therefore it can serve as an advantageous alternative to serpentine waveguide arrays.

articleTitle: Prof. Pedram Mousavi's Memorial
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Former students and colleagues of the late Professor Pedram Mousavi are still in shock and grief of his untimely and tragic death on flight PS752. May his soul rest in peace.

articleTitle: A Miniature High-Gain Low-VHF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a miniature antenna design for practical applications in wireless low-power low-VHF communications. The proposed antenna is designed to achieve a high gain for a given size (41 cm × 30 cm × 20 cm including a ground plane). To design the electrically small and efficient antenna, closely-spaced multiple short monopoles, radiating fields that are in phase, are introduced. The in-phase radiation is enabled by an efficient, shared phase shifter which is formed by a capacitive load and air-core coils connected to each short monopole. A prototype optimized for a small ground robotic platform is designed and fabricated. Performance characterization based on simulation analysis and outdoor measurements demonstrates that the proposed approach allows for a higher gain yet more compact low-profile antenna compared with recently developed low-VHF antennas.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Diplexer Using Dual Half-Mode SIW Cavity for 5G Sub-6 GHz Communications This paper is dedicated to the Memory of Professor Mojgan Daneshmand and her family
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Prof. Mojgan Daneshmand made seminal contributions to the advancements of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology together with her students and colleagues. In this paper, we present our recent work on miniaturized SIW diplexer in memory of Mojgan and her family. The proposed diplexer is centered at 3.45 and 4.9 GHz for 5G sub-6 GHz communications, which is enabled by a common dual half-mode substrate integrated rectangular cavity (HMSIRC) coupled with singlemode cavities in each channel. Besides the elimination of T-junction, HMSIRCs are also introduced for the miniaturization of sub-6 GHz circuits. Additionally, by employing the first two modes in the dual-HMSIRC, a large frequency ratio of 1.42 between 3.45 and 4.9 GHz can be realized, which is difficult to implement with the original whole cavity scheme because of spurious passband problems. A 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order example with ripple fractional bandwidths of 2% and 1.6% for the two channels is synthesized, designed, fabricated, and tested for demonstration.

articleTitle: Matching Losses Evaluation in Voltage Doubler Rectifiers for High Efficiency Rectifying Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Voltage Doubler (VD) rectifiers are known to be most effective in the design of radiofrequency energy harvesting circuits (known as rectenna for Rectifying Antenna). The performance comparisons in most of the previous work have been evaluated concerning single-wave or double-wave bridge rectifiers. However, there are several topologies of VD; this paper then proposes to compare the performance of two types of VD: the Latour VD (LVD) and the Schenkel VD (SVD). Both prototypes are designed with Schottky HSMS 2850 diode, and performances in terms of DC output voltage, conversion efficiency, and matching loss are evaluated. For operating frequencies between 0 and 3.5 GHz, it appears that the performance in terms of DC output voltage and conversion efficiency is almost similar. However, for matching losses, gaps of up to 60 μW/Ω are observed between the two types of VD. This difference can be significant if we consider the level of power consumed in most rectennas applications. The LVD is the topology that shows the least matching loss for input power between -20 dBm and 20 dBm.

articleTitle: Advances and Challenges in Handset Antenna Efficiency for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Increasing system requirements for 5G and beyond wireless systems translate into an increasing importance of antenna efficiency. In this paper we show that frequency-reconfigurable antennas are a very promising solution to increase the efficiency, exhibiting an upper bound on the radiation efficiency that is significantly increased compared to traditional designs. We then compare several efficiency measurement techniques, from which we can conclude that reverberation chamber measurements are an ideal solution for 5G and beyond.

articleTitle: Optically and RF Transparent Low-emissivity Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here, we propose a novel composite metasurface comprising a glass substrate and honeycomb-shaped spectrally selective nano-thin optical coatings. Simultaneously, the proposed structure is transparent in the visible and RF region while being reflective in the IR (low-emissivity).

articleTitle: Optimized MIMO Antenna Port Placement using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) identifies characteristic current modes in an arbitrary conductive structure. A unique property of these characteristic modes is that they give rise to orthogonal radiation patterns, making them useful for designing MIMO antennas. Our algorithm uses data from CMA to automatically place ports on a cell phone chassis and synthesize a MIMO antenna at 2.5 GHz. Using our algorithm, we show port placements and excitations that give rise to six isolated channels.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of GPS Multipath Propagation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multipath introduces error into the Global Positioning System (GPS) accuracy, which is difficult to mitigate. This paper aims to review the multipath propagation and its effect on GPS applications, through the modeling of a single reflected signal propagation behavior. Furthermore, the multipath rejection of two commercially available GPS antennas are studied. It is observed that shaping the antenna radiation pattern as well as its polarisation properties plays an important role in mitigating the multipath error.

articleTitle: Reflection-free Transmission in Time-reversal Symmetry-proteced Slot Line Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A slot line waveguide that incorporates an enclosure in the form of a perfect-magnetic conductor (PMC) is presented. The configuration exclusively supports the propagation of a quasi-transverse electromagnetic (TEM) mode, that is shown to be immune to reflections associated with bends in the propagation pathway. This is due to the mode forming time-reversal symmetry-warranted pseudospin states (decoupled polarizations), which are locked to the wavevector. Generally, spin-polarized states like in photonic topological insulators (PTIs) can exhibit backscattering-immune transmission if the scatterer does not flip the spin. Unlike PTIs, however, the proposed structure does not demand a special global behavior of the wavefunction of a periodic system. Here, the pseudospin property is intrinsic to the quasi-TEM mode and is simply enforced by eliminating all other modes including plane waves through the use of the PMC cover. We show a proof-of-concept design that is compatible with low-cost printed-circuit-board fabrication process as well as numerical full-wave simulation results. The evident competitive performance and simplicity of the proposed waveguide make it attractive for numerous microwave, millimeter-wave and terahertz applications.

articleTitle: Performance of IDMA System with Space Time Diversity over Mm-Wave Underground Channel
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Interleave division multiple access (IDMA) has become a promising solution for performance enhancement of future access networks. In this paper, we investigate the performance of IDMA scheme within millimeter (mm-Wave) underground communications, by exploiting the space- time-block coding (STBC) diversity, and adopting the group random permutation (GRP)-based interleaver, to further remove the interference from other users. The performance of the resulting system is investigated based on the real channel measurements carried out in underground mine environments at 60 GHz band. The performance enhancement in terms of bit error rate (BER) brought by the proposed scheme, is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Three-Element Pattern Reconfiguration Antenna Using Partial Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a three-element antenna with pattern reconfiguration is presented. The three elements include a square driven element at the centre of two parasitic elements. The approach of Yagi-Uda is employed to achieve pattern reconfiguration. The lengths of the parasitic elements are varied using PIN diodes to make one of them act as a director while the other as a reflector and vice-versa. Pattern reconfiguration is achieved by making the length of the parasitic element acting as a reflector larger than the size of the partial ground plane. The proposed antenna, employing two PIN diodes, is designed to radiate the main beam at -90, 0 and 90 degrees. The measured directivity obtained at various scanning angles is about 6.5 dB. The proposed antenna is suitable for WLAN applications operating around 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Printed Half Bow-Tie Antenna Array With Four Linear Polarizations for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a printed half bow-tie antenna array with four linear polarization(LP)s for UAV applications is presented. The proposed array consists of four printed half bow-tie antennas in the top substrate, two supports with a tapered balun, and a reflector with the CPW-G feeding network in the bottom substrate. In the feeding network of the proposed array, four ports and two SP3T switches are used to adjust the phase and amplitude with respect to the unit cell antenna. By controlling the switches, the proposed array can be operated on four LP modes. In addition, the printed half bow-tie antenna array improves the beamwidth at the operating frequency band (4.0 to 5.6 GHz). The simulated 10-dB impedance bandwidth, the peak gain, and the HPBW of the proposed array are approximately 31.2% (1590 MHz), 5.6 dBi, and 98.6°, respectively.

articleTitle: Narrowband WBAN system for PPG transmission signals around body
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for analyzing the performance of digital transmission of wireless Photoplethysmogpraphy (PPG) signals in terms of channel capacity and bit-error-rate (BER) in the presence of slow and fast fading channel effects is presented in this paper. The proposed prototype system operates at 2.4 GHz frequency. During the transmission the PPG signal is compressed using a discrete cosine transformation (DCT), then modulated by OQPSK method.

articleTitle: Locating Scattering Centers using Single Channel Complex ICA
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Single channel complex Independent Component Analysis (ICA) is used to locate and extract scattering centers from the frequency response data of a target illuminated using a stepped-frequency radar system. The proposed method is first tested on synthetic targets and then tested on real commercial aircraft models. The extracted scattering centers can be used for target classification. The approach used in this paper does not require an antenna array and can be applied to a single channel of radar returns.

articleTitle: A Reliable and Realtime Data Transmission System for Autonomous Valet Parking
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In modern automotive industry, realtime and reliable positioning of vehicles is urgently needed in the autonomous driving system. The objective of this paper is to support the autonomous valet parking system by proposing the reliable transmission protocol for the transmission of real-time positioning signals. A broadcast scheme which sends out the position information of the vehicles is proposed. The time-delay of this positing system is less than the 100ms, which is obviously better than the common Wi-Fi transmission protocol. Meanwhile, the multicast mode based on different channels is proposed to avoid the co-channel interface to increase the reliability of signals transmission. Performance of the proposed protocol is evaluated in some realistic scenarios. Experiment results have proven that the proposed protocol is apt for real-time data transmission with a high reliability.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low-Profile Crossed-Dipole Antenna Using a Hybrid EBG Reflector
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile crossed-dipole antenna with a hybrid Electromagnetic Bandgap (EBG) reflector is proposed in this paper. The crossed dipoles are etched on a Rogers RO4350 substrate above a hybrid EBG reflector etched on a FR4 substrate. By using the leaky wave region, the bandwidth of the EBG reflector is expanded, without increasing its thickness. The bandwidth of our antenna reaches 37.6%, and the total thickness of our antenna is only 6.16 mm. After introducing the hybrid EBG reflector, the maximum axial gain is increased to 11.98 dH i, compared to the uniform EBG reflector's 7.18 dBi.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized High-Gain High-Isolation Antenna Array for Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna array with a high-gain high-isolation low cross-polarization levels, and low-backward radiation level is designed and its features are presented. The proposed configuration allows the scalability of the array size with daul polarization feeding network at two different layer. The antenna uses the slot-coupled feed for one polarization, while the microstrip line feed with slotted ground plane is used for the other polarization. It can make good use of the space on both sides of the ground plane, as the feed circuits for two orthogonal polarizations are placed on each side of the ground plane, respectively. Dielectric lens is used to improve the gain of small size array performance. The proposed 16-element array is presented at mm-Wave applications yields a bandwidth of more than 12.6%, with high-gain around 30 dBi and isolation below 35 dB. High gain with good isolation are obtained, and the cross-polar levels are below -33 dB at both E-plane and H-plane.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Gap Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel reconfigurable antenna. The proposed antenna is designed based on a gap substrate integrated waveguide. Using sets of switches over the gaps leads to the variation of the surface current distribution. This will perturb the electromagnetic fields and leads to the electronic beam-steering. The center frequency is chosen as 28.5 GHz to accommodate 5G wireless communications networks. The width, length, and height of the antenna are 29 mm, 61 mm, and 1.1 mm, respectively. The proposed reconfigurable antenna is able to scan about 30° using the varactor capacitance range of 200fF to 500fF. The simplicity and electronic beam-steerable capability of the proposed reconfigurable antenna make it a suitable candidate for 5G wireless system.

articleTitle: Amplitude Based Beam Steerable Arrays: Mitigation of Grating lobes and Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
