abstract: Designing beam steerable arrays with amplitude as the main parameter instead of phase as in the conventional arrays brings with it its own set of challenges: earlier occurrence of grating lobes and mutual coupling. An overview of these two issues along with their mitigation strategies is discussed here along with the further steps to be pursued in this regard.

articleTitle: A Convenient Solution of Mid-Field Calibration Technology for Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Calibration is an important issue for any phased array systems to work properly. Mid-Field Calibration Technology (MFCT) provides an fast and convenient way to calibrate an antenna array in the mid-field. With the improved MFCT to tolerate the parallelism problem, an significant accuracy can be obtained. However, an inconvenient way to interchange of channel elements is required. We propose an method to overcome this inconvenience. An experiment is conducted to verify the result.

articleTitle: Delay and Doppler Variations in Device to Device Communications with Pedestrian Mobility
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper exploits the Doppler and delay spreads for pedestrian-to-pedestrian (P2P) communications based on a measurement campaign carried out at 3.8 GHz. Several propagation conditions and different mobility patterns were investigated. In particular, the impact of vehicle passing in the vicinity of a P2P links was considered. It was found that the delay spread does not only depends on the propagation environment but also on the body mutual orientation whereas the presence of a moving vehicle in the vicinity of P2P links can have an impact on the Doppler spread.

articleTitle: Theory of Space-borne Linear Antennas Fed at Arbitrary Position in an Ionospheric Plasma
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the current distribution and input impedance of a very low frequency (VLF) antenna fed at the arbitrary position in an anisotropic ionosphere are determined. By considering the ionospheric anisotropy in the VLF band, we obtain the current along the antenna fed at the arbitrary position through the integral equation, with the contributions from both the ordinary and extraordinary waves. This work helps to improve the efficiency of space-borne antennas by analyzing their electrical characteristics.

articleTitle: Existence of Effective Media Properties for Clouds of Metallic and Magnetic Particles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a model for mean field electromagnetic propagation through a volume of metallic and magnetic spheres. Particles are assumed to be randomly distributed throughout the medium, and electrically small. Mean field is calculated by coherently averaging the field scattered by many configurations of this random medium enclosed within a container sphere. Fields scattered by individual configurations of the scattered field are calculated using the Method of Moments. Mean field is then compared to the field scattered by a homogeneous, magneto-dielectric sphere the size of the container to determine the effective medium that represents mean field propagation in this random medium. Medium parameters are compared to predictions given by a mixing formula.

articleTitle: Non-Intrusive Control of Surface Impedance Using Parasitic Inclusions for Base Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents a method to locally control the surface impedance around a typical antenna, and therefore, improve the antenna cross-polarization isolation. While manipulating the antenna input parameters, this approach tends to impose minimal intrusion to the antenna far-field pattern, favorably decoupling the challenges of controlling near and far fields parameters. The enabling elements to achieve such a control are miniaturized parasitic inclusions, which are deployed around the main antenna elements. The inclusions function as effective polarization isolators in one frequency band, while being invisible at relatively higher frequencies. Even though the method is fundamental in nature, the presentation will highlight its application to Base Station Antenna Arrays.

articleTitle: Breast Imaging by Time Reverse Minimum Variance Distortionless Response
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel microwave imaging method is proposed to reconstruct the backscattered power distribution from intramammary tissue. This method has high resolution, low spurious, and does not require advanced artifact removal technology. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by computer simulation using a numerical breast phantom.

articleTitle: Investigating Stacked-Ring Based Cells for Phase Shifting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates a stacked-ring based unit cell design for near-field phase-shifting metasurfaces developed for beam-steering applications. The unit cell has two dielectric layers sandwiched between three thin patterns of conductive material. Each of the three conductive patterns has a circular ring of varying sizes to produce the required spatial phase variation across the metasurface. To validate the performance of the unit cell, a metasurface was designed to tilt the beam of a 4×4 microstrip array. The numerical simulations predict that the array beam can be tilted by an angle of 28.8° without severe degradation, verifying the unit cell phase-shifting characteristics.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Modeling Polarization Convertor Unit-cell
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this letter, a data-driven learning algorithm is presented to reduce the highly time-consuming and computationally expensive iterative progression of design using full-wave (FW)simulators. It approximates the nonlinear relationship between the electromagnetic design and associated desired performance. A polarization convertor unit-cell with n number of diagonal dipoles as a patch is considered and the effect of geometrical parameters on the required performance and frequency range is investigated using convolutional neural network (CNN). The developed CNN has the capability of fast prediction of geometrical parameters for any user-defined frequency ranges between 10 GHz to 50 GHz of desired characteristics. As a proof-of-concept, FW simulation results are presented to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed CNN.

articleTitle: A Study of Machine Learning Using Wireless and Physical Environment Data at a Factory
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless communication is expected to improve the flexibility of equipment layout or of the factory IoT (Internet of Things). In this paper, we show the result of constructing IoT sensor network using LPWA (Low Power Wide Area) in a factory, performing machine learning, and analyzing the correlation between wireless and physical environment. As a result, it has been shown that RSSI (received signal strength indicator) fluctuation of a terminal could be estimated from sensor data that recorded physical environment around the terminal.

articleTitle: Beamspace processing of Compressively Sampled Signals Received via a Uniform Linear Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper has applications in communication systems where there is a need for transmitting compressively sampled signals. Uniform linear antenna arrays are often used to receive such signals in an environment prone to multipath and terrain scattered interference. This paper introduces an approach to enable beamspace processing of arrays when receiving compressively sampled signals. The focus is on estimating the direction of arrival and recovering the received compressive signals then decompressing them. Fourier and Wavelet based beamspace processing is employed.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Multi-Ring Microstrip Antennas Fed by an L-Probe for Single-Band and Dual-Band Operations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents design of a wideband multi-ring microstrip antenna fed by an L-probe for single-band and dual-band operations. The proposed antenna consists of one or two square ring patches and an L-probe arranged in a multilayered dielectric substrate. By using a thick substrate for the L-probe and optimizing distances between the L-probe and the patches, wideband performance can be obtained. Prototype antennas for single-band and dual-band operations are fabricated and tested. Measured fractional reflection bandwidths less than -10 dB are 46.1% for the single-band antenna and 20.3% and 15.7% for the dual-band antenna, respectively. Measured gains of the test antennas in the above bandwidths are 0 to 6.9 dBi for the single-band antenna and 3.0 to 8.6 dBi for the dual-band antenna, respectively. Although the E-plane radiation pattern is slightly tilted against the frequency, stable broadside radiation is confirmed. The proposed antennas exhibit excellent performance as wideband planar antennas for single-band and dual-band operations. The proposed wideband antenna can be easily extended to a dual linearly-polarized antenna by using another L-probe at the orthogonal position.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Cubic Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Integrated 60-GHz MHMIC Short-range Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This manuscript proposes a low-profile and low-cost Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with high efficiency and full unlicensed bandwidth at the 60-GHz band for high data-rate 5G applications. The proposed antenna is based on a broadband rectangular dielectric resonator fed by a microstrip transmission line for integrated single layer MHMIC modules. The results confirm that the suggested antennas have broadband impedance bandwidth, reasonable flat gain and radiation efficiency greater than 90% across the operating frequency range.

articleTitle: Reducing the Radiofrequency-Induced Heating of Active Implantable Medical Device with Load Impedance Modification
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effect of load impedance on Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) radiofrequency (RF) induced heating of active implantable medical device (AIMD) is investigated in this study. Six different load impedance configurations are considered for a generic AIMD structure. The absolute temperature rises were measured at the tip electrode for all AIMDs used in the study. It is shown that the temperature rise is strongly related to the load impedance inside the implantable pulse generator (IPG).

articleTitle: Surface-Waves Optimization for Beamforming with a Single Omega-bianisotropic Huygens' Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a design method of a single, passive and lossless Huygens' metasurface for field transformations that do not conserve local power. Based on the optimization of auxiliary surface waves to redistribute the total power across the metasurface, independent control of the amplitude and phase of the transmitted fields is possible without incurring reflections. The method is verified by the design of a metasurface-based Taylor aperture antenna that is fed by a single current linesource.

articleTitle: A Novel 2-Bit Graphene Reconfigurable Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel 2-bit graphene-controlled reconfigurable antenna design for large-scale, millimeter-wave/terahertz reflective surfaces. Using previously characterized graphene sheet resistances, in the millimeter-wave bands, the proposed 2-bit configuration can be used for reconfigurable reflective surfaces, while reducing the quantization lobes compared to 1-bit designs with a small increase in the complexity and losses. As such, we place two, single-bit, graphene phase shifters on each differential node of a patch antenna, achieving lower insertion losses and 2-bit phase control on the reflected waves. Herein, we present the theoretical models of the proposed designs alongside full-wave simulations of a 275 GHz linear array.

articleTitle: Optimization of dual-band notched UWB Trapezoidal Antenna using Genetic Algorithm Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Genetic algorithm (GA) optimization is applied to design an Ultra-wideband UWB-CPW-fed Trapezoidal with a dual-band frequency notch. A two-dimensional (2-D) matrix chromosome is used in the GA to represent a wide-range on planar trapezoidal element. It is shown that the GA generates antenna designs exhibit equal wideband performance defined by VSWR<;2, ranging from 3.1 to 13.66 GHz (an impedance bandwidth of 126%), with a good dual-band-notched performance in the 5 GHz (WLAN band) and 7.2 GHz bands (ITU satellite communication systems). The GA-generated antenna shows almost omnidirectional radiation patterns and a good gain in the whole UWB range except at notched bands.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Antenna Backed by AMC Surface Using Genetic Algorithm for 2.4/5.8 GHz Underground Mining Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of dual-band antenna using a genetic algorithm (GA) for wireless body area network (WBAN) device is proposed. It covers the Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) bands of 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz. An AMC reflector is utilized to isolate the human body from undesired electromagnetic radiation and improve the antenna radiation characteristics. Moreover, the proposed antenna is placed on a human equivalent flat phantom in order to evaluate the performance of the antenna on a human body. The simulated results indicate that the proposed antenna is a good candidate for WBAN applications.

articleTitle: Envelope Correlation Coefficient for Multiple MIMO Antennas of Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new figure of merit called envelope correlation coefficient for multiple MIMO antennas (ECC-M) for mobile terminals working in a Rayleigh fading channel. The figure of merit is proved to be effective to reflect the impact of the radiation properties of an antenna array to the system channel capacity. The correlation of the ECC-M to the channel capacity of a MIMO system is demonstrated by simulating the channel capacity of four realistic MIMO antenna arrays using Monte-Carlo method. The proposed ECC-M can be used to evaluate the impact of a MIMO antenna array with more than two elements to the data throughput.

articleTitle: A Brief Overview of Antenna Technologies for Communications-On- The-Move Satellite Communication Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper serves as the introductory first presentation to the 2020 IEEE AP-S Industry-Focused Special Session on “Beam-Steerable Antenna Systems with High Gains for Mobile Satellite Terminals”. It presents a brief overview of established and emerging antenna technologies for Communication-On- The-Move (COTM) mobile satellite communication terminals and known or expected advantages and limitations of each technology.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Corner Reflector Using PIN-Diode-Switched Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the development of a reconfigurable corner reflector that uses a PIN-diode-switched frequency selective surfaces (FSS). A reflector aperture angle of 45° is prototyped for application at 4 GHz, and its pattern characteristics are altered by on-off state biasing of the PIN diodes. The numerical characterization of the structure is performed using analysis in CST® tools, and the results are compared with experimentally obtained data. Good agreement between simulated and measured performances is observed, thus confirming the design approach and functionality of the circuit.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Tolerance Analysis and Its Application to Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient machine learning-assisted tolerance analysis (MLATA) method is proposed by applying machine learning (ML) methods into multiple layers of the antenna tolerance analysis. The computational time for operations including worst case performance searching, maximum input tolerance hypervolume searching and robust optimization is greatly reduced while maintaining high reliability due to the introduction of the ML methods. The surrogate models which are built using ML methods have been introduced to predict both antenna performance and tolerance of parameters at given design points. The Pareto front combining antenna performance, robustness and size has been obtained to guide trade-offs for antenna robust design. A planar inverted-L antenna for mobile terminals is simulated to validate the proposed MLATA method.

articleTitle: 5G mmWave Patch Antenna on Multi-layered Alumina Ribbon Ceramic Substrates
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The thin, flexible, fully dense Alumina Ribbon Ceramic (ARC) fabricated by Corning's proprietary process of continuously sintered ceramic (CSC) is used as a substrate for the patch antenna and transmission line for 5G mmWave wireless communication systems. The microstrip line on the 40um thick ARC shows a loss of about 1.6dB/cm at 28GHz. The compact (0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), low profile and multilayered patch antenna shows a resonant frequency of 29.35GHz with 2.81dBi peak gain, which could be used for 5G mmWave mobile applications.

articleTitle: MACKEY II with reduced thickness by using a new structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: MACKEY (Meta-surface inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory), that operates not only in free space but also on a metal plate has been proposed. In this study, a new model MACKEY II with reduced thickness is proposed. Subsequently, the feed method of MACKEY II is studied and the analysis results are presented.

articleTitle: A Compact Chip-less RFID Tag for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact and cost effective chip-less RFID tag (CRFID) to be operated in 4–14 GHz band. The tag has circular and diagonal closed loop rings for generating multiple resonances to encode a 12-bit sequence. It has a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.4}\times\mathbf{1.4\ cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> and code density of 6.122 bits/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed tag is modeled upon low cost FR4 substrate and has a planar construct. Due to its attractive features such as long bit-encoding capability, compact size and ease of fabrication, this CRFID is deemed quite suitable to be used in various RFID application scenarios in Internet of Things.

articleTitle: Dielectric Characterization of Biological Samples by Using an Open-ended Coaxial Probe
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The present work proposes the use of a miniaturized open-ended coaxial probe to perform the detection of normal and malignant biological tissues, typically resulting from an excisional biopsy. The system has been numerically designed by analyzing a biological specimen having spherical shape and by varying its diameter, accordingly. The dielectric properties characterization has been carried out by using an open-ended coaxial probe combined with the virtual line transmission model reconstruction algorithm. The minimum size of the biological specimen to obtain an acceptable characterization has been assessed.

articleTitle: Artificial and Natural Dielectric Layers for Mutual Coupling Reduction of Massive MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces, for the first time, the theory and application of natural and artificial dielectric layers (ADL) for mutual coupling reduction between massive MIMO antennas. By introducing an extra route with controllable reflection phase and magnitude, the ADL is able to cancel out major couplings in a massive MIMO array. The basic working mechanism is explained in the paper together with preliminary results to demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Highly-Integrated Wideband 28 GHz and 39 GHz Array Antennas for 5G Mobile Phone Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Highly-integrated mmWave 28 GHz and 39 GHz wideband array antennas for 5G mobile phone applications have been presented. The 28 GHz array consists of directional dipole-type antennas as array elements and the 39 GHz array consists of directional monopole-type antennas as array elements. The 28 GHz dipole-type array antenna is integrated at a side edge of a PCB, and the 39 GHz monopole-type array antenna is formed with a multi-layer LTCC substrate. This article demonstrates that the proposed 28 GHz and 39 GHz two array antennas can be integrated closely and generate two wideband resonant modes to separately cover the whole 28 GHz n257 and 39 GHz n260 bands of 3GPP 5G NR specification with keeping independent beam scanning operations. This will be useful for future multiband and multimode millimeter wave mobile phone applications.

articleTitle: A Deployable and Reconfigurable Origami Reflectarray Based on the Miura-Ori Pattern
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel origami reflectarray unit-cell based on the Miura-Ori pattern. This origami unit-cell allows for efficient folding/unfolding, high packing efficiency and easy deployment. The unit-cell is composed of 4 parallelogram patches that can achieve 560° phase shift. A 20 × 20 element Miura-Ori reflectarray is optimized and designed to radiate a beam toward direction θ=20° and φ=0° at 8.425 GHz. A maximum realized gain of 26 dBi is obtained. The proposed antenna's main advantage is its ability to efficiently pack itself at its fully folded state to occupy 4 to 5 times smaller volume than the one at its fully deployed state. This is very important for small satellite applications.

articleTitle: Design of a 3D Printed Gradient Index Lens Using High Permittivity Ceramic
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the design of a gradient index (GRIN) horn-integrated lens using a zircona lattice printed using a Nanoparticle Jetting process. The electrical properties of the ZrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> lattice for a range of geometric parameters are simulated to realize a range of effective dielectric constants from 3 - 23. The properties of a 3D printed lattice are found to be consistent with the simulations. A shortened horn antenna combined with a flat GRIN lens is designed to collimate the beam and enhance directivity. The simulated directivity is 14.6 dBi at 15 GHz, which is 6.2 dB higher than the same horn without the lens.

articleTitle: Quad Frequency Rejection Bands UWB Bowtie Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniature planar microstrip antenna of bowtie shape with four frequency bands have been rejected to avoid interfering with several services operating within these bands. A quarter wavelength transformer is introduced for matching purposes. The bowtie right side has a horizontal slit to enhance the bandwidth and it is connected to the microstrip feed line, while its left side is connected to the partial ground plane in the back side through a shorting pin. The simulated Reflection Coefficient S11 has a 10-dB range from 2.69 to 15.06 GHz with rejection bands of (3.39 - 4.23) GHz, (4.64 - 6.07) GHz, (6.82 - 8.94) GHz and (9.75 - 12.19) GHz. The proposed antenna can achieve a maximum gain of 5.79 dB.

articleTitle: A Compact Monopole Patch Antenna for Future Sub 6 GHz 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact printed monopole patch antenna with finite ground for future Sub 6 GHz 5G wireless communications is presented. The microstrip patch antenna with square slot has compact size of 30×34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Good impedance match over wide range (3 - 7 GHz band) is achieved by partial ground plane and optimization of stub. The antenna exhibits omni-directional radiation pattern with high gain over the entire band. The proposed antenna is realized on FR4 laminate and good agreement with simulated results indicate that proposed design can be employed in future 5G wireless applications for wireless communication between Internet of Things nodes.

articleTitle: A Stretchable Liquid Metal Reconfigurable Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a liquid metal reconfigurable antenna. While liquid metal devices are not new, non-toxic gallium based liquid metals have caused an increase in research for related applications. Stretchable liquid metal antennas can provide the reconfigurability for wideband applications in addition to applications requiring beam control. This research focuses on the design of a stretchable liquid metal monopole at 2.4 GHz. The model was simulated using CST and initial results are documented to verify the efficacy of liquid metals as a possible antenna material.

articleTitle: Generalized principle of pattern multiplication based on the phase antenna element
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The generalized principle of pattern multiplication is proposed based on the multi-mode phase antenna (MMPA). The multi-mode phase antenna (MMPA) has dual-port, and its beam direction can scan with the phase difference between dual-port. So the phase array based on MMPA element can be achieved by the array factor multiply the MMPA element factor, and the array beam can scan in wide angle with high gain if the array factor and MMPA element factor vary synchronously, this is the generalized principle of pattern multiplication (GPPM). Based on GPMM and MMPA element, we proposed a four-element E-plane scanning linear array. The main beams of the E-plane scanning linear array can scan from -65° to +65° in the frequency band at 1.5GHz.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction using Defected Ground Structure in UWB DRA Array for MIMO Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design of a closely spaced two-element ultrawide band (UWB) Surya Yantra shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array is presented. Novel rectangular loop-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) is introduced to reduce mutual coupling between DR elements. Fabrication and testing of the antenna array were carried out. Measured UWB of about 101% (3.1-9.4 GHz) was achieved. Mutual coupling below -15 dB is achieved over the entire band of interest using DGS. The proposed antenna array is a prominent candidate for MIMO applications due to its low mutual coupling, 101% UWB, the average gain of about 4.4 dBi, and fairly stable radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Surface roughness effects on additively manufactured aluminum Ka-band waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Additive manufacturing of metal such as aluminum is an attractive alternative to rapidly manufacture high frequency waveguide components. However, the surfaces of the components can be rough, which can have an impact on electromagnetic propagation, such as additional loss and dispersion effects. To quantify the electromagnetic transmission performance, two pieces of WR-28 rectangular waveguides, three inches long, with two pairs of inductive irises were made using Direct Laser Sintering. The first piece was made from AlSi10Mg and the second is AL6061-RAM2. The AlSi10Mg was noticeably rougher, having a measured rms height variation of 1.8 mils, whereas the AL6061-RAM2 was 0.7 mils. The measured insertion loss at 32 GHz for the AL6061-RAM2 part was 1.1 dB versus 0.59 dB for the Al6061-RAM2 part. The simulated HFSS model without roughness shows at insertion loss of 0.36 dB.

articleTitle: Mechanically driven SMR-based MEMS magnetoelectric antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: During different antenna miniaturization techniques, mechanically driven antennas have been demonstrated as the most effective method over state-of-the-art compact antennas. The magnetoelectric (ME) antennas based on a released magnetostrictive/piezoelectric heterostructure rely on electromechanical resonance instead of electromagnetic wave resonance, which results in a typical antenna size as small as one-thousandth of an electromagnetic wavelength. However, the microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) devices are very fragile and delicate due to their suspending structure. Here we show that solid mounted resonator (SMR)-based MEMS ME antennas can be realized with robust and high-gain performance. Although various packaging approaches are used to handle MEMS devices and protect them from environmental damage, these methods are complicated and high-cost. Compared to free-standing membrane ME antennas, SMR-based antennas are more structurally stable with no need for removing silicon substrate, but the design and fabrication of Bragg reflector layers must be carefully done to obtain the desired resonant frequency. In this work, 1D Mason model and 2D COMSOL finite element method (FEM) simulations were performed to design the SMR-based ME antennas. Then the in-plane radiation pattern of a fabricated antenna that operates at 1.75 GHz was characterized. Our results successfully demonstrate how to design, fabricate and test SMR-based ME antennas, which are provided with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process compatibility, size miniaturization, mechanical stability and high-gain performance. These miniaturized robust ME antennas are expected to have great influences on our future antennas for internet of things, wearable and bio-implantable applications, smart phones, wireless communication systems, etc.

articleTitle: Impedance Matching Network Based on Metasurfaces (2-D Metamaterials) for Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper shows the gain-bandwidth limitations of traditional discrete component matching used in electrically small antennas can be overcome by implementing the impedance matching network with metasurface. The proposed metasurface can optimize maximum power transfer to electrically small antennas and achieve superior broadband performance.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Wearable Wideband Antenna with High Gain Based on Franklin Array for Future 5G Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A conformal wideband array antenna with low-profile, high gain, and full-backed ground plane is designed based on Franklin array antenna (FAA) for wearable applications. The antenna is designed to operate at the licensed 28-GHz band for 5G wireless networks recommended by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission. The bandwidth of the designed antenna also covers the 33-GHz band for satellite communication and navigation applications. To the best of our knowledge, the proposed antenna has the widest matching bandwidth amongst reported modified FAAs. Numerical studies are performed on the performance of the designed antenna under structural deformation such as bending and human body integration to corroborate its potential for wearable applications. It was observed that the wideband performance of the antenna is well preserved during structural deformation as well as human body integration with no significant variations. The proposed antenna features a compact size with dimensions of 80×22×0.25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and exhibits a matched bandwidth of 24.43% (27.3 GHz to 34.9 GHz), with a gain value of 14.02 dBi at 28 GHz and 15.2 dBi at 31.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Dielectric-Free Cells for Low-Cost Near-Field Phase Shifting Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a unique dielectric-free cell configuration that is useful as a building block to design low-cost transparent phase-gradient metasurfaces required for antenna beam steering using both far-field and near-field methods. Each cell is made of a few thin metal sheets each having an asterisk-shaped slot. A phase variation of 360 degrees is possible with four metal layers, with less than 2 dB drop in amplitude. This is much greater than what is possible with the conventional cross-slot which lacks such a high degree of freedom.

articleTitle: Verification of Generalized Far-Field Mode Filtering Based Reflection Suppression Through Computational Electromagnetic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel cylindrical mode-based measurement and post processing technique has recently been presented that allows data that has been acquired on a non-equally spaced abscissa to be processed rigorously. This technique was initially examined and validated using extensive, empirically derived data. However, the recent development of a digital-twin representation of a far-field antenna measurement system enables further and more detailed validation to be performed with results able to be assessed against a reliable “truth” model. This paper reports the results of that study presenting new analysis that further verifies the utility and flexibility of the very general error correction measurement and post-processing technique in configurations that hitherto have not been considered.

articleTitle: Flexible Liquid Metal Frequency Selective Surface With Tunable Second-Order Bandpass Response
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A flexible, fluidically tunable, second-order bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) operating in the X-band is presented in this paper. The proposed multilayer structure utilizes elastomeric microfluidic channels to enclose and allow precise movement of gallium-based liquid metal slugs, while preserving its mechanically flexible nature. The liquid metal slug tuning elements are integrated into two periodic Jerusalem cross layers, which are coupled together through a periodic square aperture layer. By pneumatically shifting the position of the liquid metal slugs, the capacitance between adjacent Jerusalem cross elements can be linearly tuned, with high precision, to shift the operating frequency range of the filter in real time. Full-wave simulation of the bandpass FSS is performed for three different liquid metal slug orientations to demonstrate the tunability of the design.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction of a Two-element MIMO Antenna System Using Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new defected ground structure (DGS) on the ground plane of a handheld device is proposed to reduce the mutual coupling between two Planar Inverted-F antennas (PIFAs). Mutual coupling reduction of more than 30 dB is achieved for the proposed case compared to the case of a single slot on the ground at 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Low-Cost 3D printed Dielectric Hyperbolic Lens Antenna for Beam Focusing and Steering of a 79GHz MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Extensive research has been conducted on millimeter wave (mm-wave) chipset solutions led to reduction in size and cost while adding sensitivity and accuracy. Recent 79GHz chipset solutions using antenna-in package approach were developed for various applications with a wide beamwidth and low gain. However, for some applications such as multiple people vital signs detection and corridor gait monitoring, there is still a need to achieve higher gain with thinner beamwidth, to increase the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the transmit/receive range of the system, mitigate the reflection from surrounding objects as well as reduce multi-path effects. The use of a lens is an appealing solution since it could improve the system performances while using existing chipset solution. Using low cost and rapid manufacturing 3D printing technology, we designed and fabricated a dielectric lens antenna for a 79GHz MIMO radar. Compared with the system without lens, the full-wave simulation demonstrated a 14dB improvement in gain which is in good agreement with measurement results.

articleTitle: A Dielectric Measurement-Based Design Approach for X-Band Applications on FR4 Substrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design approach based on the dielectric measurement of the FR4 substrate material at X-band. The approach mainly aims to increase the design accuracy by measuring the frequency depended dielectric constant and tangent loss values of the substrate material to be used in the fabrication, and including the obtained data as input to the design. In accordance with this purpose, FR4 is measured by using waveguide method and its electrical characteristics are obtained at X-band frequencies. To minimize the effect of design complexity, a microstrip line is designed, fabricated and measured utilizing ordinary simulation and PCB tools. The same design is re-simulated with the approach proposed in this paper and comparisons of all results validate the accuracy improvement of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave High-Gain PRGW Antenna Using a Fabry-Perot Cavity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a high-gain Antenna by using a Fabry-Perot cavity (FPC) in millimeter-wave (MMW) applications. The FPC antenna is formed by locating a frequency selective surfaces (FSS) above a slot antenna that operates at 28 GHz and fed by a printed ridge-gap waveguide (PRGW). Moreover, the bandwidth of the proposed slot antenna is enhanced using a novel design of the semi-cross slot. The simulation results show the optimized antenna design can cover impedance bandwidth from 27.77 GHz to 28.42 GHz with a high realized gain of about 20.45 dBi at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-beam Dual-Polarized Windshield Antenna with Wide Elevation Coverage for 5G V2X Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband multi-beam 5G antenna system for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication is presented. The antenna is composed of three separate arrays with radiation patterns that covers the forward upper half elevation plane. The designed arrays maxima are located at angles 10°, -20° and -40° with respect to the windshield normal. Each array is composed of three-element dual-polarized patches. The gain of the beams varies from 11 to 9.6 dBi at 28 GHz and it covers the 28 GHz millimeter frequency range from 26.5 GHz to 29.5 GHz. A feeding network for each array is carefully designed for minimal beam deviation, as low as ± 5°, across the operating frequency range. Moreover, for interior placement of the antenna the challenging issues pertaining to the windshield is discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-mode phase slots antenna with dual ports
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The multi-mode phase slots antenna with dual-port is proposed. The whole size of the antenna is smaller than half wavelength, and these two ports can work simultaneously with high isolation. By varying the phase difference between these two ports, the main beam direction of the proposed antenna can scan from -59°to +59° in the E plane with a gain fluctuation about 2 dB during 1.45GHz to 1.57GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Stacked Patch Using CMA and CMT
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The impedance bandwidth of a microstrip patch antenna may be increased by additional resonances in the antenna structure. This work uses Characteristic Mode Analysis to show that a classic stacked patch design from the literature operates in this manner and that Coupled Mode Theory governs its operation.

articleTitle: Media-Based Modulation with Reconfigurable Intelligent Metasurfaces: Design and Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With increasing global wireless connectivity in spectrum-limited congested urban environments, next-generation wireless networks require communications systems that achieve high spectral efficiency at low RF costs. In this context, media-based modulation (MBM) is a recently proposed form of index modulation with data rate, error performance, and hardware benefits. The MBM is a channel modulation technique that employs radiation pattern states of a reconfigurable antenna to encode the information bits. In this paper, we introduce large intelligent reconfigurable metasurface (R-MTS) to implement MBM in beyond fifth-generation (5G) systems. We present a system model for R-MTS-based MBM and design such a surface to demonstrate radiation pattern diversity in a realistic 5G communications system. Our numerical experiments show superior performance of R-MTS MBM in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance over traditional M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) techniques.

articleTitle: Design of Beam Steering Patch Arrays Using Self-Phased Metasurface Pixels
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a new design concept of microstrip patch antenna arrays that have analog beam steering without using phase shifters external to the array elements. This can be achieved by combining traditional probe-fed microstrip patch antenna arrays with anisotropic Huygens metasurfaces. A metasurface pixel is fed by a microstrip patch, forming the phased-array element. The phase shifts between antenna elements are obtained by the Huygens' metasurface pixel. Three layers of a metallic mesh are separated by two dielectric substrates to form the Huygens metasurface pixel, which has an overall thickness of about one third the operating wavelength. A proposed phased array is designed and simulated. The radiation pattern is shown to be able to steer the beam from minus 20 degrees to plus 20 degrees in analog fashion. This novel technique can greatly reduce the cost of a phased-array system, especially in 5G massive MIMO system.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed by Tapered Dielectric Rod Waveguide for 5G mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (RDRA) for 5G millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications is presented. The design consists of a rectangular dielectric resonator placed at the top of a rectangular dielectric rod waveguide (RDRW) to eliminate loss from metallic parts used to feed the DRA. The antenna is fed by a metallic waveguide (WR-34) that operates in the range of 22 to 33 GHz. The structural design and simulation results are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Shared Aperture Dual-band Waveguide Slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel design of the Ku/Ka dual-band shared aperture waveguide slot antenna is proposed in this paper. The rectangular ridge waveguide is used to reduce the aperture size. And the Ka-band waveguide antennas are mounted on the upper left and upper right of the Ku-band waveguide to effectively utilize the spatial size. The simulated results validate that the proposed antenna is capable of covering 15.76GHz~16.26GHz (VSWR ≤ 2) and 34.95GHz~36.74GHz (VSWR ≤ 2). The proposed antenna achieves low cross polarization within the operating band. And its structure is applicable to Ku/Ka dual-band satellite communication.

articleTitle: Holographic Metasurface Antennas with Dynamic Beam Pointing and Polarization Control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This report provides insight into Kymeta's electronically-scanned antenna technology. The antenna is based on the concept of holographic beam forming implemented through a diffractive metasurface and liquid crystal display technology. This concept provides dynamic beam pointing and polarization control.

articleTitle: Long-Range Wireless Frequency Synchronization for Distributed Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate wireless frequency synchronization of separate wireless systems over a 90 m distance using a microwave system supporting joint frequency transfer and localization. Wireless frequency synchronization represents one of the basic coordination requirements in coherent distributed phased arrays. When combined with inter-node ranging, frequency synchronization enables separate nodes to implement distributed beamforming for various applications. We build on a novel spectrally-sparse two-tone ranging waveform combined with a self-mixing receiver circuit that demodulates a frequency reference from the two-tone separation and is used to synchronize the local oscillator. Measurements conducted outdoors demonstrate basic synchronization between two wireless systems, providing a framework for future distributed beamforming with widely separated nodes.

articleTitle: A Compact Metamaterial Inspired CPW fed Multiband Monopole Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact metamaterial (MTM) inspired coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed multiband monopole antenna operate at Bluetooth, WiMAX, WLAN frequency bands. The overall dimension of the antenna is 21x29x1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna consists of meta inspired monopole along with metamaterial loading resulting in a compact electrical size of 0.23λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.17λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.013λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is calculated at first resonating frequency 2.4 GHz. The proposed antenna gives quad band operation with centre frequencies 2.4 GHz, 3.4 GHz, 5.1 GHz and 5.8 GHz with -10dB impedance bandwidths of 9.17%, 11.44%, 3.73% and 4.66% respectively.

articleTitle: Machine Learning to Immune Microwave Sensors from Temperature Impact
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a planar microwave sensor is used for contactless material characterization at~2.7 GHz. The extraneous impact of temperature is shown to cause interleaved data (amplitude) traces for various material that leads to potential confusion for sensor readout. This issue is resolved with proper Artificial Neural Network (ANN) design with single hidden layer. Various concentrations of water in acetone (0 - 50% with 10% increments) are exposed to temperature rise of 25°C - 60°C. The output of the proposed system confirms successful discrimination of the flowing aqueous solutions up to 91% accuracy.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling of UWB Antennas Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A convolutional neural network (CNN) model is proposed for parametric modeling of ultra-wideband (UWB) antennas. Given the image of an antenna, CNN fast predicts its electromagnetic (EM) responses and speeds up the design process. The validity and efficiency of the proposed model is confirmed by a parametric modeling example of a UWB band-notched antenna. The results also demonstrate that this model has potential use in mapping the relationship between the antenna structure and corresponding EM responses.

articleTitle: Impact of Miniaturization on a UHF tri-fillar antenna for IoT communication from satellite
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the use of a three element solution is studied for Internet of Things (IoT) communication from space using Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite. A compact circularly polarized and wide beam-width radiation pattern performance is desired. Impact of miniaturization on frequency bandwidth and peak gain is studied. Simulation results show that antenna performance are strongly degraded for maximal dimension below lambda over 5.

articleTitle: A Study of Received Power in Distributed Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, microwave wireless power transfer (MWPT) for loT devices has been researched. However, there are some problems with high-power microwave transmission such as effect on the human body, interference to other devices and cost. In this study, we propose a distributed MWPT system that enables to reducing of transmitted power density and improving the received power level. By the simulation and experiment, the effectiveness of the distributed MWPT system has been shown.

articleTitle: 320 GHz On-Chip Circularly-Polarized Antenna Array Realized with 0.13 μm BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 320 GHz on-chip circularly-polarized (CP) antenna array that has been facilitated with 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS technology is presented. It is the first designed and prototyped THz-band on-chip antenna array with circular polarization and high directivity. The antenna is realized by designing a 4 ×4 microstrip-fed CP patch antenna array inside the silicon dioxide layer on top of a silicon base. A sequential phase rotation scheme is applied to the four 2 ×2 subarrays to achieve wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth (8.7 GHz). The antenna array was successfully prototyped in a 3.6×3.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area on a silicon wafer. Consequently, it easily combined with other integrated circuit (IC) components. The developed THz on-chip CP antenna is highly desired for the emerging ultra-high speed wireless applications.

articleTitle: Dualband Stacked Metasurface Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reflectarray antenna operating at two distinct frequencies is reported. The antenna consists of two metasurfaces (subwavelength patterned metallic claddings) above a ground plane, separated by dielectric substrates. The metasurfaces are homogenized and the reflectarray is designed using a system of coupled volume-surface integral equations. The system includes three surface integral equations for the currents on the thin metasurfaces and ground plane, and two volume integral equations for the polarization currents within the dielectric substrates. The system of integral equations is discretized using the method of moments and simultaneously solved for the currents and the electric sheet impedances of the metasurfaces needed to collimate an incident cylindrical wave upon reflection at two different frequencies. The system is initially nonlinear as both the currents and the sheet impedances are unknown. A guess and update design procedure is used to linearize the system and solve it iteratively. The performance of the metasurface reflectarray antenna is verified using a commercial finite element solver, validating the design algorithm.

articleTitle: Compact and Reconfigurable Multiband 2-Element MIMO Slot Antenna for Advanced Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a compact, multiband and reconfigurable MIMO antenna for wireless systems is designed and presented. The antenna element is composed of three open-end quarter-wave slots fed by proximity coupling via a 50 ohms microstrip feed line. The total area of the MIMO antenna is 24 x 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. For the decoupling mechanism, T-shaped and vertical slots are embedded between the two elements of the antenna. As a result, the MIMO antenna achieves a maximum isolation of 25 dB (15 dB of improvement), 12.5 dB (4.5 dB of improvement) and 35 dB (15 dB of improvement) at frequencies of 2.4 GHz, 3.5 GHz and 5.25 GHz, respectively. In addition, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.02 and the gain diversity (DG) is more than 9.9 for the three considered operating bands. The proposed reconfigurable antenna can be switched between simple, dual and triple band modes, which is a good candidate for use in cognitive radios and wireless systems.

articleTitle: RF Coupling Suppression Circuit for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless technology is growing at a fast rate to accommodate the expanding user demands. Currently the radio frequency (RF) spectrum is highly congested and more susceptible to signal fratricide and interference. Therefore, full duplexing techniques are required to enhance the access to the spectrum. Simultaneous Transmit and receive systems (STAR), also known as in-band full duplex systems, are gaining higher attention due to their capability to double spectral efficiency. However, successful implementation of STAR systems requires significant isolation between the transmit and receive signals to reduce self-interference (SI) signal. To minimize this self-interference, front-end coupling cancellation circuits are employed in STAR system. In this paper, an RF coupling suppression circuit is presented based on a hybrid finite impulse response filter (FIR) and resonator architecture. Notably, this newly developed FIR-resonator circuit achieves >30dB cancellation across a >1.5:1 bandwidth.

articleTitle: High Gain Series fed Planar Microstrip Antenna Array using printed L—probe feed
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a series fed linear and planar microstrip antenna array using L-probe feed technique. The L-probe feed technique provide extra design parameters for tuning the impedance of the antenna array. The 5×1 linear array has gain of 15.5 dBi and S11 ≤ -10B bandwidth of 5.75-6.23 GHz. In addition, a 5×5 planar array is also designed to achieve a gain of 18.6 dBi. The S11 ≤ -10dB bandwidth for the planar array is 5.5 - 6.42GHz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Rx/Tx Phased Array Antenna With a Spiral Lattice for Sidelobe Level Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A hybrid antenna array in a compact shared aperture for Rx and Tx is presented in this paper. Each antenna is a dual-band, polarisation reconfigurable, circularly polarised radiator. It consists of two concentric elements, a slotted circular patch nested in an annular ring. The inner element operates in the Tx band (30 GHz) and the outer element operates in the Rx band (20 GHz). Both the elements are excited with two orthogonal feeds in phase quadrature which generates a reconfigurable, circularly polarised axial beam. The Tx and Rx beams have a directivity of 6.6 dBi and 6.4 dBi respectively. Further, an array scanning performance of such elements in triangular and spiral geometry is compared and investigated for sidelobe level reduction.

articleTitle: Demonstrating Device-free Localization based on Radio Tomographic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio tomographic imaging (RTI) is a localization technique that can estimate the position of an object on the basis of the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) acquired by WiFi or other wireless networks. In this paper, we demonstrate the RTI approach by utilizing full electromagnetic simulations of an indoor environment. In particular, we consider dielectric cylinders with varying permittivities but fixed radius in which 20 WiFi nodes are deployed on the perimeter (6 m by 3 m) of a room to perform RTI. RTI based on the line-of-sight (LOS) weighting model with total variation based regularization was then used to demonstrate device-free localization. The results indicate that device-free location is possible, even for very high permittivities of greater than 30, motivating further future investigations.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Cross-Dipole Antenna With L-shape Slots
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized cross-dipole antenna with L-shape slots is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna contains two pairs of orthogonally placed wide rectangular dipoles and a metal ground. Two L-shape slots are embedded into each arm of the cross dipoles to broaden the AR bandwidth. Simulation results show that an impedance bandwidth of 66.2% from 1.77 GHz to 3.52 GHz and an AR bandwidth of 42.2% from 2.26 GHz to 3.47 GHz are obtained. The average CP gain of the proposed antenna within the operating frequency band is 8 dBic.

articleTitle: Transparent Circularly-Polarized Antenna with Tilted Beam for Vehicular Platforms
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a transparent microstrip CPW-fed antenna which could be used in Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) bands has been proposed. The antenna is designed on a glass substrate which can be mounted on the windshield of a car. The beam of the antenna is tilted for 30 degrees as lots of cars' windshields are inclined around 30 degrees. This design has 59% 10-dB return loss bandwidth (0.97-1.78 GHz) and 3-dB axial ratio of 12% (1.14-1.3 GHz) and 14% (1.43-1.65 GHz) over lower and upper frequency bands of interest, respectively. The obtained optical transparency of the proposed antenna is 88%.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly-Polarized Slot-Array Antenna in Ka-Band fed by Groove Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual circularly-polarized slot-array antenna fed by a Groove Gap Waveguide (GGW) and operating in the Ka-Band is presented in this paper. A simple mechanism is proposed to switch the polarization, from RHCP to LHCP, and viceversa. The lid of the antenna has two pieces: one fixed and one sliding. The fixed piece hosts T-shaped slots, and the sliding block is in charge of adjusting the offset of the perpendicular grooves with respect to the longitudinal slots. Preliminary results show an axial ratio below 1.5 dB for both, RHCP and LHCP, within a bandwidth of 1 GHz centered at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: RF-Induced Heating of Spinal Cord Stimulator under Different Implantations and Body Loading Orientations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of RF-induced heating for spinal cord stimulators (SCS) under different implantation procedures. Eight different SCS models were used to evaluate the temperature rises. 16464 temperature rise (ΔT) samples are calculated and analyzed against variations of landmark positions and implantation locations. Results show that implantations can have a significant effect on the RF-induced heating.

articleTitle: Four-Port CSRR-Loaded Dual-Band Dual-Mode Patch Sub-Array for Massive MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a four-port sub-array of dual-band dual-mode square patches loaded with complementary split-ring resonators (CSRRs), for application in massive MIMO base-stations. The CSRR loading induces an additional lower frequency radiation mode with orthogonal current distribution with respect to the fundamental mode. Full wave simulation results further validate the achieved high-gain (> 5.5 dBi) broadside pattern in both the bands, as well as the pattern/polarization diversity achieved via rotationally symmetric patch-arrangement.

articleTitle: 2D Dirac Leaky Wave Antenna with Circular Polarization for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A two dimensional photonic crystal (PC) based antenna is presented that radiates a `circular polarization' (CP) directive pencil beam at broadside with low side-lobe levels, at millimeter. This is owing to the PCs a closed band gap at the center of the Brillouin zone. The PC consists of air columns in a low permittivity grounded substrate. This PC based antenna is corner excited from the backside using a coaxial cable and generates a broadside pencil beam with a maximum gain of <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">~</sub>18 dBi. The antenna exhibits an good impedance bandwidth, and is overall well suited for millimeter-wave applications such as emerging 5G and IoT that require reliable directive CP beaming.

articleTitle: Compact and Reconfigurable Leaky Wave Antenna Based on a Tunable Substrate Integrated Embedded Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A leaky wave antenna (LWA) based on a substrate integrated embedded metasurface (SIMS) is proposed and simulated. The SIMS is obtained by blind vias in the middle of a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and filling the gap beneath the blind vias with liquid crystals (LC). Different capacitive impedances are obtained by biasing the LC, which impacts the propagation characteristics of the LWA and thus changes its beam angle. A 30° beam steering at 52.5 GHz is achieved according to simulations of the proposed SIMS-LWA. The unique advantages of this LWA include high realized gain, simple mechanism for beam steering, frequency-fixed reconfiguration, non-complex design with much reduced bias lines and control circuits, low cost, low profile, compactness, and mature of LC technology, to name a few.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Antennas Design for Microwave Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present two novel antennas for microwave imaging applications with compact size, i.e., 70 mm ×10 mm ×15 mm and 66 mm ×9 mm ×15 mm, respectively. Despite their reduced dimensions, they retain a substantially large frequency band (1.28-2.34 GHz) considering a -10 dB reflection coefficient as reference, which can be usefully applied for microwave brain imaging. The combination of compactness together with large operative bandwidth make them excellent candidates for portable head imaging systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Planar Coupled-resonator Cavity-backed Slot Array Filtenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel planar array antenna with filtering functionality is presented. The main idea is to integrate both the antenna and filter with a combined treatment. The coupled radiating resonators are effectively adopted to obtain a fourth degree steep roll-off filtering antenna (filtenna). The proposed antenna is a 2*2 cavity-backed slot array antenna built by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The proposed slot array filtenna take the advantages of total size reduction, efficient utilization of RF power and spectrum as well as enhanced signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The design methodology is verified by achieving return loss and realized gain better than -15 dB and 9 dBi, respectively, which exhibits unique capability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Zirconia for UWB Stacked Conical Ring DRA
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a 3D printed ultrawideband (2.95 GHz-20 GHz) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) fabricated using Nano-Particle Jetting (NPJ) of high permittivity, low loss, mechanically tough ceramic, zirconia. 3D printing enables fabrication of geometrically complex DRA design without machining or high pressure shaping. The wideband impedance response was achieved with a hybrid monopole/DRA design that uses the fundamental and higher order modes of the monopole and the parasitic DRA rings for a wide impedance bandwidth (VSWR <; 3). In the future, the 3D printing technique can enable building DRAs with more complex shapes or ceramic lattices to build graded index lenses.

articleTitle: A Spiral Radial Line Slot Array Antenna for NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART)
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A spiral Radial Line Slot Array (RLSA) Qualification Model (QM) High Gain Antenna (HGA) was designed, fabricated and tested for the DART spacecraft. The antenna operated at the X-band Deep Space Network (DSN) frequencies of 7.2 and 8.4 GHz. The fabricated antenna exceeds the given requirements, agrees well simulations, and has been tested through environments resulting in a TRL-6 design.

articleTitle: Printed RGW 3-dB Backward Coupler for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work introduces a flat coupling backward-wave directional coupler based on a printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology for mm-wave applications. The construction of the proposed coupler is based on a coupled PRGW lines connected by a central rectangular junction. The coupler is demonstrated to have 8% relative bandwidth at 30 GHz. The prototype of the proposed coupler is fabricated and measured, where the measured and simulated results show good agreement.

articleTitle: Mm-Wave Beam Steering Antenna Based on Extended Hemispherical Lens Antenna Subarrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A mm-wave beam steering antenna based on lens antenna subarrays (LASs) is presented. Different from the recent work, the antenna employs extended hemispherical dielectric lenses and achieves 2D beam steering. To maximize the scan range with minimum number of antennas (M), the solution of the disk covering problem is employed to find initial positions of the feed antennas. A new design procedure is developed to maximize the scan range and reduce side lobes with systematically employed 3D full-wave simulation based parametric sweeps on lens geometry and feed antenna positions. Compared to the conventional planar phased array antenna occupying the equivalent aperture (L <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sub> M elements), the presented antenna utilizes a single phase shifter per lens (L) to reduce the hardware complexity. It is demonstrated that the presented antenna performs with the largest scan range and low side lobe level (SLL) compared to previous subarray-based antenna arrays. Specifically, the antenna operates at 38 GHz with L = 7, M = 17 and provides 12.8% S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB, 19.8 dBi peak realized gain, a scan range of 80° and SLL below -9 dB.

articleTitle: Low Loss Cu/Co Metaconductor Based Array Antenna in Ka Band for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Performance enhanced array antennas are implemented using multilayer Cu/Co metaconductor in K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> band for 5G applications. A 4×4 array antenna has been designed and fabricated using 10 pairs of Cu/Co (150 nm/ 25 nm) nanolayers and its performance has been compared with a solid copper counterpart with the same overall dimensions. Due to eddy current cancellation and skin effect suppression, nearly 6 dB improvement in signal reception power has been demonstrated using the Cu/Co metaconductor based antenna compared to the solid Cu based antenna. The contribution of conductor loss has been extracted using signal path loss and Friis transmission equations. The effective RF conductivity of the Cu/Co metaconductor is nearly twice as large as that of the reference solid copper at 31 GHz.

articleTitle: 10 GHz-100 GHz Compact Double-Ridge Horn Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Millimeter-Wave Biomedical Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact double-ridge horn antenna for radar-based ultra-wideband millimeter-wave (mm-wave) biomedical diagnostics. The proposed antenna is composed of a coaxial to double-ridge waveguide (DRW) transition and a free-space matching section. The antenna is designed such that it can be fed using a commercial 1.00 mm coaxial flange launcher. The effect of the ridge profile inside the back-cavity structure of the designed transition is investigated and optimized to achieve an ultrawideband single-mode bandwidth. Finally, to achieve a smooth transition and a good impedance match to the free-space, exponentially-tapered matching section is employed and optimized. The antenna has small aperture size of 20 mm×24 mm and demonstrates stable gain and symmetric radiation patterns across the bandwidth.

articleTitle: Intelligent Wristbands - Fabrication of Wearable RFID Solutions by 3D Printing Pen
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present RFID (radio frequency identification)-based passive UHF (ultra-high frequency) wristbands fabricated with a 3D printing pen. The used 3D printing material is flexible and biodegradable, and thus suitable for fabrication of such inexpensive and widely useful wearable wireless platforms. The tag antenna (that is fabricated from conductive thread) and the RFID IC (integrated circuit) are embedded into the platform by using 3D-printed fasteners. This paper presents the wristband fabrication, ensures their reliability, and carries out practical testing in normal use environments. Based on the achieved results, the studied combination of conductive thread and 3D printing pen is a suitable fabrication solution for intelligent wearable platforms. The fabricated wristbands show high moisture reliability and excellent wireless performance in practical testing situations.

articleTitle: The Waveguide Slot Array Antenna in Millimeter Waveband using the Reflection Canceling Stairs for the Sidelobe Suppression
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We numerically demonstrate significant aperture efficiency improvement by employing reflection cancelling stairs in slotted waveguide arrayed antenna. The antenna includes 10 linearly allocated elements (slot with corresponding step). In this paper, we confirm the good performance by calculating the radiation patterns of the proposed antenna. Aperture efficiency up to 64.9% is obtained by a compact antenna with reflection canceling stair. In addition, we achieve extremely good directional property by arranging 10 identical antennas as an array.

Author Keywords: arrayed antenna and aperture efficiency improvement

articleTitle: A Heatsink Integrated Antenna with Controllable Electromagnetic and Thermal Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an antenna with integrated heatsink. The heatsink is connected with antenna through Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) cantilever switches for controllable and optimum electromagnetic (EM) and thermal dissipation performance. The integrated heatsink codesigned antenna can achieve 14 °C and 27°C temperature reduction and controllable reflection coefficient of -23 dB and -15 dB when the switches are OFF and ON, respectively. In addition, the EM performance of antenna is improved with optimized heatsink having an increased gain of 8.1 dB from 5.9 dB.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Compact ME Antenna Design for Implantable Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a new ultra-compact antenna design based on magnetoelectric coupling effect for implantable wireless communication is introduced. This ME antenna is driven by acoustic wave and the resonance frequency is decided by the geometric size of resonator. An NPR antenna is fabricated by MEMS technology and tested. The size of one antenna resonator is 8×350μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the whole antenna is designed to 730×940μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with 16 arrays in parallel. An antenna gain of -54.81dBi is achieved at the resonance frequency of 371.125MHz. The Q-factor of 123.1 is calculated by MBVD model. Because of the short wavelength of acoustic wave, the antenna size is effectively scaled down, which gives a new solution for the miniaturization of entire implantable device.

articleTitle: Non-Conventional Cavity Backed Sinuous Antenna for UWB Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper illustrates the design of a ultra-wideband (UWB) four arms non-conventional sinuous antenna for radar electronic support measures (RESM) systems.
