The antenna works from 1.5 GHz to 18 GHz with a slant 45 polarization ensuring good matching impedance and stable radiative performances. The installation on platform is simplified by exploiting several miniaturization techniques that allows to obtain a definitive diameter of 6 cm. The radiating element exhibits directive stable patterns, good polarization purity and high realized gain in the whole frequency band. Finally the design provides an effective miniaturization of the sinuous antenna with encouraging simulation results.

articleTitle: High Directive Fabry-Pérot Cavity Antenna by Using Reflecting Metasurface for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high directive Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity antenna by using highly reflecting metasurface at 28 GHz for 5G applications. A highly reflecting metasurface is designed to achieve transmitting all energy in the cavity with minimum reflection. The structure of the antenna is a source antenna (patch antenna), a half-wavelength cavity and a highly reflecting metasurface (MS). The proposed antenna at 28 GHz have a good radiation performance in terms of directivity with 9 dB directivity improvement.

articleTitle: Dualband Patch Antenna Design Using Binary Grey Wolf Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Various antenna design problems are discrete-valued. To address these problems, binary-coded algorithms suited for combinatorial optimization problems are required. Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is a recently proposed evolutionary algorithm based on grey wolves' behavior. Although GWO was originally designed for real-valued problems, discrete versions also exist. In this paper, we apply a binary GWO algorithm (bGWO) for arbitrary-shaped dual-band patch antenna design. Computational results demonstrate that bGWO is quite efficient and can be further applied to discrete valued problems in electromagnetics.

articleTitle: A High Gain Beam-Steering Luneburg Lens Antenna For 76–81 GHz Automotive Radars
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The complex scenarios for the autonomous vehicle require high resolution, long range, beam-steering radar systems with new millimeter wave antenna concepts at 76-81 GHz. In this paper, a new structure for generating the beam-steering based on Luneburg lens (LL) is presented. The designed antenna is configured with a spherical Luneburg lens placed on the top side of a linear array of seven dielectric resonator antennas (LLDRA). The simulated results show beam-steering performance from -30° to 30° in a broad-bandwidth (76-81 GHz). In addition, the DRA antenna's gain and directivity have been significantly boosted after using the Luneburg lens to 25 dBi.

articleTitle: Wideband Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) With 5.4:1 Bandwidth on a Miura-Ori Pattern
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a foldable Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) implemented on a Miura-Ori pattern. This array achieves a wide broadside bandwidth of 5.4:1 (viz. 1.14 GHz – 6.16 GHz) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 3$</tex>. This paper is the first to show the foldability of a Miura patterned TCDA using standard printed circuit board (PCB) substrates and practical feeds. A simple differential pair of conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50-\Omega$</tex> coax cables are included, with low profile snap-on connectors to enable foldability.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of 3D Wire Grid Antenna An Integrated Method for Optimization in Constrained Volumes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design concept, optimization methods, simulated radiation properties, and additive manufacturing methods for 3D wire grid antennas in symmetric and non-symmetric arbitrary volumes are presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupled Circularly Polarized Hybrid Antenna for LTE Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication, a hybrid antenna is presented with Circular Polarization (CP) for Long-Term-Evolution (LTE-2600 MHz) applications. The proposed hybrid-antenna is composed of a hexagonal-shaped patch loaded with a hexagonal-split-ring slot and a parasitic rectangular dielectric resonator block. Electromagnetic (EM) coupled-feed (Proximity-Coupled-feed) used to feed the antenna structure. A hexagonal split-ring has been etched diagonally at 45 degrees on the hexagonal patch to obtain the CP-radiation. By loading parasitic rectangular Dielectric-Resonator (DR) block along the edge of the patch, the Return Loss (RL) bandwidth, Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth, and AR beam-width enhanced without disturbing the CP radiation. The performance of the proposed hybrid antenna versus split-ring slotted hexagonal patch is analyzed and discussed in this paper. The gain obtained for the proposed antenna is 6.75 dBic.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Bifunctional Triple-Band Heatsink Antenna for RF and Thermal Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Future IoT environment requires billions of wireless sensor nodes where energy consumption of these devices will be a concern. This problem can be solved by harvesting energy from ambient environment to power these sensor nodes. Ambient RF and thermal energy have a great potential, as both of them are available in most of the places. When combining these two energy harvesters into one module, optimized design is required. This work presents a bifunctional heatsink antenna, which serves as a part of a triple-band RF energy harvester (GSM900, GSM1800 and 3G) and also acts as a heatsink which boosts the performance of the thermal energy harvester. The antenna has been designed by using Ansys HFSS and Solidworks in parallel for optimal RF and thermal performances. Average 3dB of gain boost for antenna performance and 3 times more heat transfer is achieved when heatsink antenna is used compared to flat antenna.

articleTitle: Integrated Multilayer Horn Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a wide band slot antenna with a two-section T-shaped ridge is designed at 30 GHz based on printed ridge gap waveguide technology. Later, to enhance the antenna gain, a multi-layer stepped horn is designed with PCB substrates. The horn results in an overall increase in gain up to 11.5 dBi, and the bandwidth exceeds 26.5% from 26.5-34.6 GHz. The steps walls are realized by metal vias. To control the leakages between the conducting surfaces of the layers, two rows of mushrooms are used around the metal vias to form PEC/PMC parallel-plate waveguides that don't allow for leakage between them. In addition, three rows of mushrooms act as a soft surface around the horn opening to improve the radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Stealth Communication Via Smart Ultra-Wide-Band Signal in 5G, Radar, Electronic Warfare, etc.
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To meet cybersecurity and privacy needs, “Stealth Communication” (SC) is a new approach to enable information transmission with a very low probability of being detected or interfered with. A wireless SC requires that the operating RF signal be smart, Ultra-Wide-Band (UWB), in full-fledged spatial waveform, and mimics noise. “Communication” here is broad-scoped, encompassing electronic warfare (EW), radar, communications, etc. For terrestrial 5G wireless, MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) is needed. Empirical study on implementation of SC in 5G has produced promising results, especially for the early-bird 5G which operates at frequencies below 11 GHz only.

articleTitle: Controlling Wavefront using a Coarsely Discretized Dielectric Huygens' Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports a coarsely discretized dielectric Huygens' metasurface that comprises of only three elements per grating period. The resulting metasurface, which we termed as tripartite dielectric Huygens' metasurface (TD-HMS), greatly simplifies the design leading to a cost-effective and robust metasurface for efficient electromagnetic wave manipulation. Through full-wave electromagnetic simulations at 60 GHz, we show that the proposed TDHMS can achieve efficient anomalous transmission, where the desired diffracted mode contains more than 80% of the total transmitted power.

articleTitle: Flat Meta-Lens Antenna Synthesis Via Geometrical Optics and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A customized numerical synthesis algorithm for the design of flat meta-lens antennas is presented. The algorithm is based on a linkage between Geometrical Optics (GO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The presented technique, which was previously applied for the design of shaped inhomogeneous lens antennas, is now applied to synthesize flat meta-lens antennas. It is general enough to synthesize the inhomogeneity of a flat meta-lens for any desired aperture phase with circular symmetry. An example of an on-axis fed flat meta-lens optimized for uniform aperture phase is presented. Another flat meta-lens is synthesized based on the assumption of previous works that the ray path is straight within the volume of the lens. Full-wave simulation results for the two lenses demonstrate the superior performance of the optimized flat meta-lens and validate the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Broadband Transparent Antenna Integrated with an Indoor Solar Cell for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a broadband transparent antenna integrated with an indoor solar cell for WLAN communication systems is described. The transparent patch antenna is realized using two layers of copper mesh with micron-sized linewidth. Measurement results show that a broad bandwidth of 20% covering the WLAN band from 4.8 to 5.9 GHz and a uni-directional radiation pattern with backlobe and cross-polarization below -20 dB can be achieved. By utilizing a transparent copper mesh ground on top of the solar cell, a good antenna gain of up to 7 dBi can be achieved. We also utilize two methods to evaluate the transparency of the proposed antenna and it is found to be at least 83%.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Approach to Synthesize Multilayer Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The synthesis of a metasurface exhibiting a specific set of desired scattering properties is a time-consuming and resource-demanding process, which conventionally relies on many cycles of full-wave simulations. It requires the designer to choose the number of the metallic layers, the scatterer shapes, and the type and the thickness of the separating substrates. Here, we propose a machine learning (ML)-based approach to automate the inverse design of dual-layer metasurfaces, which is extendable to multilayer metasurfaces. This approach allows synthesis of thin structures where higher-order mode coupling between the layers is significant, and hence, can be leveraged for extra degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Polarisation-Reconfigurable Half E-Shaped Antenna Array for Q-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a Dual-Band (30GHz & 38GHz) Half E-shaped antenna array that provides reconfigurable circular polarisation and shared aperture capability for Q-band applications. Q-band communication is attractive due to the higher data rates and capacity at these frequencies. However, the smaller antenna size at Q-band means that intricate broadband antenna concepts (e.g. spirals) are difficult to implement. Therefore, this paper proposes a resonance antenna sub-array to provide key benefits while maintaining low complexity and low cost. The sub-array consists of four linearly polarised Half E-shaped antennas arranged in rotational symmetry of a 2x2 array configuration. Each element has been kept electronically small so that the size of a 2x2 subarray is about 0.8λ38GHz. This enables beam steering in both azimuth and elevation planes from a large phased array. Each Half E-shaped antenna provides dual-band resonance for shared aperture functionality. By feeding each antenna with a sequential +90° or -90° phase shift, the combined beam can be reconfigured to provide either RHCP or LHCP respectively. This paper provides solution for future high-performance Qband applications by realising a shared aperture array with small size, simple fabrication and low cost.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Polarized Vivaldi Antenna for Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact dual-polarized Vivaldi antenna is presented. Four Vivaldi elements are used as radiators, and are positioned obliquely and connected in a horn shape. By exciting two sets of elements, two orthogonally polarized radiations can be achieved. The dual-polarized antenna features a low operating frequency band with a wide bandwidth, high port isolation, good directional radiation performance, and a very compact size, making it highly suitable for the ground penetrating radar (GPR) application.

articleTitle: Analysis of an E-shaped Patch Using CMA and CMT
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The impedance bandwidth of a microstrip patch antenna may be increased by additional resonances in the antenna structure. This work uses Characteristic Mode Analysis to show that the E-shaped patch operates in this manner and that its operation is well-modeled by Coupled Mode Theory.

articleTitle: Fractal X-Shaped FSS Employed Electromagnetic Shield for X-band SATCOMs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) based electromagnetic shield is designed to avoid interference for SATCOMs in X-band. The proposed FSS unit cell is a modified X-shaped geometry and has a band-stop frequency selective behavior. The proposed unit cell has compact dimensions with at least 32 dB attenuation to provide electromagnetic shielding in X-band. Moreover, this FSS based EM-shield achieves a stable frequency response up to 60° for both transverse electric (TE) and the transverse magnetic (TM) polarization. Finite Element Boundary Integral (FEBI) Method, equivalent circuit modeling of the proposed FSS also verify its suitability for SATCOM applications.

articleTitle: Practical Bending Studying on UWB Pentagonal Flexible Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the effect of bending on UWB pentagonal shape antenna. The antenna is considered to be used for modern UWB wearable technology including RFID, mobile devices, wearable GPS, to mention a few. The antenna is built on polyimide substrate of 50um in thickness. The effect of bending has been studies in term of S-parameters and radiation pattern. The pentagonal shape UWB antenna bandwidth before and after the bending is 111.6% which extended from 2.93 GHz to 10.3 GHz. While the gain of the antenna is averaging around 3dB at 3.5 GHz, 5.2 GHz, and 5.8 GHz before and after the bending. The antenna is suitable solution for modern wearable technology.

articleTitle: High-Gain Simple Printed Dipole-Loop Antenna for RF-Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact dual-band antenna for RF energy harvesting applications is presented. The basic antenna structure is formed using a combination between a dipole and a loop antenna to operate at 900 MHz and 1600 MHz, respectively. To enable the antenna to resonate at a dual- band within a compact substrate, two L-shaped vertical arms as a dipole connected with a trapezoidal slot loop. A meandered transmission line is connected to the coplanar slot line to act as a stub to match the input impedance of the dipole and the loop. On the back of the antenna, a reflector is positioned to enhance the forward to back ratio and provide a unidirectional radiation pattern. The antenna has a compact size 0.149λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>×0.23λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> (with respect to the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency), making it comparatively smaller than similar designs. It has a measured fractional bandwidth of 11% at 0.970 GHz at the lower band and 52.9% at the upper band from 1.5 to 2.58 GHz. The antenna performance has a peak gain of 6.5 dB. To prove the antenna normal operation, a prototype is fabricated, tested and the measurements are compared against the simulation results. This antenna is intended for the RF wireless energy harvesting applications.

articleTitle: Low Cost Flexible Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact flexible conformal antenna for multiband applications is proposed. The antenna is useful for the wide range of applications such as the IoT, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and ISM band. With a -6 dB impedance bandwidth, the antenna covers frequency bands from 0.773 -0.883 GHz, 2.1 - 2.7 GHz and 5.2 - 6.4 GHz. The antenna is designed on a flexible Acrylic sheet which makes it suitable for the conformal applications. The scheme to integrate the antenna to the IoT devices is also proposed. Additional results would be shown during the symposium.

articleTitle: Radial Gaussian Beam Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A general method for designing metasurface antennas with radially-polarized, azimuthally invariant aperture fields is introduced. The antennas consist of a metasurface (a cascade of inhomogeneous electric sheets) above a coaxially-fed, cylindrical cavity. The metasurface covering the cylindrical cavity matches the antenna to the feed and establishes the desired aperture field through modal conversion. The impedance profiles of the electric sheets comprising the metasurface are found through optimization. The optimization routine is accelerated through the use of the Discrete Hankel Transform (DHT) and modal network theory.

articleTitle: In Vivo Monitoring of Dog’s Knee Flexion Using Wearable Wrap-Around Coils
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Our aim in this paper is to validate a new class of wrap-around coils for seamless monitoring of joint flexion angles under in vivo settings in dogs. Resonant wrap-around coils operating at 31 MHz of unequal radii are integrated on a knee brace and are shown to measure knee joint flexion of a dog (golden retriever) from 30° (full extension) to 110°. This method has the potential to operate in non-contrived environments, hence overcoming shortcomings in state-of-the-art motion capture. By allowing for continuous monitoring of joint flexion, large datasets can be collected in natural settings to better understand knee function and help develop improved rehabilitation protocols.

articleTitle: CmWave to MmWave Reconfigurable Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable antenna with a tunable operating frequency from mmwave band (e.g., 28GHz) to microwave frequency band (e.g., 6GHz and below). The antenna consists of multiple individual antenna elements at mmwave frequency connected with Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) based switches. Considering the location, dimension, and the number of MEMS switches, this paper thoroughly studies their effects on the performance of individual antenna elements and the entire array. A 3×3 antenna array has been implemented to demonstrate frequency tunability from 6GHz to 28 GHz with good performance. Better frequency reconfigurability can be achieved with more optimized antenna elements and switches.

articleTitle: A Steerable Beam Patch Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Band Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter-wave (MMW) coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed microstrip antenna with a steerable radiation pattern is designed. The beam steering characteristic is achieved by creating a proper elliptic slot into the circular patch structure and a proper radiating element of modified Gielis curves (MGCs). A full ground plane is utilized to improve the antenna pattern, as well. The achieved steering beam variation is from -14<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> to 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> over the frequency band of 26 to 28.5 GHz with a proper antenna gain. The proposed antenna is applicable in millimeter-wave band systems and 5G communication networks where an steerable beam with a satisfactory antenna gain is required.

articleTitle: Rapid Alternative Calibration Procedure of Reverberation Chamber Using Coupling Transfer Gain Function
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study proposes an alternative fast calibration procedure for the estimation of the well-stirred condition of the reverberation chamber (RC) using coupling transfer gain function. The novel coupling transfer current gain function of RC environment is developed using the measured two-port S-parameters. The proposed procedure involves the determination of the frequency corresponding to the well-stirred operation ( fwso) of RC through the assessment of RC EM-field distribution using high order goodness of fit tests, and checking of the requirements of the independent samples for the particular stirred environment. The proposed procedure requires a portion of time (around 30 minutes) as compared to the conventional field uniformity long RC calibration procedure.

articleTitle: Analysis of Schottky Multistage Voltage Doubler Rectifiers for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multistage Voltage Doubler Rectifiers (MVDR) are known to increase the level of the output DC voltage of a Rectifying Antenna (rectenna). However, the RF / DC conversion efficiency is very sensitive to the internal electrical characteristics of the used diode. This paper then proposes an analysis of the performance of an MVDR according to the features of the Schottky diode. A Rectenna Figure of Merit (RFoM), considering the DC output voltage as well as the RF / DC conversion efficiency, is defined to analyze MVDRs with up to ten stages. This analysis makes it possible to obtain that the most effective rectifier diode differs depending on the number of stages of the rectifier. More specifically, it is observed that, for two stages, the most efficient diode is the Schottky diode HSMS2820. For MVDR with more than five stages, the SMS 7630 diode is more suitable for low input power levels (less than 5 dBm). It is also observed that, for power levels higher than 5 dBm, the HSMS2850 diode offers the best compromise in terms of output DC voltage and conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Broadband Conformal Antenna Array for Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an efficient methodology of modeling broadband antenna arrays for applications on curved surfaces. In addition to precise anechoic measurement and accurate generalized theory applied to the newly developed open-waveguide radiator model, improvements on array-feed beamforming network (BFN) is also utilized to obtain broad-banding effects. Performances of various conformal arrays of different radii and numbers of radiators are investigated in terms of radiation patterns and gain flatness at k-band over a wide bandwidth. A newly developed array pattern formulation which involves the use of scattering matrix of BFN is also presented. Prior to the obtained results are some fundamentals about the theoretical generalized radiator models and BFN are also given.

articleTitle: A UWB Dual-Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Ultra-wideband (UWB) dual-polarized magnetoelectric dipole antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of two magneto-electric dipoles, two Γ -shaped probes and a rectangle cavity. Simulated results reveal that the antenna can achieve a common impedance bandwidth of 105% . The isolation between two ports is more than 15dB and the front-to-back ratio is more than 20dB. The simulated gain is about 9.85 ±1.95 dBi.

articleTitle: Mu-Negative and Near-Zero Lined Disks for Surface-Enhanced Mid-Infrared Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report a novel resonant metasurface (MTS) based on mu-negative and near-zero (MNNZ) metamaterial (MTM)-lined disks for improved surface-enhanced mid-infrared spectroscopy, which relies on the strong electric-field enhancement near plasmonic metals. The design consists of an array of gold disks patterned with meandered capacitive gaps using electron-beam lithography on a ZnSe substrate. These gaps allow the electric field to be enhanced over a much wider area. The MNNZ MTM-lined disk MTS operates at a wavelength of 15 μm (667 cm-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> or 20 THz) with miniaturized, polarization-insensitive unit cells that exhibit plasmonic-like field enhancement of > 30 over a wide area. In this operation band, the MTS may be applied to CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> detection with enhanced sensitivity and subwavelength resolution.

articleTitle: Accelerated Antenna Optimization Using Design Database and Kriging Surrogates
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of accelerated design optimization of antennas. The proposed approach involves a design database and kriging interpolation models yielding a good initial point and an initial Jacobian matrix for further optimization. The latter involves Broyden-based trust-region gradient search. The operation of the method is demonstrated using a dual-band uniplanar dipole antenna optimized for wide ranges of operating frequencies (2 GHz to 3 GHz for the lower band and 4 GHz to 5.5 GHz for the upper band). The re-design cost is just a few full-wave simulations of the structure for all considered verification cases.

articleTitle: Geometry-based Optimization of an in-Plane Nanomagnetic Majority Circuit
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Nanomagnetic circuits are characterized by propagating information via dipolar coupling. When a nanomagnetic wire is inserted to extract the result of a majority gate it fails to propagate the information in some cases. This happens due to undesired diagonal couplings between magnets of the majority gate and those that compose the wire. In this paper we analyze the dipolar coupling tensor to identify particles involved in such error cases. After that, we minimize undesired interactions and maximize desired ones by inserting geometry alterations in some nanomagnets of interest. All circuits are simulated using a Runge-Kutta numerical implementation of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. The proposed optimized circuit works for all input combinations.

articleTitle: Yagi-Configured Electrically Small Antenna with Quad-Polarization Diversity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A polarization-reconfigurable, high-directivity, Yagi-configured, near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP), electrically small antenna (ESA) is presented. The antenna is composed of a director, a reflector, and an electrically-controlled driven element loaded with four p-i-n (PIN) diodes. Two linear polarization ( x-LP and y ·LP) and two circular polarization (LHCP and RHCP) states are achieved simply by controlling the ON/OFF states of the PIN diodes. The measured results demonstrate that in its x(y)-LP state, the peak realized gain, front-to-back ratio, and radiation efficiency values are, respectively, ~3.08 (3.2) dBi, ~11.0 (11.05) dB, and ~77% (73%), and that in its LHCP (RHCP) state they are, respectively, ~3.0 (3.1) dBi, ~ 12.1 (11.18) dB, and ~ 72% (70%).

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Stretchable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Effective stretchable antennas are receiving increased demands in applications from inflatable antennas to smart cars. Recognizing the trade-off between the stretchability and antenna gain as a key design consideration, this paper presents a cost effective and realistic method to achieve an effective antenna with a high stretch ratio.

articleTitle: Estimation of Small Antenna Performance Using a Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an approach based on Machine Learning (ML) to estimate the performance of small antennas in practical applications. As a proof of concept, the case of printed antennas integrated into compact terminals, such as for Internet of Things (IoT) or 5G applications, is considered.

articleTitle: Human Body Phantoms for Wideband Radiometry
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to enable wideband radiometry as a noninvasive and accurate means by which to detect human body core temperature, phantoms that mimic the electrical properties across a wide frequency band and wide range of temperatures need to be explored. This paper proposes the use of 90% ground beef (10% fat) to represent the human brain across a wide bandwidth from 200 MHz to 10 GHz. Our proposed phantom is found to exhibit minimal error compared to the actual human brain gray and white matter properties. Temperature-dependent electrical property measurements from 11°C to 47°C align with the few existing temperature-dependent studies on animal tissues. This study will enable further research into more easily constructed and attainable phantoms for testing a wide range of radio frequency devices.

articleTitle: Array Reliability Analysis for Irregular Subarrayed Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the reliability of irregular subarrayed phased array antenna is analyzed. In order to access the performance of this kind of array structure, the failure rate of subarray tiles is simulated. Moreover, the low sidelobe tapering beam pattern degradation case is also proposed. Numerical results are presented to validate the effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna using an Open Stub Coupled-Line Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design, simulation, fabrication, and measurement of a proximity-fed circularly polarized microstrip antenna is presented. The two major design components are (1) a stepped impedance open stub (SIOS) coupled-line 90° phase shifter, and (2) a dual-probe proximity-fed circular patch. The 90° phase shifter consists of two microstrip lines: one with an SIOS and coupled-line, and a second that serves as a reference. The antenna is a 64.4 mm diameter circular patch printed on top of a 140 mm ×140 mm×0.8 mm FR4 substrate. The antenna feed network is on a separate FR4 substrate and consists of a cascaded Wilkinson power divider and phase shifter. Connecting the feed network and patch antenna substrates are T-shaped probes that extend from the two outputs of the phase shifter to the bottom of the antenna substrate through a 16.7 mm air layer. A prototype was fabricated, and measurement results show a gain of 6.8 dBic at 2.0 GHz and a 3-dB AR bandwidth of 38% from 1.66 GHz to 2.44 GHz with more than 10-dB of return loss over this band.

articleTitle: The Shape-Dependence and Near-Singularity of Singularity Cancellation Transformations for the Integral Equation Methods
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The near-singularity and shape-dependence are two main topics in the singularity cancellation methods which are well-known for the treatments of weakly singular and near-singular integrals. The cancellation transformations for near-singular integrals are inefficient for the deformed triangles, and this phenomenon is referred to as shape-dependence in this paper. We first investigate the reason of these problems via the theoretical analysis with the numerical verification. Second, a new singularity cancellation method for weakly near-singular integral is proposed, which have fast and consistent convergence rate for both regular and irregular triangles. Some numerical results are presented to show the effectiveness of the theoretical framework and the proposed transformation.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Coaxial Liquid Metal Yagi-Uda Antenna with Arbitrary Directivity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a reconfigurable Yagi-Uda antenna using liquid metal eutechtic gallium and indium (EGaIn). The antenna consists of three coaxial circular capillaries inserted with electrolyte and certain amount of liquid metal according to their different functions. Arbitrary intended directions in 2D-plane can be realized by changing the position of EGaIn in each capillary electrochemically. The resonant frequency is also adjustable by altering the location of the feed element. The results of HFSS simulation show that the antenna has resonant frequencies of 1.69 GHz and 2.03 GHz with high gain in the intended directions.

articleTitle: Sorting of Archaeological Samples in D-band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Identifying the making of prehistoric pottery is one of the valuable means of tracing technical traditions and human mobility. We are interested here in the settlement in the Western Mediterranean through the sorting of pottery samples. The aim is to discriminate between two building techniques, looking for the features formed by the air bubbles embedded in the pottery samples. Current methods make use of heavy characterization systems such as the CT-Scan or the synchrotron. Microwave imaging offers an interesting alternative due to the possibility to have compact and portable acquisition systems. In this paper we investigate for the first time the sorting of potteries based on sub-mmWaves measurements. We process the images obtained from measurements with a non-linear SVM. Given the `mm' size of the desired aggregates, we work in D-band and take advantage of frequency and spatial diversities to have large training and test datasets. The first results show that the accuracy reaches up to 70% and depends on the choice of samples repartition among training and test datasets.

articleTitle: Fast $O(N\log N)$ Algorithm for Generating $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-Representation of Electrically Large Volume Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast algorithm to generate an H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-representation for solving electrically large volume integral equations (VIEs). Unlike existing methods whose complexity is as high as quadratic, the proposed algorithm has linearithmic complexity, and thus it can handle problems with large electrical sizes. Furthermore, the algorithm is purely algebraic and kernel independent. Numerical experiments on electrically large 3D arrays of dielectric cubes having over 33 million unknowns demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi-Faceted Reflectarray Antenna for Spatial Bandwidth Improvement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of the multifaceted reflectarray (RFA) antenna for spatial bandwidth improvement. Geometries of faceted RFA have been designed by segmenting the phase correcting surface in tilted 3-panel and 5-panel configurations. Phase distribution over RFA surface and directivity variation with frequency have been computed using Geometric Optics (GO) based technique and achieved 6.5% and 7.4% 1-dB gain bandwidth in case of 3-panel and 5-panel faceted RFA, respectively as compared to a flat RFA having 1.8% 1-dB gain bandwidth.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Sensor Design With Split Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The resonant characteristics of a double gap split ring resonator-based metamaterial have been analyzed. The structure of a split ring resonator consists of double gaps with a circular shape having diameter ranging from 50μm to 6mm which can be used as a biosensor from GHz to THz range. The simulation has been done using 3D FEM based EM simulator for various cases including substrates with different thickness, permittivity and ring radius. Unit cell with equivalent circuit model is developed for implementation in periodic structures. The simulation results are compared with analytical results for verification. The prototypes have then been manufactured and the structure is tested from 1GHz to 6GHz. It has been shown that the simulated, analytical, and measurement results are all in good agreement. The proposed method in this paper can be used to design filters, antennas, tuning elements, and biosensors.

articleTitle: High Gain 3D Printed Antenna with Corrugations and High Aperture Efficiency Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a 3D printed antenna for X-band applications. The antenna is compact and it has high measured gain performance with high aperture efficiency over wide bandwidth covers 5 GHz. The proposed antenna consists of two layers stacked on top of each other, where the top layer is the radiating structure. The radiating structure consists of central slots surrounded by corrugations and cavity to improve the gain of the antenna. The proposed antenna is directive, compact and with high aperture efficiency performance. The antenna has a peak measured gain of 18.7 dBi at 11.3 GHz with a peak aperture efficiency of 56.6%.

articleTitle: Modeling Sinusoidal Motion of Harmonic Tags Objects for Harmonic Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Harmonic Doppler radar combines Doppler measurement of moving objects with harmonic tags to improve detection in cluttered environments. Using a harmonic tag that generates and retransmits the second harmonic of an incident continuous- wave signal, the shift on the second harmonic can be used to determine the motion, even when the fundamental scattered signal is obscured by clutter return in amplitude and frequency. In this work, we present a model of the response of a harmonic tag under sinusoidal motion and compare to experimental results. We derive the time-frequency response of the scattered harmonic signal and present time-frequency simulations and measurements of tags with sinusoidal motion, demonstrating the ability to model simple motion.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Localization in Joint Radar and Communications Systems Using Multi-Tone Waveform Modulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a multi-tone modulated waveform for high-accuracy localization in joint radar-communications systems for the Internet of Things, human computer interaction, and other connected device applications. By modifying a preamble channel-estimation signal with linear-frequency modulation, high-accuracy localization can be obtained without modification of the hardware. We present the waveform design and theoretical lower bound on delay estimation. Experimental results demonstrate range estimation accuracy of 5.2 mm using a four-tone LFM over a total bandwidth of 100 MHz and duration of 2.5 μs.

articleTitle: Quad-Polarized Leaky-Wave Antennas for Communication and Polarimetry Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quad-polarized periodic leaky-wave antenna (P-LWA) is introduced as a simple system for communication and polarimetry applications. This system consists of a pair of parallel P-LWAs that radiates circularly-polarized (CP) waves with opposite handedness. The four polarizations are obtained by exciting each of P-LWA solely for right or left CPs or simultaneously in-phase and out-of-phase for horizontal and vertical linear polarizations (LP). The proposed quad-polarized structure is demonstrated by full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Results in Goal-Oriented Error Estimation for MoM Input Impedance Computation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Error estimation is widely used in electromagnetic (EM) analysis and forms a crucial step in adaptive refinement algorithms. Goal-oriented a posteriori error estimators produce error estimates for quantities of interest relating to the original numerical solution by solving additional, dual problems. In this paper a goal-oriented error estimator is formulated for computing antenna input impedance in the electric field integral equation (EFIE) based method of moments (MoM) context. The estimator is used to drive an h-refinement of the mesh and is shown to produce a similar decrease in error as uniform refinement but with far fewer degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Performance Verification of SA 5G Device
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Due to the multi-functional characteristic of the 5G, the design of 5G devices become more and more complicated. To this end, we designed three sets of test experiments to study the transmission performance of 5G mobile phones, and added a hand model to simulate the impact of human hands on the mobile phone. We tested and analyzed 5G terminals in the N78 band under the SA network. The measurement result is evaluated by the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP). The measurement results show that under the SA network, the left and right hands will have different impacts on the performance of 5G mobile phones, but the impact is very small and the overall performance is stable.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Multiband Monopole Antenna With CSRR Loaded on Ground plane
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact multiband planar antenna based on the inclusion of complementary split ring resonators (CSRR) in the ground plane. The antenna is composed of an inverted L monopole, that presents a 30% reduction length with respect to the conventional one, and a partial ground plane in which the CSRRs are etched to generate the multiband characteristic. First, two equal radius CSRRs are etched in the ground plane and excited by a meandered microstrip feed line. As a result a broad dual band frequency. Secondly, a stub feed is introduced to create a triple band by making the CSRRs's radius different. For both cases simulations and measurements show good agreement.

articleTitle: Perfect-Frequency-Converter Metasurface Consisting of Twin Time-Modulated Radiators
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a perfect-frequency-converter meta-surface based on the effects of inharmonic photonic transition in twin time-modulated radiating patches. The medium is characterized with a periodic temporal modulation and a tailored aperiodic spatial profile. Such an aperiodic spatial profile provides aperiodic photonic bandgaps which prevent photonic transitions to unwanted time harmonics. Full-wave simulation results demonstrate a pure frequency conversion. The unique property of the proposed platform is the large frequency difference between the incident and transmitted waves. Therefore, this makes it suitable for modern wireless telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Characterization of Radar Absorbing Materials at 75 GHz - 90 GHz using Free-Space System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a focused beam free-space measurement methodology for characterizing radar absorbing materials in the W-band. The measurements are obtained in the transmission mode using a PNA network analyzer with millimeter wave frequency extenders to provide four S-parameters over the W-band from 75 to 90 GHz. Good agreement is achieved between the calculated and the measured S-parameters of the sample under test that validates the extraction algorithm. The extracted complex relative permittivity results are compared with the commercial data.

articleTitle: A Phenomenological Study of Vertical SAR for Underground Pipe Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A numerical study is carried out to investigate the use of airborne, downward-looking synthetic aperture radar (SAR), or vertical SAR, for pipe imaging and detection. Significant differences in the imaging responses are noted between the two illumination scenarios examined, viz., vertical and horizontal dipole excitation. The discussion considers the causes behind the various important target imaging features observed, the effects of ground surface reflection, the effects of uncertainty in the soil dielectric properties on image reconstruction, and the application of a hybrid far-to-near field transformation for calculating the response from the rough ground surface.

articleTitle: Characterization of Thin Film Enabled Engineered Substrate for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Engineered substrate enabled by Permalloy (Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub> Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>, Py) thin films has been well developed for RF applications with high and tunable permeability and moderate loss. A full investigation on the characteristics of the engineered substrate is presented in this paper. The loss and equivalent permeability generated by the Py patterns are characterized through a microstrip line model. Multiple factors of Py patterns are taken into consideration to define the performance of the engineered substrate, including filling density, thickness, dimensions, and locations. The analytical results give a detailed guideline for the design of engineered substrate.

articleTitle: A New Tightly-Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a new tightly-coupled dipole array (TCDA). The feeding part utilizes a microstrip to coplanar stripline (CPS) balun. The compact planar balun provides wideband balanced output and performs as impedance transformer. The TCDA achieves a bandwidth of 2.8:1 (1.74-4.9 GHz) and can scan up to 70° in the E plane, 65° in the H plane, and 70° in the D plane, respectively. The proposed TCDA exhibits wideband, wide angle scanning, low cross-polarization, easy fabrication, and low cost.

articleTitle: Highly-efficient GRIN Lens Optimization Through Differential Ray Tracing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new differential ray tracing (DRT) formulation for optical lenses with gradient-index (GRIN) properties is presented. The metric function gradient required during lens optimization is obtained by DRT, which requires very few function evaluations when compared to the finite difference (FD) approach. Numerical results validating the accuracy of the proposed method are presented.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Polarized Multi-beams with Shared Aperture Metasurface in Terahertz Regime
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Based on Generalized Snell's law, we have proposed a kind of new metasurface, which consists of cross I-shaped structures and a ground plane separated by a dielectric substrate. The normally incident linear-polarized waves can be reflected by the elements, and the reflection phases of x- and y-polarized waves can be controlled independently by adjusting its length along x and y directions, respectively. Inspired by its good ability in beam shaping and reflecting, we have extended it to a multibeam generating metasurface, by which a series of reflection multi-beam waves can be observed in terahertz regime when these unit elements are arranged appropriately. The simulation results show that the designed metasurface has a good performance in manipulating orthogonal polarized waves independently at a frequency of 0.3THz. The presented method provides a new idea in orthogonal polarized multibeam generation, which has a good potential application in detection technology, multiplex communication and beam shaping.

articleTitle: A novel Baravelle Spiral Multilayer Frequency Selective Surface for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel spiral multilayer frequency selective surface (MFSS) is proposed with element based on the concept of Baravelle spiral. A dual-band behavior at WLAN frequencies bands (2.4 GHz, 5.0 GHz or 5.8 GHz) has been obtained. The proposed structure is found to show stopband characteristics in the frequencies ranges from 1.67 GHz to 3.1 GHz and from 4.1 GHz to 5.9 GHz. In addition, the proposed MFSS shows an interesting characteristic of polarization stability.

articleTitle: SIW-Feed for 20 GHz Active Phased Array (1024-Element) Antenna with Modular Architecture
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the simulation and measurement results of 64-way substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) power splitter/combiner suitable for 1024 ( 32×32)-element active phased array antenna (A-PAA) with modular architecture are presented. In the design, the structure of SIW feed has 64 outputs with separation equal to 2λ0 (λ0: free-space wavelength @ 20 GHz). The measured results shows an average insertion loss less than 2.5 dB with phase variation less than 10 deg. over the operating bandwidth 18.6-20.2 GHz.

articleTitle: An FFT-Accelerated and Tucker-Enhanced Inductance Extraction for Voxelized Superconducting Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An integral equation simulator is proposed to compute the inductance of the superconducting structures discretized by voxels. The proposed simulator extends the VoxHenry inductance extractor by taking into account the superconductivity in the computations. In addition to possessing all distinctive features of the VoxHenry simulator, the proposed simulator makes use of Tucker decompositions to compress its large data structures involving the block circulant tensors. By doing so, it reduces the memory requirement of these tensors from gigabytes to megabytes and CPU time required to obtain these tensors from hours/minutes to seconds for the large-scale problems.

articleTitle: Advanced Computational Methods for Compact Range Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Compact Ranges are widely used for antenna measurements across wide frequency ranges spanning frequencies as low as 350MHz to as high as 60GHz and above. Advances in electromagnetic (EM) simulations have significantly improved the design process for compact ranges, resulting in reduced costs. Asymptotic methods such as Geometrical Optics (GO), Physical Optics (PO) are widely used due their reduced simulation costs for electrically large reflectors used in compact range design. With advances in availability of computer hardware, full wave methods such as Method of Moments (MoM), Adaptive Cross Approximation (ACA), and Multilevel Fast Multipole Method (MLFMM) can be used for more accurate analysis of compact ranges within reasonable simulation cost. In this paper, we will review computational techniques that are becoming popular to analyze compact ranges. Accuracy of simulations using full wave and asymptotic techniques will be presented.

articleTitle: A Wide-Band Metasurface with Wide Angle Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study presents simulation and analyses of a multifunctional single layer metasurface performing both linear and circular polarization conversion. The unit cell of the metasurface comprises of tilted umbrella shape with a slit in it achieving both linear and circular polarization conversion in frequency bands of (10.34-10.57 GHz and 13.53-16.98 GHz) and (10.14-10.219 GHz, 10.84-12.55 GHz and 18.12-18.98 GHz) respectively with more than 90% efficiency. The overall optimized structure of the unit cell results in a stable response for oblique incidence angle up to 45° both for both operations. The proposed metasurface offers a simple planar structure, with compact size and angular stability and is thus suitable for various applications like microwave filtering, satellite communication and polarization conversion devices.

articleTitle: Ambient Radiofrequency Energy Mapping of Montreal for Far-Field Wireless Power Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work summarizes an outdoor dynamic radiofrequency (RF) power density measurement on the island of Montreal, QC, Canada. Different from previous stationary measurements, our scheme captures ambient power density along major streets, roads, and highways, through a moving vehicle carrying equipment. This work focuses on the populated downtown area in the city of Montreal. Results show that GSM/LTE-850 band reserved for mobile communications has the highest power density in general within the spectrum of interest (400 MHz to 2700 MHz). Whereas, despite lower density, digital TV signals are distributed more evenly in this area. Based on this observation, this work then gives several suggestions on far-field wireless power harvesting (WPH) for smart city, IoT, and other metropolitan wireless applications.

articleTitle: Fast Source Reconstruction Method in Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a new approach is proposed to accelerate the numerical calculation of electric field integral equations (EFIE) and near-field to far-field transformation in source reconstruction methods (SRM). In this method, the optimum number of quadrature points to have accurate results is derived. Thereafter, inspired by an adaptive integration approach, the position of the quadrature points and corresponding weights are calculated analytically as closed-form expressions in a matrix representation. Thus, for all the triangles in the discretized mesh, the vertices can be simply plugged into the derived expressions that work as an analytical lookup table. This method avoids the intrinsic inaccuracy of the polynomial-based Gaussian quadratures and long processing time of iterative schemes.

articleTitle: Deformation Localization of Reflector Antenna Based on Focal-Field Distribution with CapsNet
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An artificial intelligence-assisted reflector antenna deformation localization method based on the focal-field distribution (FFD) feature is presented. Exploring the characteristics of FFD, a capsule network (CapsNet)-based estimation method is used to locate the deformation. The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) model is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, and the experimental results confirm that our method can accurately locate the deformation of the reflector antenna.

articleTitle: Achieving Wideband Beam-Splitting with an Ultrathin Discrete Huygens' Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose the design of a Huygens' metasurface whose elements can realize stable reflection characteristics from 21 GHz to 30 GHz (37% bandwidth). The proposed metasurface features two markedly different elements which provide a reflection phase difference of 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>±37<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> over the aforementioned band. This design methodology allows one to broaden the bandwidth of various metasurface designs that rely on a variation of reflection coefficients. As a simple example, we demonstrate a metasurface that reduces the reflectance of a normally incident electromagnetic (EM) wave by redirecting the energy into oblique scattering directions. A wideband beam splitter is hence designed with very thin substrate thickness and utmost simplicity. This work paves way to the design of wideband Huygens' metasurfaces.

articleTitle: EurAAP WG GSM Antenna Model Validation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The European Association on Antennas and Propagation Software Working Group has found significant discrepancy between computer model and measurement of the RangeStar Ultima™ “World GSM” antenna. This work shows good agreement between our model and the Working Group model as well as with our measurement. It briefly explores several possible sources of error in the Working Group measurements.

articleTitle: Wideband Miniaturized Dual-Polarized TEM Horn
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Analysis and design of a miniaturized wideband dual-polarized transverse electromagnetic (TEM) horn antenna is presented in this work. Miniaturization is achieved by combining the dual-polarized TEM horn with a collocated loop antenna routed behind the former. The TEM horn and loop geometries are engineered to excite their fundamental TM and TE spherical modes coherently and improve the performance at the low frequency end. Good impedance match and gain are demonstrated over greater than 3 octave bandwidth.

articleTitle: Imaging Breast Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS) using Pulsed Terahertz Spectroscopy System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes the use of terahertz (THz) reflection imaging method for investigating breast ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). The tumor handled in this work is formalin fixed and paraffin embedded tissue block (FFPE). The goal of this research is to differentiate between DCIS and invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). In the previous research, THz spectroscopy has shown successful differentiation between cancerous (IDC) and normal breast tissue in freshly excised tumors. The study conducted on IDC has demonstrated interesting signatures in the absorption coefficient of cancer tissues. Similar studies will be conducted in this work for FFPE tissue blocks to investigate the potential invasiveness level of DCIS tumors.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator based rectenna for multi-band RF harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A modified cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna for multi-band application with microstrip feed mechanism is proposed. The antenna operates in the frequency range of 1.72 GHz to 2.2 GHz and 2.3 GHz to 2.48 GHz. The proposed antenna shows circular polarization in the operating range of frequency. Gain of the proposed antenna lies between 5.98 dBi -6.03 dBi. The antenna 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth ranges from 1.74 GHz to 2.15 GHz and 2.28 GHz to 2.42 GHz. The Antenna is fabricated on FR4- epoxy substrate of dimension 80×80×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The L-shaped matching circuit is designed using inductors for the operating range of frequency which is connected to the Greinacher voltage doubler topology-based rectifier to convert the electromagnetic wave to dc voltage. The proposed antenna simulation and analysis has been carried out by using HFSS EM simulation software whereas Advanced design systems (ADS) software was used for analysis of matching and rectifier circuit.

articleTitle: Plane-Wave Scattering off Sinusoidally-Modulated Metasurfaces With Normal Susceptibilities
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We analyze plane-wave scattering off metasurfaces (MSs) with sinusoidally-modulated normal magnetic susceptibilities. To this end, the typical continued-fraction formalism is rigorously generalized to cover relevant irregular stability conditions, and validated via full-wave simulations. It is observed that the scattering of the dominant Floquet mode exhibits a resonant angular notch due to strong coupling into surface-wave modes. In the future, such spatially-modulated normal components are expected to enhance the performance of MSs and aid controlling their angular response.

articleTitle: Supra-Electroporation of Irregularly Shaped 3D Cell Morphologies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: If the duration of the external excitation field in an electroporation setup is less than the membrane charging time, the induced electric field can penetrate to the internal cell organelles. This phenomenon, otherwise known as supra-electroporation, is a breakthrough in cell biology engineering because of its potential application in drug delivery and gene transfection. The emphasis of this study is to computationally analyze the effect of the three-dimensional (3D) cell shape on its supra-electroporation behavior. The computational experiments are conducted using a multiphysics solver that combines a quasi-static electromagnetic solver with a well-established non-linear membrane model to account for the changes in membrane conductivity due to the formation of nanopores. The spatial and temporal variations of the nanopores introduced to the nucleus membrane are quantified for realistic cell shape, indicating the importance of the consideration of the actual 3D cell morphology in supra-electroporation studies.

articleTitle: Efficient Iterative Method for Computation of Antenna Array Embedded Element Patterns
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient, fast-converging iterative scheme based on many local method of moments (MoM) solutions, to accurately solve the surface currents on large, single-element excited antenna arrays. Embedded element pattern computations require such solutions. The theory is developed for planar antenna arrays of identical disjoint elements. Preliminary numerical results demonstrate that very few iterations are required for accurate results, and that the rate of convergence is related to the size of the local solution domains.

articleTitle: SIW Center-Fed Series Rectangular DRA Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An 8-element substrate integrated waveguide series rectangular dielectric resonator antenna array, with two types of feeding structures, center slot-fed, and center probe-fed, are presented. A simulation study is performed to investigate the performance of both structures. The simulated radiation patterns demonstrate a broadside beam with a maximum radiated gain of 14 dB over an operating impedance bandwidth of 3.1 GHz.

articleTitle: A Wideband Wide-Angle Beam-Steering System for Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the performance of an optimized wideband beam-steering antenna system for mm-wave applications. The antenna is passive and can provide continuous two-dimensional beam scanning up to ±40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> away from broadside direction in elevation and any direction in azimuth. It uses a pair of near-field dielectric phase transformers, inspired from optical prisms, introducing a pre-determined phase gradient to the incoming wave front from a source antenna, and redirecting the radiated beam to specified direction with in a conical region with an apex angle of 80°. A prototype of the antenna system along with the mounting structure has been fabricated and tested.

articleTitle: An Implicit Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method to Solve S-parameters in the Waveguide Port
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: It is important about energy coupling for the waveguide port. In order to compute its transmission characteristics, an implicit hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (imHDGTD) method is proposed to solve the S-parameters. Compared with classical discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method, the imHDGTD method has a fewer number of degrees of freedom (DOFs). By using the matrix solving technology, the imHDGTD method can accelerate the iterative solutions of the global linear system when using the implicit time scheme. Since the waveguide excitation source takes the field disappearance in the computational region as the sign of iteration termination, the imHDGTD method can effectively shorten the computational time. What's more, in order to reduce the numerical reflection caused by space truncation, the waveguide port is truncated with the perfectly matched layer (PML) in the imHDGTD method. Some tests show the S-parameters of the imHDGTD method are consistent with the results of DGTD. When the computational region is made up with locally refined meshes, the time step of the imHDGTD is larger than the DGTD method.

articleTitle: Direct dark mode excitation of electromagnetically induced reflection effect in enantiomer-based metasurface and its application in terahertz detection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An enantiomeric flexible metasurface based detector with highly sensitivity is designed for detections in terahertz. The sensitive property primarily is based on electromagnetically induced reflection (EIR) response of a bilayered enantiomeric split Zs (BESZs) structure, which arises from dark mode resonances directly excited by 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> incident waves. The reflection amplitude of EIR resonance with high quality factor is highly sensitive to surrounding environment. By setting splits, the sensitivity of EIR resonance can be further improved slightly. The sensing performance of proposed detector was evaluated by different thickness of germanium in simulation, and the results show that its reflection amplitude difference can reach about 0.3 even for 10 nm thickness of germanium, which demonstrates the functionality and great potential of enantiomeric structures in sensing and detection.

articleTitle: The accuracy of a low-power approach for jammer angle-of-arrival estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Approaches to the geolocation of radio emitters typically involves the down-conversion, digitisation and subsequent signal processing of signals impinging on an antenna array. For geolocation using angle-of-arrival (AoA), a variety of different super-resolution algorithms have been proposed. Although these vary in performance and assumptions, they often present a significant computational burden, requiring the determination of covariance matrices, subsequent eigen-decomposition and analysis. This has a significant impact on ultimate power consumption. In this paper we consider the AoA accuracy of an approach using a low-power array based on steerable sum/difference beamforming. We evaluate its use and accuracy in an application for the identification of Global Positioning System (GPS) jammers in vehicles. It is shown that this relatively simple approach performs well when the signal to noise ratio is sufficiently high.

articleTitle: Genetic Programming for Coplanar Waveguide Continuous Transverse Stub Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Genetic programming (GP) is developed to design an antenna array with new topologies resulting in improved performance. Three elements of a coplanar waveguide continuous transverse stub (CPW-CTS) antenna are synthesized and optimized by GP. These antenna elements are placed in series to create a 3-element frequency scanning linear array. The fitness function used to design the CPW-CTS elements accounts for impedance bandwidth, radiation pattern, cross polarization, and transmission coefficient. Simulation results are verified experimentally. The GP designed CPW-CTS antenna array was able to achieve nearly 4 times the bandwidth of a conventional CPW-CTS array design. The GP designed array maintains the array's gain when compared with the published CPW-CTS antenna array design.

articleTitle: Statistical Modeling of the Battery Recharging Time in RF Energy Harvesting for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radiofrequency waves are increasingly seen as a promising solution for powering Wireless Sensor Nodes (WSN) dedicated to the Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, by considering the RF source as a WSN power solution, Battery Recharging Time (BRT) becomes a critical performance metric, especially when the Quality of Service (QoS) is a requirement. In the literature, very few works propose an analysis of BRT based on an RF Energy Harvesting system. In this paper, the characterization of the BRT as a function of the harvestable power is analyzed, and modeling of the BRT is then proposed. The results are based on the ambient power density level measured in a building. It is obtained that the BRT undergoes as the received ambient power, a large scale fading effect shadowing more specifically the lognormal Shadowing.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Slot Antenna Arrays with Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel slot antenna array, which are able to operate at both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{S}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C}$</tex> bands with dual polarizations in each band and wide bandwidth, is presented in this paper. This shared antenna aperture can operate as a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}\ \boldsymbol{S}$</tex> -band array covering 2.65 to 4.05 GHz and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}\ \boldsymbol{C}$</tex> -band array covering 4.65 to 7.57 GHz at the same time. The antenna arrays at both bands exhibit dual polarizations by using a diagonal feeding method. By properly controlling the relative phase of each port, either vertical or horizontal polarization can be realized. The isolation between the ports for different bands is better than 15 dB in most of the frequency range.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Surface Damage Localization for FAST Active-reflector
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach of surface damage localization for the Five hundred meters Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) based on the focal-field distribution (FFD) is proposed. Firstly, according to the structure of the FAST, we model the FAST with surface damage caused by down-tied cables fatigue fractures. Then the FFD with different damage locations obtained by simulation are collected to form a full FFD feature database. Finally, the received signals of the FAST array feeds with surface damage is matched with the database to obtain the damage location. Simulation results show that the matching algorithm can effectively estimate the damage location.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Millimeter-Wave Beam-Steering Lens antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel high efficiency single-layer circularly polarized (CP) unit cell based on Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase is proposed for a meta-lens design at millimeter-wave band. The unit cell presents a stable high efficiency (>0.8) from 31 GHz to 33 GHz. Based on the unit, the meta-lens in function of focusing and waveform transformation is then designed and simulated with an overall size of 27×27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulation is in great agreement with the theoretical calculation, which indicates the lens would be a considerable candidate for high frequency wireless-communication system.

articleTitle: Measurement of Finger Effects on Coverage Efficiency for User Equipment Mm-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents simulation and measurement calculations of total scanning power and coverage efficiency parameters. The simulated and measured coverage efficiency Cumulative Distributive Function (CDF) are similar for high gain. Important discrepancy are observed for low gain because of uncertainties in simulation model and measurement processes.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Dual-Band Double-Stub Matching Network Using MTM-EBGs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
