abstract: This work proposes a novel method of rendering a double-stub tuner dual-band through the introduction of embedded, metamaterial-based electromagnetic bandgap structures (MTM-EBGs). The MTM-EBG, which has predictable dispersion characteristics and is both compact and uniplanar, effectively changes tuner's stub lengths as a function of frequency, allowing matching of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50-\Omega$</tex> source impedance to an arbitrary, frequency-dependent load at two frequency bands, while maintaining a size no larger than the corresponding single-band double-stub tuners. The dual-band, double-stub matching network operates comparably to conventional single-band structures, with return loss of over 20 dB observed in each band.

articleTitle: Robustness of Sparse Reconstruction Methods in Spherical Antenna Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The robustness of reconstruction strategies for the application of compressed sensing to a spherical antenna nearfield to far-field transformation is investigated. More precisely, the minimum number of measurement samples is determined for different noise levels such that a predefined far-field accuracy is achieved. Considered are the strategies iterative hard thresholding, hard thresholding pursuit, orthogonal matching pursuit, and compressive sampling matching pursuit in a modified form, as well as the quadratically constrained basis pursuit (BP). Modified phase transition diagrams show that depending on the noise and sparsity level a different recovery strategy should be used, while in general the quadratically constrained BP is outperformed by the other considered strategies.

articleTitle: A rectangular slotted waveguide array for high power microwave applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a rectangular slotted waveguide array is proposed for high power microwave applications. The antenna has been designed in the context of implementing a non-lethal high power transmission device onboard a drone to stop and neutralize non-cooperative vehicles. The proposed antenna comprises 16 slotted waveguides and a beamforming network, which is folded to maximize the compactness of the antenna. It has been specifically designed to send maximum EM energy in the range 20°-30° off-axis direction to avoid undesired ground reflections during operations. It has the ability to withstand a peak power of 500 kW. A measured gain of 27.7 dBi has been obtained at 3.15 GHz. The antenna has been successfully used to stop a car engine from a distance of approximately 9 meters.

articleTitle: Wideband Ultrathin Huygens' Metasurface element for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a symmetric double-layer wideband ultrathin Huygens' metasurface unit is presented. This unit cell is a good candidate for flat lens antenna for 5G applications. In this work, the bandwidth of the element is improved 34% which primarily affect the flat lens antenna bandwidth. This structure consists of a symmetric copper double layer unit including square ring and fractal patch structure etched on the one substrate. The proposed unit-cell excites both electric and magnetic dipole resonances with mutual interference. The simulated results show a high transmission (-2dB criteria) and 200° phase control at the same time, which cannot be realized by unit structures with double-layer. The whole thickness of the unit is also 0.046λ0 at mm-wave frequency of 28GHz.

articleTitle: A New Method to Design a Rectifying Antenna for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Due to their ever-increasing energy density, Rectifying Antennas (Rectenna) are increasingly being used as a power source for ultra-low-consumption electronic devices. However, most designers only define the optimal features of the rectenna, which does not account for performance in real-life situations. In this paper, an analysis of the real-time performance of the main characteristics of a rectenna (the DC output voltage and conversion efficiency) is proposed. Ambient power density measurements at 2.4 GHz are made, and based on observations, an optimized rectenna in the 2.45 GHz band is designed for voltage and efficiency characterization. The designed rectenna demonstrates an optimal conversion efficiency of 47.4% and a DC voltage of 0.46 V, for an input power of -4 dBm. Analysis of the performance of the rectenna according to the ambient data allows observing over 17 minutes, the average efficiency of 28%, and an average voltage of 0.14 V.

articleTitle: Frequency Tunable Ferrite Based Metamaterial for Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a frequency tunable ferrite based metamaterial which can operate as a transmission type linear-to-circular polarization converter when it stays in a static magnetic bias field H0. When the magnetic field intensity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> varies from 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> to 3.05×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> A/m, the operational band can be tuned from 7.2 to 10.9 GHz, while the transmission coefficients are better than -1 dB. The tuning bandwidth of the proposed frequency configurable ferrite based metamaterial is 40.9%, and the thickness of proposed prototype is only 0.057 λ0.

articleTitle: Vector Potential Dyadic Green’s Function and Normal Modes in Cavity of Arbitrary Shape
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A semi-analytical approach for rapid calculation of the vector potential normal modes and dyadic Green's function inside the cavity of irregular shape over a broad range of frequency is presented. The method is based on the extraction of the Green's function at an imaginary wave number from itself to obtain a rapidly convergent hybrid spatial-spectral expansion of the Green's function. The extracted term encompasses the singularity of the Green's function and is computed using surface integral equation. The method is applied to a V-grooved cavity to obtain the vector potential Green's function inside the cavity.

articleTitle: Research on Co-channel Interference between LTE-R and GSM-R Wireless Networks in 900MHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper mainly investigates the impact of cochannel interference between the Long Term Evolution-Railway (LTE-R) wireless channel and the Global System for Mobile Communications-Railway (GSM-R) wireless channel on the Quality of Service (QoS) of GSM-R network in 930-935MHz band. The measurement environment and measurement system are presented. The measurement results of transmission interference period ( TTI) and transmission recovery period ( TREC) in the circuit switched domain (CSD) of GSM-R network reveal the LTE-R signal received power threshold that affects the QoS of GSM-R network. This practical research can be used for evaluating the impact of co-channel interference between the LTE-R wireless channel and the GSM-R wireless channel on GSM-R network performance.

articleTitle: Ku-band Reflectarray Antenna Using Cross-shape element Attached with Circular-Delay Lines
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reflectarray antenna consists of an offset-fed is designed for Ku-band applications. The unit cell comprises of modified cross-shaped element along with quad-circular delay-lines. The dimensions of delay-lines are varied to obtain the broad phase range. A low-cost FR-4 laminate is used to design the reflectarray unit cell with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.45\lambda_{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> periodicity. The far-field radiation characteristics are obtained by simulating a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15\times 15$</tex> reflectarray while keeping the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{D}=1$</tex>. A gain of 28 dBi is achieved for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-planes.

articleTitle: A Novel Channel Model for Clustered CubeSat Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a new channel model is proposed to describe communication between clustered CubeSats. The channel is presented as a normalized sum of the line-of-sight, specular, and diffuse components of a three dimensional, double bounce, stochastic model. Normalization is performed using the Ricean K-factor. This model also accounts for the transmit and receive antenna characteristics making it useful for optimization. The channel properties are explored using a reconfigurable antenna with variable inter-element spacing. Results indicate that the mean channel capacity and inter-element spacing are proportionally related.

articleTitle: Transmitarray Antennas: Focal Point Shift and Possibility of Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A transmitarray far-field beam scanning performance is illustrated based on the behavior of its focal region fields. It is shown that the oblique incidence of a plane wave on a transmitarray surface, forces the near-field focal point to shift mainly laterally with respect to the transmitarray surface. This behavior is shown useful in investigating a transmitarray far-field beam scanning. A beam scanning of 30 degrees is shown possible with no more than 1dBi gain loss.

articleTitle: A Quad-Polarization Horn Antenna with Wide Overlapped Operating Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a quad-polarization horn antenna is proposed based on the waveguide septum polarizer and 3-dB hybrid coupler. The hybrid coupler can be set at on- or off-state mechanically, so that the horn works with either dual linear polarizations or dual circular polarizations. The proposed horn antenna is demonstrated at the X-band. An overlapped bandwidth of 38.8% is obtained. Gains of different polarization modes are close and range from 12.7-17.3 dBi.

articleTitle: Study of a wide-area coherent/synchronous system for next generation Very Large Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The ngVLA is a wide-area synthesis array, and the antennas will be linked to the central reference system via long haul fiber optics. The main purpose of this research is to provide a highly stable microwave-photonics signal over a large broadband from microwave to millimeter-wave frequencies and to provide a precise timing signal through a long-haul optical fiber using the same optical signal generation/transmission system, these techniques make wide spread antennas a coherent / synchronous system.

articleTitle: Dispersion Characteristics of Bent Radiating Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dispersion properties of closed and slotted radiating bent rectangular waveguides are rigorously studied. Our analysis shows that the propagation constant changes significantly when the waveguide is curved. This change depends on the particular mode, the curvature radius, the operating frequency, and the geometry's properties (e.g., existence or non-existence of slots). For different bending angles, leaky-wave phenomena are studied here across the spectrum of the different dispersion characteristics.

articleTitle: Open-sleeve Dipole Antenna for an Airborne VHF/UHF Ice Sounding and Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple, ultrawideband, and high gain VHF/UHF open-sleeve dipole antenna and array for airborne ice measuring radar are presented. To satisfy the desired bandwidth of 300 MHz and realized gain of 10 dBi or higher in the frequency range of 170 and 470 MHz, the geometry and dimensions of the antenna are optimized under the real aircraft wing structure. The simulation results show that the 4-element antenna array having a dipole length of 720 mm, a parasitic element length of 280 mm, a separation between dipole and a parasitic element of 64 mm, and separation between antenna elements of 640 mm satisfies the desired bandwidth and gain requirements.

articleTitle: Bending Performance of Thin 3D Printed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) techniques are used to fabricate several-layer thin antennas. A uniplanar coplanar waveguide fed monopole is proposed, and the physical effects of bending are investigated.

articleTitle: Compact Hight-Gain DRA Antenna Array At 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact, wideband, high gain, dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array is proposed. The antenna structure works at 28 GHz band which makes it suitable for 5G wireless communications. The proposed antenna structure uses an array of four rectangular DRAs to enhance the gain. Simulation results show that the antenna design covers about 2 GHz of bandwidth (S11<; -10 dB) while delivering high gain of 14.7 dBi.

articleTitle: Novel Conformal RF Tag for Level Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel conformal monopole antenna used for liquid level identification in tanks. Designing RFID tag antenna on a liquid detection is challenging due to the relative permittivity, high conductivity and the diversity of liquids. A comparison between planar and conformal designs has been done using a CST microwave studio simulator. The antenna has been fabricated on Roger 3850 flexible substrate material. The conformal Antenna has been designed to work on a cylindrical tanks made of PVC material. The proposed antenna resonance frequency is shifted forward from the planar antenna at 0.9 GHz to 0.8 GHz in conformal design. The impedance bandwidth is 0.29 GHz where a planar antenna gives bandwidth 0.35 GHz. The antenna gain is 2 dB in case of conformal antenna while is 2.28 dB in case of planar design.

articleTitle: Wideband Single-Layer FSS-Based Electromagnetic Absorber Using Complementary Susceptances
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates the circuit model of an electromagnetic absorber based on a single-layer frequency-selective surface exhibiting a thin profile and broadband absorption. The circuit model is decomposed into series and parallel susceptances, which are then made complementary near ω0 in an effort to maximize bandwidth. As a result, a versatile design strategy is developed with only three input dependencies: mean absorption frequency ω0, desired absorption magnitude, and desired absorber thickness t. The required circuit values can be directly defined in terms of these three design specifications.

articleTitle: Compact Omnidirectional Antenna Using SRR for WIFI Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact horizontally polarized omnidirectional WIFI antenna based on split-ring resonators (SRRs) for base station application is proposed. A novel SRR structure is built with (metal-insulator-metal) MIM capacitor and metallic screws. It is analyzed and justified by the equivalent circuit model. Four rotating SRRs are excited in phase by a simple quartile power divider, and an electric loop is generated, leading to the realization of a vertical magnetic dipole. This antenna based on SRR exhibit not only miniaturization flexibility, but also an easy matching. It shows a compact size of 0.29λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ° 0.29 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ° 0.04 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The measured -10 dB bandwidth, gain and radiation efficiency are 2.40-2.48 GHz (3.3 %), 1.56 dBi and 92 %, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency Independent Millimeter-Wave Beamformer via Cross-Mixing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The need for high data rate communications has led to the exploration of the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) spectrum. But, significant losses at these frequencies imply high gain phased array antennas. Concurrently, low cost fabrication and beamforming across wide bandwidths is a foundational challenge. In this paper, we present a novel hybrid beamforming design using the concept of element-to-element mixing for the signal delay compensation. Notably, our novel architecture eliminates bulky phase shifters and local oscillators. Further, our system is combined with a baseband on-site coding technique for further hardware and cost reduction. Studies show that our design offers unparalleled flexibility in signal reception and promises 95% reduction in cost and power consumption.

articleTitle: Computational Imaging Using Frequency-Diverse Scattering from a Rough Reflector
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a random rough reflector with walls to produce frequency uncorrelated scattering to image an object. The conducting rough surface, surrounded by 4 walls, resembles an open-ended cavity. First, the scattered fields are computed using the geometrical optics (GO) approximation. Next, the least-squares computational imaging algorithm is implemented and numerical images are computed using 401 frequency samples within the frequency range 2-20 GHz. Finally, the imaging setup is made and measurement is conducted. Both simulated and measured data reveal a clear image of the target. For a one square meter (m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) image, a descent pixel size of about 1/401 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (5 cm x 5 cm) is obtained.

articleTitle: An Automated Inversion Algorithm for Noninvasive Specific Absorption Rate Characterization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An automated regularization parameter selection method is incorporated into an existing inversion algorithm for noninvasive specific absorption rate characterization. This augmented algorithm is evaluated using simplified two-dimensional transverse magnetic problems.

articleTitle: Position Sensing using an Asymmetric Carbon Nanotube Dimer and a Tree-Based Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a nano-particle sensing system composed of an asymmetric carbon nanotube (CNT) dimer along with a tree-based classification approach. Electromagnetic coupling in asymmetric CNT dimers split the CNT plasmonic resonances into two distinct resonances known as the bonding and anti-bonding modes. The proximity of an external nano-particle (NP) to the CNT dimer perturbs the dimer's near-field distribution and causes different shifts in the bonding and anti-bonding resonances depending on the NP location. We have studied one such case of the NP sensing system, where the NP is lying on the dimer plane and moving perpendicular to the dimer axis. The NP movement is divided into six regions around the dimer and a dataset is created for 150 different locations of the NP by mapping them to the relative shifts in bonding and anti-bonding resonances. Finally, a tree-based machine learning algorithm is applied to fit the training data and predict the NP location for a given random pair of relative shifts in bonding and anti-bonding resonances. This new sensing modality predicts the NP location correctly in 90% of the test cases.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Neural Network for Inverse Source Modeling of Wire-Like Objects
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a new electromagnetic neural network to extract the spatial features of wire objects via a novel spatial singularity expansion method (S-SEM). The proposed approach utilizes a recently-found radiation function that holds the spatial parameters of targets defined as the surface current and the geometrical details. Through EM machine learning, an estimation of these parameters is performed in a form of inverse problems for a single wire system. The estimated parameters, which are the S-SEM's poles and strengths, are validated and compared with numerical results obtained from the EM solver where an excellent agreement is observed.

articleTitle: Micromachined 160 GHz Endfire Antenna in 130-nm BiCMOS Technology for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave printed Yagi-Uda endfire antenna at 160 GHz for sensing applications. The backend of line (BEOL) of a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology is utilized to feed the Yagi antenna that is printed on the top most metal layer. The silicon under the antenna is removed to synthesize high efficiency endfire radiation pattern while complying with the process rules. The radiation pattern has 92° and 51° half-power beam widths in the two principal planes and -9 dB back-lobe level. The radiation pattern is stable over 10 GHz bandwidth. A prototype chip is fabricated to validate the design where the radiation pattern is measured. Simulations and measurements agree with each other and the measured peak gain is 2 dBi with integrated balun. This developed endfire antenna mitigates the radar cross-section (RCS) of the final sensor.

articleTitle: A Concept for a Leaky Wave Antenna Oscillator With Second Order Degeneracy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We exploit a second order exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD) to enhance frequency purity and oscillation stability in oscillators. The EPD we consider in this paper is a regular band edge (RBE) that exists in lossless and gainless periodic waveguides. We present an example of single-ladder oscillator that may act as a leaky wave antenna (LWA). The oscillator we develop has 8 unit-cells that form a resonant cavity and an active element is used to compensate for the losses and start the oscillation. We show that the oscillation frequency is in proximity of the RBE frequency thanks to the second order degeneracy.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Metallic Retroreflector Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an all-metallic device demonstrating perfect retroreflection for both transverse magnetic and transverse electric polarized plane waves. To this end, we utilize a mode-matching-based analytical formalism for the analysis and synthesis of a grating composed of periodic rectangular grooves in a metal slab. Following the spirit of recent work on metagratings (MGs), we formulate a set of analytical constraints tying the desired functionality with the geometry of the structure, facilitating the dual-polarized retroreflection by resolution of two degrees of freedom: the depth and the lateral dimension of the grooves. The analytical design is verified by full-wave simulations, paving the path for the development of versatile all-metallic MGs, suitable for high operating frequencies and spaceborne systems.

articleTitle: Statistical Performance of Circular Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The radiation performance of circularly bound random arrays with uniform and Gaussian distributions are analyzed statistically to identify metrics of radiation pattern performance. Isotropic radiators are preferred in this analysis since they provide relevant information on the fundamental beamforming behavior, which can be applied to provide reasonable estimates and ideal limitations on the performance gain, peaking sidelobe, and average sidelobe behavior. Numerical results illustrate scanning from zenith to meridian elevation angles to evaluate the theory and compare the behavior of linear, planar circular, and volumetric spherical arrays against the traditional linear periodic array.

articleTitle: A Wide-Beam Power Gain Optimization Algorithm with Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Solving the power gain pattern synthesis (PGPS) problem has been proved to be able to increase the array gain instead of solving the shaped-beam pattern synthesis (SBPS) problem. However, the existing PGPS-based algorithm is, sometimes, non-convergent and the worse is its optimal solution is usually seriously affected by the initialized array weight. The paper sets up a new model for the PGPS problem with convex structure. A power gain optimization algorithm for wide-beam synthesis is designed to maximize the minimum gain in the wide-beam mainlobe. The advantages of the proposed algorithm are that it does not need any array weight initialization and its convergence is theoretically guaranteed. Besides, the performance of proposed algorithm is similar to that of the existing PGPS-based algorithm and better than the SBPS-based algorithms.

articleTitle: Corrugated Tapered Slot Antenna with Band-stop Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a tapered slot antenna with band-stop characteristic at Ka-band. In order to create a 28 GHz stopband and reduce sidelobes, SRRs are added on the feedline and corrugations are formed on both sides of the antenna. Through these structures, total efficiency decreases from 92.0% to 2.3% at 28 GHz and the front-to-back ratio improves from 12.0 dB to 27.8 dB at 35 GHz.

articleTitle: 5-50GHz Tapered Slot Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 10:1 bandwidth finite size tapered slot antenna array is proposed. The configuration is composed of 8 columns of 8 tightly coupled elements corporate-fed and arranged in their E-plane. Antenna can scan to 60° in H-plane with across the 5-50GHz bandwidth. A free-standing design accounting for practical multi-layer PCB fabrication is presented.

articleTitle: Multiple-Beam mmW-Slotted-Waveguide Leaky Wave Antenna with Control on Polarization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: By performing the Floquet-mode analysis of a periodic slotted waveguide, a multiple-beam leaky wave antenna is proposed in the millimetre-wave (mmW) band. Considering the direction of surface current lines on the broad/side-walls of the waveguide, the polarization of constructed beams are also controlled. The simulation results are well matched with the initial mathematical analysis.

articleTitle: RF Exposure Measurement System for Biological Media Using Multiple Optimized SAR Distributions
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The objective of this work is to develop and optimize a system to evaluate the effects of RF exposure on biological cell cultures, operating at a wide range of frequencies using multiple specific absorption rate (SAR) distributions simultaneously. In-vitro RF exposure measurements are time-consuming, and in order to show meaningful statistical results, multiple measurements are required. Additionally, many parameters may have to be varied to evaluate the effects of frequency, dosimetry, time, etc., leading to a long series of measurements that can be quite time consuming. Here, we propose a system that is able to achieve multiple optimized SAR distributions by varying the dosage of the cell culture medium in each well of a multi-well plate. Additionally, the setup avoids any resonating modes by using RF absorbers placed around the antenna and the multi-well plate, making it functional at a wide range of frequencies.

articleTitle: A Novel Feeding Technique for Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRAs) for Broader Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article reports on a novel Coplanar Wave-Guide (CPW) loop feed structure with an isolated circular slot in the middle to excite a higher order mode in the cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA). The proposed feeding structure is etched on the bottom side of the substrate and it allows the cylindrical DRA to achieve a broader bandwidth and higher gain. For demonstration, the proposed feeding structure with the DRA is optimized at the X-band over the frequency range from 7.88 GHz to 8.78 GHz. The simulation results and experimental validation confirmed that the proposed feeding structure for the DRA can be used for achieving a broader bandwidth, higher gain, and broadside radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Single-Field Radial Point Interpolation Method (RPIM) for Long-Range Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The computational performance of the radial point interpolation method (RPIM) based on the second order wave equation is analyzed in a two-dimensional wave propagation scenario. Our results indicate that RPIM may outperform FDTD where simulations of electrically large problems are concerned and maintenance of phase integrity is desired.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Impedance Bandwith of a Proximity-Coupled Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article proposes a new strategy to design and estimate the impedance bandwidth of a two-layer and single-material PC-MSPA through a math close form. The simulated and experimental results present good agreement with the bandwidth model presented. The proposed analytical enable the evaluation of a proximity-coupled microstrip patch antenna (PC-MSPA) bandwidth that allows developing a framework for more effective designs.

articleTitle: Interference-Enhanced Optical Magnetism in High-Index Resonators
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we show that optical magnetism in high-index resonators can be enhanced by adding a highly reflective back mirror and this effect can be used to enable low-pump power ultrafast nonlinear optics as well as efficient directional surface plasmon wave couplers. Our results indicate that the interference-enhanced magnetism of high-index resonators offers the potential for applications in various linear and nonlinear photonic devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Personal RF-EMF radiation exposure within Public Transportation Buses
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The advent of context aware environments within the implementation of Smart Cities and Smart Regions is supported by communication systems integrated within elements such as Intelligent Transportation Systems. In this paper, the impact of wireless communication system integration within public transportation buses will be analyzed, in order to assess regulatory compliance as well as to identify potential issues such as hot-spot location due to user density and wireless system usage.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Foliage Growth in Precision Viticulture from 3D Radar Proximal Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The estimation of the foliage growth of vineplants based on 3D radar proximal sensing is proposed in this paper. Measurements are performed with a ground-based 24GHz FM-CW radar and for different field polarizations. The statistical estimator derived from the 3D radar images is defined and correlated with the foliage growth of vineplants. This work and results may find applications in precision viticulture for estimating the leaf -to fruit ratio.

articleTitle: Invasive Weed Optimization for Antenna Design: Case of 4G/5G Multi-band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 5G is the latest generation of mobile communication and promises considerably higher data rates, lower latency, and increased number of instantaneous connections. This could not be achieved without the use of antennas that operate on several frequencies including those already-used by the current 4G technology. In this paper, we propose a new approach for the design of 4G/5G antennas based on the Invasive Weed Optimization algorithm. We show that our proposed algorithm outperforms the built-in optimizer of the CST simulator when applied to several 4G/5G antenna designs.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Optimal Uniform and Nonuniform Lossy Helical Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present results for comparison of gain of the optimal uniform and nonuniform helical antennas taking into the account conductor losses. Critical conductivities are observed, for the given operating frequency and the helix axial length. Above the critical conductivity, the gain of the nonuniform helical antennas with linearly varying geometrical parameters is up to 2 dB higher than the gain of the optimal uniform antennas. However, below the critical conductivity, the difference between the gain of the nonuniform and uniform helical antennas is reduced, and the gain of those antennas becomes comparable. Data for the normalized critical conductivities are presented.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Vertically Polarized Wearable Antenna with Omni-Directional Radiation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer planar antenna with vertical polarization and omni-directional radiation is proposed for wearable applications. The antenna consists of two identical shorted patches which are face-to-face located and fed by a microstrip line at the center. Due to the structural symmetry, the current distribution and electric-field distribution are symmetrical regarding the feed, which result in vertical linear polarization normal to the antenna and omni-directional radiation pattern in the azimuthal plane. To verify the design concept, an antenna prototype operating at 2.45 GHz is designed, fabricated and tested. Measured results concur well with the simulations, showing that the antenna has a good impedance matching, omnidirectional radiation pattern, and vertical polarization in the band of interest. The proposed antenna can be a good candidate for wearable and other wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Two-port Design of Y-shaped Patch using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of two antenna ports for a compact Y-shaped patch on top of a square ground plane is considered. Specifically, characteristic mode analysis reveals candidate regions to locate two direct probe feeding ports to jointly excite two significant modes of the Y-shaped patch with low mutual coupling and correlation. The feed design procedure, based on both the amplitude and phase distributions of the characteristic electric near-fields, is validated by full-wave simulation with two example realizations of two-port designs.

articleTitle: A Parabolic Torus Compact Antenna Test Range for 5G NR Massive MIMO OTA Multi-User Test Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel design for a compact antenna test range (CATR) that uses a parabolic toroid as the main reflector which possesses superior pseudo-plane wave scanning capabilities than existing comparable CATR designs. The wide-angle scanning capability is a crucial feature for successful over-the-air test and measurement of mm-wave 5G NR Massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna systems in multi-user applications where existing far-field multi-probe anechoic chamber (FF-MPAC) systems become unattractive due to their large far-field distance requirements. CATR quiet-zone results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Micrawave/Millimeter- Wave MEMS- Based Multiport Switches and Switch Matrices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reviews currently available technologies for microwave/millimeter-wave switches with a focus on MEMS switches. In particular, it outlines the research efforts carried-out and the results obtained over the period 2002-2008 to develop MEMS multiport switches and switch matrices. It also surveys MEMS-based switches developed for high-power applications as well as MEMS switches capable of operating up to 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Dielectric Properties of Skin-Mimicking Tissue Models in the 5 – 20 GHz Range
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The research of microwave-based medical systems requires accurate knowledge of dielectric properties of biological tissues. For the development and validation of such systems, tissue-mimicking models (phantoms) are needed for controlled laboratory experiments. This study investigates the dielectric properties of two commonly used skin-mimicking phantoms which are composed of different material configurations. The dielectric properties are characterized using a performance probe over the frequency range of 5-20 GHz. We observe the relative permittivity and conductivity in the range of interest for three different configurations of each tissue phantom: a thicker, “block” geometry and a thinner 2-mm sample representative of the human skin in its thickness and positioned on a fat-mimicking phantom layer.

articleTitle: Compact Dual Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna with High Ports Isolation for MIMO WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a design of two-ports circularly polarized stacked patch antenna with square ring slot feeding technique for multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) application. The antenna with a quarter-wavelength slot and chamfering patch., which radiates at 2.4 GHz., occupies an overall area of 96×96×42 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The 7.6-dBic gain antenna prototype presents an axial ratio lower than 0.4 dB in the operating frequency band (2.4 to 2.485 GHz) as well as a port isolation higher than 27 dB. Therefore., this antenna demonstrates good port-to-port isolation., axial ratio (AR) as well as a compact dimension and is suitable to be used in systems that operate in a wireless local area network (WLAN) frequency band.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Electrically Small Microstrip Patch Antennas on Finite Ground Planes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new technique to obtain greater than 30% 2:1 VSWR bandwidth, using a coaxial probe fed rectangular patch antenna, has been presented. The exact quality factor Q of the antenna is calculated using its input impedance and is compared to the approximate Q expressions applicable for electrically small antennas (ESAs). The D/Q optimization technique, given by Gustafsson et al., has been used for the performance optimization of the designed antennas on finite ground planes.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Wideband Low Cross-Polarization L-Probe Fed Asymmetric Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An L-probe fed low-profile asymmetric metasurface antenna is proposed for wideband and low cross-polarization operation. An asymmetric metasurface with reduced periodicity along the H-plane is utilized to suppress the undesired cross-polarization radiation. The proposed asymmetric metasurface antenna has a low profile of 0.044λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency), achieving low cross-polarization levels of less than -20 dB in E- and H-planes, reflection coefficient of less than -10 dB, and stable radiation patterns across a bandwidth of 25.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%.</sup>

articleTitle: Compact Substrate Integrated Choke Ring Ground Structure for High-Precision GNSS Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-band substrate integrated choke ring (SICR) ground structure has been designed and presented. Miniaturization has been achieved by using a high permittivity substrate and employing only two corrugations rather than the commonly used four to six corrugations. Besides, the dual-band behavior is obtained by engineering the location of via holes and partial copper cladding of the substrates in a multilayer structure. The performance of a right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) global navigation satellite system (GNSS) antenna has been investigated while it is mounted on the designed SICR ground, on the classic one and by itself. The proposed SICR demonstrates high multipath mitigation ability, comparable to the classic choke ring, while it eliminates the disadvantages of the classic one such as large size, heaviness, and high fabrication cost. An example design shows miniaturization of 70% in height and 44% in diameter compared to the classic choke ring.

articleTitle: Design of High-Gain Miniaturized Patch Antenna by Hybrid Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high-gain miniaturized patch antenna is designed by using a modified hybrid topology optimization (HTO) method. The HTO that combines scalar isotropic material with penalization (SIMP) and level set method (LSM), is based on gradient optimization with fast convergence speed. The performance of the optimized antenna is verified by simulation and measurement. Compared with the reference antenna, the patch size of the miniaturized antenna is reduced by 45%, while the realized gain and efficiency remain basically unchanged, achieving 6.2 dBi and 95%, respectively. The proposed antenna has the advantages of simple processing, low cost and easy integration. It can be utilized as a unit of array antennas.

articleTitle: Auto-calibration of Linear Array Antenna Positioning for Single Snapshot Direction of Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel joint auto-calibration of array positioning and single snapshot direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. This technique is useful in scenarios where the array position has uncertainties which lead to degradation in DOA estimation performance as well as in an environment where the snapshot samples are limited. Our proposed joint technique presented an improved DOA estimation performance gain of 75.22% when compared to a non-calibrated estimator. Also, our results presented similar average DOA estimation performance when compared to existing state-of-the-art joint techniques without the need for high snapshot values.

articleTitle: 3-D printed Helical Antenna for UAV Transmission Signal Direction of Arrival (DoA) Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present the implementation of a 3-D printed helical antenna operating at 5.9 GHz, intended for the detection of the direction of arrival (DoA) of a received signal that is transmitted from a flying Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). The ground based receiver consists of four identical 3D printed helical antennas which have four different ports. Based on the differential signal from the four directive antennas as they are interpreted by RSSI receivers, the directivity of the four elements array is aligned with the DoA. The rotation of the system is achieved using two servomotors which are controlled by one Arduino based microcontroller. The current paper discusses the fabrication of the supportive cylinder of the helical antennas and the challenges that were encountered during the use of a filament 3D printer and a resin 3D printer. Radiation pattern and gain simulations, and the conducted S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> measurements verify that the fabrication of helical antennas using 3D printing is both predictable and reliable.

articleTitle: Empirical Analysis of Millimeter-Wave Propagation in Indoor Transitional Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Based on double-directional channel measurement data, empirical analysis of millimeter-wave (mmWave) indoor transitional propagation is presented. A dual-slop path loss model which takes in-building blockage effects into account is developed. Compared with the traditional single-slop path loss model, the proposed model has physical basis and performs well for having smaller shadowing factor. The site-specific measurements reveal that the penetration loss of 25 mm double-glazing wall with 15 mm air layer is approximately 22 dB, which is in line with the step loss in the dual-slop model. The results can be further used to analyze space-time propagation characteristics in transition region, and have considerable benefits in coverage analysis of millimeter-wave wireless networks.

articleTitle: 3D Indoor Localization of RFID Tags with Phased Array and Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents indoor localization of RFID tags with a phased array antenna and a deep neural network (DNN). The antenna can steer the linear null in its radiation pattern crosswise, and the DNN estimates the 3D location of a tag (x, y, z) in a chamber using all received signals back scattered from the tag for all steered radiation patterns. The antenna and indoor radio propagation are simulated at 920 MHz, and the obtained received signals are used as the input of the DNN to train and test itself. Finally, the generalization capability for the polarization and height of a tag, etc. are compared with the conventional MUSIC method.

articleTitle: Near-Field Kandonian Loop Antenna With Wide Interrogation Zone for UHF RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A near-field kandonian loop antenna with small loop array and opposite directional current (ODC) for using ultra high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) system is proposed. The proposed antenna is constructed by array four loop antennas smaller than the wavelength of the operating frequency. The proposed antenna expands the interrogation zone at near-field and has a uniform field distribution because each straight line at the top and bottom of the substrate in the small loop utilizes ODC to canceling current and form one large loop electrically. In addition, the proposed antenna has a lower E-field compared to the conventional single loop, which prevents detection of adjacent tags outside the interrogation zone. The proposed antenna has a maximum read range of 48 mm and the detailed characteristics of the proposed antenna are verified by comparing the simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: A Millimeter Wave Circularly Polarized Microstrip Array Fed by SIW Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A millimeter-wave circularly polarized microstrip array fed by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) network is proposed in this paper. By combining SIW feeding network with circularly polarized microstrip antenna, the parasitic radiation and insertion loss of the feeding network is decreased effectively andgood radiation performance of the array is realized. The proposed array can realize sum beam and difference beam from 36.0 to 37.0GHz, the reflection coefficients of two ports are less than -15dB while the isolation is higher than 30dB. At the center frequency, the gain of sum beam is 23.3dBi and the sidelobe level is below -23.8dB, the axial ratio in half-power beam width is less than 1.6dB, the null depth of difference beam is 30.3dB.

articleTitle: Ultralight, Flexible Log-Periodic Dipole Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel construction technique to realize ultralight and flexible log-periodic dipole array antennas for weight-sensitive applications is described. Simulated and measured s11 and 3D radiation patterns for a design covering 1-6 GHz and weighing only ~13 g show good agreement.

articleTitle: A Method for Bandwidth Enhancement of Cross-Dipole Antennas with Compact Configurations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new method to broaden the bandwidth of dual-polarized cross-dipole antennas is presented. By connecting a thin loop to a traditional cross-dipole, additional resonant points are introduced and the bandwidth is broadened. This method does not increase the physical dimension of the antenna and has little influence on radiation performances. A loop-connected cross-dipole antenna is presented to verify the method. The bandwidth it achieves is 66.7% from 1.65 GHz to 3.30 GHz with a very compact radiator size. The antenna also has a high port isolation level and stable radiation performances, making it highly suitable for the base station application.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction for UWB MIMO Antenna with High Frequencies Rejection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact planar two-element UWB antenna for MIMO and cognitive radios applications is presented. The antenna element used in this work is a monopole antenna with slotted ground plane. The proposed antenna is fed by a microstrip feed line of 50 ohms. The total area of the MIMO antenna is approximately 49×26.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The considered operating band covers the frequencies between the WiMax band and the WLAN band with a 76% of bandwidth. The proposed structure has a good isolation of 20 dB in the entire operating band. The envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.01 and the gain diversity (DG) is more than 9.9 over the entire band. Moreover, the antenna is able to filter higher frequencies (including the WLAN band). For frequency reconfiguration, two slots and two switches are integrated in the ground plane. The “On” and “Off” states of the switch are modelled by the presence / absence of a perfect conductor (PEC), respectively. The obtained results show good performances in terms of isolation, ECC and DG.

articleTitle: A General Formula for the Half-Power Beamwidth of 1-D Unidirectional Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A general and accurate formula for evaluating the single-sided beamwidth in one-dimensional unidirectional leaky-wave antennas has been recently proposed. The half-power beamwidth is then estimated by simply doubling the value of the single-sided beamwidth. However, this approximation may lead to inaccurate results as the beam approaches endfire; at that point, the left- and the right-sided beamwidth may considerably differ one another. This conference paper proposes and numerically validates a more general formula to solve this issue.

articleTitle: Near Field Radiation from a Monopole Antenna on an Electrically Large Conducting Convex Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The extended uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) solution is used to predict near fields of a monopole antenna on an electrically large perfectly conducting convex surface. The proposed approach is validated with the results of the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM) obtained using FEKO commercial electromagnetic simulation software for a monopole antenna on canonical shapes. It will be useful towards prediction of co-site interference between monopole antennas.

articleTitle: On the Applicability of TRL Calibration for Dielectric Waveguide based 2-Port-1-Port Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we expand standard TRL-calibration and investigate its applicability to novel 2-port-1-port measurement systems. Next to a short introduction on the functionality of dielectric waveguide based 2-port-1-port systems, the signal processing steps of the modified TRL calibration are explained in detail. Measurements and the calibration on a transmission line are presented and the applicability evaluated.

articleTitle: Investigation of Ringing Effects on Phase Shift Keyed Direct Antenna Modulation Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a method of direct antenna modulation (DAM) transmitting phase shift keyed (PSK) high data rate signals using a narrowband antenna is described. We analyze the result of an over the air DAM PSK measurement and degradation are observed in QPSK DAM compared to the ideal case. We demonstrate that it is the parasitics of the circuit that reduce the ability of the system to store voltage and achieve fast transitions, particularly between certain combinations of symbols. This degradation is studied and it can be predicted by circuit model simulation.

articleTitle: A Perturbation Method for the Analysis of Eccentric Coaxial Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a novel analytical solution for the modal analysis of eccentric coaxial waveguides based on a perturbation method. Different techniques have been used for solving this kind of problem, and the majority of then rely on solving a complicated transcendental equation obtained from the Graf's addition theorem, or on numerical methods such as the finite-element method (FEM). In our approach, instead, a transformation optics is employed to turn the original problem into a concentric coaxial waveguide filled with anisotropic and in-homogeneous medium. A corresponding (transformed) Helmholtz equation is then solved via a perturbative approach that allows us to obtain field solutions in terms of a set of orthogonal transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes. We present validation results which show that our technique can accurately model eccentric coaxial waveguides providing cutoff wavenumbers and field pattern in a computationally efficient manner.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Spatial Location of RSU in Trilateration Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A trilateration method of 3 reference stations or Roadside Units (RSU) to find the accurate position of an Onboard Unit (OBU) is presented in this paper. This study is based on drive test results. To investigate the effectiveness of the trilateration method., a comparison of the results obtained from the computation using 2 RSU (test 1) and 3 RSU (test 2) is presented. Results from trilateration has been validated by using Global Positioning System (GPS) solution. Results revealed that the separation distance and spatial location of RSU will affect the accuracy of the trilateration method. Meanwhile., trilateration method using 3 RSU can reduce systematical error effectively. Finally., output from this study is crucial to develop the network of RSU for supporting accurate positioning in future.

articleTitle: Coupled Surface Mode Resonances in Finite Transverse-Width Superlenses
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Superlens slabs excite coupled surface wave modes to provide amplification to incident evanescent waves. If a super-lens slab has a finite transverse-width, surface wave reflections at the edges of the lens restrict allowed coupled surface modes within the lens. In this paper we simulate the coupled surface modes of a two dimensional finite-width, finite thickness, double negative superlens slab. By calculating the scattered electric field intensity and radiated power we show how a superlens slab with finite transverse-width supports discrete, radiating resonant modes, whose solutions closely align with the locus of mode solutions for an infinitely wide lens.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Performance of Wearable Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the performances of wearable Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems are enhanced using ferromagnetic materials. The effects of the human body on the Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) of a Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) WPT system are further investigated. Two pairs of CSCMR, one on FR-4 PCB and one on flexible ferrite sheet are designed to operate at the 27.12 MHz ISM band. Simulations and measurements of these two configurations were performed on 26 different locations on the human body. It is found that printing CSCMR WPT systems on ferromagnetic substrates (i.e., ferrites) can prevent the reduction of PTE by isolating the effects of the human body.

articleTitle: Milk Characterization Using Time Domain Wide Band Dielectric Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wide band time domain dielectric spectroscopy system for milk characterization is presented. The system is a kind of quasi mono static free space dielectric spectroscopy in which all measurements have been done with Xethru X4 sensor. The permittivity of low-fat milk and a mixture of 50% whole milk and 50% water have been calculated by mapping phase and amplitude differences of calibration materials. The calculated permittivity for low-fat milk and milk-water mixture show good agreement with their Debye model between 6.4 GHz-7.4 GHz.

articleTitle: A multi-layer Partially Reflecting Surface Antenna for cost-effective 3D printing manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multi-layer partially reflecting surface(PRS) based antenna is proposed. The PRS is designed such that it meets the considerations to increase the broadside directivity of the antenna, yet is suited for manufacturing with a common benchtop 3D printing technology. The resulting antenna is wideband in nature (40% directivity-bandwidth) predicts a best-case improvement of 15 dBi in broadside directivity. Overall, profile of the antenna is 2λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where λ = 25mm.

articleTitle: On the performance of Alamouti-coded Cooperative MB-OFDM scheme for Wireless Body Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ultrawideband communications adapt quite well with body communications because of their low power levels and co-existence with other ambient communication systems. In this context, we propose in this work a new scheme, which_combines the viable features of cooperative diversity and Alamouti coding, in offering an additional immunization against wireless body ultrawideband channel errors. The bit error rate (BER) performance of the resulting scheme is investigated with different modulation orders and numbers of relays.

articleTitle: High Gain and Ultra-broadband RCS Reduction Fabry-Perot Antenna with Checkerboard Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Owing to the F-P cavity and its novel checkerboard superstrate, the natural combination of radiation and scattering characteristics in this paper contributes a lot to develop the stealthy antenna system. The superstrate interleaves single- and dual-band frequency selective surfaces (FSSs), building a check-board up, which overcomes the restraint of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180^{\circ}\pm 37^{\circ}$</tex> reflection phase difference (RPD) required for −10 dB radar cross-section reduction (RCSR). The 82.39% RCSR bandwidth is consistent with the theoretical, ranging from 3.74 GHz to 8.98 GHz. Not only that, the simulation by ANSYS HFSS 18.0 shows a 3.25 dBi peak gain enhancement after the application of F-P cavity.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Analytical Formulations and Variable Transformations for Near-Singularity Quadrature Involving the Static Potentials
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we first investigate the problem of the near-singularity and shape-dependence in the analytical methods. It is found that the analytical methods are not immune to the two problems, due to the subtractive cancellation and round-off error. In order to increase the stability of the analytical formulations, an investigation is performed to find alternative formulations for the extreme cases. On the other hand, we propose a new variable transformation which can achieve machine-precision accuracy for the extreme case with a fast convergence rate. Some numerical results are presented to compare the modified analytical formulations and the singularity cancellation methods.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarization Reflectarray Unit Cell for a Ku-Band SAR Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarization reflectarray unit cell is proposed for a spaceborne synthetic aperture radar application. The unit cell consists of a set of four dipoles aperture-coupled to striplines for phase control. Two pairs of dipoles work respectively at 13.6 GHz and 17.2 GHz, two frequencies selected for snow mass measurements. Very low mutual coupling between the dipoles allows independent phase control for both frequencies and polarizations. Phase ranges over 360° are achieved without affecting the phase of other reflected coefficients.

articleTitle: Multi-band, Flexible, Lightweight Antenna on LCP for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new planar, multi-band antenna for vehicle-to-anything (V2X) automotive applications is presented. The single-fed antenna operates at cellular (800 MHz) and C-V2X (5.9 GHz) bands. It is linearly polarized and has omnidirectional radiation pattern at the lower frequencies. The mean measured realized gain is 0.23 dBi at 800 MHz and 0.0429 dBi at 5.9 GHz. The designed antenna is fabricated using lithography on Liquid Crystalline Polymer (LCP) substrate. As a dual-band antenna, covering two bands whose wavelengths have a ratio of 7.4, it contributes in the decrease of the number of antennas that are necessary in automotive industry.

articleTitle: A Ten-port Multi-band 5G MIMO Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a MIMO antenna array for 5G mobile terminal is proposed. The antenna bandwidth was broadened by opening either L-shaped slot or square slot in the ground plate. The covering bandwidth of the antenna array is 3.3GHz-3.6GHz and 4.8GHz-5GHz. CST software was used to simulate and optimize the parameters of the designed antenna array. The prototype antenna was manufactured and tested. The performance of the simulation shows that the proposed antenna array can be used in 5G mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Wide Azimuth Beam Coverage Three-Beam 4×4 MIMO Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of low-profile slant 45° dual-polarized 4×4 MIMO three-beam base station antenna at the frequency band of 2.3-2.7 GHz. By reducing the azimuth spacing and increasing the row number of the antenna array, a high gain three-beam antenna with wide azimuth beam coverage (i.e., 120° 10dB beam-width) is realized. Through arranging two three-beam arrays side-by-side, a 4×4 MIMO three-beam antenna are designed and tested. Detailed array architecture and the corresponding measurement results of the proposed multibeam antenna are given.

articleTitle: A Fast Blocking Matrix Generating Algorithm for Generalized Sidelobe Canceller Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fast algorithm to generate the Blocking Matrix for Generalized Sidelobe Canceller (GSC) beamforming is proposed in this paper. The proposed algorithm uses a simplified zero placement algorithm (SZPA) to directly generate the independent null space vectors by specifying the zeros of the corresponding Z domain polynomials following the constrained signal incoming angle. Compared to the conventional methods based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), this method can be more than 10 times faster for scenarios with 15 constraints and will be even more advantageous for more constraints with the same converged state performance. Numerical simulation confirms the efficiency and effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Microstrip Ridge Gap Technology Based Rat-Race Coupler for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A rat race coupler design for millimeter wave applications is presented in this paper. The coupler design is realized using microstrip ridge gap technology where the propagation is done between the two metallic parallel plates in the air that minimizes the radiation losses and eliminates the dielectric losses. The coupler is designed for wideband characteristics (25-35 GHz) with in-phase and anti-phase properties that can be integrated with other RF front-end components. Equal power division ( 3.5±0.5 dB) for the coupled output ports over 27-33 GHz with ±10° error in the 90° phase difference are obtained using this technology.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystal Material based Electronically Beam Steering Antenna at Ka-band for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A meander line phase shifter based on liquid crystal (LC) material is used to electronically steer beam of an antenna arraydesigned for ka-band. Based on biasing voltage applied on LC based meander line phase shifter, phases can be adjusted for antenna elements to steer the main beam in the desired directions. For theexample of a 1×4 array antenna with LC based meander line phase shifters, the main beam can be steered in the range of ±17<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>.

articleTitle: A 1D Gaussian Function for Efficient Generation of Plane Waves in 1D, 2D, and 3D FDTD
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 1D Gaussian expression is derived and used as the 1D E/H incident field in the TF/SF formulation to efficiently generate plane waves in 1D, 2D, and 3D FDTD simulations. The analytic expression is simple, and it eliminates the need for computational resources to store and compute the E/H-field incident arrays and their associated absorbing boundaries. FDTD simulation results at the magic time-step in 1D, 2D, and 3D FDTD show good correlation between plane waves generated by the 1D analytic Gaussian function vs. those generated by 1D FDTD incident arrays.

articleTitle: Mitigating People Blockage by Angular Diversity at Millimeter Wave 5G Bands
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A measurement campaign was carried out in order to characterize the channel response when people are passing between transmitter and receiver in the 5G Frequency Range 2 and beyond (40 GHz and 60 GHz). We also studied the possibility of using angular diversity to compensate for the resultant fading. After analyzing the data, interesting results are obtained: fading values over 25 dB were measured at both bands; the level crossing rate is very similar in value and distribution at both frequencies, and the average duration of the resultant fadings is almost double at 60 GHz. It was also observed that the fading depth seems to be related to the stature of the person obstructing the radio link. A deeper fading is observing with taller individuals.

articleTitle: Guided and Leaky Mode Characteristics of Solid Dielectric Horn: Analytical and Numerical Solutions
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: When a solid dielectric horn antenna is excited by the fundamental mode, one expects the radiation to be because of the fundamental mode only. Often this is not the case as higher order modes are also excited due to the large axial length or even due to physical defects. A metal wave guide to solid dielectric horn transition is proposed for eliminating the higher order modes. The equation for axial propagation constant of higher order guided and leaky modes is also proposed and is compared with numerical results.

articleTitle: FDTD-based Extraction of Diffuse Scattering Models for Ray-Tracing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ray Tracing (RT) has been widely used to evaluate the characteristics of wireless channels in indoor and outdoor environments. However, for RT to be accurate at mm-wave frequencies, it is essential to account for the effect of diffuse scattering, especially at rough surface boundaries. This paper is aimed at modeling diffuse mm- wave reflection and transmission from rough slabs, such as walls and windows. We use the Finite-Difference Time-Domain method to derive reflection and transmission coefficients for rough slabs and map them to diffuse scattering models that can be directly integrated with ray-tracing.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Wideband CPW-Fed Circularly-Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new approach of square slot element combination is proposed to design a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed circularly-polarized antenna. The proposed antenna has 91% 10-dB impedance bandwidth (1.16-3.25 GHz) and 3-dB Axial Ratio (AR) of 94% (1.2-3.24 GHz). The compact size and ease of fabrication, makes the proposed antenna a good candidate for various multifunctional communication applications.

articleTitle: Wearable Electrically Small Loop Antennas for Monitoring Joint Kinematics: Guidelines for Optimal Frequency Selection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We have recently reported a new class of wearable electrically small loop antennas (ESLAs) that can seamlessly monitor joint kinematics (i.e., flexion and rotation). In this paper, we aim to provide generic guidelines for optimally selecting the operating frequency of such designs. Key to our approach is to first establish crucial performance benchmark criteria (i.e., received power level, angular resolution, and effect of tissue dielectric property variation). The frequency range we consider spans from the antenna mode of operation to the electrically small antenna mode (24 MHz to 1028 MHz chosen here). Based on the frequency-specific tradeoffs for each of the aforementioned performance benchmark criterion, a suitable optimal operating frequency is eventually selected (34 MHz identified as optimal in our example demonstration).

articleTitle: Integrated Reflection Amplifier/Phase-Conjugating Mixer Design for Dual-Mode Retrodirective Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel integrated switchless reflection amplifier/phase-conjugating mixer (RAPM) design for dual-mode active Van Atta/phase-conjugating array is presented. The proposed RAPM comprises a single GaAs heterojunction-FET (HJ-FET) transistor with suitable matching networks. Switchless feature, avoiding using external mixers, and improved backscatter communication are the main advantages of this component for the dual-mode retrodirective array design. Also, to demonstrate the performance of the proposed structure with respect to other reported structures, an integrated RAPM is designed and fabricated which shows an acceptable performance in both modes.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Machined-Metal Array Radiator for Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple implementation of the Frequency-scaled Ultra-wide Spectrum Element (FUSE) antenna aperture was developed for manufacturing as a self-supporting metallic structure using either subtractive or additive technologies (or a hybrid combination). This low-profile ultra-wideband array aperture is shown to be precisely built for operation from roughly 10 GHz to 40 GHz with VSWR below 2.0 for 45-degree scans in all planes for an optimally-sampled square lattice. Modeling predictions are validated with measured results.

articleTitle: A Survey of MIMO OTA Test Methodologies for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The automotive test environment poses unique challenges with its diversity and complexity of wireless onboard systems and the large electrical size of the test article. In this paper, we discuss one of the challenging aspects of such testing: MIMO OTA testing of terrestrial wireless communications systems. We offer an overview of five MIMO test methods and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each for both 4G and 5G testing. Three of these methods are well-known; given the challenges associated with these methods for automotive testing, we propose two new MIMO test methods and discuss next steps for exploring them.

articleTitle: A Phase-only Pattern Synthesis Method for Large Satellite Array Antenna
