publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of minimizing the maximum side lobe level (SLL) for a given secondary amplitude distribution by phase-only control. A novel fitness function based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is introduced to optimize the phase of the excitation. Eamples of beam pattern synthesis for large planar phased array are presented, and simulation results verify the effectiveness of the design. Indeed, it has a good robustness in amplitude and phase errors.

articleTitle: New Design of Mirror Shape Antennas with Band-Rejection Characteristics suitable for UWB Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, two mirror shape antenna with capability to operate in the application narrowband mode (WiMAX, WLAN) from 3.15 to 4.1 and 5 to 6.1 GHz for Antenna 1 and from 5.5 to 6.3 and 7.5 to 8.2 GHz for Antenna 2 with switchable notch bands of 5.1 to 5.9 GHz for Antenna 1 and 4 to 5 GHz for Antenna 2, is presented. The proposed antenna has a simple configuration and compact size of 35×20 mm2. To make the band-notches, methods of slot antenna are used. The antenna performance both by simulation and by experiment indicates that it is suitable and a good candidate for UWB applications.

articleTitle: An Effective Plane Wave Synthesis Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to decrease the amplitude and phase ripple in the quiet zone (QZ) generated by plane wave generator (PWG), two non-uniformly distributed arrays of PWG based on Chebyshev polynomials are proposed. The weighting coefficients of the PWG array are calculated by sparse optimization algorithm. The methods are verified by computer simulation.

articleTitle: A Compact High Data Rate 4-FSK HF Transmitter through Direct Antenna Modulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Achieving high-bandwidth RF performance in electrically small and compact volumes remains a continuous challenge. The difficulty lies in the inability of electrically small antennas to radiate high-bandwidth RF signals efficiently because of their narrow bandwidth performance resulting from their high radiation Q-factors. Consequently, the RF signal is heavily distorted and/or reflected back to the source, while at the same time, the antenna suffers from minimal antenna gain. In this paper, we propose using a capacitively loaded loop antenna (CLLA) that utilizes Direct Antenna Modulation (DAM), enabling radiation of a high-bandwidth high data rate quadrature frequency shift-keyed (4-FSK) signal between 27 MHz and 39 MHz. The CLLA was integrated with two pairs of high figure-of-merit semiconductor transistors, modulating the RF signal to produce 4-FSK. The antenna ( 0.009λ x. 013λ) was prototyped and measured, showing a high-data rate 4-FSK transmission of 1.58 Mbps, beyond the inherent narrow bandwidth of the antenna. The design achieves superior high-efficiency bandwidth performance, enabling compact RF communication in electrically small volumes.

articleTitle: Split Ring Resonator Based Metamaterial Absorber for Antenna Radar Cross Section Reduction Applications in Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article reports on a compact metamaterial based electromagnetic absorber for Ku band radar applications. The proposed absorber offers -10 dB absorption from 14.29 GHz - 14.73 GHz having a maximum absorption peak at 14.6 GHz. The simulated and experimental results showed stable absorption response. Furthermore, it is experimentally shown that the proposed metamaterial absorber exhibits stable frequency response when illuminated by waves at oblique angles of incidence and polarization insensitive behavior up-to 60°. A good compliance between the measured and simulated results is observed.

articleTitle: All-Passive Composite Right/Left-Handed (CRLH) Antenna Array for Sum and Difference Patterns
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Monopulse tracker is well-known for using the sum and difference radiation patterns for track, typically done electronically. The objective of this work is to create a dual band all-passive antenna array with composite right hand feed transmission lines to obtain the sum and difference patterns. A dual-band Wilkinson power divider has been designed for inphase output at 2.6 GHz and a phase difference of 180° at 1.8 GHz achieved by using a CRLH transmission line in one of the output arms. This is incorporated in a microstrip feed system to obtain the sum and difference patterns. Design optimization has been done using ANSYS HFSS. The antenna array has been fabricated and the sum pattern has been validated. Work is in progress to validate the difference pattern.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study on Improving Microwave Stroke Detection using Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a feasibility study to enhance microwave imaging (MWI) for intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) detection using an innovative metamaterial (MM) design. To this end, we simulate a radar-based approach in CST Microwave Studio and use a previously developed algorithm based on Huygens principle to produce images with and without the MM. Our results indicate that the proposed MM film can significantly improve target localization and decrease image artefacts when closely fixed on the antennas of our MWI system.

articleTitle: Simplified Transmitarray Unit Cell for 1-Bit Beam-Steering Operation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a simplified design of transmitarray unit cell for 1-bit beam steering operation is proposed. It can provide 1-bit phase quantization by switching on/off the loading capacitors, which could be realized by using varactors and switching the dc bias voltages between a predetermined value and zero. The proposed unit cell is made of two identical, back-to-back rectangular patch antennas, coupled through a ground slot. Each patch is cut into halves by a transverse slit, at the middle of which the varactor is loaded. For preliminary verification, two test pieces of fixed-beam X-band transmitarray (0° and 20° from broadside, respectively) based on the proposed unit cell (loaded with and without capacitors) are fabricated and tested. The agreement between the simulated and measured results is satisfactory.

articleTitle: A Space-Time Modulated Distributed Antenna Array for Multiple Target Angle Estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a method to estimate the angle of multiple targets using a millimeter-wave distributed antenna array with a single transmit and three receive elements. The three receive elements are placed on a minimum redundancy layout forming three correlation interferometers with unique baselines. The transmitter emits a linear frequency modulated signal from 36 to 39.5 GHz which generates a space-time modulated radiation pattern. Each interferometer captures the angle information of each target with a simple frequency estimation. The ambiguities of multiple targets are resolved by combining the detections common to each baseline. Experimental results of the detection of multiple targets are presented.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of an Origami Yagi-Uda Antenna Using an Adaptive Fitness Function
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An automated design and multi-objective optimization of an origami-enabled deployable Yagi-Uda antenna is presented. The antenna is appropriately designed on a foldable Miura-Ori substrate using our custom origami toolset. To electromagnetically analyze the origami antenna, ANSYS HFSS is used by utilizing Visual Basic Scripting (VBS) as a communication bridge between our toolset and the software. The origami Yagi-Uda antenna is optimized for impedance matching, forward gain, side-lobe gain and bandwidth using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm and an adaptive fitness function.

articleTitle: A Phase Modulation Scheme for Super-Low Frequency Handheld Mechanical Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports on the design and experimental demonstration of a novel direct phase modulation technique appropriate for mechanical antennas operating at the Ultra-Low Frequency band (0.3-3 kHz) and lowers. Such antenna system can be utilized to establish reliable wireless underwater and underground communication links. It is proposed that through mechanically rotating a permanent magnet sandwiched between two pairs of orthogonal bow-tie shape layers of high μ material (ferrite) which vibrate slowly, the phase profile of transmitted signal can be modulated smoothly. Another unique advantage of the proposed mechanical antenna is its capability to generate higher harmonics of the rotation frequency and thereby radiate at a much higher frequency than the rotational frequency of the motor and thus achieve higher range. Numerical simulations using ANSYS Maxwell along with measurements are performed to verify these concepts.

articleTitle: HF Radar Cross-Section of Ocean Surfaces With Arbitrary Wave Heights
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The high-frequency radar cross-section (RCS) for ocean surfaces with arbitrary wave heights is presented. By removing the height restriction of the ocean surface, a new form of the first-order electric field is obtained, which in turn is used to derive the RCS at arbitrary wave heights. A new correction term for the first-order is derived, with previously-derived first-and second- order RCSs being preserved. Through simulation it is shown that the new term impacts small Doppler frequencies of the total RCS at high sea states. The present work can contribute to improving target detection and wave direction estimation at high sea states.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna with 8-Ports for Polarization Diversity Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An 8-port dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) was investigated to provide polarization diversity; i.e. right-handed circular polarization (RHCP), left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) as well as both vertical and horizontal linear polarization (LP). The antenna performances in terms of gain and radiation efficiency are compared and reported for the various polarization states. The prototyped DRA has simple slot feeding and can offer high polarization diversity, and this agile feature, can be useful in communication or satellite systems including the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) where the RF environment is challenging, more specifically, where the optimal polarization scheme might not be known apriori. In such configurations, this type of polarization diverse antenna can support approaches to circumvent such fading and improve overall system performance.

articleTitle: Epsilon-near-zero plasmonic waveguides to achieve multi-qubit quantum entanglement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multi-qubit entanglement is of paramount importance to perform truly secure quantum optical communication operations. In this work, we present efficient long-range entanglement mediated by plasmonic waveguides operating at their cut-off frequency, where they exhibit an effective epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) response. Only the excited ENZ mode at plasmonic waveguides has a strong and homogeneous electric field distribution compared to different modes excited at groove and rod waveguides, resulting in an efficient two- and multi-qubit entanglement that can persist over extended time periods and long distances. Efficient multipartite entanglement from three equidistantly arranged two-level quantum emitters (qubits) inside the ENZ waveguide is also demonstrated by using three different multi-qubit entanglement criterions, i.e., pairwise concurrence, negativity, and genuine multipartite entanglement. The findings of this work stress the importance of ENZ plasmonic waveguides as an ideal nanophotonic platform to support efficient quantum optical effects.

articleTitle: On the Image Analysis of Conducting Magneto-Responsive Micro-Particles for Applications in Leaky Wave Antenna Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Magneto-static responsive micron-sized particles are useful for their ability to be manipulated to create columns of conducting particles. Their uses have mainly been to be concealed in a substrate and connect the top and bottom copper layers, creating a switch. This use in many situations is practical when only ON and OFF states are required. However, more research on the magneto-static responsive particles is needed. The work presented in this paper is further study on the characteristics of the particles and how they can be used for antenna design purposes, such as leaky wave antennas.

articleTitle: Advanting Throughput Antenna Structure for $4\times 4$ MIMO WiFi 6 Mini PC Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A four-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with high isolation is proposed for WiFi 6 dual-band mini PC applications. The single antenna with a compact size of 18.5 mm×6.5 mm jointly with asymmetric co-planar waveguide (ACPW) feeding structure, to operate at 2400MHz-2500MHz and 5150MHz-5850MHz is presented. Based on suppressing surface wave and near-field coupling, a printed ground-line which protrudes from ground-plane is introduced to increase isolation. It is found that isolation of more than 20 dB can be achieved between each two polarization diversity dual-band monopole elements. The throughput of WiFi 6 of channel 6, 36, 100 and 149 are measured, the good results are shown.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Microstrip Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to design a filter with good frequency selectivity and wide stopband, a notch H-Shaped DMS (defected microstrip structure) microstrip filter is applied. The DMS structure is cascaded with two 1/4 λ terminal short resonators. The filter is designed and analyzed by using HFSS. Measurement results show that the bandwidth of the filter is 0.95GHz-1.45GHz, the stopband below -20dB is 1.6-3.7GHz. The insertion loss of the filter over the whole bandwidth is less than 0.57 dB.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Curved Beam-Shaping Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a two-step procedure for synthesizing curved beam-shaping metasurfaces. First we simplify the problem by projecting the desired field distribution from a virtual plane onto the outer boundary of the metastructure structure. We use this to determine the initial metasurface impedance distribution. In the second step, we optimize the metasurface design using a developed Moment Method-based program as core of the optimization procedure. Measurement results are compared to design expectations to verify the procedure.

articleTitle: A Beam-Steerable Rollable Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a novel beam-steerable Reflectarray Antenna (RA) at Ku-band. This RA consists of a 58×30 square patch elements printed on a flexible plastic substrate. The RA is rolled around two cylinders to form a 30×30 RA aperture. Mechanical rotation is used to turn the two cylindrical tubes in both the left and right directions to steer the beam. The phase synthesis optimization procedure is also introduced. The obtained primary results using array theory show that the beam is able to steer from -24° to +24° in elevation with a steering step of 4° and provide a 4 dB directivity variation by mechanically rotating the RA. These results show that our proposed design is suitable for implementing high gain antennas with beam-steering capabilities that require less power. Such antennas are needed in CubeSat and space applications.

articleTitle: Integrated Wideband Circularly Polarized Leaky Wave Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel wideband circularly polarized (CP) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is developed in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of sixteen unit-cells, each of which combines a slot (magnetic dipole) and an electric dipole. A conventional slotted substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) LWA in the lower layer and the electric dipoles are etched on the upper layer. Two kinds of dipoles are placed in parallel to produce two orthogonal polarization components which results in the required CP operation. The CP LWA is designed and fabricated to operate at the 26 GHz Ka band. Measured results show that the antenna has a peak gain of 17.1 dBic with circular polarization throughout the frequency range from 24-28 GHz.

articleTitle: WPT Systems on Ferromagnetic Substrates with Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, ferromagnetic materials are used to improve the performance of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems. A Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) system is miniaturized by placing ferrite sheets under its transmitting (TX) and receiving (RX) elements. When the ferrite substrates are used, the operating frequency of the CSCMR system shifts from 40 MHz (without the ferrites) to 32 MHz This reduction of the operating frequency is achieved while maintaining the same dimensions, thereby miniaturizing the WPT system. Additionally, the effects of a metallic surface were also investigated. Without the ferrite substrates, the Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) of the system is approximately zero, whereas with the ferrite substrates the system is able to provide a maximum PTE of 62.9%. These results show that ferromagnetic materials can be used to enhance the performance of CSCMR systems for multiple applications.

articleTitle: Research on Distributed Nested Array Pattern Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a method of grating lobes and sidelobes suppression for distributed two-level nested array is presented. The method combines the distributed nested array structure and the pattern product theorem to obtain a distributed two-level nested array two-way pattern, which can effectively suppress the grating lobes and sidelobes. The Chebyshev window is used to design the weights of the transmit array pattern to achieve ultralow sidelobes performance. Numerical simulations are provided for testing the proposed method. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which will help to improve the detection performance of radar.

articleTitle: Self-Reconfigurable Dual-Mode Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study realized a novel dual-mode metasurface that exhibited a self-reconfigurable characteristic between the high direction antenna (M1) and the radar cross-section (RCS) reduction (M2). The proposed structure consists of a source patch antenna and an active metasurface with each unit cell loaded with a Schottky diode and two lumped resistors. The switching mechanism of the metasurface is realized by considering the different power levels of the patch antenna. In mode M1, the metasurface acts as partially reflecting surface (PRS) to enhance the directivity of the source antenna. In another case (M2), the ground plane of the antenna and metasurface are used to prevent the transmission and reflection of the incident wave, respectively. Therefore, the absorption function is obtained in the mode. The proposed structure has been investigated and studied using fullwave simulation and confirmed with the experimental demonstration. As result, the proposed structure realizes as the high gain antenna with the pack gain of 13.3 dBi at 4.6 GHz in the mode M1, and as radar absorbing structure with absorptivity of 98% at 4.6 GHz in mode M2.

articleTitle: Ka-band Full Polarization Reconfigurable 1D Beam Steering Staggered Butterfly Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel full-polarization reconfigurable 8×12 Butterfly phased array antenna with wide-angle 1D beam steering performance is proposed at Ka-band (28 GHz) for increased system capacity of 5G communications. The butterfly unit cell of the proposed array is a novel sequentially-rotated series-fed microstrip patch antenna with simple, versatile, and adequate radiation performance characteristics. The proposed staggered planar array configuration reduces the spacing between the adjacent series-fed linear array to 0.45λ0, where λ0 is the free-space wavelength at 28 GHz. This reduced spacing can enable larger beam steering angle radiation performance without any grating lobes. The 16-channel Analog devices ADMV4821 RFIC Ka-band beamformer is used to provide excitation weights for achieving the desired beam steering, full-polarization reconfiguration, and reduced sidelobe level. The ADMV4821 beamformer chip is characterized; the average measured phase imbalance is less than 10°, and the average measured channel gain imbalance is less than 1 dB. The proposed Butterfly staggered phased array antenna is being prototyped and integrated with the beamformer board to verify the analysis and simulation results experimentally.

articleTitle: Conical Monopole Antenna with Integrated Tunable Notch Cavity Filters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As wireless communication systems are allocated more spectrum, and use digitally configurable transceivers, there is a stronger impetus to use a single broadband antenna. However, broadband antennas are susceptible to interference or radiating out-of-band emissions, so filtering is commonly required before RF front ends. As such, a broadband conical monopole antenna with integrated physically tunable notch cavity filters is presented. By simulation, the proposed antenna is shown to have an azimuthally symmetric radiation pattern and notch-filters that have very wide tuning ranges, resulting in a versatile broadband antenna.

articleTitle: Deep Integration of Power Amplifier-on-Antenna in Standard CMOS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a deep integration strategy of multiple active devices within antenna for simultaneous power amplification and radiation through a unified design and integration space. In this work, these active devices are configured in parallel to enhance the power handling capability, and an E-patch antenna is utilized to improve the matching bandwidth. A brief analysis on active device characterization along with the prototype design and simulation results are discussed and presented. The realized prototype at 100 GHz in 65nm CMOS process exhibits an amplification of around 7.5 dB across 4.5% matching bandwidth along with broadside radiation.

Author Keywords: unified integration of circuit and antenna (UNICA)

articleTitle: Generation of Vortex Beam using Circularly Polarized Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a planar transmitarray to generate a spiral phase front in the far-field radiation pattern. The transmitarray is composed of 12×12 circularly polarized unit cells, which are rotated individually in order to generate the desired phase distribution. The novel presented unit cell is designed on a double-layer dielectric slab, and three identical metallic sections are positioned on top of each other in a stack. Through rotation of the unit cells a full 360-degree spiral phase progression on the transmitarray can be obtained. The simulated results for the designed spiral phase transmitarray show a desirable performance in the frequency band of 22.5-23.5 GHz ka-band.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneous Lens for use with Small Phased Array Feeds
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here we outline the development techniques used to design a millimeter-wave lens antenna that is fed by a single chipset phased array feed. The lens significantly increases the gain and retains the scanning capability of the array. The resulting system is only slightly more expensive than the array alone but has the directivity of a system with many more elements.

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized Filtering Monopole Antenna for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple and compact broadband circularly polarized (CP) filtering planar monopole antenna for C-band applications is presented. A printed falcate-shaped monopole with a modified ground plane is applied to realize broadband impedance matching and circular polarization radiation. By symmetrically etching a pair of rectangular complementary split-ring resonators (CSRRs) on the ground plane directly beneath the feedline, good filtering performance in the upper stopband is achieved and CP radiation towards high frequency is enhanced. The proposed antenna provides -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 72% ranging from 3.8 to 8.1 GHz, and the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 63% ranging from 4.1-7.9 GHz.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Loop Yagi Array With a Parallel-Plate Driven Element
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A few examples of loop yagi arrays capable of generating circular polarization have appeared in the literature. However, each design has one or more major disadvantages, such as extremely narrow bandwidth or fabrication challenges. It is shown here that a loop yagi array can be driven using an element consisting of two parallel plates with the feed point located on a wire bridging the plates. The array produces circular polarization over a 2% bandwidth, should be relatively easy to build, and is mechanically robust.

articleTitle: Multilobate Patch Antennas for Circular Polarization Operation in the C-band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact circularly polarized patch antenna for operation in C-band is presented. The shape of the patch is inspired to a multilobate contour, derived as a perturbation of a conventional circular patch antennas. The antenna design is suitable for generating Circularly Polarized far-fields, exploiting the mechanism of modal degeneration. Controlling the additional parameter defining the shape of the profile a fine tuning of the central frequency of operation is possible in feasible way.

articleTitle: Assessing the Salt Constituents Characteristics in Aqueous Solutions Using Terahertz Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a viable technique for the precise quantification of various amounts of salts added to distilled water using terahertz (THz) frequency. For this purpose, Fourier transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) system was employed to observe the absorption spectra and characteristics of salts solutions with varying level of salts. In this study, distinct absorption spectra peaks were achieved for different concentrations of salt solutions at certain sensitive THz region. The height of absorption peaks showed a strong correlation with the amount of salt added to the solution reflecting meaningful information about the presence of salts molecules added in distilled water. Through the outcomes of our study, we propose a method through which different minerals and potentially harmful contaminants can be found in water.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized Electromagnetic Energy Harvesting Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a dual-polarized electromagnetic (EM) energy harvesting system that is constructed using concentric bow-tie dipoles and channeling features that make it possible to efficiently combine and transfer the collected power from multiple unit cells. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the strong absorption characteristics of the proposed energy harvesting surface. The scalability of the design is also demonstrated in super cell configurations.

articleTitle: Application of the Inverse Fast Multipole Method to Antenna Array Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The analysis of antenna arrays using the Method of Moments (MoM) is limited by the electrical size due to the high computational cost associated with the MoM. Fast numerical techniques such as H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -matrices with iterative solvers can be used to solve for larger arrays efficiently. However, direct solvers are preferred for array analysis due to the need to solve for many different excitation schemes. The Inverse Fast Multipole Method (IFMM), which provides a direct solution for an H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix formulation, is proposed for antenna array analysis.

articleTitle: A mm-Wave True-Time-Delay Beamformer Architecture based on a Blass Matrix Topology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As fifth generation (5G) wireless communication systems roll out, significant challenges exist towards the design of critical hardware, that is needed in order to realize the performance goals of 5G systems. One such challenge is the development of antenna arrays with multiple beams. This work, proposes the design of a mm-Wave beamforming network based on a modified Blass matrix architecture, which is loaded with appropriately designed cross couplers. The proposed implementation shows a constant time delay in the 27.5-32.5 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Isolation Antenna Array for in-Band Full-Duplex Radios
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this article a wide-band high-isolation antenna with operating frequency of 1.85 -2.55 GHz is presented. This design consist of co-located TX and RX antenna arrays at different angles with absorbing material between them to get the high isolation of -75dB over the fractional bandwidth of 31.8%. This antenna array can be useful for GSM-1900, Wi-Fi, LTE bands and simultaneous transmit and receive applications in several wireless communication bands.

articleTitle: Broadband Millimeter-wave Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the development of a wideband dual-polarized crossed bowtie scanning array for millimeterwave systems, as well as 5G applications. Simulation results of the antenna element and a 1×8 subarray are presented in this paper. The developed antenna element has reflection coefficient less than -10 dB, gain of 7 dBi over the frequency band of 27 to 40 GHz. The 1×8 subarray has a gain of 13 dBi. Measurement results and detail description of the antenna array and feed system will be presented in the conference.

articleTitle: Modeling Radiation Reaction Induced Superradiance in Quantum Dot Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We simulate the collective emission effect known as superradiance in quantum dots ensembles by considering interactions with their classical radiation reaction field. We show that this reaction field emerges from the secondary radiated field via an expansion of the associated time domain Green's function. Incorporating this reaction field in a Maxwell-Bloch simulation, we reproduce characteristic superradiant behavior.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Antenna Surrogates By Domain Confinement and Principal Components
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Data-driven surrogates are convenient tools to reduce the cost of electromagnetic (EM)-based design tasks such as optimization or statistical analysis. However, their construction for the majority of practical antenna structures is a challenging task, primarily due to the curse of dimensionality and nonlinearity of antenna characteristics. This paper proposes a novel technique for reliable antenna modeling in multidimensional spaces over wide ranges of geometry parameters. It involves domain confinement based on pre-optimized reference designs and principal component analysis for dimensionality reduction. Our approach is demonstrated using a dual-band dipole antenna and compared to state-of-the-art approximation methods. The results indicate that accurate surrogates can be set up using small training data sets.

articleTitle: A Scalable Dual LFM Waveform for Unambiguous Localization in Distributed Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Distributed antenna arrays, comprising a set of transceivers wirelessly-coordinated at the level of the RF wavelength, require high-accuracy localization to form beams in arbitrary directions. The phase relationship between the transmitted signals are corrected based on the beamsteering phase and the direction of interest, thus any error in the distance measurement will lead to degraded beamforming gain. Previously, it was shown that a spectrally-sparse two-tone waveform can achieve near-optimal localization accuracy between nodes, but results in ambiguous range measurements that must be accounted for. In this work, we present a novel waveform combining spectral sparsity for high-accuracy localization, modulation for range disambiguation, and time-frequency duplexing to enable scalability for accurate ranging between multiple nodes simultaneously.

articleTitle: Remote Temperature Sensing Based on Battery-Free Harmonic Backscattering
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a battery-free temperature sensor based on a reconfigurable sensing antenna (RSA). Temperature-dependent varactors are loaded on RSA to detect temperature differences. Thus, temperature variations are first converted into capacitance changes of varactors and further into resonant frequency shifts of RSA. A harmonic radar interrogates this sensor by sending a fundamental signal, and then the sensor backscatters a second-harmonic signal with certain frequency shifts. Finally, the radar could decode temperature information based on the frequency shifts remotely with a doubled resolution through harmonic generation. Such an entirely passive temperature sensor is believed to find many potential Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-enabled Reflectarray Antennas for High-power Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metamaterial reflectarray antennas are attractive options for reducing system SWaP (size, weight, and power) compared to conventional reflector antennas. However, it has been a long-held belief that metamaterials are unsuitable for high-power microwave applications due to their strong field enhancement behaviors. Here we demonstrate that, fortunately, this challenge can be overcome by judiciously combining state-of-the-art optimization with intelligent material selection and metamaterial geometry.

articleTitle: Graded Index Dielectric Superstrate for Phased Array Scan Compensation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the use of additively manufactured graded index materials to improve the scan impedance variation of phased arrays. Solvent-based extrusion permits the programmatically controlled printing of chosen material properties with relative permittivity ranging from 2 to 24.5. This low-loss material shows promise for improvement of scan impedance variation for high scan angles in a smaller footprint than discrete layers.

articleTitle: Gain Analysis of In-motion Magnetic Inductive Coupling-based Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) using wearable sensors is becoming widely used in a large range of applications. Magnetic induction-based human activity recognition system (MI-HAR) is a new wearable-based HAR system that captures human motions by variations in the magnetic induction (MI) signals received from transmitter coils placed around the human body. In this work, we focused on the performance analysis of the MI-HAR system using experimental measurements. The main aim of this study is to show the sensitivity of MI signals to spatial translation and rotations of MI coils and verify the capability of the MI-HAR system in detecting relative motion between coils. Moreover, we compare the simulated MI-motion data generated by the MI system model with the data measured by vector network analyzer (VNA).

articleTitle: Wideband aperture coupled patch antenna for Ka-band exploiting the generation of surface waves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The growing demand for mobile data traffic is actually driving the deployment of innovative wireless networks, such as the 5G ones. The mobile satellite communications (Sat-Com-On-The-Move) at Low Earth Orbit (LEO) are meant to play a central role in this context. Innovative low-cost antenna solutions are required for Sat-Com-On-The-Move user terminals in order to bring this technology to the consumer mass-market. Hence, this paper proposes a low-cost wideband aperture coupled patch antenna (ACPA), working in Ka-band (18 - 31 GHz) and fabricated in standard PCB technology. The proposed antenna supports a double linear polarization feature with a simulated broadside realized gain ranging from 2 to 6 dBi in the (19.5 - 31) GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: A Uniplanar $3\times 3$ Nolen Matrix Beamformer with Beam Squint Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a uniplanar 3×3 Nolen matrix is proposed to improve the beam squinting for spatial FFT beamformer. The proposed multiple beam feeding network has three input ports and three output ports, and the signal is divided into three equal magnitudes and features unique progressive phase shifts at its output ports for each input ports excitation. To reduce the variation of progressive phase delay across the frequency band, a group delay compensation approach is proposed to minimize the changes of phase response across the wide operating bandwidth. To prove the concept, a 3 ×3 Nolen matrix with group delay compensation operating at 5.8 GHz is designed, and it shows that the beam squint is reduced for three radiation angels.

articleTitle: 3D Printable Embedded RF Connectors
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Agile design methods are considered for the Additive Manufacturing (AM) of standardized RF connectors. A 3D printed UMCC is presented, the design process is discussed, and fabrication issues are considered.

articleTitle: Investigation of Continuous Tunable Load-Modulated MIMO Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for implementing continuous tunable load-modulated multiple-input multiple-output (LM-MIMO) transmitters is proposed and investigated. A T-type configuration for the loading network is considered for the load modulator (LM) design, in which a closed-form expression for the load values is also derived for arbitrary constellations. The lumped element topology of a continuous tunable LM is also provided. Simulation results show that the proposed continuous tunable LM is able to handle phase modulation on a hypersphere (PMH).

articleTitle: Huygens Source Antenna using Stacked Dielectric Resonators
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an antenna made of two dielectric resonators is proposed to realize a Huygens source in linear polarization. The goal is to design an antenna with a radiation pattern oriented in one half-space without the use of ground plane. The principle relies on the combination of two collocated electric and magnetic dipoles at the center frequency of 2.42 GHz. The optimization of the antenna dimensions is performed with numerical analysis using far-field simulations in ANSYS HFSS. As a result, the antenna achieves a front-to-back ratio of 41 dB.

articleTitle: Multi-Resonance Stacked Patch Antenna for Detection of Elemental Sulfur
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a stacked microstrip antenna with multiple resonance frequencies, the antenna is implemented by introducing slots on the radiating patches and the ground plane. The proposed antenna is used to sense the deposition of elemental sulfur. The sulfur-deposited is considered as a superstrate to the microstrip antenna. The superstrate will cause the antenna reflection coefficient to change, and the resonant frequency to be shifted. By analyzing these changes in the antenna resonance behavior, the presence of sulfur deposition can be identified. HFSS software is used to optimize the antenna design for optimum response.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Circular Polarized Stub-Array Scheme for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel mechanism to produce circularly polarized (CP) waves using low-profile single-layer stub-arrays is proposed. A line delay of 90-degree and a differential feeding network are incorporated into the single-layer antenna design in order to reduce the feeding network complexity into one radiating package. The proposed low-profile structure leads to a gain of 11 dBi within the 60 GHz ISM Band with an adjustable frequency-selective CP radiation.

articleTitle: Optimized NUFFT for 2D array antenna radiation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose an optimized approach for implementing Non-Uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NUFFT) algorithms under a general and new perspective for two-dimensional transformations. A case study of electromagnetic interest is carried out by applying the developed NUFFT to the radiation of a planar irregular array antenna onto a set of regular spectral points.

articleTitle: High-Density Component Integration in Fabrics with Thin Flex Interposers
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Device or component integration in textiles is critical to achieve heterogeneous electronic functions. These functions include sensing, power supply (which includes harvesting, storage, conversion and low-impedance delivery), wireless communication and photonics. Pre-packaged devices or components are fabricated in rigid cases or chips that create several incompatibilities with the textiles in terms of pitch, wiring density, mechanical compliance at interfaces and associated reliability issues. In order to address this challenge, a novel approach is proposed and demonstrated in this paper to enable scalable and reliability electronics integration in textiles. The key innovation to realize this approach is in the embedding of thin chips in flexible interposers, followed by fan-out interconnections to other system components inside the textiles. Chip-on-flex or chip-in-flex are demonstrated with high-density copper semi-additive patterning techniques. The flex terminations are extended into the textiles with flexible silver-elastomer adhesives that are encapsulated with water-resistant elastomers. Initial process demonstration is shown for chip-flex-fabric integration.

articleTitle: Modeling the Effects of Gaseous Absorption and Cloud Attenuation for V-band using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A deep neural network is proposed to study the attenuating effects of the Earth's atmosphere on the W/V-bands of the millimeter wavelength portion of the spectrum. Validation of atmospheric propagation models in the W/V-bands has become an increasingly important subject of communications research, but presents significant hurdles when testing these models due to the great variability in the atmospheric parameters that influence propagation attenuation. The effects of molecular gas resonances and hydrosols become very pronounced due to the short wavelength in these bands. This research employs a multilayered deep learning model to learn and predict the attenuation at V-band frequencies. The data is collected from the ongoing W/V-band Terrestrial Link Experiment (WTLE) in Albuquerque, NM. WTLE uses weather sensors and the received power data across the link to study the effects of atmosphere on V-band propagation.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Beam-Steering Antenna Composed of Metacurl and Metaloop Elements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) antenna is investigated for steering its CP beam at two different frequencies. The antenna is composed of metamaterial curl (metacurl) and metamaterial loop (metaloop) elements. The antenna height is extremely small: approximately 0.01 wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. The metacurl element radiates a CP broadside beam and the metaloop element radiates a CP conical beam. A tilted beam is formed at two different frequencies by exciting both the metacurl and metaloop elements. It is revealed that the tilted beam is moved in the azimuth plane by changing the phase of the excitation voltages for the metacurl and metaloop elements.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized U-Slot Array with High Polarization Purity and Wide Axial Ratio Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circularly polarized antenna array with high-polarization purity and wide axial ratio beamwidth is proposed. The antenna element is a circularly polarized asymmetric U-slot patch. A sequential rotation technique has been implemented that not only improves the circular polarization performance of the array, it also resolves the issue of beam pattern tilt in asymmetric U-slot antenna configurations. The proposed 2 ×2 planar array achieves a gain of 13 dBic with a 54 degree axial ratio beamwidth.

articleTitle: Modulated Reactance Surface Synthesis for Ideal 1-D Leaky-Wave Radiation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Modulated reactance surfaces for ideal 1-D leaky-wave radiation are designed based on complete aperture field synthesis over both propagating and evanescent spectra. For a desired far-zone radiation pattern specified by the visible-region part of the aperture field, the invisible-region part is introduced and optimized such that the total aperture fields render the radiation aperture passive and lossless everywhere. When excited by a surface wave, the resulting modulated reactance surface generates the synthesized near fields and produces the intended far-zone pattern.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Wideband Microwave Absorber with Reactive Screen
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the development of radar technology, reduction of radar cross section (RCS) is becoming more and more important in the electromagnetic field. Microwave absorber is one of main methods to reduce radar cross section. In this work, we propose a novel design of microwave absorber with resistive screen. The equivalent circuit method is implemented in the design and we adjust values of L and C to get a better result. In addition, it has the good performance with total thickness is 0.25λ and it covers the frequency range from 3.4 GHz to 15.85 GHz. Furthermore, the reflection peak reaches -18.2 dB at 14.2 GHz. Finally, we draw a conclusion that the microwave absorber that we proposed is better design.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Continuous Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed a circularly polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with high gain continuously beam steering. As rotatable component, a spherical resonator can adapt its position under the physical movement or the action of gravity, which exploits a continuously wide scanning angle of ± 40° in 2D plane. At the same time, 44% impedance bandwidth and 38% AR bandwidth are achieved. The proposed beam steering antenna provides a novel solution for WLAN base station to effectively cover the indoor users.

articleTitle: PCB edge antennas for mm-wave communications user equipment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an antenna design using the edge plating of a PCB for communications in the 30 GHz band, such as needed for 5G-New Radio. Such antenna structures can be ideally incorporated in existing PCB designs.

articleTitle: On the Design of Circularly Polarized MIMO Antenna with Polarization Diversity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple-topology circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with polarization diversity is presented. The proposed design comprises two parallel placed coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed antennas with the opposite senses of polarization. Circular polarization is induced in the antenna by simple geometrical modification of the conducting coplanar ground planes on the right/left side of the microstrip transmission line. To achieve polarization diversity, the left-hand and right-hand CP is realized by simply switching the positions of the ground plane with respect to the microstrip line monopole. Owing to this configuration, the proposed antenna features a wide impedance bandwidth (|S11| ≤ -10 dB) and axial ratio (AR) bandwidth from 5.2 GHz to 6.3 GHz along with high isolation of |S21| ≤ -20 dB in the entire operating frequency range. The peak realized gain of the antenna is 5.8 dBic, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.004 with the maximum diversity gain (DG) of approximately 9.99 dB.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Control of Two-Way Pattern for Linear Distributed Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A kind of method for suppressing the grating lobes (GLs) of linear distributed array pattern is proposed in this paper. The method combines the linear distributed array structure and the pattern product theorem to obtain a linear distributed array two-way pattern. The Chebyshev window is used to design the weights of the transmit array pattern to achieve ultralow GLs performance. This method reduces the GLs by 29.5 dB, which can effectively suppress the GLs compared with conventional solutions. Simulation analysis results show the feasibility and the effectiveness of the method, which will help to improve the ability of radar detection.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Illusions created using Metasurface Holograms with Finite-Sized Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A methodology to synthesize metasurface holograms to produce desired electromagnetic illusions is presented and demonstrated using a numerical example. The metasurface is described in terms of surface susceptibilities, which are synthesized using Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs), and the scattered-field computation using Boundary Element Method (BEM). The impact of spatial phase discretization on the reconstruction of the fields is further shown using a numerical example of plane-wave scattering from a PEC rectangular object.

articleTitle: An Ultrawideband Unidirectional Bowtie Antenna with Enhanced Radiation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An improved ultrawideband (UWB) Bowtie Antenna (BA) with low profile is presented in this paper. The basic geometry of the proposed antenna is combined by a novel acorn-shaped bent Bowtie patch and a hollowed stepped back cavity. The hybrid utilization of loop circuits and loading techniques that including resistive and capacitive loading can improve the radiation efficiency of the BA while expanding the low-frequency bandwidth. Additionally, a novel technique of cavity groove is proposed to design the reflector. The optimized cavity tightly coupling with the radiation part overcomes the shortcomings of conventional cavity-backed BAs. The simulated −10dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is over 100MHz-1000MHz while the experimental bandwidth is 250MHz-850MHz. This BA of folded type obtains a high realized gain of 5dB at 850MHz. Field tests for practical ground penetrating radar (GPR) application have been carried out and the results demonstrate the advanced performance.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Array Antenna with Element Separations Adjusted to Excitation Distribution
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An amplitude distribution on a linear array antenna can be transformed to element separation distribution. This paper discusses the extension of such a separation-controlled array antenna from one-dimension to two-dimensions We study a two-dimensional array antenna composed of plural linear arrays with radial arrangement. The radiation patterns are compared between the amplitude-and separation-controlled arrays in reference to the equivalent parabola antenna. The dependence on the number of linear arrays is presented.

articleTitle: Broadband Quasi-continuous Metasurface for OAM Generation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The purpose of this study is to generate a broadband high-performance vortex wave. By using the waveguide theory and the grating vectors model, a broadband quasi-continuous metasurface is proposed to generate the l=±2 vortex beams with a measuring mode purity of 0.68 operating from 9 GHz to 19 GHz. In compare with previous designs, this metasurface provide a significant bandwidth improvement with continuous upper surface feature. The measured far-field patterns have a good agreement with those obtained from the simulation. This work offers a useful route of producing high-purity orbital angular momentum waves.

articleTitle: Friendship and Electromagnetics: In Memory of Professors Pedram Mousavi and Mojgan Daneshmand
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper is dedicated to the memory of Professors Pedram Mousavi and Mojgan Daneshmand as well as their two daughters Darya and Dorina who tragically lost their lives on January 8, 2020 when Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 was shot down shortly after takeoff near Tehran, Iran. Despite their young age, Professors Mousavi and Daneshmand were superbly accomplished scholars who had made important contributions to the fields of Electromagnetics, Microwaves, Sensors, and Antennas. More importantly, they have touched and changed the life of many students and scholars by their teaching and research programs. They were beautiful soles who had an even brighter future ahead of them and were on the path of offering far more to the scientific and academic communities. Their tragic death is a significant loss for our community as well as their friends and family. This paper reviews some of their scientific contributions and provides a brief commentary on the cherished friendship of the authors with them.

articleTitle: Single-Cut Antenna Characterization from Near Field Data
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new method providing the partial reconstruction in near-field antenna characterization is presented. Its goal is to determine the optimal near-field sampling distribution required to reconstruct the antenna pattern just along some cuts.

articleTitle: Trapping electromagnetic signals in time modulated and non-linear cavities
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we explore the possibility of trapping electromagentic signals in lossless cavities by using time modulation or nonlinearities. Contrary to other approaches addressing similar questions, our approach is based on slow adiabatic modulation, instead of fast periodic modulation, and works for continuous wave signals, instead of exponentially increasing ones, allowing the efficient trapping of the incident signal for long (ideally infinite) periods of time.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Beam Switching Antenna With Horizontal Parasitic Element Reflector (HPER) for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a novel beam reconfigurable antenna for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), in which beam is reconfigured by controlling Horizontal Parasitic Element Reflector (HPER) arranged around monopole antenna which operates at unmanned aerial frequency (5030-5150 MHz). The proposed method consists of monopole antenna at axis of circular substrate with distributed HPER in the form of bow-tie with pin diode in between which connects both arms. The pin diode that bonded to the center of the HPER used to control the operation of each HPER according to the ON-state and OFF-state of the pin diode. The antenna has directivity elevation in eight directions of 0°, 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°, 225°, 270°, and 315° through the control of HPER using pin diodes. In this method the antenna gains has 4.9 dBi during ON-state of pin diode with efficiency of 100% respectively. This designed antenna applied to UAV with features lightweight and weight balance is centered, simple structure without any complicated equipment such as converter, amplifier, phase shifter, etc and detection applications that require radio convergence.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Limitations for Sequentially Rotated Circularly Polarized Phased Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the effect of sequential rotation on the beam steering capabilities of a circularly polarized phased antenna array is analyzed. Two different topologies for a phased antenna array operating at Ka-band between 28 GHz and 40 GHz are studied where each structure is tailored to produce a maximum gain of almost 19 dB with an axial ratio below 0.5 dB. The individual elements of both topologies are dual fed with a differential phase shift of 90° respectively. This paper proves that the steering capability of a phased antenna array is doubled when sequential rotation is omitted from its feeding network.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Lens Design for Electronically Steered Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metamaterial lens (metalens) is engineered to improve the scanning performance of a dipole array. When placed within the lens, each dipole has an embedded element radiation pattern with a relatively flat top and a much narrower beamwidth than without the lens. This is ideal for an electronically steered array (ESA) with large element spacing, since the narrow beamwidth of the embedded element pattern suppresses grating lobes. When only the permittivity of the lens is optimized, the lens creates a flat-top pattern in only one plane; however, when both the permittivity and permeability are optimized a flat-top embedded pattern in both planes is achievable. Simulated results indicate that for a small square array, the lens enables a directivity increase of 9 dB. Furthermore, grating lobe levels are significantly reduced without increasing scan loss.

articleTitle: Realistic Numerical Modelling for 3-D brain stroke monitoring
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper aims to provide a realistic 3-D modelling framework of a real-world microwave imaging system for brain monitoring that mimics pre-assessment experimental clinical scenarios and lab setups. The model considers an anthropomorphic adult head with multiple tissues, a hemorrhagic brain stroke and a detailed prototype of a modular microwave antennas helmet. The set of antennas detect changes in the permittivity of biological tissues and then imaging reconstruction algorithms generates a 3-D representation of stroke using EM fields and scattering data generated by a full-wave numerical simulation. As results, it is presented a reconstruction of onset stroke in the white matter area of the brain using a TSVD algorithm and the born approximation for imaging.

articleTitle: Efficient Power Amplifiers for Radio Science, Remote Sensing, and Space Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents the development of high efficiency traveling-wave tube power amplifiers at K-band, Ka-band, and Q-band frequencies for radio science, remote sensing, and space communications. The saturated output power of these amplifiers is in the range of 40 to 200 watts and the corresponding efficiency is in the range of 45 to 60%.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Interleaved Multi-Beam Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-band dual-polarized interleaved six-beam base station antenna is proposed for LTE 1800/2600 carrier aggregation applications. It consists of two separate six beam subarrays: low band six beam array working at the frequency band of 1.7-2.4 GHz and high band six beam array working at the frequency band of 2.3-2.7 GHz. Through the asymmetrical non-uniform azimuth and elevation spacing arrangements, the azimuth beam coverage of the proposed dual-band 6/6-beam antenna at low band matches one of the antenna at high band.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Wideband Perforated Semi-cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the development of dielectric resonator antenna, the wideband of dielectric resonator antenna becomes more and more significant. In this paper, a design of wideband perforated semi-cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna is proposed. Cylindrical perforations and edge grounding is used for semi-cylindrical dielectric resonator, by optimizing the size and shape of the perforations, the antenna in this paper achieves a wide impedance bandwidth (5.2 - 8.95 GHz). The simulation results show that the antenna peak gain reaches 7.0 dBi approximately.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Estimate of the Extinction and Phase Matrices of Collections of Metallic Particles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents full-wave estimates of the extinction and phase matrix for random collections of electrically large, metallic particles in two and three dimensions. These objects, which represent the coherent and incoherent parts of the field scattered by random collections of particles in a free space background, are compared to the same results predicted using single scattering theory in both two- and three-dimensional propagation environments. The full-wave methods expand on single scattering, as they correctly treat the effects of both multiple scattering and near-field inter-particle interactions that are assumed to be negligible in the single scattering theory. The results given by the full wave method and those predicted using single scattering theory are found to differ in both the mean and fluctuating components of the scattered field.

articleTitle: Detection of Electric and Magnetic Dipole Moments Using a Three Loop Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Three Loop Antenna Systems (TLASs) enable the measurement of total electromagnetic energy density, including simultaneous electric and magnetic field vectors, and electric and magnetic dipole moments. The small electrical size of the loops makes their characterization and radiative testing very difficult. Here, we investigate the radiative performance of a TLAS through simulations. We compare the system's numerically measured dipole moment against theory for centrally located electric and magnetic dipole moments, and show that the system's field component discrimination is greater than 20dB.

articleTitle: Gone but not Forgotten: Memories of Prof. Mojgan Daneshmand and Prof. Pedram Mousavi
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The author relates fond personal memories of his friends and colleagues of 10 years, Profs. Mojgan Daneshmand and Pedram Mousavi, who, along with their lovely daughters and several other members of the University of Alberta community, were lost in the Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 disaster on January 8, 2020 in Tehran, Iran. They shall not be forgotten.

articleTitle: Numerical Mode Decomposition for the A-Φ Formulation with Inhomogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Compared with the E-H electromagnetic field formula, the A-Φ formula is immune to low-frequency breakdown, which makes it an accurate model over broad frequency range. Besides, the A-Φ formula plays an essential role in the quantization of the EM field and taking other quantum effects into consideration together with EM field. In this paper, the numerical mode decomposition expressions for the A-Φ formula are derived based on the finite element method for inhomogeneous dielectric materials, which can be used as a fast numerical solver for and finding the eigenmodes of the A-Φ formula with inhomogeneous EM background.

articleTitle: A High Frequency Electromagnetic Scattering Algorithm Based on Physical Optics Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Geometric diffraction is based on Keller's principle, and one of its major disadvantages is that it causes caustics point and the field volume is singular. Although the consistent geometric diffraction takes into account the calculation of the shadow area, the influence on the caustic area cannot be ignored. Therefore, a better algorithm is needed to deal with the problem of caustics and its singularity. There are two kinds of frequency approximation algorithms that can effectively solve the caustics problem. One is the physical theory of diffraction (PTD) proposed by Ufimtsev, another solution is the equivalent electromagnetic current algorithm. In the above two algorithms, the equivalent electromagnetic flow method can perform more effectively on calculate the field of the diffraction caustics area. Their common way is use source to make diffraction integration. In 3D calculations, the physical optics (PO) algorithm is based on the integration of surface current or surface magnetic current. The equivalent electromagnetic current method is based on the integration of line current or line magnetic current. For 2D calculation, the equivalent electromagnetic current method does not require integration. PO algorithms are simplified to line integrals.

articleTitle: A Dualband Dielectric Resonator Antenna over a Metasurface with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ahstract-A dualband rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with a circular patch over a metasurface for achieving circularly polarized radiation is proposed. The proposed antenna is comprised of a substrate with ground plane, a rectangular dielectric resonator (DR), a metasurface, a circle patch, and a coaxial probe. The metasurface upon the substrate can realize the circular polarization. The circle patch upon the rectangular DR can increase the reflection coefficient and realize the dual-band working mode. Simulation results show that the proposed DRA has a dual band of operating frequency which is 24.7% (4.23 GHz - 5.42 GHz) and 8.5% (5.60 GHz - 6.10 GHz), respectively. Also, the antenna has a circular polarization in the frequency range 5.60 GHz - 6.10 GHz and it could be widely used for 5G wireless communication. The antenna proposed in this paper has achieved dualband and circular polarization of dielectric resonator antenna simultaneously.

articleTitle: Fast HF Antenna Tuner with a Parasitic Inductor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Synchronously tuning an electrically small antenna at the symbol rate of a frequency shift keyed (FSK) modulation has been shown to efficiently increase the throughput of the transmitter. A major challenge for realizing synchronous antenna tuners is identifying a tuning element that can both block high voltages and retune quickly. This paper explores using a switched, inductive, parasitic tuning element to quickly tune a medium-power HF transmitter.

articleTitle: Double-layered Metamaterial Structure for Chemical Concentration and Strain Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a multifunctional multilayered metamaterial sensor with operating frequency in the range of X-band (8 - 12 GHz) having broad range of applications in field of chemical, biomedical and strain sensing. In the proposed design structure, sensor layer is sandwiched between two resonator structures each composed of four rectangular shaped split ring resonators. Methanol and edible fat solution samples are investigated for concentration sensing. Sensor design showed consistent behavior of decrease in resonant frequency by at least 8 MHz with increase in concentration of methanol and edible fat. In case of strain sensing, resonant frequency decreased by at least 140 MHz with increase in thickness of sample layer.

articleTitle: A Planar Low-Cost Electrically Small Antenna For NB-IoT Sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-cost planar Electrically Small Antenna (ESA) is presented. The ESA is designed for operation at 1.8 GHz which makes it suitable for integration with loT devices that utilize Narrow-Band loT (NB-IoT) protocol. To allow for reliable power reception, a suitable feeding structure is designed with the aid of characteristic modes to excite a magnetic mode leading to a horizontal omnidirectional pattern. The design is realized using the two layers of a commercially available low-cost substrate and is fed using a twin line balanced configuration to mitigate the effects of common-mode radiation. The ESA has ka of 0.47, a realized gain of -0.4 dB and a simulated total efficiency of 60%. It is suitable for integration with circuits to develop a compact communication system for loT sensors without changing the antenna's radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Low profile, Wideband Crossed Dipole Antenna Utilizing Parasitic Helical Arms
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed a crossed dipole antenna with wide axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW), which combines a couple of crossed dipole and four parasitic helical arms (PHAs). In contrast to the previous planar parasitic elements, the PHAs parasitised in vertical contributes a compact size, 0.51×0.51×0.23λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Meanwhile, the PHAs produce three CP modes working with different mechanisms. The simulation shows this work obtains a 57.4% impedance matching bandwidth (IMBW), VSWR≤2: 1.68 GHz - 3.03 GHz, a 51.9% ARBW ranging from 1.85 GHz to 3.07 GHz, and an average gain of about 6 dBic.

articleTitle: A LTCC-based Loaded Dielectric Resonant Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel X-band cylindrical dielectric resonant antenna loaded with dielectric slab designed on LTCC technology is proposed. The antenna is fed by a probe integrated with the dielectric built in the same LTCC stack. The designed antenna operates in the HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub> mode and has a gain of 6.8 dB with the radiation efficiency of 90%. The bandwidth of 18.05% at the resonant frequency is obtained. These properties make this antenna suitable for satellite and terrestrial communications. Furthermore, the use of LTCC technology makes it possible to achieve very high levels of integration with other front-end components.

articleTitle: Scattering of Electromagnetic Plane Waves by a Vertically Stratified Two-Layer Medium
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new integral formulation is introduced to compute the electromagnetic (EM) fields scattered by a vertically stratified half-space. The proposed approach is applied to lossless media illuminated by an electromagnetic plane wave. The computed results are compared with those obtained by the physical optics method.

articleTitle: High Q-factor frequency selective surfaces based on coplanar waveguide transmission line
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we introduce coplanar waveguide transmission line resonators as bandstop frequency selective surfaces, which exhibit very high Q-factors and low passband losses. By simulating the influence of design parameters, we can obtain the bandstop frequency selective surfaces resonating at specific frequency point. Moreover, the calculated sharp transmission response shows its potential applications in the sensing of refractive indices at free space.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Artificial Metamaterial Substrates for Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a design of a linear-to-circular polarization converter based on a 3D printed anisotropic metamaterial substrate (AMS) is presented. The AMS is a stack of thin sheets of PLA material, with air gaps in between, placed over a ground plane. This produces a metamaterial structure composed of periodic anisotropic unit cells, enabling the conversion of a linearly polarised (LP) incident wave to a circular polarised (CP) reflected wave.
