Using the AMS as a substrate, CP antenna applications are proposed operating within the Ku-band reducing the complexity of designing/feeding and fabricating of the primary antenna hence this is particularly important for higher frequencies.

articleTitle: A Rotman Lens Inspired Antenna for Unlicensed 60 GHz Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A monopole antenna inspired from Rotman Lens is presented in this paper. It is designed to operate in the unlicensed 60 GHz millimeter-wave band from 54.318-64.477 GHz. It also has a high gain of 5.25 dBi, suitable for millimeter-wave communication. It has more than 90% of radiation efficiency due to the use of Rogers 5880 low loss substrate. It has dual beam radiation pattern in azimuth plan and back radiations are less than -10 dB. The antennas overall dimensions are 5×4.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, ensuring small form factor. It has a planar structure and along with its other attractive features such as high gain, large bandwidth and dual beam, is deemed quite suitable for future 5G, millimeter-wave communication in the unlicensed 60 GHz band as well as indoor communications.

articleTitle: Artificial Magnetic Conductor key angular stability parameters for improving antenna performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper attempts to reveal the main features that should exhibit an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC), in terms of angular stability, to be optimally combined with an antenna aiming at improving not only the antenna's bandwidth, but also its radiation properties. The paper tries to provide a relation between the antennas radiation properties and the AMCs angular stability, through a study that combines two different AMCs, which exhibit different frequency deviations and stable bandwidths, with a patch based antenna.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz Wideband Array on Low-cost Organic Substrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Further advances in satellite communication and imaging will rely on the implementation of sub-terahertz (sub-THz) systems using flip-chip technology. Recently, low-cost organic substrates have demonstrated stable electric properties over a very large bandwidth making them suitable for sub-THz antennas. In this paper, we present the first ultra-wideband sub-THz antenna array implemented on a low-cost organic multilayer printed circuit board substrate. The array has dual-linear polarization and achieves a 3:1 contiguous impedance bandwidth at broadside with across the entire band. Full-wave simulation of the array demonstrates >80% efficiency across the entire band.

articleTitle: Nested Reduction Algorithm for Generating $\mathcal{H}^{2}$-Matrix Representation of Electrically Large Surface Integral Operators from FMM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we develop a fast algorithm to generate a rank minimized H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix from multi-level FMM to represent electrically large surface integral equations (SIEs). The rank of the new H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix is determined based on prescribed accuracy and is found to be much smaller than the original FMM's rank. The resultant rank-minimized H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix can be used to accelerate both iterative and direct solutions. Numerical experiments on large-scale surface IE-based scattering analysis having millions of unknowns on a single CPU core have demonstrated its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Broadband Dolph-Chebyshev Array Synthesized by Slow-Wave Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband, low sidelobe level (SLL), microstrip array excited with a Dolph-Chebyshev distribution that is implemented with a periodic-stub loaded slow-wave transmission line (SW-TL) feed network is presented. The desired Dolph-Chebyshev excitation of the uniformly spaced microstrip array is achieved simply by modulating the widths of the stubs along the SW-TL feed network. Simulated results demonstrate that the array is low profile, 0.023λ0 in height, has a broad fractional bandwidth, 9.7%, and exhibits SLLs as low as -30dB.

articleTitle: RFID Based Tire Classification Algorithm Using Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio frequency identification (RFID) readers record enormous amounts of data from passive tags located throughout the environment. Due to the large data sets RFID readers collect, machine learning approaches can be used to train robust models. This paper develops an RFID based tire classifier using support vector machines (SVMs). The algorithm correctly identifies all tires in a lab environment and simulations show how the algorithm performs with increased path attenuation.

articleTitle: In-flight Connectivity Analysis Using Ka & Ku-band HTS with Hybrid Compatibility Solution
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a connectivity analysis solution to integrate satellite-based ground gateways with terrestrial networks capable of transmitting Terabit/s of data throughput to fast moving narrow body and wide body planes. Taking into consideration the need for higher bandwidth and lower latency communication, we propose a gateway connection for backhauling traffic through terrestrial base stations. These satellite gateway feeder links will significantly improve overall throughput by utilizing feeder links in parallel with minimal ground network topology alternations. The proposed solution will provide real-time services to LEO, MEO & GEO satellites in connection with In-Flight Connectivity (IFC). This will include all types of managed broadband services on the plane, on-board monitoring, tracking and control services available in a fiber-like connection.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Methodology to Optimize Antenna Isolation in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electronic devices possess very complex environment with many RF and electronic components. Although full-wave simulations are accurate to model the coupling mechanisms in the device, it can be very time-consuming to optimize the antenna designs for high isolation requirements. In this paper, the closed-form formula of coupling between antennas is combined with minimum number of full-wave simulations to provide a very fast and efficient approach to optimize antenna positions and orientations. The proposed approach is applied to an example where two 2.4GHz antennas are to be mounted in a complex environment. The proposed method can predict the antenna isolations with a reasonable amount of accuracy.

articleTitle: 20 GHz-23 GHz Antenna with Tri-State Output Beam-Steering using Fluidic Lens
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fluidically reconfigurable lensed antenna is reported that covers 20 GHz to 23 GHz. The antenna is a modified antipodal Vivaldi antenna element with a fluidically-loaded dielectric lens to facilitate single-element beam-steering for three discrete beam-steering states. The fluid used in this work is ethyl acetate (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=6.0+j0.059, tanδ = 0.35 at 2.4 GHz. The antenna element and lens are fabricated using a substrate with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=3.55 and tanδ = 0.0027. Experimental results show that the antenna can produce up to 30° of beam-steering across the band.

articleTitle: Mesurement and Modeling of Indoor Channel Propagation at 28GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ray tracing method is widely applied to a site-specified radio propagation estimation for wireless applications. In order to better understand the propagation characteristics of millimeter-wave channel, the measurements of millimeter-wave are carried out in indoor environment at 28GHz, this study included a development of state-of-the-art wideband channel sounder. At the same time, the multipath receiving power is simulated and analyzed based on ray tracing method. A good agreement is obtained between the measured results and the simulated results.

articleTitle: A Current and Charge Integral Equation for Dielectric Regions in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Emerging classical and quantum applications require computational electromagnetics methods that can efficiently analyze complex structures over wide bandwidths, including down to very low frequencies. This work begins to address these needs by presenting a type of charge and current integral equation that has been formulated in the time domain and is applicable to dielectric regions. This system introduces charge densities as unknowns in addition to the current densities, resulting in a system that does not exhibit a low frequency breakdown. An appropriate marching-on-in-time discretization scheme is discussed so that stable and accurate results can be achieved down to very low frequencies. Numerical results are shown to verify the accuracy and stability of this formulation.

articleTitle: Magnetic Metamaterial based Wideband Frequency Reconfigurable Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a magnetic metamaterial based wideband frequency reconfigurable antenna is reported. The antenna consists of a rectangular monopole printed on the top face of a gyromagnetic ferrite substrate. Four split-ring resonators (SRR) are optimally printed on the bottom face to realize a wide impedance bandwidth from 2.61 to 4.5 GHz (53.2%). When externally magnetized with H=100 KA/M, the metamaterial antenna demonstrated frequency reconfigurable properties. Commercial software (HFSS) is used to optimize and demonstrate the frequency configurable properties. The radiation pattern of the antenna remained fairly consistent across the operating bandwidths.

articleTitle: Design of A Ku-Band 1-Bit Broadband and Low-Loss Reconfigurable Transmitarray Element
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a Ku-band 1-bit reconfigurable transmitarray element with good performance is presented in this paper. The element is designed based on the Rx-Tx approach. The U-shaped slot patch is the receiving (Rx) structures and the C-shaped probe-fed patch is the transmitting (Tx) structure. By adopting this design, the element results in simple procedure. Two PIN diodes are integrated symmetrically on the C-shaped microstrip line. By turning them ON or OFF simultaneously, the induced current directions are reversed, thus achieving two phase states with 180° phase difference. The low insertion loss of 0.47 dB is achieved by optimizing the position of the diodes. Fullwave simulation results show that the element performance on oblique incidence remains very stable in the desired frequency band. These results verify that the proposed element has good characteristics of broad bandwidth and low insertion loss.

articleTitle: A Polarization Insensitive Frequency Selective Surface for Triband GSM Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article reports on a compact, single layer Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for tri-band GSM shielding applications. The proposed FSS unit cell comprises of three independent elements. The outermost square ring suppresses GSM-900 MHz signals, the innermost annular ring is incorporated in the design to stop GSM-2100 MHz signals and the middle square ring is used to suppress GSM-1800 MHz signals with a -10 dB rejection bandwidth of 600 MHz, 100 MHz, and 250 MHz, respectively. Furthermore, the proposed FSS exhibits a stable frequency response when illuminated by waves at oblique angles of incidence and a polarization insensitive behavior up-to 60°. The proposed FSS unit cell is realized on an FR4 substrate. A finite prototype containing 8 ×7 unit cells with an overall size of 270 ×230 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is also fabricated and tested. A good agreement between the measured and simulated results showed that the proposed FSS can be employed for suppressing unwanted signals in the GSM-900, GSM-1800 and GSM-2100 bands.

articleTitle: An Integrated MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz and Millimeter-Wave Bands for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2-element MIMO antenna is presented for 5G standards covering both the sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave (mm-wave) bands using the same radiating structure. The antenna consists of a five concentric pentagonal slots. For the sub-6 GHz band, the antenna is excited by a single open-end microstrip transmission-line, while eight transmission-lines, connected through T-junction excites the mm-wave band. Designed on a substrate of of size 120×60 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the antenna covers 1.4-1.58 GHz, 1.82-2.14 GHz, 2.48-2.9 GHz, 3.1-3.8 GHz, 4-4.5 GHz and 27.8-28.3 GHz. The antenna not only provides backward compatibility with 4G bands, it also covers the sub-6 GHz 5G bands and 28 GHz bands.

articleTitle: Comparison of RF Cancellation approaches for UWB STAR Radios
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To double spectrum efficiency, a well-known approach is that of using Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) radios. The goal is to suppress the coupling from the transmitter to the receiver, by using the knowledge of the transmitted signal. Successful implementation of STAR requires self-interference cancellation of at least 100 dB across the entire band. Antenna Tx/Rx signal isolation must be very strong to ensure no saturation occurs in the LNA and other components in the Rx chain. In this paper, we present to compare approaches to achieve improved isolation for single and multi-antenna radios across wide bandwidths. Measurements show that a combined 2 stage isolation of > 65 dB can be achieved.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Coexisting Interference between LTE-R and DTTB Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: LTE for Railway (LTE-R) system will be deployed at 450-470MHz in China, which is adjacent to the frequency band of Digital Terrestrial Television Broadcasting (DTTB) system, so the two systems may interfere with each other. To analyze the compatibility and coexistence of LTE-R and DTTB, a measurement system is built in laboratory to measure the influence of coexisting interference on them. Based on the measurement results, we provide the suggestions about separation distance between the transmitters and receivers of the two systems.

articleTitle: 64-Elements mmWave Detachable Phased Array Antenna for 5G 26GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The need for high data transfer rate and low latency for the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Generation (5G) technology in mobile communication has led to millimeter-Wave (mmWave) Phased Array Antenna that can offers high antenna gain and ability in beamforming at different angles. This paper presents a 5G 26GHz Band mmWave Phased Array Antenna with Phase-Shifter Integrated-Circuits (IC) as the RF Front End. The mmWave Phased Array Antenna is made up of 64 antenna elements arranging in an 8×8 rectangular array layout. 16 Phase-Shifter ICs are meant to be distributed in 4×4 rectangular layout, to introduce phase difference to the respective antenna elements in the array antenna, so as to achieve beam-forming to points at different directions. This paper describes the design of the 64-Elements Phased Array Antenna along with its simulated antenna performance and its beamforming characteristics.

articleTitle: Dual-band Slot-Based MIMO Antenna Design with Independent Tuning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a concentric annular slot based dual-band, low-profile frequency reconfigurable (FR) 2-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna design is presented. FR is achieved using two varactor diodes per antenna element. The unique features of the proposed work is its independent and concurrent tuning of each band over a wide frequency range from 1.7~3.5 GHz. The proposed antenna is fabricated using RO-4350 substrate with dimensions 60×120×0.76 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna is a low profile, compact planar structure with dual-bands of operation. The proposed antenna is suitable to be utilized in the current 4G wireless standards as well as for the upcoming 5G with sub 6-GHz bands of operation.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal-Beam Metasurfaces Based on Asymmetric Frequency-Phase Transitions in Time-Modulated Meta-Atoms
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a full-duplex nonreciprocal-beam-steering transmissive phase-gradient metasurface realized by leveraging the unique characteristics of the frequency-phase transition in twin time-modulated meta-atoms. Such a metasurface can provide directive and diverse radiation beams, and steerable beams by simply changing the modulation phase. The proposed twin meta-atoms inherently suppress undesired time harmonics, yielding a high conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: A GPU-Accelerated Hybrid Numerical Method for Modeling Multiscale EM Radiation Problems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a hybrid method (called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{FEM} +\text{DM}$</tex>) for efficient numerical modeling of multiscale electromagnetic (EM) radiation problems that involve thin wire antennas placed near objects. The proposed hybrid method incorporates the Dipole Moment (DM) approach into the Finite Element Method (FEM) in order to circumvent the bottlenecks pertaining to certain computational issues, such as mesh refinement, ill-conditioning, memory overload and long CPU time. The use of dipole moments for handling fine features as well as for modeling mutual interactions, enables us to employ parallelization techniques to accelerate the computation. The hybrid method with GPU computing has been programmed in MATLAB. Numerical results generated by using the proposed technique are presented, and are compared to those obtained from a commercial EM solver.

articleTitle: Laplace-Beltrami Eigenfunctions for the Inverse Source/Design Problems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Laplace-Beltrami operator has a broad breadth and depth of application in the fields of engineering, machine learning, and computer graphics. In particular, the operator's salient feature of defining a spectral method, enabling the manipulation of its eigenfunctions as a basis set, has been driving its popularity in many fields. The eigenfunctions form a basis referred to as the manifold harmonic basis (MHB). MHB are constructed over C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> subdivision surfaces, further enhancing its ability to capture very fine features such as convexity, edges, corners, etc., with relatively few eigenfunctions. MHB proves to be a great candidate for developing the inverse source/design framework due to their natural means of compressing data. We pose a shape optimization problem that aims to find the boundary, in terms of MHs, wherein sources are defined to produce the desired fields constrained. Numerical results are presented for validation.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Dual Band Antenna Using 2D Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel reconfigurable dual band liquid metal antenna on a 2D surface is proposed in this paper. The structure of the proposed antenna comprises a pair of symmetrical T-stubs and an inverted T-stub on a 3D printed substrate. Depending on the fluidity of the liquid eutectic gallium and indium (EGaIn), the proposed antenna allows liquid metal to move on a 2D surface. An electrochemical method generates a DC loop between EGaIn and NaOH solution that is used to transfer a DC signal to the surface of EGaIn. By inducing a changing in the length of EGaIn, this liquid metal antenna offers an ability to accomplish the reconfigurable frequency properties with dual band. The advantages of liquid metal antenna on a 2D surface lie in the continuous tunable frequency band and complicate conductor topology. The propose antenna can accomplish four tunable states with dual band. The first band of frequency reconfigurable range is from 1.06 GHz to 1.18 GHz and the second band is from 2.24 GHz to 2.99 GHz.

articleTitle: Printed Antenna With Pattern Reconfiguration in Both E- and H-Planes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a printed antenna with pattern reconfiguration in both E-plane and H-plane is presented. It consists of five elements which include 4 parasitic elements forming a square shape centered at the driving element. Pattern reconfiguration is achieved by employing the operational principles of Yagi-Uda antenna, in which the positions of the director and reflector are interchanged using electronic switches. The proposed antenna employing eight integrated PIN diodes is designed to radiate in both H-plane (-30°, 0° and 30°) and E-plane (0° and 28°). The antenna resonates at 3.65 GHz with impedance bandwidth and gain of about 7% and 7 dB, respectively, in all switching modes, making the proposed antenna suitable for WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: An Introduction to Impedance Matching Using the Analog Discovery Board
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a simple, yet effective hands-on introduction to impedance matching in the frequency domain using the Digilent Analog Discovery Board. This experiment avoids the need for expensive RF/Microwave test equipment, by using basic low frequency measurement equipment that is common to the typical electrical engineering laboratory (a basic oscilloscope and signal generator setup can also be used). Through this experiment, students observe the importance of impedance matching first-hand, via measurements, and then design and build a basic narrowband lumped LC impedance matching network at low frequency and verify its performance.

articleTitle: Wideband Integrated Quad-Antenna Building Block for 5G 8×8 MIMO Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To increase the integration level of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas for accommodating the size-limited environment in fifth-generation (5G) smartphones, a wideband integrated quad-antenna building block is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the integrated yet decoupled quad-antenna building block is fulfilled by the combination of two wideband decoupling techniques between back-to-back and face-to-face open-slot antennas. For validation, an 8×8 MIMO system, constituted by two sets of quad-antenna building blocks, is simulated, fabricated, and measured. Both the simulated and measured results show that, the 8×8 MIMO system can offer an isolation of better than 10 dB and total efficiency of large than 41.4% across 3.3-5.0 GHz, which is a promising candidate for the future highly-integrated wideband 5G smartphone antennas.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement in Compact MIMO Antenna Using Dual-Stub Loaded Resonator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a compact MIMO antenna using a Stub Loaded Resonator (SLR) providing enhanced isolation between the radiating elements. The compactness is achieved by introducing slots at the edges and inside the patch antenna. The antenna is designed such that the resonant frequency is at 3.48 GHz. The edge to edge separation between the antenna elements is 4.4 mm (0.052λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>). The SLR results in the improvement of the isolation between the radiating elements by 32 dB at the operating resonant frequency. The proposed antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured isolation at the resonant frequency is 48 dB. The measured peak gain at the resonant frequency is 2.34 dBi. The proposed antenna has a compact area of the antenna 0.61λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.38λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> being the free space wavelength at the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: A SIW-based Antenna with Paired Radiating Arms for Q-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An antenna which contains paired radiating arms is proposed in this paper. The antenna utilizes a coupling slot on a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) transmission line for feeding the paired arms. On each radiating arm, a shorting-pin is loaded respectively. Measured results clear that the proposed antenna achieves an bandwidth of 36.6-40.2 GHz and a gain of 7.9 dBi at 38GHz. And thus the antenna is a practical candidate for the fifth generation (5G) millimeter-wave (mmW) wireless applications.

articleTitle: New FMM Identity and MLFMA for Scattering by Large PEC Objects Above Lossy Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new FMM identity for a lossy half-space Green's function is proposed. Then, the proposed formula is applied to a multi-level fast multipole algorithm for the calculation of the electromagnetic scattering by an arbitrarily shaped and perfectly electrical conducting body in the presence of the lossy half space. The simulation is verified with the results of the FEKO.

articleTitle: Dynamic Channel Modeling of WBAN at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the increasing demand of high data rate, the interest of Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) working in millimeter wave (mmWave) band is growing. This paper analyzes the path loss fluctuations of the waist-to-chest, waist-to-knee, waist-to-wrist and waist-to-head links when the human body is walking and running. A path loss model of dynamic channels for WBAN is established at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Metasurface Cavity Redirection Cloaking
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce the concept of metasurface cavity redirection cloaking. After presenting the general concept, we full-wave demonstrate a particular implementation of it, where wave redirection is performed by a bow tie shaped metasurface cavity that cloaks a rhomic region of space.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized High Efficiency Rectifier with Wide Input Power Range for Microwave Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For microwave power transmission technology, improving the efficiency of rectifier can always be the crux of the matter. However, the performance of conventional rectifiers are highly dependent on the input power, and the external structures added together are not convenient for integration. Therefore, in this paper, a miniaturized high efficiency rectifier with wide input power range is proposed. According to the results, over 50% of the efficiency is obtained in a wide range (24.5 dBm and 21.8 dBm for simulated and measured results respectively), where the peak efficiency are 82% and 77% respectively.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode of a 3D Printing Hollow Sphere Antenna Fed by Conformal Wires
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 3D printing technology is promising for fabricating dielectric antennas. In this work, characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is adopted for analyzing 3D printing antennas. A hollow sphere made of low permittivity PLA material is considered for economic reasons but it is not resonant when its diameter equals to a half wavelength. Therefore, it is not efficient to excite those modes. Instead, a conformal wire feeds the hollow sphere. Based on the CMA, its properties such as the resonant frequency, Q factor, and power contributions by the metallic and dielectric parts are investigated. The hollow sphere works as a load to the conformal feed, and it has an optimum thickness. The antenna is resonant at 520 MHz and 350 MHz with different feeding wires.

articleTitle: Efficient Bi-fidelity Gradient-Based Method for Non-Linear Inverse Problems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Solving a non-linear and high-dimensional inverse problem is challenging in computational science and engineering. Sampling-based methods require a large number of model evaluations; gradient-based methods require fewer model evaluations but only find local minima. Multifidelity optimization combines the low-fidelity model and the high-fidelity model to achieve both high accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, we present a bi-fidelity approach to solving non-linear inverse problems. In the bi-fidelity inversion method, the low-fidelity model is used to acquire a good initial guess, and the high-fidelity model is used to locate the global minimum. Combined with a multi-start optimization scheme, the proposed approach significantly increases the possibility of finding the global minimum for nonlinear inverse problems with many local minima. The method is applied to the inversion of electromagnetic well logging data, which is difficult to solve using traditional gradient-based methods. The bi-fidelity method provides promising inversion results and can be easily applied to traditional gradient-based methods.

articleTitle: 3D Propagation Environment Reconstruction for RF Coverage and Capacity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a drone assisted method to perform simplified 3D reconstruction of real-world buildings for Ray Tracing (RT) and wireless system analyses. The efficiency of the method is assessed via the accuracy in predicting the RF coverage and capacity of simple antenna wireless systems in the resultant propagation environment.

articleTitle: A Corrugated SIW Based Slot Antenna for Terahertz Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguide (CSIW) based slot antenna for THz application. A CPW to CSIW transition is realized and the antenna operates around 0.9 THz. The antenna uses Cyclo Olefin Copolymer (COC) as a dielectric material which exhibit a loss tangent of 0.0007 at THz frequencies. The proposed slot antenna has realized gain of 5.9 dB when using Gold. The radiation, as well as total efficiency of the antenna, is around 50% using Gold which increases to 85% with a gain of 7.6 dB by replacing it with Graphene.

articleTitle: Design of 4D Irregular Tiled Arrays Based on Mixed Integer Second Order Cone Programming
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for the design of 4D tiled arrays based on mixed integer second order cone programming (MISOCP) is presented. The method guarantees to simultaneously achieve the maximum directivity and lowest sidelobe level by exploiting the convexity of the problem with respect to the subarray weights and transforming the non-convex clustering problem into a convex one. Numerical simulations show that the reduction of directivity is only 3.77dB with up to 75% reduction in number of transmit/receive (T /R) modules when scanning to 30° for E/H plane as compared with conventional fully-populated Taylor array.

articleTitle: Generation of Mixed Multi-mode Vortex Beam using Uniform Circular Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the generation of mixed multi-mode vortex beams by means of uniform circular array is presented. Vortex beams have desirable characteristics which make them a suitable candidate for many modern applications such as high data rate short-range telecommunications and also for short range high resolution two dimensional imaging.

articleTitle: Beyond Passivity and Reciprocity with Time-Varying Electromagnetic Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Time-varying electromagnetic systems have raised significant interest in recent years, in particular in the context of magnet-free nonreciprocal devices. Here, we discuss our recent progress on the analysis, design and applications of time-varying antennas, guided systems and metasurfaces that can break reciprocity, impart gain, and overcome some limitations of time-invariant systems, such as bandwidth constraints and sensitivity to disorder.

articleTitle: Mesh Partitioning Based Direct Domain Decomposition Methods for FEM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work generalizes the direct domain decomposition method (D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>M) for FEM problems to decompositions automatically generated through mesh partitioning. To avoid direct factorization inefficiencies attributed to interface imbalances (very small/large interfaces) a custom block supernodal LDL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sup> factorization of the auxiliary interface problem is proposed. Preliminary numerical investigations and comparisons with well balanced geometric partitioning based D3M on electrically large problems suggest that the proposed approach remains very competitive in terms of time and memory.

articleTitle: Digital Beamforming and Nulling in Conformal Antennas Using Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conformal antenna arrays are of significant interest for automotive and aerospace applications. Such arrays can be conformed to the surface of vehicles and aircraft while providing minimum impact on aerodynamics. However, the design and analysis of such antenna systems differs from the planar case. Also, beamforming and nulling for curved antenna arrays with directional elements requires modification of the beamforming and nulling algorithms. Here, a linear array of four elements is considered on a curved surface. Instead of using traditional beamforming with phase shifters, software defined radio (SDR) is used. A method is proposed to achieve adaptive beamforming and nulling of the flexible array, by using a SDR platform to feed the antenna array, in various conformed configurations. Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) beamforming is used and adapted to the conformal antenna. Experimental results show good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: IBFD Indoor Self-Interference Channel Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In-Band Full-Duplex (IBFD) systems generate self-interference (SI) that is highly dependent on the environment surrounding each node. The design of various SI mitigation techniques requires an understanding of the potential SI channels that may be encountered in practical scenarios. This paper provides the results of measured multipath SI channels in an indoor location using two dipole antennas that cover many of the proposed fifth-generation new radio (5G NR) bands below 6 GHz, which should help designers better understand SI variation for future IBFD system deployment.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Metasurface for Half-Mirror and QWP Operations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel ultrathin flexible multifunctional metasurface is presented and analyzed. The design comprises of bat shaped metallic patch which is printed on ultrathin flexible polyimide substrate having thickness of 0.06mm. The designed metasurface is achieving half-mirror operation (1:1 beam splitter) in ultrawideband frequency of 9.70-20.27 GHz. The metasurface also achieving twofold operation (simultaneous quarter wave plate (QWP) and half mirror) at two frequency bands of 9.70-10.91 GHz and 19.31-20.27 GHz. The metasurface provides similar response against oblique incidence up to 30°.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Dual Polarized Dielectric Rod Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual polarized dielectric rod antenna for polarization diversity applications at 35 GHz millimeter wave frequencies is proposed. The antenna is printable via a commercial 3D printer resulting in a very low fabrication cost. Two planar transition from microstrip to the rod antenna is proposed to excite the orthogonal modes. Co and cross polarization gain of each modes are 10db and less than 0dB toward end fire. The antennas 3 dB beam-width, radiation efficiency and its 10 dB matching bandwidth are 45 degree, better than 94% and 5 GHz, respectively. low profile, easy and low cost fabrication and good performance make the antenna a good candidate for dual polarization communication in millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Secret sharing holographic encryption with off-axis dual-channel metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Different from traditional metasurface holographic encryption with phase-only encoding technology, we proposed a kind of secret sharing encryption scheme with off-axis dual-channel metasurface. The secret information can be recovered only by decoding and stacking all the off-axis angle channels, while chaotic images could be extracted in single channel decoding process, further improving the information security.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a multimode microwave absorber
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a microwave absorber with tunable absorption frequency is experimentally demonstrated. The equivalent circuit model (ECM) is derived to provide corresponding theoretical analysis and the numerical simulation is conducted for device performance prediction. The experiment results agree excellent with both ECM and numerical simulation. The device demonstrates single, dual and broad band microwave absorption by turning the voltage applied on the PIN diodes of the device.

articleTitle: Contactless and Flangeless Pipe Contact for Standard Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A contactless and flangeless circular waveguide pipe contact made of a bed of pins is proposed. The bed of pins are surrounding a circular waveguide opening from one end to be connected to another circular waveguide of similar structure. The bed of pins surface is making an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) and the smooth pipe covering the pins acting as a perfect electric conductor (PMC). Aligning these openings together and covering them symmetrically with the smooth pipe prevent signal leakage even if no contact is assured. No flange is required for the pipe contact, and it can be used for circular waveguides covering multiple mm-wave frequency bands between 50 and 110 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna Excited on Higher-Order Cylindrical Leaky Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Fabry-Perot cavity antenna constituted by a grounded dielectric slab covered by a partially reflecting surface in the form of a thin periodic metal screen is designed to radiate cylindrical leaky waves of orders 0, ±1, and ±2 at microwave frequencies. A circular phased array of coaxial probes is employed as a feeding structure, optimized by including parasitic metal vias in order to achieve excellent input passive scattering parameters, both in terms of matching and isolation, and thus good values of the active reflection coefficients, at the operating frequency and for all the considered azimuthal orders.

articleTitle: Reduction of the 6 × 6 TD Vector Wave Equation into a 3 × 3 Complex Set on a Single FD Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The six scalar components of the Maxwell's real time domain equations are reduced in this work into two decoupled sets of 3 × 3 complex equations. Each set consolidated the entire information into three new complex field constituents. Contrary to the conventional staggered grid, all field samples reside on a single finite difference grid. The total number of unknowns is thus reduced, and interpolations are eliminated.

articleTitle: Direction Finding Based on Time Modulated Array with Multiple Modulation Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel single channel direction finding method is proposed and verified, based on a two-element time modulated array (TMA). Periodic `ON-OFF' modulation is added to two elements, and the modulation frequency of one element is twice of that of the other one. After the power combiner, the incident direction is estimated by analyzing the phase relationship of generated harmonic components. The proposed method has a simple structure and concise signal processing. An experiment is provided to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Leaky-Wave Antenna with Longitudinal Slots for Millimeter-Wave Security Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A slotted substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with a simple structure for millimeter-wave security applications is proposed. The antenna is embedded in a double-sided copper clad substrate and is manufactured at low cost. The antenna is categorized as a periodic leaky-wave antenna (PLWA). The antenna is designed so that -1st order space harmonic radiates into the backward quadrant. This leads to the achievement of a wide scan angle in a limited bandwidth. The design of the antenna with 100 series radiating slots is demonstrated. The simulated beam scan angle of the designed antenna is 20.4 degrees over the bandwidth from 77 GHz to 81 GHz.

articleTitle: A Physical Patch Model with Topography Effects for GNSS-R Land Applications and DDM Dimulations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we study the wave scattering problem of land surfaces for Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) applications. Because the receivers are in the specular direction, both the coherent waves and the incoherent waves make contributions. The effects of Topography slopes and elevations, in addition to the microwave centimeter roughness, influence the coherent waves. Simulation results for Pr/Pt over the 20km by 20km area near the specular point is compared with other models and found to be smaller than coherent model and larger than incoherent model for small rms heights. The results are also found to be smaller than the physical patch model results with elevation effects only. The delay-doppler maps (DDMs) are simulated based on the patch model.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurface for Airy Beam Generation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Due to its intriguing diffraction-free, self-bending, and self-healing properties, the Airy beam has attracted enormous research interests. An electronically-engineered reflective 1-bit coding metasurface is proposed to generate the Airy beam on a wide frequency range by designing two distinct coding states with opposite reflective phase of 0° and 180° as digital bits of “0” and “1”. Both numerical simulations and experimental measurement are performed at microwave frequencies to verify the Airy beam properties from 9 GHz to 12 GHz.

articleTitle: A Bound on Radial Velocity and Observation Time in Interferometric Angular Velocity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Interferometric radars enable the direct measurement of the angular velocity of moving objects by estimating a frequency shift imparted as objects passing through the interferometer grating lobe pattern. Highly effective when implemented at millimeter-wave frequencies, angular velocity measurements manifest from the time-varying phase shift between widely separated antenna elements. When implemented with a direct-downconversion architecture, the hardware is greatly simplified, however the time-varying phase shift only manifests when a residual frequency shift is present on the scattered signals from radial motion of the targets. When this motion is negligible, the differential phase and thus the interferometric frequency shift fails to manifest. In this work we present a bound on radial velocity and integration time in interferometric radar measurements of angular velocity using direct downconversion architectures.

articleTitle: Fast Computation of RCS of Large Metallic Platforms Covered With RAM: Benchmark with a Metallic Cube at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radar Cross Section of electrically large platforms which are partially coated with RAM is computed by employing a time effective algorithm based on hybridization of Geometrical Optics (GO) and Physical Optics (PO) numerical methods. A benchmark at 94 GHz on a cube with a side length of 5 cm is presented. The RCS of the metallic cube is computed with and without covering a face with a metamaterial absorber with a stable absorption with respect to the incidence angle.

articleTitle: Frequency Tuning of Annular Slot Antenna using Liquid Metal Overlay Line
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A CPW annular slot antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna is loaded by a PDMS microchannel filled with liquid metal to generate a reconfigurable behavior. The operating frequency is controlled by changing the length of the liquid metal load. The antenna operates at 6 GHz without loading effect while it can be tuned from 4.52 to 5.64 GHz (tuning range of 19.9%) by changing the length of the overlay stub.

articleTitle: An 8-Channel RF Coil based on Microstrip Yagi-antenna for 7T Magnetic Resonance Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new RF coil based on microstrip Yagi-antenna for 7T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is presented in this paper. The RF coil element consists of a driver which is a pair of dipoles printed on the dielectric substrate and two reflectors distributed on either sides of the driver. Simulation results show that the proposed 8-channel RF coil array with these elements has high magnetic field intensity and uniform magnetic field distribution in the transverse plane, and can also maintain relatively low specific absorption rate (SAR) in the human body electromagnetic model. In addition, by comparing the RF field distribution of healthy organs and diseased organs, the feasibility of 8-channel RF coil array for human body imaging in MRI system is confirmed.

articleTitle: Beam propagation method for cylindrical waves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a method to calculate the propagation of cylindrical waves in inhomogeneous parallel plate waveguides. Like the beam propagation method, it consists of separating the wave into a known solution for an homogeneous waveguide and an unknown slowly envelope function. The envelope, the field, and the waveguide perturbation are expressed as Fourier series, leading to a system of first-order differential equations that can be solved numerically. The validity of the approach is verified by comparing results with those of full wave simulations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modeling of shielded differential annular Through-Silicon Via Using Artificial Intelligence Technique
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent advancements of artificial intelligence have been inspiring applications in various fields. In this paper, an advanced electromagnetic modeling method of shielded differential annular through-silicon via (SD-ATSV) based on well-known deep learning framework “Tensorflow” is introduced. Physical data including SD-ATSV structures and S parameters are used as training data in multi-layer neural network. Optimized weighting and bias parameters for each layer of the multi-layer neural network are generated, thereby leading to fast electromagnetic modeling engine. The example of a SD-ATSV is demonstrated to validate the accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: An Amplitude Distribution Network in the T/R Module for Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To catch up with the rapid technology changing trend in the smart antenna industry, the modular design approach is inevitable amongst the researchers and manufacturers to maintain their competitiveness in term of cost and technology adoption. In the smart antenna system, the modular approach has gained its popularity, particularly the building block such as transmit and receive (T/R) module which is complex and subjected to upgrade due to its components upgrade and technology improvement over the time. Amplitude Distribution in the beamforming antenna array system is crucial to achieve the optimum antenna radiation performance such as gain, half-power beamwidth (HPBW), side lobe level (SLL) etc. The highly flexible and scalable T/R module with Amplitude distribution network has been proposed, the Amplitude Distribution for the linear array can be easily simulated using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) tools eliminating the needs of going through the complex and time-consuming mathematical analysis approach. The Amplitude Distribution has been simulated using CST tools and the performance was validated using the T/R module with the 4×4 array.

articleTitle: Isolation Metrics for Single-Channel and Multi-Channel Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Isolation is an important characteristic of simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) systems. This paper provides a formal definition for two different isolation metrics and shows that the common electronic isolation metric suffers from several significant limitations: it fails to fully account for all antenna effects and it loses physical meaning when applied to multichannel phased array systems. An alternate metric effective isotropic isolation is valid for both single-channel and multichannel systems and offers a more complete measurement of total system isolation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Dissipative NLTL Soliton Solution Based on KdV Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Hybrid dissipative non-linear transmission line (NLTL) soliton solution based on KdV approximation is analyzed, developed, and validated through simulations and measurements. It is confirmed that the proposed technique is valid for a large class of NLTL structures including capacitive, inductive, and hybrid schemes. The proposed technique is validated by analysis through solitary wave solution in case of dissipative hybrid NLTL.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact CPW Antenna Operating at the 920 MHz ISM/RFID Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an attractive compact design of a small antenna suitable for radio-frequency identification (RFID) and energy harvesting (EH) applications in the UHF band (ultra-high frequency). The proposed antenna is constituted of a nonunifrom radiator fed by co-planar waveguide configuration. The antenna is constructed such that the radiator length is comparable with the wavelength of the electromagnetic wave at the operating frequency. Using this technique reduction in antenna size of equal to 62% with respect to the conventional patch antenna was achieved. The antenna features a simple nonuniform structure and small size of 50×60mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> or 0.153 λo×0.2 λo. It has been fabricated on a low-cost FR4 substrate and the measurements were conducted to validate the practical results with the simulation performances. The antenna performance is slightly shifted to the higher band and it provides an impedance bandwidth of 0.04 MHz (940 - 980 MHz) with reflection coefficient less than 10 dB, which covers all of the ISM band in Japan band (902 - 928 MHz), and Japan RFID band (917 - 923.5 MHz). The design simulation was accomplished using the electromagnetic HFSS software. A good matching results were obtained between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuits for Electric Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 3-element equivalent circuit proposed by Chu [1] is used to simulate regions of the time-harmonic impedance spectrum of an electric dipole (monopole) antenna near 1st and 3rd (short-circuit) resonant frequencies. As an intermediate step toward the creation of an accurate broadband equivalent circuit, a 6-element circuit is created by combining the two 3-element sub-circuits in parallel; the final step is to insert a capacitance at the input to simulate the spectral region near 2nd (open-circuit) resonance. This completes a broadband equivalent circuit. This method of circuit development is illustrated by applying it to a thin, center-driven, electric dipole. Extension of this technique to more practical antennas having significant ohmic loss and near-base capacitance is suggested for future work.

articleTitle: Compact MIMO Slot antenna for UWB Applications with single Notched-band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a compact MIMO slot antenna for UWB applications with single notched band is presented. The proposed antenna has a very compact size 30×30×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. A stepped slot is integrated in the ground plan to obtain an UWB band width. L-shaped slot is integrated near the stepped slot to create notched band. Acceptable results are obtained in terms of mutual coupling and ECC between the antenna elements. The radiation pattern is omnidirectional for H-Plan and bidirectional for E-Plan.

articleTitle: Ultra-Broadband 3-D Absorptive Frequency-Selective Transmission Structure Using Commercial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an absorptive frequency-selective transmission structure (AFST) with two-sided absorption bands and free of lumped elements is presented for the first time. The proposed design of AFST structure is realized by integrating commercial absorbers with bandpass and bandstop frequency-selective structures (FSSs) to produce a transmission band within a wide absorption band. An AFST prototype is designed and then fabricated. It is shown through the measurement that less than 0.8 dB insertion loss is obtained at 10 GHz with 12.8% bandwidth. Under the normal incidence, 10 dB reflection reduction is realized with 161.4% fractional bandwidth. A good agreement between simulation and measurement verifies the design concept.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing Driven ANN Propagation Models for Indoor Environments at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ray-tracing is widely used for radio propagation modeling of indoor environments, such as hallways and offices. Shooting and bouncing ray-tracing methods are faster than fullwave methods in such environments, especially as the frequency of operation increases following the new 5G specifications. Still, a machine learning approach can generalize a few ray-traced points into full signal strength maps of arbitrary resolution. In this paper, a feedforward standard artificial neural network is trained by ray-tracing data at 28 GHz to predict signal strength in a Γ -shaped corridor. The network's accuracy in reconstructing the actual signal levels is on par with that of the ray-tracer.

articleTitle: Limitations of aperture antenna theory for accurate transient field calculation in the time domain
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the research of an electromagnetic (EM) field in the time domain emitted by a planar circular aperture is presented. Numerical modeling and analytical calculation of EM realizations at specific points inside and outside of the spotlight beam are carried out using the finite integration technique (FIT) method and the analytical method of calculating impulse response function (IRF) of the aperture. It is shown that the analytical method of calculating impulse response function can provide adequate estimation of an aperture antenna EM field while emitting ultra-wideband (UWB) signal. The criterion for the applying region of the analytical method with an accuracy of less than 1% is obtained.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized Stacked Reflectarray Antenna with Changing Beam-direction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent studies have proposed a multi-beam system that requires fewer mirror surfaces. This is made possible by sharing V and H polarized waves, which is one of the unique properties of a reflectarray antenna, in a single mirror surface. In this study, we used five line elements as in previous studies; however, we examined a reflectarray that radiates beams in different directions depending on V and H polarization using three line elements. It was found that separating the elements into two layers allows independent phase control and, as a result, beams can be radiated in different directions for each polarization.

articleTitle: Metasurface Specular Isolator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a metasurface specular isolator. This device leverages nonreciprocal normal susceptibilities to produce an angularly asymmetric reflection coefficient. We demonstrate a transistor-based metasurface implementation with the desired response as a proof of concept.

articleTitle: Polarization and Bandwidth Reconfigurable Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A polarization and frequency reconfigurable dielectric resonator antenna with two-port probe feed is proposed. This antenna is made up of a rectangular dielectric resonator, two probes, a Wilkinson equal power divider and three pairs of adjustable phase shifters using electric switches. By controlling the on-off states of different shifters, polarization and frequency reconfigurable performance is achieved. When the phase difference of the two feed path is 90 degree, left-hand and right-hand circularly polarized characteristics are obtained with same wide impedance and axial ratio bandwidth for the structural symmetry. When the feed paths are equal or have 180 degree phase shift, linearly polarized characteristics are obtained. For the antenna operated at linearly polarized states, bandwidth reconfigurable characteristic is achieved for the different lengths of feed path. The presented work is suitable for multi-polarization and multi-frequency systems.

articleTitle: Global Optimization of Sparse Pencil Beams with Constrained Dynamic Range Ratio
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Array pattern with reduced dynamic range ratio (DRR) of excitation coefficients simplifies the design of array's feeding network. However, constraining DRR pushes small coefficients towards higher values, which might not be optimal from the array-pattern point-of-view. Better results are expected by setting these coefficients to zero, what leads to a sparse design. In this paper, we present a method for global optimization of sparse linear pencil beams with constrained DRR. The method is suitable for calculating coefficients for the hardware at hand whose feeding network supports specified DRR and allows disabling of the antenna elements.

articleTitle: A Novel Single-layer Microstrip Antenna with Tilted Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-layer millimeter-wave (MMW) antenna with tilted beam characteristic is presented. The proposed antenna has a bandwidth of 5.6% (27.75-29.35 GHz) with the center frequency of 28.5 GHz, which makes it suitable to be used in 5G systems. The proposed microstrip antenna has a compact size of 15×14.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A tilted beam of 45° and an antenna gain of 8.75 dBi are achieved at the frequency of 28 GHz. The proposed antenna is suitable for applications where the antenna needs to be installed on an inclined surface.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Performance FSS-AMC Radome Unit
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-performance frequency selective surface and artificial magnetic conductor (FSS-AMC) radome unit is investigated. Composed of a double-layer miniaturized bandpass FSS unit and a single-layer AMC unit, it can achieve high-efficiency wideband transmission and have a great potential application in wideband RCS reduction (RCSR). The bottom FSS structure can achieve a wide flat in-band frequency response and fast roll-offs with a simulated -1 dB passband ranging from 4.1 GHz to 5.4 GHz (relative bandwidth 27.4%). In addition, the double-layer FSS has a total reflection characteristic from 7 GHz to 18 GHz, which indicates that it can be used as the ground plane of the top AMC unit. Two types of AMC units possessing 0 and π reflection phase respectively are designed, which proves that the proposed FSS-AMC units can be used in antenna RCSR field once they were formed into a chessboard structure.

articleTitle: Coherent jamming method for wideband radar with time modulated technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel coherent jamming method with time modulated technology against wideband linear frequency modulation (LFM) radar is proposed in this paper. With periodic modulation of radio frequency switches, the received radar signal can be modulated as the summation of multiple harmonic components with the same LFM slope, and these harmonic components can be transmitted as the jamming signal. By properly setting the modulated frequency, the jamming signal generated by the time modulation can form multiple verisimilar false targets when received and processed by the victim radar receiver due to the harmonics' independence in the time-frequency domain. Assuming that the pulse compression technology is used by the victim radar, the closed-form expression of the jamming processing is derived. Numerical simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed jamming method.

articleTitle: Double-OAM-mode Generation by Octagonal Microstrip Ring Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a double-mode orbital angular momentum (OAM) antenna is proposed. By using an octagonal microstrip ring antenna with a matched load can generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams with different OAM modes at the same frequencies. When the inner ring is fed, this antenna can generate an OAM mode of l=1 at 5GHz. Similarly, when the outer ring is fed, vortex waves with l=2 can be generated. Because of its low profile and small size, this antenna is more potential in wireless communication, mobile devices, remote sensing and so on.

articleTitle: Highly Flexible and Conformal 2×2 Antenna Array on RTV Silicone for the 2.4 GHz ISM band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A highly flexible and conformal 2×2 antenna array on room temperature vulcanized (RTV) silicone is presented. The patches are realized in the top layer consisting of copper clad polyimide. Three different ground planes (copper clad polyimide, copper mesh, and conductive polymer) were realized to determine their flexibility, conformability, and impact on RF performance. The reflection coefficient, boresight antenna gain, and radiation pattern are presented and compared with a reference antenna array on RTV silicone with copper clad polyimide for the top layer and ground plane. To prove its flexibility and conformability, a flat case and two curved cases are considered. The reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, and antenna gain are not very significantly affected when the antenna arrays are conformed.

articleTitle: A K/Ka Dual-band Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS) Antenna Array With Sidelobe Suppression
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel parallel-plate waveguide (PPW) continuous transverse stub (CTS) antenna array with high gain and low-sidelobe performances is presented for K/Ka dual-band applications. The array comprises 32 radiation slots and is fed by a 32-way unequal-feed network with a cosine magnitude distribution. Experimental results show that antenna gains of more than 36.3 dBi and 40.4 dBi are achieved in K-band and Ka-band, respectively. The sidelobe levels (SLLs) are below -20 dB in both E-plane and H-plane at these two frequency bands.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive Meta-Radome with Wide-Angle Matching at Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An improved uniaxial magneto-electric metamaterial matching layer is discussed in order to construct a reflectionless radome structure at millimeter-waves. To obtain a millimeter-wave (mm-wave) physically robust radome with a minimized reflection for oblique scanning angles, a pair of uniaxial meta material matching layers is applied, sandwiching a relatively thick dielectric slab. The extracted uniaxial layer permittivity and permeability tensors are adjusted to synthesize a realizable cell geometry exhibiting maximum scan angle coverage. The resulting radome structure works for both TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: Tightly Coupled Dipole Array for 5G Multi-band Cellular Base Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we study the application of Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) to support multi-band cellular base stations. The benefits of TCDA to such applications and some system concepts to enable such applications are discussed. The design is carried out and simulated fully in Ansys HFSS software. Its performance is examined against the requirements of cellular base station antennas and found to be promising. This design is capable of supporting 700MHz, 1.7GHz, and 2.6GHz bands simultaneously with ±60° scanning in the diagonal plane (D-plane). A physical prototype is being built and the measurement results are to be disclosed at the conference.

articleTitle: 1D & 2D W-band Frequency Scanning Metamaterial Antenna and Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 1D & 2D W-band frequency scanning metamaterial antenna and array are proposed in this paper. Unlike the traditional microstrip-based design [1], we hereby highlight a relatively lower cost/loss antenna solution to the W-band beam steering application using stripline-based composite right/left handed (CRLH) leaky wave antenna (LWA). Our proposed passive CRLH LWA element is able to deliver positive, zero, and negative phase progression from 76 GHz to 81 GHz, thereby ensuring the backward (-28°) to forward (23°) fan beam frequency scanning when CRLH unit cells are periodically cascaded to form a 1D CRLH LWA. To further broaden the frequency mapping range to the hemisphere, we have also realized a 2D CRLH LWA that can produce highly directive pencil-beam radiation patterns. A coverage area of about -10° to 10° by -28° to 23° in elevation angle along the two orthogonal planes with a maximum gain of 26.1 dBi is realized by the proposed 2D CRLH LWA. In-depth analysis and simulated validation of both 1D/2D designs in this paper confirm the aforementioned functionalities.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Wideband Butler Matrix and Rotman Lens Beamforming Network for Millimeterwave Applications at Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates two low-cost beamforming network approach for millimeter-wave and 5 G applications at frequency band of 27 to 40 GHz. As a result, an 8×8 Butler matrix and an 8×8 Rotman lens are developed. Both beamforming network have similar physical sizes and have return loss less than -10 dB. In comparison with the Butler matrix, the Rotman lens has better and more stable insertion loss, it also has less deviation in the phase shift in between the output ports. Prototype of the beamforming networks are fabricated. Experimental validation results together with further comparisons such as array factor and scanning angles will be presented in the conference.

articleTitle: Single Module UHF & ISM Rectennas for MIMO Energy Harvesting or SWIPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present the implementation of two rectennas, on the same planar module, one in the UHF frequency band and the second one in the ISM frequency band. The two MIMO antennas were designed considering the expected mutual coupling effect and based on good design practices the mutual coupling was suppressed. The presented radiation patterns and the estimated antenna gains indicate the good isolation between the two radiators. Two voltage coupler topologies were implemented, one for each radiator and their integration with the MIMO antennas resulted in the two rectennas which divert the rectified voltage on two different loads. The presented rectennas can be used for MIMO energy harvesting systems or Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer Systems - SWIPT.

articleTitle: Inversion Theory and SSTDR Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: It is the purpose of this paper to explore the viability of spread spectrum time domain reflectometry (SSTDR) to be used as an electrical system analyzer for complex impedance. The ability to extract the complex impedance of any generalized load using only the incident and reflected SSTDR signals would allow the SSTDR to be employed on a wide range of electrical applications, and greatly aid in troubleshooting active electrical systems without the need of removing the system from service.

articleTitle: Low-Cost PUMA Array on a BGA Package
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-cost Planar Ultra-wideband Modular Antenna (PUMA) array on a ball grid array (BGA) package is proposed. The PUMA array has been designed to operate with 7.25-31GHz instantaneous bandwidth and at wide scan angles. This array-on-package uses non-collapsible solder balls to further enhance the modularity of PUMA and meets low-cost organic PCB fabrication design rules. Infinite array simulation results that include the BGA transition predicted broadside VSWR <; 2 and less than 2.7 at θ = 45° in E- and H-planes, while maintaining cross polarization isolation levels better than 10 dB out to θ = 45° in all diagonal planes.

articleTitle: Cloaking and Decoupling of Interleaved Microstrip Monopole Arrays at 28 GHz and 39 GHz Using Elliptical Metasurfaces for 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two tightly spaced, interleaved microstrip monopole antenna arrays operating at microwave frequencies are decoupled by employing mantle cloaking method. We use elliptical metasurfaces specifically tailored for the cross-coupled elements of the distinct arrays and show that by wrapping each antenna element with the metasurface cloak, the undesired cross-coupling between the elements at frequencies 28 GHz and 39 GHz is eliminated, restoring their radiation patterns as if the arrays were isolated from each other. In this paper, the cloaking and decoupling effect is scrutinized and evaluated to improve the functionality of the coupled arrays in terms of their radiation patterns and realized gain, when all the antenna elements are excited simultaneously. Consequently, the monopole antenna arrays, even though placed in close proximity, can radiate independently for a wide range of beam scanning angles.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Wideband Antenna with High Gain and Efficiency for 5G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband antenna for fifth generation (5G) wireless communication application is proposed.
