The antenna is designed on a FR4 substrate whose size is 6 mm ×4 mm×0.5 mm and is composed of sector patch arms, a microstrip gradient balun line, a microstrip transmission line, and a substrate layer. The parameters are adjusted and optimized according to the simulation results. By adjusting their shapes and sizes, the operating frequency range of the proposed antenna is from 26.32 GHz to 37.30 GHz, which is within the working frequency band of 5G wireless communication. Also, the antenna has a resonant frequency at 28 GHz with a high efficiency of 86.39% and its realized gain is up to 4.92 dBi. This antenna has the advantages of small size, high gain, high efficiency, and wide frequency band, and is very suitable for 5G wireless communication.

articleTitle: 3D Metal Printed Polarization Reconfigurable Horn Antenna with Solid & Meshed Structures: Future works for SATCOM applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Future SATCOM terminals need highly accurate phased array antennas. However, with higher frequency and smaller antenna sizes there are few challenges when using typical patch antennas. For instance, in K, Ka and Q band the small sized feeding topologies and antenna structure can suffer from variation due to manufacturing and material tolerances. For beam steering this may affect the final beam position and its gain value. For GEO this could be more crucial due to limited power margins. Increasingly, highly accurate (accurate to microns) and repeatable 3D metal printing technology is gaining attentions for producing horn antennas for mm wave Satcom operations. Horns are bigger than the standard half wavelength patches. Due to this they have lesser structural variation and reproduction error. This aspect could guarantee the array beam performance under fixed excitation conditions. In this paper, using a 3D metal (titanium) printing technology, a K and Ka band polarization reconfigurable horn antenna is fabricated. The 3D printed antenna prototype results are validated with simulation results. Further, to minimize the antenna weight while maintaining its performance, a 3D printed horn antenna with a meshed structure is also proposed in this work.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Distributed Conformal Phased Array Antenna with Hemispherical Beam Coverage
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel low-profile distributed conformal phased array antenna (DCPAA) with hemispherical beam coverage is presented in this paper. All conventional spherical phased array antennas (SPAAs) have large beam coverage but high profile because of their spherical carrier. In this design, the proposed low-profile DCPAA is reconfigured by readjusting positions and directions of some antenna elements on the conventional SPAA symmetrically. Elements in distributed areas of the DCPAA cooperate to realize the distributed virtual aperture synthesis. In this case, the low-profile DCPAA can roughly keep the original effective radiation aperture of the SPAA and their performances are almost the same. Thus, the profile of the proposed DCPAA is 44.45% lower than that of the SPAA. In addition, the gain flatness of the low-profile DCPAA is as same as that of the SPAA (1.3 dB) within hemispherical beam coverage. Moreover, the DCPAA has only 0.5 dB gain loss within the scanning range compared with the SPAA.

articleTitle: Circular Polarization Antenna with Elliptic Stripline Resonators on Glass Epoxy Substrates
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a X-band circular polarization antenna with elliptic stripline resonators on glass epoxy substrates. An elliptic antenna provides high efficiency to microwave energy transmission. Glass epoxy substrate provides reduced fabrication cost compared to conventional Teflon substrates. Wideband directive gain 16.5 dB and 1dB axial ratio in bandwidth 10 % by the array of 16 antennas. The directive gain became lower by dielectric loss of the glass epoxy substrate compared to Teflon.

articleTitle: Estimation of Real Ground Effect in Absorber-Based Automotive Measurements: Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Testing of antennas installed on vehicles are typically performed in large spherical near field systems truncated at or close to the horizon. The spherical scanning surface is usually terminated to a floor covered by absorbing material or to a conductive ground. The two scenarios are considered to either emulate a free-space or a perfect electric conductor (PEC) environment, respectively. The behavior of the vehicle antenna over realistic grounds, such as asphalts and soil, is often a desired information. It has been shown in previous publications that the realistic ground information can be estimated by post-processing using image theory in the post-processing on the free-space response of the vehicle. This technique has been implemented in the AnyGround post-processing tool. In this paper, AnyGround is validated by experimental investigation using scaled automotive measurement scenarios. As AnyGround is an approximation, the limitations and applicability parameters of the methods and the achievable accuracy is investigated.

articleTitle: On Microwave Imaging with Absorbing Metasurface Enclosure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Matching fluids used in microwave imaging are often lossy to reduce the reflections from the system enclosure. To enable the use of low-loss matching fluids, we investigate the use of absorbing metasurfaces as the enclosure. This has the potential to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio of the data, thus, enhancing the achievable image accuracy. The presented example has the following limitation: as opposed to design and simulation of the physical structure of the metasurface enclosure, it uses two impedance boundary conditions on top of a metallic-backed substrate. Thus, the angular dependency of a practical absorber is not completely taken into account by this model. At the conference, we'll also consider a microwave imaging metasurface enclosure via design and simulation of a physical structure.

articleTitle: Broadside Radiation Problem in Leaky Wave Antennas: A Metasurface Perspective
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The conditions for broadside radiation with no open stop-band are derived using a field based metasurface model of a general leaky-wave antenna (LWA). Using the Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs), the unique set of surface susceptibilities describing the metasurface to enable broadside radiation is obtained and it is found that the LWA must exhibit orthogonal electric and magnetic field dipole moments forming a Huygens' source configuration. The susceptibilities must further be lossy and satisfy a unique amplitude and phase relationship between the two.

articleTitle: Experimental Validations of Characteristic Mode Analysis Predictions Using GTEM Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Numerous simulations and measurements are typically required to quantify the electromagnetic interference statistics of a device due to radiation at different angles of incidence, polarization, and frequency. Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) has the potential to reduce the number of necessary measurements and simulations by revealing the device's modal behavior, which allows the prediction of the variations in the interfering current. In this work, we describe an experimental setup to verify the CMA predictions of the coupling and interfering current to different devices. The experimental setup involves placing the device inside a GTEM cell to emulate far-field excitation. The currents coupled to different devices are compared with the CMA predictions and excellent agreement is achieved. This experimental verification demonstrates the versatility of CMA for electromagnetic compatibility and interference applications.

articleTitle: Planar Reactively Loaded Array Antenna With Flat-Top Radiation Pattern Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel antenna array structure featuring a flat-top symmetric two-dimensional radiation pattern. The radiating structure consists of an active antenna surrounded by reactively loading elements. The flat-top radiation pattern is achieved by properly tuning the reactive loads, which are realized as metal waveguides filled with a homogeneous dielectric material and terminated on a short circuit. The reactance of the parasitic elements is modulated by controlling the length of the waveguides. An antenna array with 11×11 radiating elements has been designed and analyzed. The optimized structure exhibits a [-25°; 25°] flat-top radiation pattern, supports two polarizations, and is inherently matched.

articleTitle: Design Properties of a 26 GHz Circularly Polarized Square Patch Antenna With Rectangular Slot
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A square microstrip patch antenna with a diagonally symmetric rectangular slot is edge-fed with a 50 Ω microstrip line and designed to produce RHCP at 26 GHz. Rectangular slots with lengths from 1.1 mm to 1.7 mm and widths from 0.05 mm to 0.30 mm are considered. Increasing the size of the rectangular slot perimeter improves the impedance match between patch and feed line while reducing resonant frequency. Larger slots are shown to damage the axial ratio. A compromise slot size of 1.4 mm ×0.20 mm is suggested with best axial ratio frequency at 24.6 GHz., a minimum axial ratio of 1.27 dB, and S11=-6. 53 dB at 24.68 GHz. This optimized patch element is designed for use in a N×N array for satellite communication.

articleTitle: Enhanced Isolation of MIMO Slot Antenna Array Employing Modified EBG Structure and Rake-Shaped Slots
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a novel MIMO slot antenna array with enhanced isolation. Two wideband decoupling structures consisting of modified electromagnetic band gap (M-EBG) structures and rake-shaped slots are employed to achieve isolation improvement of up to 40 dB throughout the impedance wide bandwidth of the antenna (i.e., 4.4-6.3 GHz). The radiation patterns of the antenna are observed to be consistent after the isolation enhancement. Thus, this wideband MIMO antenna with an impedance bandwidth of 36% is suitable for miniature wireless handheld devices.

articleTitle: A Slotted Waveguide Antenna Array for High-power Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A slotted waveguide antenna array (SWAA) has been optimized for high power microwave (HPM) applications in the L-band. Through the use of global optimization, the dimensions of the feed layer and radiating slots were fine-tuned to minimize S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and electric field enhancement, while maintaining high directivity. The radiating slots are encapsulated in dielectric, minimizing the electric field magnitude in air, while allowing the SWAA to be pressurized to further improve power handling capability.

articleTitle: Closely Spaced Dual-band Quad-Element Compact MIMO Antenna with Polarization and Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a dual-band compact quad-element MIMO antenna design with pattern and polarization diversity. The compactness is achieved by considering an H shaped antenna element. The H-shaped antenna resonates at 3.525 GHz operating frequency. Two slots are incorporated at two wings of the H-shaped antenna to achieve dual-band operation. Thus, the slots provide a second resonant frequency at 4.82 GHz. The four elements are separated edge-to-edge by 0.046λ0 (where λ0 is the free-space wavelength at 3.525 GHz) and placed orthogonally to get diversity performance. The isolating networks are introduced between the elements, which provide enhanced isolation of 9.6 dB and 4 dB at lower and upper frequencies of operation respectively. The proposed antenna is fabricated and measured. The measured isolation at lower and upper bands is 16.5 dB and 16.4 dB respectively. The measured peak gains at the respective frequencies are 1.91 dB, -0.354 dB. The proposed antenna has a compact 2D profile having a total footprint of the antenna 0.42λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.42λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.0296λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Near-Field Meta-Steering
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reviews the recent advances in Near-Field Meta-Steering (NFMS). In this relatively new low-profile tilt-free antenna beam-steering method, beam steering is achieved by independently rotating a pair of metasurfaces that are placed in very close proximity to a high-gain antenna aperture, obviously very much in the near-field region. Many advantages of this low-cost method have been identified and independently verified by different groups. Recent advances since its seminal paper published in 2017 include methods to minimize grating lobes that may occur during beam steering, realization of high-power microwave systems with beam steering, demonstration of the steering of dual-polarized beams for satellite communications and development of an accurate phase method to substantially reduce the error in analytically predicting the beam direction (azimuth and elevation angles) when metasurfaces are rotated independently, especially at large elevation angles.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Wide Bandwidth Printed Quasi-Yagi Antenna with Semi-Elliptical Monopole Driver
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new configuration of printed quasi-Yagi antenna fed by semi-elliptical monopole for ultra-wide bandwidth. The elements of PQYA are modified using a semielliptical monopole as a driven element, a half bow-tie shaped truncated ground reflector, and elliptical director elements. Consequently, the operating band of 1.65-6 GHz is achieved with a simple feed structure. The proposed PQYA possesses not only the advantage of 114% ultra-wide bandwidth but also a compact size of 55 × 55 × 1.6 mm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. The prototype is fabricated on a low-cost FR4 substrate and tested. The measurement results show that it has a peak gain of 6.9 dBi and a stable end-fire radiation pattern over entire impedance bandwidth with the front-to-back ratio, and cross-polarization levels better than 9.2 dB and 20 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband Phase Switched Screen based on Tunable Artificial Magnetic Conductor Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The phase switched screen for cloaking is realized by periodically control two working states of the screen, i.e. inphase reflection and out-of-phase reflection, and therefore the ideal phase difference between the two states is π. In this paper, it is proved that, the effective phase difference between the two states might be in a range other than a single value; based on this finding, a new technique of enhancing the bandwidth of the phase switched screen (PSS) is proposed. The wideband PSS is consist of a tunable artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) and a biasing network controlled by periodical switch sequence, while the tunable electromagnetic band gaps are realized through varactors. By controlling the voltage of the varactors properly, the in-phase reflection frequency of the AMC can be tuned from 2.15GHz to 3.23GHz, and the phase differences between adjacent states are all fit in the effective phase difference range, and hence a broadband phase switched screen is realized. Based on a new proposed AMC structure, we finally realize a phase switched screen with the relative bandwidth of over 40%.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of a Tunable Coplanar Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the optimization of the design of a tunable coplanar patch antenna and results thereof are presented and discussed. The design optimizations resulted in a coplanar patch antenna that could be tuned over a range of 240 MHz (1.79-2.03 GHz) for a minimum return loss of 10 dB. The antenna has an Omni-directional radiation pattern and the gain is nearly constant over the tuning range with an average value of 2.2dB.

articleTitle: Air-Filled Substrate Integrated Waveguide (AFSIW) Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cavity-backed slot antenna based on air-filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) with the technology of multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) is proposed for the 5th generation (5G) mobile communication system at 28 GHz for the first time. The whole antenna is made of five layers and its size is 10 mm ×9 mm. The top and bottom layers are Rogers RT6002 and the medium layer is based on an air-filled substrate integrated waveguide. According to simulation results, compared with the antenna which has the same structure but based on a substrate integrated waveguide (DFSIW), the antenna proposed in this paper increases the gain by 5.8 dB (4.8 dB), the total efficiency by 92.0% (69.7%) and the bandwidth by 990 MHz (207 MHz).

articleTitle: A Single-Source Surface Impedance Formulation for Modeling Arbitrary Penetrable Media
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel single-source surface integral formulation is proposed for efficient modeling of penetrable media, without the need for dual basis functions. The differential current density concept is leveraged to yield a well conditioned system matrix. The new formulation leads to significantly reduced GMRES iterations compared to existing single-source formulations, over a broad range of frequency and material parameters.

articleTitle: Overview of Some mm-Wave Antenna Designs Embedded in Metal Exteriors of Cellular Phones
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The overview of some mm-Wave antenna designs embedded in metal exteriors of cellular phones presents an evolution from the 5th generation mobile communications (5G) single-band single-polarized mm-Wave antennas, dual-band single-polarized mm-Wave antennas, dual-band single-polarized mm-Wave antennas in a non-mm-Wave antenna, dual-band dual-polarized mm-Wave antennas, dual-band dual-polarized mm-Wave antennas in a non-mm-Wave antenna, wideband dual-polarized mm-Wave antennas in a non-mm-Wave antenna, to 60-GHz single-band single-polarized mm-Wave antennas in a non-mm-Wave antenna.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Compact Eco-friendly Textile Antenna for IoT: Zigbee Application Example
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new ultra-thin compact eco-friendly textile antenna for IoT applications in the 2.45GHz band is presented. Comparison with common substrate and with state of the art on IoT antennas and using a Zigbee based range test is shown.

articleTitle: Inductively Coupled Split Ring Resonator as Small RFID Pressure Sensor for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an inductively coupled split-ring resonator based small passive RFID pressure sensor for wireless intracranial pressure measurement. The proposed sensor has a volume as small as π×(4 mm)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ×1 mm. In the simulation, the proposed sensor can provide nearly 1 m operation distance when implanted in the intracranial environment. In our preliminary measurement in the air, the sensor has a resolution of 3 cmH2O.

articleTitle: Diffusion model for cluttered industrial environments at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Path gain in a cluttered industrial environment at 28 GHz is found to be well modeled by diffusion with a single absorption parameter, with 5.2 dB RMS error. Shadow fading variance and azimuthal spread are found to increase with range, also consistent with theory.

articleTitle: Simulated and Measured Power Density using Equivalent Currents for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In 5G applications commercial devices must be tested to verify compliance of human exposure to electromagnetic (EM) radiation with radio frequency (RF) safety norms [1]. At frequencies above 6GHz, testing comprises evaluating the radiated power density in proximity of the device. This procedure, especially at millimeter-wave frequencies, can require very long measurement times. In order to overcome this limitation a fast technique has recently been presented [2]. By applying the equivalent currents (EQC) method on standard near field (NF) measurements of the device, field and thus power density can be evaluated at any distance in order to verify compliance with RF safety guidelines. In previous studies, validation was performed on a mobile phone [2] and on a Dual Ridge Horn (SH4000) [3]. Results and achievable accuracy have been investigated and validated by full-wave modelling using Computational Electromagnetic tools (CEM). In these investigations, power densities using full wave simulations and EQC were compared in the same CEM tool by importing the measured device as a Huygens box [4]. In this new study, the power density is calculated directly applying the NF/NF transformation from the EQC. Power density results from measured and simulated data of the SH4000 will be analyzed and compared.

articleTitle: Efficient Band Characterization of 3D Periodic Scatterers Using Broadband Dyadic Green's Function of Vector Potential A
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The broadband Green's function method is applied to characterize the band diagram and modal fields of 3D periodic PEC scatterers, and it converts the band characterization problem into a linear eigenvalue problem. This is the first time that the broadband Green's function method is used to deal with 3D scattering problem of periodic scatterers. Distinct from the conventional surface integral equation (SIE) formulation using electric field E and the magnetic field H, we formulate the SIE using the vector potential A and its dyadic Green's function. The periodic dyadic Green's function of vector potential A is represented in a fast convergent Floquet plane wave series and an exponentially convergent spatial series evaluated at an imaginary wavenumber. The Galerkin's method is applied to discretize the SIE into a matrix form, where RWG basis functions and rooftop basis functions are used to represent the vector and scalar unknowns on the surface, respectively. This matrix equation is then converted into a linear eigenvalue problem of a moderate size with the help of the hybrid representation of the periodic dyadic Green's function. The solution to the linear eigenvalue problem then yields all the band solutions and modal fields of the periodic scatters simultaneously.

articleTitle: Frequency Consensus for Distributed Antenna Arrays With Half-Duplex Wireless Coordination
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a decentralized approach for achieving frequency consensus in distributed antenna arrays that considers the effects of half-duplex wireless coordination between nodes. Reaching a common frequency among the separate elements in a distributed antenna array is necessary for distributed beamforming, and is beneficially implemented in a decentralized manner where no single point of failure exists. In this work we present a gossip-based randomized half duplex (directed) algorithm and demonstrate convergence to a common frequency for arrays of size 5, 20 and 100 nodes within 100 iterations.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneous metasurface to enlarge cloaking bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The main issues of cloaking problems are to increase the bandwidth of operation and to efficiently cloak electrically large objects. In order to overcome these problems, in this paper an inhomogeneous metasurface is proposed. The metasurface unit cell is composed of two metallic square patches with different lengths. Two arrangements of the single patches are analysed in terms of scattering field reduction and compared with a homogeneous structure.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of RF GRIN Lenses
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: There is great interest in designing broadband GRadient INdex (GRIN) lenses due to their ability to improve the gain of an antenna over a wide frequency range. However, conventional approaches (e.g., transformation optics) are either difficult to realize due to the required material properties or yield suboptimal performance. Better performance can be achieved by implementing a true inverse-design (optimization) procedure which allows the lens permittivity to vary in a nearly-arbitrary manner. To this end, an adjoint-based topology optimization method is employed which can calculate gradients for an arbitrary number of design variables with only two full-wave simulations. This method is extremely versatile and can be used in conjunction with any arbitrary source, lens shape, and permittivity range to quickly find the best performing designs.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized L-band Flat-wire Open Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a differentially fed dual-polarized L-band flat-wire open loop antenna is proposed and investigated. Despite being relatively small, the antenna has excellent performance, with wide bandwidth (904 MHz), high radiation efficiency (99%), high average realized gain (8.72 dBi), high isolation (>35 dB), and low principle plane cross-polarization (<; -40 dB) over the entire frequency band. We investigated cross-polarization in the diagonal planes (i.e., φ = 45° and 135°) and found that the peak cross-polarization could be > -25 dB outside a certain θ range. By introducing a sidewall on the ground plane, we are able to control the range of θ by varying the height of the sidewall and accepting a small reduction in bandwidth.

articleTitle: Experimental UWB ON-Body Channel Modelling: Effect on Antenna Transmission Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper briefly sketches the effect of antenna radiation characteristics for UWB (ultra-wideband) On-body channel modeling demonstrated through various set of experiments. An UWB monopole antenna (LxW = 50mm x 60mm) having a circular monopole diameter of 25mm (#Ant 1) , a Vivaldi antenna (L x W = 35mm x 45 mm) ( #Ant 2), and another UWB planar monopole of dimensions LxW = 22mm x 40mm (#Ant 3), all working over the 3-10 GHz frequency band are used as Antennas Under Test (AUTs) in two different case studies to set up an On-body Channel model for experimental verification: (i) #Ant 1-#Ant 3, (ii) #Ant 2#Ant 3. Each of the AUTs are placed on the inner palms of a female volunteer. The S21 characteristics were analyzed in both near field and far field of #Ant 1 and #Ant 2.

articleTitle: Propagation Over the Sea Between Ship and UAV
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Marine applications of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) need a good insight on propagation phenomena over the sea. Several tests have been developed at 2.4 GHz band in order to check the communication range and the received power at different distances between a radio station located onboard a ship and an UAV. Using the gathered data, two classical propagation models have been tuned in order to provide predictions on the behavior of such radio channel. This contribution covers a gap claimed by companies working with UAVs in sea science applications, both at coastal locations and in offshore operations.

articleTitle: Improving Homogeneity for MRI RF Field at 3T Using a Huygens' Box
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: RF magnetic (B1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) field homogeneity is essential to obtain high-quality magnetic resonance (MR) images. Whereas the recent advent of high field MRI makes it very difficult to achieve B1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> field homogeneity with traditional RF coils, we hereby propose an active metasurface-enabled scheme to achieve B1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> field homogeneity for 3T MRI. After explaining our methodology, we present simulation results which show superior B1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> field uniformity in both longitudinal and transverse cross-sections, compared to a traditional birdcage coil at the same frequency and phantom sizes.

articleTitle: A New Method for Tuning Transistor-Based Non-Foster Negative Impedance Circuits for Low-Frequency Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new method for tuning a transistor-based non-Foster circuit is introduced. Traditional non-Foster circuits invert a load impedance to create a negative impedance slope. Adjustments are made by modifying the load impedance. Previous work has added tunability by replacing the load with a varactor. This paper presents a new method of creating a tunable non-Foster circuit that does not rely on modifying the load.

articleTitle: An Improved Widebeam Circular Polarization Microstrip-Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The beamwidth of microstrip-monopole antenna is further broadened by adding a circular perfect electric conductor shell under its ground in this paper. Using this simple method, the 3dB beamwidth of the proposed antenna is increased to about 188° at central frequency, which is 2.54 times of the classical microstrip antenna. The relative 3dB AR bandwidth of this antenna is 3.12% while the relative -10dB impedance bandwidth is 15.94%. The simulation results of this microstrip-monopole antenna are given in this paper can prove the superiority of our design.

articleTitle: A Fast Analytic Multiple-Sources Angle-of-Arrival Estimation Algorithm for Automotive MIMO Radars
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Traditionally, the angle of arrival (AOA) estimation problem for multiple sources is considered as a nonlinear problem with no analytic solutions. In this paper, an analytic iterative multiple-source AOA algorithm (AIMA) is presented for fast and accurate estimation of the AOA. The approach is most useful for automotive MIMO radars where there can be a large number of scatterers in the scene. The AOA estimation problem is divided into two main tasks: (1) estimate one AOA with the prior knowledge of all other AOA; (2) estimate all AOA by iteratively solving Task 1. It can be shown that for a uniform linear array (ULA) Task 1 has analytic solutions and Task 2 converges very fast, which makes this method effective, efficient and practical for real-time processing. Unlike many other AOA estimation methods, this approach doesn't need the information about the number of sources and can be applied for coherent signals and single snapshot as well.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Wideband Fabry-Pérot Cavity Antenna Using Sparse Array Feed
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates the use of a 2-D sparse array feeding as a primary excitation source of a wideband planar Fabry-Pérot Cavity (FPC) antenna for gain enhancement. The antenna is constructed from a thick partially reflective surface (PRS) mounted on top of an air-filled cavity. The antenna is fed by a 2×2 array of magnetic dipoles (slots) located on the ground plane. A proper choice of the array interelement distance gives a maximum gain of 18.1 dB and a 3 dB gain-bandwidth of 36.4%, which is remarkable for an FPC antenna. Results show a significant enhancement in the broadside gain by employing sparse array feeding with 2.7 times improvement in the gain-bandwidth product as compared to the conventional single element excitation source.

articleTitle: Over-The-Air Calibration of a Dual-Beam Dual-Polarized 28-GHz Phased-Array Channel Sounder
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes an over-the-air (OTA) calibration procedure for the impulse response of a 28-GHz phased-array antenna channel sounder. The silicon-germanium (SiGe) antenna board is composed from two 8×8 planar arrays; each array can generate a distinct beam in the vertical and horizontal polarizations that can be steered in both azimuth and elevation within ±50° and ±25°, respectively. As part of the calibration procedure, unique pre-distortion filters were designed per steer angle, achieving a peak-to-sidelobe ratio in the impulse response of up to 56.5 dB, with less than 1 dB variation across the steer angles. Critically, we show that performance degraded up to 10.1 dB when applying the pre-distortion filter designed at one steer angle to the other steer angles, underscoring the need for angle-specific filters. Finally, we show that performance between both polarizations is comparable thanks to the array symmetries in the fabrication process.

articleTitle: A Ku-band 1-Bit Broadband and Widebeam Phase-Reconfigurable Antenna Element
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Ku-band planar 1-bit phase-reconfigurable antenna element is proposed in this paper. The element consists of three laminates, two bondply layers, and five metallic layers, where a probe-fed O-slot patch, with a compact stripline feeding line is designed. Two PIN diodes are symmetrically integrated on the O-slot patch. By, respectively, activating these diodes, this element is able to generate two phase states with 1-bit phase resolution (0°/180°). The simulated 1-dB gain bandwidth of the proposed element is from 11.8 GHz to 14.8 GHz, and the gain at 12.5 GHz is 3.95 dBi while the radiation efficiency is 79.4%. Simulation results show that the proposed design has the characteristics of flexible phase tuning and good radiation performance.

articleTitle: An Off-Broadside Zero Beam-Squinting Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on NRI-TL Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar, off-broadside zero beam-squinting leaky-wave antenna operating at 5.5 GHz is presented. It consists of two oppositely-directed branches of negative-refractive-index transmission-line (NRI-TL) leaky wave antennas (LWAs), one operating in the left-handed region and another operating in the right-handed region. The two NRI-TL LWAs are fed through a 50 Ohm transmission line. The two antenna branches each radiate their main beam in opposite directions, and the combination of the two beams results in an off-broadside beam. The antenna maintains its fixed-beam operation for a wide bandwidth of 0.75 GHz, with a gain in excess of 5 dBi and radiation efficiencies greater than 70%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Training Data Sets in Artificial Neural Networks Applied to a Radio Frequency Problem
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel study has been carried out to understand the functionality of artificial neural network (ANN) algorithms on a radio frequency (RF) problem. Determining the dominant TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> resonant frequency of a rectangular microstrip patch located above dielectric substrate backed by a ground plane has been chosen as our RF problem. Extensive training has been carried out using two widely used ANN algorithms: radial basis function (RBF) and feed-forward backpropagation network (FFBNET). Later, a different input testing data set was generated and fed into the ANN algorithms to determine the resonant frequency. Comparative analysis indicated that the RBF is suitable for small data sets whereas the FFBNET is applicable to large data sets.

articleTitle: Bistatic Radar Cross Section Prediction Using Iterative Physical Optics with Physical Theory of Diffraction for Plate Geometries
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: It is proposed in this study to use the iterative physical optics (IPO) in conjunction with the physical theory of diffraction (PTD) to improve accuracy in predicting bistatic radar cross section (RCS) of electrically large perfectly conducting plate geometries. The improvements achieved by using PTD to include effects of edge diffractions are demonstrated in comparison with the results of the method of moments (MoM).

articleTitle: Investigation on Statistical Behavior of Radiation Pattern in Analog Beamforming System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In millimeter-wave wireless communications systems, analog beamforming technology is being used to overcome technical drawbacks such as limited service coverage, high atmospheric loss, and insufficient signal-to-noise ratios. However, the errors caused by circuit implementation, quantized control, and imperfect isolation between antenna elements result in radiation pattern distortion and performance deterioration. In this work, we derived the statistical behavior of radiation pattern distortion due to random error, quantization noise, and mutual coupling. The analysis revealed that the radiation pattern distortion follows the Beckmann distribution.

articleTitle: Mm-Wave Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna with Multilayer Integrated Microfluidic Actuation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microfluidically reconfigurable frequency tunable mm-wave patch antenna is presented. Different than the previously reported work on microfluidically reconfigurable RF devices, the actuation of the multiple metallized plates reconfiguring the antenna is carried out by using a piezoelectric disk within a multilayered fluid reservoir stack. The antenna operates with 7% and 9%|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <;-10 dB impedance matching bandwidth in its 28 GHz and 38 GHz states respectively. Additionally, it exhibits a simulated realized gain of 5.66 dBi and 4.9 dBi at 28 GHz and 38 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband Series-fed Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a broadband series-fed circularly polarized microstrip antenna array is proposed. The series fed array consists of four sequentially rotated circular micro-strip antenna connected to a circularly polarized patch antenna. The center patch is fed by two orthogonal L-probes with 90° phase shift between them. In addition, four sequentially rotated parasitic patches which resonates at higher frequency band are coupled to the center patch. The parasitic patch improves the axial ratio and gain of the antenna at higher frequency band. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna is from 3.77-6.30 GHz (50.2%). The axial ratio <; 3 dB bandwidth of the antenna is from 3.77-5.85 GHz (43.2%). The maximum gain of the series-fed CP antenna array is 12.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a 9.4 dBi gain patch antenna with additively manufactured dielectric lens
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an additively manufactured dielectric RF lens is presented for increasing the gain of a patch antenna. A hemispherical shape is selected for an easy integration with a planar antenna, allowing it to keep a low profile while having a narrower beamwidth. The advantageous 3D printing technique is used to fabricate the dielectric lens for its ease. The fabricated dielectric lens is inherently wideband from 4 GHz to 10 GHz, which makes it an ideal choice for C-band operations. The designed dielectric lens can be used with any directive radiator, for example, a waveguide or horn antenna.

articleTitle: Design of Switchable Circularly-Polarized Phased Array Based on Sequential Rotation and 45-degree Rotated Linearly Polarized Elements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is presented to improve the performance of switchable circularly polarized phased array antenna (CPPAA). The CPPAA is designed with 45-degree linearly polarized element (45LPE) rather than conventional pure linearly polarized element (PLPE). Sequential rotation technique (SRT) is applied to achieve circular polarization (CP). Compared with CPPAA using PLPE, the proposed CPPAA not only exhibits high gain but also shows low axial ratio (AR) with wide-angle scanning.

articleTitle: Dielectric Based Triangle-type AMC Structure for RCS Reduction at Mmwave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper triangle type checkerboard surface is presented to reduce radar cross section (RCS). The design is based on plannar dielectric non-absorptive artificial magnetic conductors (AMCs) working at mmwave. For the proposed surface -8 dB normalized RCS reduction is achieved from 59 GHz to 73 GHz. It is shown that the triangle type proposed structure redirects the scattered energy into several lobes, which means further RCS reduction. The angular stability of dielectric based triangle type checkerboard surface is also studied up to 40°, where reasonable results are obtained.

articleTitle: A Digitally Tuned Flexible Reconfigurable Antenna for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a digitally tuned flexible antenna is proposed for integration onto devices within the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm. The antenna design caters for the various IoT communication standards by reconfiguring its operating frequency. Accordingly, the antenna reconfiguration allows operation at 868 MHz, 915 MHz, 1.8 GHz and 2.1 GHz. The reconfiguration is achieved digitally by resorting to a digitally tunable capacitor (DTC). The DTC changes its capacitance, and hence its frequency operation, by relying on 5-bit sequence commands through a microcontroller. The proposed antenna is coplanar waveguide fed with its ground plane surrounding the radiating structure. The gain of the antenna varies between 4 dB and 6 dB for different frequencies of operation. Its radiation efficiency varies between 78% and 92%. The antenna is fabricated and tested on a flexible substrate, where the resulting reconfigurable prototype maintains its performance characteristics for different bent states.

articleTitle: Singular Integration by Interpolation (SIBI) for Integral Equations via Tensor Trains
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient approach for populating the near weakly-singular and near singular integral interactions in the Boundary Element Method (BEM) solution of the Electric (EFIE) and Magnetic Field Integral equation (MFIE) on flat triangular meshes is outlined. The singular integration problem is recast into a multidimensional interpolation problem, where the quadruple singular integral, corresponds to a six-dimensional function, which is interpolated by a set of pre-computed universal (frequency, materials independent) look-up tables. In a previous version of SIBI this interpolation was performed via multidimensional sparse grids. In this paper, a low-rank tensor, the Tensor Train (TT) decomposition is used. The proposed method is compared to singularity subtraction, as well as Sparse Grids SIBI. The proposed method offers improved accuracy and computational cost.

articleTitle: A 3D-Printed mm-Wave Deployable Origami Dielectric Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-the-art fully 3D-printed mm-wave origami-inspired reflectarray with one-shot deployability. The prototype is fabricated with flexible photosensitive resin using stereolithography 3D printing technology. The proposed design demonstrates a tremendous size reduction in its retracted state which can be very useful for various outer-space and terrestrial applications such as CubeSats, 5G stations and long-range mm-wave backscattering applications.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Wideband Yagi-Uda Array on a Kresling Origami Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized, wideband, high gain antenna supported by an origami structure is presented. This antenna consists of a Yagi-Uda inspired end-fire array of crossed bowties. An ideal phase shift was implemented to obtain a circular polarization. Each element of the proposed array is printed on FR-4 substrate and inserted in different sections of a Kresling origami pattern. The proposed antenna exhibits wideband operation from 200 to 350 MHz (54.5%), where S11≤ -10 dB and axial ratio≤ 3 dB are maintained. High gain (7 to 9 dBc) is achieved by such an array of parasitic elements. The origami structure allows a compact stowage (i.e, packaging efficiency of ~95%) as well as fast and easy deployment. The antenna design procedure and analysis are also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Integrated 4-Element MIMO Antenna and mm-Wave Arrays for 5G Access Points
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a dual-band 4-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna design for 5G application, which operates at sub-6 GHz and millimeter-waves. The sub-6 GHz MIMO antennas consists of wideband monopoles that covers the 2.5GHz and 3.5GHz bands, while the mm-wave antenna is a planar connected array with slots acting as radiators covering the 28GHz band (27-29GHz). The proposed antenna system is designed on a RO4003 substrate with a thickness of 0.81 mm. The overall size of the antenna is 100×100 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Broadband Numerical Evaluation of SAR Distribution Due to High-Intensity Radiated Fields by Portable Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the present work, we provide a methodology for dosimetry evaluation when a human body is exposed to a high-intensity broadband frequency signals. By performing numerical simulation on a scenario representing a detailed numerical model of human body, with the presence of a source in its proximity, we obtained a set of worst-case frequencies, in order to give a guideline to fast-up the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) measurements. Furthermore, we observed how the hotspots along the human body change their position according to the frequency, also giving us a method for optimizing probe positioning.

articleTitle: Conformal Patch Antennas for an UAV employed in Agricultural Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, simulation and measurement results of two conformal antennas are presented. The antennas will be mounted under the front of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). The substrate was built using a 3-D printer and the material PLA (εr= 2.7). These antennas will operate at the 5.8 GHz frequency band. Simulation and measurement results present good agreement between them. The first antenna presents a return loss greater than 10 dB between 5.5 and 7 GHz (BW=24 %) and the second between 5.6 and 6 GHz (BW=6.9 %). Both radiation patterns present a directional behavior with gain around 6 dB.

articleTitle: mm-Wave Tunnel Diode-Based Rectifier for Perpetual IoT
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this effort, the authors propose, for the first time, a tunnel diode-based rectifier for 5G/mm-wave energy harvesting. The tunnel diode, a unique semiconductor device with a negative resistance region, is often used in oscillator and amplifier circuits. However, this work exploits one new property for tunnel diodes, that sets a strong foundation for 5G long-range self-powered IoT nodes. This property is verified by the high sensitivity/low turn-on power and self-voltage-regulating behavior of the tunnel diode-based rectifier over a large range of load variations. Compared to a Schottky diode-based rectifier at 28GHz, the tunnel diode counterpart demonstrates a superior compatibility with the ambient mm-wave energy harvesting challenges and needs.

articleTitle: A Linear Array of Patch Antennas for a Ku-band Phased Array With a Rotatable Polarization Plane
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a Ku-band linear array that can change the main-beam direction and the polarization angle of a linearly polarized (LP) wave electronically. The radiating elements are dual circularly polarized patch antennas, and an LP wave is generated by combining left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) and right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) waves. A four-element linear array is designed at 14.25 GHz, and both the main-beam direction and the polarization angle are controlled by changing only the excitation phases of the radiating elements.

articleTitle: Calibration of Wideband Autocorrelation Radiometer with a Comb Filter for RFI Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new calibration for a microwave radiometric technique known as time domain wideband autocorrelation radiometry (TD-WiBAR). TD-WiBAR is a new method which can measure the thickness of low-loss layers, such as snow and ice packs, in the time domain which is faster than in the frequency domain. We propose a new comb filter which acts like a Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) in optics for suppression of radio frequency interference (RFI) in the received spectrum of the WiBAR.

articleTitle: Single-input Single-output SAR-FFT for Fast Multistatic Millimeter Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, fast multistatic millimeter wave imaging (MMWI) is considered. A single-input single output (SISO) SAR-FFT algorithm using significantly less data is proposed. The novel algorithm implements SISO configuration to acquire echo data. Such a scheme leads to faster acquisition of less data and faster reconstruction at negligible cost of image quality. It has been validated by both synthetic and experimental imaging.

articleTitle: Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Loaded with Meta-Lens for Beamforming and Dual-Beam Radiation Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a wideband beamforming double-fed magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna fed by a printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) operating at millimeter wave bands. An ME-dipole antenna is designed as a quasi TE source to achieve a wide bandwidth of 40% (24–36 GHz) with a maximum realized gain of 10.8 dBi at 30 GHz. To deflect the beam in the E-plane, three layers of split-ring resonators (SRR), each with an array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 10$</tex> unit-cells, are located horizontally and offset from the center of the double ME-dipole antenna. The SRR operates as a meta-lens and offers a low permeability over a broad bandwidth in the Ka-band. The proposed structure provides beamforming with dynamic range from −25° to +25° and a dual-beam at ±25° over the operating bandwidth, while providing a maximum gain of 13.4 dBi at 32 GHz and maintaining the impedance bandwidth of the unloaded antenna.

articleTitle: Flexible Ink-Based Interconnects for Textile-Integrated RF Components
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present methods to improve the flexibility of fabric integrated RF structures by modifying solder contacts to epoxy based interconnects. Specifically, we assess the loss exhibited by two textile-based transmission lines (TLs) using interconnects made of CM-127-48 epoxy ink and solder. The TLs were fabricated with conductive surfaces embroidered onto fabric. The measurements revealed that TLs made of ink-based interconnects exhibited a loss of up to 0.2 dB/cm for frequencies from DC to 5 GHz. This represents 50% of improvement over their solder-based counterparts. For validation, a 7-element Yagi-Uda antenna was fabricated by embroidering onto denim fabric to operate at 2.45 GHz. The RF performance of the textile antenna with ink-based interconnects performed better than its solder-based counterpart. This result can be used as a guideline to integrate the textile RF modules into clothing.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband 3-stage Monocone Antenna with Top-hat Loading
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband 3-stage monocone antenna with top-hat loading is proposed. By employing the 3-stage monocone with top-hat, slot, and shorting pins, the miniaturization is achieved while maintaining the desired antenna performances. By connecting the shorting pins from the monocone top-hat to the ground plane, the antenna bandwidth at the low frequency limit is expanded. The slot inside the top-hat improves the impedance matching in the mid-frequency band. Furthermore, by adjusting the gradient of each stage, the impedance matching at the high frequency band is improved. The -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of the proposed antenna is ranging from 0.47 GHz to 12.37 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Band Dual Polarized Active FSS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual band dual polarized active frequency selective surface (AFSS) with the bandpass response to operate over 1.99-6.11 GHz and 11.0-14.52 GHz bands. The structure has a −3dB wide fractional band bandwidth (FBW) of 75.8% and 28.16% bandwidth in these two bands, respectively. Tuning ratio is defined as the ratio of the resonant frequencies corresponds to the maximum and minimum biasing voltages and in these two bands, it is 3.07 and 1.32, respectively. Additional results will be shown during the symposium.

articleTitle: Europa Clipper High Gain Antenna Prototype
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An Electrical Test Unit (ETU) for NASA's Europa Clipper High Gain Antenna (HGA) was fabricated and tested. The HGA is an Axially Displaced Ellipse (ADE) geometry with a dual X/Ka-band feed. The electrical performance and boresight metrology of the reflector was measured at NASA Langley Research Center's (LaRC) Experiment Test Range (ETR) with good correlation between simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Spider Web shaped Near-field UHF RFID Reader Antenna for Healthcare and IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a spider web-shaped antenna for near-field UHF RFID applications. The proposed design consists of concentric decagons, and open-ended microstrip lines etched on the circular substrate. The proposed design features a uniform and fairly strong electric field distribution in the nearfield region. In addition, this antenna exhibits impedance matching ranging from 902 MHz - 925 MHz and further poses low gain characteristics, that is required for most of the nearfield application in order to avoid misreading of other tags. Moreover, this design provides symmetric current distribution throughout the structure, thereby solves orientation sensitivity problems of low-cost linearly polarised tag antennas. The measurement results demonstrate tag can successfully read expensive jewellery items, tagged pills and tag placed in different orientations. Therefore, the proposed reader antenna is a good candidate for near field RFID, health care and IoT Applications.

articleTitle: A Compact E-Shaped Reconfigurable Monopole Antenna for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile frequency reconfigurable antenna suitable for wireless communications is presented. This antenna has a simple monopole E-shaped patch structure printed on low-cost FR-4 substrate with a compact size of 20x22x1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Reconfigurability is achieved by inserting two PIN diodes switches in `E' shaped slot, to strategically manipulate the flow of current path and consequently change the characteristics of the antenna. The proposed antenna is able to operate in different wireless communication standards including 2.4 GHz (WLAN), 3.2 GHz (WiMAX), and 4GHz (C-Band). The simple configuration, compactness, and low-cost nature of the proposed antenna is suitable for multi-standards wireless applications.

articleTitle: Measurement-based Fading Model with Leaky Coaxial Cables for Urban Rail Transit in Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dispatcher commands should be executed accurately and timely, which are transmitted to train drivers through Trans European Trunked Radio System (TETRA) at 860 MHz. In order to increase the reliability and availability, leaky coaxial cables are utilized to provide stable communication channel and anti-interference capability. In the paper, a fading model with leaky coaxial cables in tunnel is developed based on filed measurements in Beijing Subway Line 7, where characteristics of large scale fading and small scale fading are demonstrated. Through the polynomial fitting, it is found that a fading model of large scale fading with leaky coaxial cables is linear. Based on AIC (Akaike information criterion), the small scale fading is close to the normal distribution. The results can be used for the design of wireless communication networks and the parameter optimization of handoff schemes.

articleTitle: Simple Superstrate Antenna for Connectivity Improvement in Precision Farming Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a concept of a simple circularly polarized antenna with partially reflecting surface (PRS) has been adopted for precision farming applications. The investigation contains an analysis of the dependence of the antenna performance on the elements number in the PRS structure in X-and Ka-band frequencies. Especially meaningful parameters from point-to-point connectivity perspective are axial ratio less than 3 dB and high gain of the antenna. Simulation results show that all antennas proposed in the paper comply with these requirements providing the gain greater than 13 dBic in any case. All of the presented designs have high efficiency and also are characterized by a compact size and lightweight.

articleTitle: Investigation on Distribution of Measurements for Microwave-induced Thermoacoustic Imaging Based on Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microwave-induced thermoacoustic imaging (MITAI) has received much attention in the past three decades. Compressive Sensing (CS) based MITAI is a novel method that can extremely cut down the number of measurements while keeping good imaging quality. This work investigates how the reconstructed image quality can be influenced by the distribution of measurements in CS based MITAI. Three different distributions of measurements with the same number of sensors is studied by simulations. The results show that the even distribution can result in the best imaging quality.

articleTitle: Beam Deflection Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A beam deflection reconfigurable antenna based on the metamaterial is proposed for macro station or integrated small base station applications. The proposed antenna consists of a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) and a reconfigurable 2 × 2 array of metamaterial. The proposed antenna can steer the main beam by 20°, 43°, -26°, -48° in the E-plane over 3.6-3.8 GHz according to the simulation results.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Common-Aperture Antenna System Based on Spatial Power Divider for Use in E-Band Fully Polarimetric Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A two-port antenna system is proposed that uses a polarization-independent spatial power divider to align the beams from two orthogonally oriented dual-polarized feeds. This antenna system is compatible with fully polarimetric radar and provides high port isolation. It simultaneously provides a common aperture for transmit and receive to minimize radar parallax. The spatial power divider is designed using a combination of all-dielectric metamaterial techniques and the concept of miniaturized-element frequency selective surfaces, and is fabricated on a silicon wafer using standard microfabrication technology. The measured device exhibits at most 0.9 dB of difference between reflection and transmission for both TE and TM incident waves at 45-degree incidence, over a band from 76 GHz to 84 GHz.

articleTitle: A Frequency Reconfigurable Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a frequency reconfigurable Fabry-Perot Cavity antenna which can continuously change its operating frequency from 5.1 GHz to 6.0 GHz. It consists of a rectangular patch antenna with a parasitic square patch structure acting as the cavity exciter, a superstrate with 9×9 square-patch-type unit cells, and a high impedance surface with 48 phase-varying elements. Each phase-varying element is composed of a bowtie patch printed on the top layer of a substrate and a varactor diode is inserted in the middle of the patch. By tuning the varactor diode on each element, its operating frequency can be varied. Moreover, the antenna's maximum directivity can be shifted with the frequency.

articleTitle: Antenna Characterization in Reverberation Chamber at Frequencies Close to the Lowest Usable Frequency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Research works done in the last years have shown a growing interest for antenna characterization measurements within Reverberation Chambers (RCs). Several studies on antenna characterization within RCs have led to interesting results for gain, radiation pattern and efficiency. In this work, a similar study is conducted at frequencies close to the Lowest Usable Frequency (LUF) of an RC. This study aims at obtaining a better understanding of the limitations of antenna characterization methods as well as the accuracy of the obtained results when measurements are conducted close to the LUF.

articleTitle: 5G Antenna for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Cellular Communication is rapidly being adopted and developed into several vehicle line in the automotive industry. The 5G New Radio (NR) Standards are also being finalized and the 5G Sub-6 GHz MIMO Antenna being designed for mobile devices and for automotive applications. This paper will examine the various performance properties of automotive 5G Sub-6 GHz MIMO Antenna such as Gain, Directivity, Efficiency, Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) and Radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for 2-D Scattering Analysis using Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Machine learning is used to determine the polynomial regression of the coefficients of surface currents approximation for a curvilinear 2-D scatterer. The training data are obtained using method of moments with higher order basis functions and Galerkin testing procedure. The effect of polynomial regression order to the accuracy of calcualted radar cross-section is explored.

articleTitle: Selection of Hydrodynamic Models for the Nonlocal Response of Plasmonic Nanotopologies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Much attention has been attracted by the nonlocal hydrodynamic model, which provides the first-order approximation of non-classical effects, essentially governing the light-matter interaction at deep-nanometer scale. Several hydrodynamic models, together with additional boundary conditions, have been introduced to describe the behavior of the free electron gas in metals. This work investigates the performance of the following models: the hard wall hydrodynamic model (HW-HDM), the quantum hydrodynamic model (Q-HDM), the curl-free hydrodynamic model, and the shear forces hydrodynamic model. The analysis is conducted for the mode structure (natural or quasi-normal modes) of a canonical spherical nanoparticle. In contrast to HW-HDM and Q-HDM, the other two models break down, due to artifactual mode interference.

articleTitle: Analysis of Pinwheel type Aperiodic Clustering for Sidelobe level Improvement in Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of phased array antenna where elements are clustered using Pinwheel type aperiodic tiling pattern, to improve side lobe level (SLL). Parametric analysis has been carried out to select optimum subsection of Pinwheel pattern for clustering of array which is excited with required phased excitation to achieve 10° and 20° beam scan. Worst SLL in 3D radiation pattern of an array with Pinwheel clustering is improved by 3.8dB and 6.6dB for 10° and 20° beam scan respectively. Moreover, no. of TRMs has also been reduced by 68% while maintaining significantly low SLL.

articleTitle: A Novel Nearfield Reader Antenna for UHF RFID Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The nearfield antenna with well-distributed field is required in radio frequency identification (RFID) system. In this paper, a nearfield antenna, with planar quadrifilar spiral antenna and feeding network is presented. The proposed antenna exhibits uniform field distribution with maximum variation of 10dB for both E and H fields in simulation, and field difference between inside and outside the range of antenna is 30dB.

articleTitle: TM Scattering from 2D Homogenous Anisotropic Cylinders Using a Multifilament Current Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The formulation of the multifilament current method (MFCM) to analyze TM scattering from homogeneous anisotropic cylinders is introduced. The radiation fields of an electric line source in unbounded space occupied with an anisotropic material are derived in detail. With the help of the derived fields, the application of the MFCM is expanded to anisotropic materials. The scattering field is then obtained in terms of these line sources. The bistatic scattering widths of cylinders with and without sharp edge are investigated under different incident wave polarizations and material characteristics. Although only TM scenario is investigated in this paper, the solution for TE case can be straightforwardly obtained through duality. Numerical results obtained with this proposed scheme are also in good agreement with published ones whereas the proposed technique has its merits on simplicity and conciseness in comparison to existing numerical methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Multi-Beam Higher-Order Space Harmonics-Enabled Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates the concept and feasibility of using higher-order space harmonics (HSH) in the development of one-dimensional periodic leaky wave antennas (1D-periodic LWAs). A methodology for analyzing the behavior of the propagation constant ( βn) of HSH is presented by introducing two new concepts, namely safe zone area (SZA) and boundary region. They allow us to identify the number of beams and frequency bands to achieve multi-band and multi-beam antennas (MBMBAs). The proposed analysis methodology is experimentally validated by prototyping a dual-band multi-beam LWA (MBMB-L WA) based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology where the n ε[-1, -2] space harmonics are utilized for achieving such a design. The measurement and simulation results show a good agreement with the theory and analysis of HSH.

articleTitle: Examining the Bandwidth Potential of Volume-Constrained, Electrically-Small, Platform-Based Antennas at the HF Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, two primary bandwidth considerations for electrically-small, platform based antennas in the HF band are analyzed: coupling element (CE) location and CE design. First, we analyze an all-metallic cuboid platform with dimensions of 3.20×2.76×7.54 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 5 MHz. In this analysis, a variety of electrically-small CE designs, each occupying a fixed hemispherical volume with radius 0.5 m, are considered. The bandwidth potential of each element is examined when mounted at different locations on the platform. This analysis is then extended to a more complex platform: the U.S. Marine Corps Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV). The CE type and placement were found to have a significant impact on the impedance bandwidth of the antenna. Though one characteristic mode of the platform is dominant at 5 MHz, contributions of higher-order modes play a significant role in the obtained bandwidth. A scaled model of the cuboid platform and the spherical-cap monopole were fabricated and experimentally characterized. Measurement results were found to be in good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: An ADMM-Based Method for Near-Field Multi-Focus Array Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an effective method to synthesize nearfield multi-focus with array antenna is proposed. With the assigned foci positions, we introduce the constrains on both foci and sidelobe regions. Moreover, the designed optimization problem can be solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) effectively. Synthesis numerical comparisons with the existing near-field multi-focus methods indicate that the proposed method can achieve an improved accuracy.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Broadside to End-Fire Antenna Fed by a Switchable Substrate-Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a design of a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) structure that can switch between a filter and a broadside radiating antenna is proposed and used as a feeding network for a quasi-Yagi-Uda antenna. The resultant structure is a single-layer PIN-diode switchable broadside to end-fire antenna working at 2.5 GHz. Based on the simulation results, the antenna efficiency for both operating states is expected to be more than 90% with the broadside maximum realized gain of 5.1 dBi and end-fire maximum realized gain of 3.8 dBi.

articleTitle: Experimental performances for LTE operating on 2.6 GHz in underground gold mine
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports a preliminary study of 4G mobile network platform in terms of coverage and radio signal analysis for LTE network operating in band 7 (2.5 to 2.57 GHz for uplink and 2.62 to 2.69 GHz for downlink) in a former gold underground mine tunnel. Results show functional and comparable connectivity in mine. The coverage and signal analysis of the LTE mobile platform using the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), path-loss exponent n are presented and compared to some experimental results collected from existing LTE technology measurements works.

articleTitle: Induced Effects of Moving People in an Indoor Radio Channel at sub-6 GHz 5G Bands
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A deep knowledge of radio propagation is necessary before deploying wireless networks. In indoor environments, when people are moving, experimental analysis is needed, as many elements are difficult to model with a deterministic simulation tool. Thus, before deploying 5G systems at the 3.5 GHz band, insights on the effect of people moving in the indoor channel are required. This contribution describes the results of a measurement campaign considering different conditions. For analyzing the results, box plots of measured attenuations due to the people moving are compiled. Both the speed of the people and their concentration seem to influence the narrowband parameters of the radio channel. However, the position of the people seems to provide fewer effects on the radio channel.

articleTitle: Progress Review of General Holographic Millimeter Wave Imaging System Based on Linear Frequency Modulation for Safe Personnel Screening
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter wave imaging (MMWI) has proven itself an irresistible revolutionary technology for safe personnel screening. The progress of in-house research on general holographic MMWI based on linear frequency modulation (LFM) is summarized in this paper. Major innovations including distinctive system framework, staggered transceiver antenna array (STAA), inventive calibration, and novel imaging algorithm are highlighted. Prototype evaluation has also been presented.
