articleTitle: Analysis of Gaussian and Isotropic Beams on Power Link Gain Enhanced with Large-Focal-Distance Reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an analysis on the power link gain enhanced by a large focal distance (LFD) reflectarrays with both Gaussian and isotropic beams. The power link gain of LFD-reflectarrays is introduced and compared with two other cases: no reflector, and an equal-size PEC. It is seen that, even though the power link gain can be increased significantly up to 8 dB for F/D ≈ 2, it becomes non-effective for larger focal distances.

articleTitle: Pedram Mousavi - Pioneering Research on Low-Cost/Complexity Phased-Array at Waterloo
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Prof. Pedram Mousavi has been one of my closest and dearest friends and colleagues for more than 20 years. Extremely bright, highly innovative, very hardworking, a real problem solver, unbelievably positive, and above all a sincere and dependable friend. Mix all these with an amazing sense of humor, and then you have Pedram! In this talk I want to focus on Pedram's pioneering work on low-cost/complexity phased-array technologies and his significant contributions to commercial intelligent antenna technologies. Pedram's research work had substantial impact on the current extensive research programs on modular active phased-array system architecture at the University of Waterloo Centre for Intelligent Antenna and Radio Systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Backpropagation Reconstruction Algorithm for 3D Microwave Imaging of Body Part Anomalies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate the performance of a fast reconstruction algorithm based a Backpropagation algorithm for 3D Microwave Imaging of Body Part Anomalies.

articleTitle: A Flat and Thin Wideband Antenna with Band-Notch and Monopole-like Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low profile wideband circular patch antenna with monopole-like radiation patterns and band-notch characteristics is presented. The proposed antenna covers from 3.8 to 9.3 GHz with a band rejection in 5 to 6.2 GHz. This is achieved by loading the antenna with two rectangular slots and two parasitic rings. By combination of two modes of TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub>, the monopole-like radiation patterns are achieved over the entire bandwidth. The profile of the proposed planar antenna is only 0.04λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub> height.

articleTitle: Characterization of Impairments in the Detection of RFID Tags for Smart Agriculture Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a detailed study for one of the major problems in crops tracking inside and outside the warehouses is presented. Two different RFID tags attached to bottles of liquids and boxes of vegetables have been used to measure the received signal strength for various positions separating the antenna and the tags. The appropriate RFID tags have been chosen carefully depending on tag performances attached to the type of crops and liquids. Radio communication quality between the antenna and the tags at 868 MHz is studied to avoid non-read and undetected tag problems. Measurement results show that the study helps to find the optimal position for detection and also compatible tags for each type of crops and liquids.

articleTitle: Concept of Mean Effective Gain for Optimizing Ambient Energy-Harvesting Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces the Mean Effective Gain (MEG) as a key parameter for optimizing the performances of RF energy harvesting antennas. This parameter is computed for various kinds of antennas based on full-wave simulations. It is seen that the three-orthogonal-arm dipole has a stable MEG (around -3dB) independently to the incident cross-power ratio. This interesting characteristic makes it a good candidate for collecting ambient RF energy without power shutdown within a random environment. Experiments will be conducted further.

articleTitle: Stochastical-Empirical Modeling for an on-Body Channel Inside a Mine
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a statistical-empirical model for the on-body channel is presented. This novel model allows generating the impulse response, which approximates the 2.4 GHz measurements' based one. The path arrivals' time steps are best described by the Weibull distribution and the path amplitudes follows an exponential model that assumes the multipath components' amplitudes follow a Gaussian distribution. The impulse response model approximates the measurements with a minimum mean square error (MMSE) of 0.0019.

articleTitle: Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Rotman Lens without Dummy Ports or Matching Loads for 5G
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Rotman Lens beamformer (RLB) is loaded with the low-reflection open-ended tapered profile microstrip transmission lines (MSLs) instead of the conventional dummy ports terminated with matching loads. Based on this concept, a printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) RLB is designed at 30 GHz, and beam-switching performance is verified through fullwave analysis.

articleTitle: A Compact Singly-Fed Electromagnetically Coupled Circularly Polarized Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a singly-fed patch antenna array based on electromagnetically coupled patches is presented. The proposed device operates in circular polarization exploiting the sequential rotation architecture applied to four disc-based patch elements. Each element is proximity coupled to a stacked director patch of similar shape, placed at opportune distance. The resulting structure exhibits a flat band of operation in the C-band, with a gain of 9 dB from 5.9 GHz to 6.4 GHz, suitable for Mid-Band 5G operation.

articleTitle: Method for Improving Detection Efficiency of Microwave Staring Correlated Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for improving the detection efficiency of Microwave Staring Correlated Imaging (MSCI) is proposed in this paper. Via the judgment from Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization and the process of expanded selection, a refined collection of feasible independent radiation fields are picked out from huge amount of original radiation fields, ensuring that the imaging matrix keeps a full rank property at the same time. Numerical imaging results based on the selected radiation fields demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the detection efficiency of MSCI, which makes MSCI better applied in fast imaging applications.

articleTitle: A Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Linear Array with High Gain and Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: By linear arrangement of four magneto-electric dipole antennas, a high gain magneto-electric dipole antenna linear array with wide bandwidth is presented, especially for the new unlicensed frequency band. Through the reasonable arrangement of multiple antennas, the gain of the antenna array is significantly improved. The proposed antenna has low profile to be easily integrated. The proposed antenna achieves a simulated impedance bandwidth of 53.8% covering 44.4 GHz to 77.1 GHz. It includes the new unlicensed frequency band (57 - 71 GHz) totally. The maximum gain in the Z-direction is up to 16.01 dBi. The proposed antenna has the advantages of high gain, wide bandwidth and low profile.

articleTitle: On Computing the Constitutive Parameters of a Lossless Double Positive Dielectric Layer with Branch Compensation from Frequency Tracking
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the field of electromagnetism, knowing the permittivity of a material can be useful in applications such as tuning antennas. When using the scattering parameters to identify the permittivity of substrates or metamaterials, there can be the issue of branch discontinuities. These branches do not always occur in measurements or analysis and they can be difficult to recognize. This paper presents a novel method for branch recognition and compensation, specifically as it relates to determining the permittivity from S-parameters of a lossless, double positive material.

articleTitle: Optimal Zernike Parameterization in Global Phase Retrieval of Large Reflector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Phase retrieval is a widely-used technique to reconstruct the surface deformations of large reflector antennas. To cope with the local stagnation of the classical phase retrieval algorithm, we previously proposed a hybrid global algorithm named CMAES-HIO, in which the Zernike polynomials are first used to parameterize the aperture initial phase. This paper investigates the effect of the Zernike order on the algorithm performance. By introducing a hybrid evaluation parameter combining algorithm accuracy and time consumption, the effect of Zernike order on algorithm performance is investigated for the cases of gravitational and simulated random continuous deformations. The results show that, for the cases studied, which are representative of a wide class of deformations, the Zernike order in the range of 5 or 6 is optimum for the comprehensive performance of algorithm with respect to time and accuracy.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of Multi-antenna Electromagnetic Compatibility Based on Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a fast electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) analysis method for multiple antennas using finite element method (FEM). In this method, an efficient matrix solving technology is proposed to greatly reduce the computing cost of EMC analysis of multiple antennas. By comparison with HFSS, the numerical results demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Building Recognition for Capacity and RF Coverage
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a method of using Machine Learning (ML) to automatically recognize buildings from 2-d images and subsequently create 3-d objects for ray tracing and wireless system analyses. The accuracy of the building recognition by ML is assessed via the capacity of MIMO wireless systems in the resultant propagation environment.

articleTitle: Beam Switching of Massive MIMO Antenna for Base Station using Low-loss Passive Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Beam coverage switching of sub-6 GHz massive MIMO antenna is presented using low-loss passive phase shifter. A single-bit phase shifter which minimizes the loss caused by series resistance of a switch is designed and integrated with antenna. The massive MIMO array is fabricated and measured to examine beam switching function while maintaining low-loss characteristics.

articleTitle: Sparse Array Topologies for 5G mmWave Base-Stations: A System-Level Study
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A system-level study is conducted that evaluates the performance of various sparse array topologies for application in 5G base-stations. The performance metric is the probability a user experiences an outage, when applying a Zero-Forcing precoder in a Line-of-Sight scenario. The outage probability is shown to significantly decrease for sparse irregular arrays as compared to sparse regular and dense regular arrays. A re-configurable sparse array design at 28.5GHz is realized as a demonstrator.

articleTitle: A Fast Full-Wave Data Generation Method for Bistatic Subsurface SAR
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This papers presents a fast full-wave method for generating data in bistatic subsurface SAR. The method considers a fix transmitter, a fixed target and a moving receiver that samples the scattered field. The method works by illuminating the target by the transmitter (in the absence of the receiver) and saving the resultant current distribution on the surface of the target. After that, the receiver is excited (in the absence of the target and the transmitter) and its field in the lower half space is saved. Reciprocity is then used to relate the voltage across the receiver terminals to the target current distribution and the field in the lower half space due to the receiver. Following this approach leads to a reduction in data generation time by a factor of N/2 where N is the number of the samples required in the SAR simulation. The proposed method is evaluated by comparing the data it generates with the data generated by the brute-force full numerical approach.

articleTitle: Dielectric Parameter Estimation at Ka-Band using Bayesian Inversion Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the estimation of dielectric material properties such as relative permittivity and thickness, using the well-known Bayesian inversion method. The free space measurements are conducted to obtain the S-parameters of the materials under test and passed forward to the time domain Bayesian inversion process to estimate the material properties and show the confidence on the accuracy of the results. The measurements were carried out at Ka (26-40GHz) band using commercial Vector Network Analyzer and MATLAB was used for post-processing of results. This method can provide better accuracy and improvement in Nondestructive Testing (NDT) and various quality control systems.

articleTitle: 3D Isotropic High Index Interleaved Metamaterials Realized by Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An arrangement of three-dimensionally isotropic high index metamaterials composed of modified metallic crosses that are extended beyond a single unit cell to form an interleaved configuration with the arms of the crosses from all adjacent unit cells is developed. It is shown that at greater degrees of interleaving of the cross elements the metamaterials exhibit increasingly larger effective refractive indices at increasing miniaturization of the unit cell. The symmetry of the structure ensures that a polarization and propagation angle insensitive effective index is attained. Fabrication of the metamaterial is addressed by fused filament fabrication (FFF) 3D printing.

articleTitle: A 3.5/28 GHz Shared-Aperture Dipole Array with Enhanced Cross-Polarization Suppression
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a large-frequency-ratio shared-aperture antenna with enhanced suppression of cross-polarization. Based on the previously reported topology, the antenna integrates a 3.5 GHz dipole antenna with a 28 GHz 4-element array. The array employs a double-layer dipole element fed by a stripline to counteract the cross-polarization components. Combined with the separate feeding network of the substrate integrated coaxial line, the array can generate a steerable millimeter-wave beam. The experimental results indicate that the antenna has good performances in both frequency bands, including a cross-polarization lower than -24.5 dB.

articleTitle: Minimizing scattering from a densely packed antenna boom on the Europa Clipper Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The placement of multiple antennas onto a single antenna boom on a spacecraft is often done to meet size and mass requirements. On the Europa Clipper spacecraft, one particular boom consists of three unique antennas and an instrument, a sun-sensor. The co-location of these can cause strong scattered fields that can degrade the radiated fields from the antennas. These degradations manifest as ripples or deep nulls in the radiation pattern, resulting in lower data-rates or complete loss of the communications link. To minimize these degradations, a numerical solver based on the Method of Moments (MoM) was used to solve for the scattered fields. The scattered fields are then minimized through an iterative process of changing placement and orientation of the boom's constituents. To validate this approach, a mockup of the antenna boom was constructed and tested in a compact antenna range. The results showed that the measured mockup and modeled radiation patterns compare well, showcasing the value-add of the electromagnetic scattering analysis in-lieu of an expensive full-scale prototype mockup.

articleTitle: Filtering Leaky-Wave Antennas: Composition Principles, Design Considerations, and Multifunction Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the concept of filtering leaky-wave antenna (FLWA) is introduced and demonstrated. First of all, the state of the art of filtering antenna techniques is briefly described. This is followed by the proposed concept of FLWAs with focus on its composition principles, design considerations, and especially multifunction characteristics. Finally, a practical FLWA example is examined and demonstrated, simultaneously exhibiting both high frequency-selectivity and rapid beam-scanning behaviors.

articleTitle: Flexible-substrate Microstrip Antenna Fed by Substrate Integrated Waveguide that Follows Along Spacer for 5G Sub-6 Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A feeding structure that consists of a thin flexible substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) fed to a thick microstrip antenna (MSA) is proposed. The flexible-substrate MSA is fed by an SIW that follows along a spacer. The SIW-to-MSA transition is through two lines in differential mode connected to the top and bottom of the MSA. The fabricated MSA has a frequency of 3.6 to 3.7 GHz, which is in the 5G sub-6 band. Excellent return loss and a measured radiation pattern that agrees with the simulation results are shown.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Quantum Maxwell Solver
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present finite-difference time-domain schemes to numerically solve quantum Maxwell's equations for arbitrary inhomogeneous media based on the macroscopic theory on quantum electrodynamics. In the Heisenberg picture, quantum Maxwell dynamical operators are expanded by a set of ladder operators defined in the coordinate space while non-orthogonal basis corresponding to a new long-range propagators different from the classical Green's function. The proposed time-domain quantum Maxwell solver is useful to study the local nature of quantum information propagation such as virtual photons or near single photon sources. We provide numerical examples associated with two photon interference occurring in a quantum beam splitter, called Hong-Ou-Mandel effect. Moreover, we emulate the recent interesting experiment on quantum interference across an astronomical distance.

articleTitle: Point Spread Function of Circular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate new mean valued solutions of the point spread function of uniformly distributed circular apertures. Our work analyzes approximations with the use of statistical characterization of routine optical techniques. In doing so, we provide a greater understanding of what is to be expected of the imaged data. A final comparison of the mean valued point spread function over a linear aperture is also provided in closed form for the first time in this work.

articleTitle: Temperature Drift Compensation Technique for Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A temperature compensation technique for the resonant frequency of microstrip patch antenna is proposed. The drift compensation is achieved with the use of an appropriate ratio between the coefficient of thermal expansion and the thermal coefficient of permittivity. The equivalent circuit of a coax fed patch antenna is extracted by using a cavity model. The parasitic effect of the higher order modes, caused by the coax-to-microstrip transition, is accounted for analytically. The temperature drift derived by the circuit model is validated by a full wave analysis.

articleTitle: A new definition of the Radar Cross Section suitable for surface wave propagation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper deals with a new definition of the Radar Cross Section suitable for surface wave propagation in the HF band. Indeed, it can be shown that the classical definition of the RCS cannot converge for this kind of propagation. This is an issue for the performance assessment of High Frequency Surface Wave Radars. Thanks to the analysis of different wave propagation models, the differences between the space wave propagation and surface wave propagation have been highlighted. The required modifications of the RCS should then be performed. The new definition is explained in the paper and it is shown that it is suitable for the surface wave propagation. Moreover, this new definition has been used for the computation of the RCS of 3D naval targets and the obtained results will be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Wirelessly Powered IoT Sensor Facilitated by A Planar Electrically Small Huygens Rectenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wirelessly powered Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensor system is presented in this paper. It is facilitated by a highly compact, planar electrically small Huygens rectenna. The rectenna is based on two metamaterial-inspired electrically small structures, an Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) and a capacitively loaded loop (CLL). The near-field resonant parasitic EAD and CLL structures are carefully designed to be a compact entity that excites a short dipole. A highly efficient rectifier circuit is seamlessly connected to this driven dipole, forming a rectenna. The whole rectenna system is fabricated on a single piece of PCB substrate. It is electrically small, has an ultra-thin profile, and is low cost and lightweight. The developed rectenna is able to wirelessly power IoT devices to realize battery-free systems. A wirelessly powered light detection sensor system is successfully demonstrated by augmenting the rectifier with a photocell.

articleTitle: Coplanar Triple-Independent-Element Model for Power Quasi-Isotropic Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to reduce the gain variation (GV) for quasi-isotropic antennas, a coplanar triple-independent-element model (CTIEM) has been proposed and quantitatively analyzed. According to the analytical model, a GV as low as 0.014 dB can be obtained, which is very close to an ideal isotropic source.

articleTitle: A Pixelated Resonator for Mutual Coupling Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a systematic procedure to reduce mutual coupling between linear 2 ×1 array microstrip antennas is proposed. The proposed design procedure is based on pixelization of the surface between two patch elements and the application of a binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) algorithm. In the binary optimization algorithm, each pixel is represented by a bit that gets a binary value of 1 or 0 indicating the presence or absence of copper on the area of the pixel. The optimization goal is set to minimizing the mutual coupling between two elements while the impedance matching and radiation pattern are not degraded. The concept of the work is validated by full-wave simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Evaluation of 12-GHz-band Compact Planar Receiving Antenna for Satellite Broadcasting for Low C/N Reception using ISDB-S3
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The ISDB-S3 system used for 4K/8K (UHDTV) satellite broadcasting in Japan can transmit at about 100 Mbps. This system has several combinations of modulation schemes and error correction coding rates. We designed and fabricated a compact planar receiving antenna for low C/N ratio reception of 12-GHz-band satellite broadcasting that is adjustment-free in the elevation angle. Investigation of the link budget for satellite broadcasting using the antenna showed that it can attain an information bitrate of 10.9 Mbps. The received C/N ratio in a field test at the maximum receiving antenna gain was 2.1 dB.

articleTitle: PSO-Algorithm-Based Design of Arbitrary Focal Distance Reflectarrays for Beam Collimation Objective
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an efficient PSO-algorithm-based approach to design arbitrary focal distance (AFD) reflectarrays. The approach is based on the array factor formulation, which can manage both infinite and finite focal distances, and any kinds of sources and polarizations. It helps reducing the design time and complexity of this kind of electromagnetic problem. An optimized reflectarray is designed by considering a mushroom-type structure with delay lines as the unit cell. Theoretical results compare well with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Validation of 4–40 GHz free-space permittivity measurements using dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Previously, a simple transmission-only method was applied to extract the complex permittivity of common building materials in the 4-40 GHz range using a low-cost anechoic chamber and a vector network analyzer. This technique is validated using small dielectric resonators fabricated from the same materials as used in the free-space measurements. Agreement of the two methods indicates acceptable accuracy of the developed techniques. Measurement of Teflon, a well characterized material at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies, is also reported, further validating these methods.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Metasurface by a Thin Slab of Constant Voluminal Susceptibility
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a critical perspective of the modeling of a metasurface by a thin slab of constant susceptibility. The key results are the following. 1) The modeling approximating the slab fields as uniform might be somewhat helpful, but has a restricted range of validity, 2) The modeling involving varying slab fields is essentially exact for a monoisotropic metasurface under normal incidence, 3) The modeling of monoisotropic metasurfaces under oblique incidence is much more complex, involving a pair of nonlinear integro-differential equations, 4) The modeling of more complex bianisotropic metasurfaces is certainly very involved to the point that it loses practicality.

articleTitle: A Wideband Planar Inverted-F Antenna for Ka-Band 5G System Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband millimeter-wave slotted planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is proposed and developed. A slotted patch is printed on a substrate with gridded ground plane structure and overlapping cells. A particle swarm optimization (PSO) is employed to widen the operational bandwidth by searching for the optimal localization of the slots on the ground plane. The proposed antenna covers a wide operating bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10dB) of 12.5 GHz (24.5 -37 GHz) and has a nearly omnidirectional radiation pattern at its resonant frequencies. The radiation efficiency varies from 81.5% to 99%.

articleTitle: A New Quadrature Method for Singular Integrals of Boundary Integral Equations in Electromagnetism
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we present a new method to compute singular integrals and nearly singular integrals in the context of boundary integral equations for electromagnetism. In particular the method is well suited for integral equations of the second kind. The method consist of splitting the integral in two parts, one regular, which is computed via adaptive integration, and another singular and local (with very small support of the integrand) which is computed using asymptotic expansion. This method can be applied to any second kind integral equation arising in CEM, like MFIE, Charge-Current integral equation, Non Resonant Charge Current Integral Equation (NRCCIE).

articleTitle: Scattering from Uniaxial 3D Objects with a Smooth Boundary Using an Equivalent Source Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The formulations for three-dimensional (3D) scattering from uniaxial objects with a smooth boundary using an equivalent source method (ESM) are introduced. The proposed technique uses two sets of sources distributed inside and outside of a scatterer to simulate outside and inside scattered fields, respectively. The uniaxial dyadic Green's functions are deployed in the ESM in order to obtain the scattered fields. A stable solution is achieved by using the proposed multiple-layered distribution scheme of sources. Two numerical examples are present to study bistatic radar cross section (RCS) responses under different scenarios. Excellent agreements are achieved by comparing numerical results with those obtained from commercial software packages, while the CPU time and the required memory are drastically reduced by using the ESM.

articleTitle: Rigorous Modeling and Optimization of Fractal SRRs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new efficient method that characterizes the distributed capacitance and inductance within fractal-shape split-ring resonators is proposed. The electrical charge distribution along the inner fractal-shape inclusion was calculated using a simplified method that manipulates the method of moments' solution of the Green's functions for the equivalent circular ring resonator. Also, a systematic approach, that finds the inclusion's self and mutual inductances, was investigated. This new advanced analysis leads to an accurate estimation of the inclusion's resonant frequency. A Koch fractal-curve layout was used as a proof-of-concept to validate the proposed method. Moreover, the particle swarm optimization technique was applied to find the inclusions' dimensions from a search-space of solutions for a given resonant frequency. Extracted theoretical lumped-element values agreed well with both the simulated and measured values.

articleTitle: A Quad-Band MIMO Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work a novel quad-band MIMO microstrip patch antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of four rectangular patches operating at their dominant mode with edge-to-edge spacing of 0.0025λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>. The four patches operate at 750 MHz, 1.35 GHz, 1.42 GHz, and 2.07 GHz. It is shown that by appropriately positioning the patches in relation to each other, an isolation greater than 10 dB is achieved. The proposed antenna is low profile, compact, simple to design and fabricate, and it is well suited for MIMO base station applications.

articleTitle: Toward the design of tightly coupled parallel dipoles arrays in the presence of the Human body, based on port impedance characteristic modes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a phased array consisting of eight tightly coupled parallel dipoles is studied. The array is placed adjacent to the human body in an attempt to define the effects of its dielectric constant and losses on the array design. The analysis of the array is carried out with characteristic modes. The ultimate scope of this effort aims at the establishment of an orthogonal eigencurrent basis, which will be exploited in the synthesis of desired radiation patterns. Its novel aspect refers to the pattern synthesis in the presence of lossy Human body.

articleTitle: An Origami Inspired Polarization-Insensitive FSS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An origami inspired frequency selective surface (FSS) design is proposed. Using the Miura-Ori origami pattern, traditional rhombic loop resonators are appropriately oriented to form a dual-band frequency selective surface. The proposed FSS consists of two identical layers that are rotated 90° in respect to each other. Due to this configuration, the designed FSS exhibits polarization insensitivity in a 2.5:1 bandwidth for broadside scan.

articleTitle: 60 GHz Imaging/Detection System Experimental Evaluation on Concealed Weapons
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An experimental analysis for 60 GHz imaging/detection for concealed weapons is presented in this paper. The imaging technique based on time domain reflectometry (TDR) is conducted that utilizes low profile multi sin-corrugation antipodal tapered slot antenna (MC-AFTSA-SC). The analysis is carried out with a step resolution of δx=δy=3 mm with 100 ×100 pixels size of the detected images. This paper presents an experimental analysis to show the ability of 60 GHz sensor in the detection of the concealed weapon such as a plastic gun and a metal gun comprising of aluminium material.

articleTitle: Solving the Scattering of Combined Conductor-Dielectric Bodies Based on EPA
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new method for analyzing the scattering from combined conductor-dielectric bodies based on equivalent principle algorithm (EPA). The object is decomposed into several different parts. In each part, it can be an inhomogeneous dielectric or a perfect electric conductor (PEC) of arbitrary shape. Equivalent surfaces (ES) are built for the interactions between each parts. And the current translation from the object to ES can be accelerated by the transformed multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). Numerical result demonstrates the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Surface Cancellation Methods for Ground Penetrating Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of different methods for cancellation of surface reflections in ground penetrating radar (GPR) technology. Mean subtraction and singular value decomposition are studied and compared using the same experimental data set from real soil medium. Besides, a new method named dual-band cancellation method is also presented in the comparison. Experimental results show that the conventional surface cancellation methods have their own drawbacks when the medium surface is not flat. The newly proposed method has advantages in soil surface clutter cancellation.

articleTitle: A MWIR 3D Plasmonic Asymmetric Transmission Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 3D metasurface structures can achieve higher performances (e.g., wider FOV, broader bandwidth, higher efficiency) than their 2D counterparts due to the extra degrees of freedom available to designers. A promising technique to fabricate 3D metasurface structures is membrane projection lithography. In this paper, we present a 3D metamaterial unit cell that is designed to achieve broadband asymmetric transmission in the mid-wave infrared (MWIR) regime. The structure was optimized by pairing a genetic algorithm with a fast periodic finite element boundary integral solver. The metasurface design has a max y- to x-polarization light efficiency of 80% in the forward direction, while transmitting less than 10% in the reverse direction. Moreover, this structure can be fabricated using the membrane projection lithography technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of Correlated Rayleigh Fading Massive MIMO Uplink Channel: The IDM-CGF Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we showcase the effectiveness of an infinitesimal dipole modelling-cross correlation Green's function (IDM-CGF) methodology, integrated with Karhunen-Loeve approach, for correlated massive MIMO uplink channel modeling. Considering a uniform rectangular array (URA) of horizontally/vertically polarized infinitesimal dipoles (IDs) in the massive MIMO base-station (BS) and four user-equipment (UE) units located along the azimuth angular direction, we use the proposed approach to visualize the channel and critically assess the effect of element pattern/polarization. We further demonstrate the impact of the number of BS-elements in tailoring the channel eigenspace, especially the singular value spread.

articleTitle: High Frequency Diffraction by a Rectangular Hole in a Thick Conducting Screen -E Polarization Case-
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Diffraction of a transverse electric (TE) electromagnetic plane wave by a rectangular hole in a thick conducting screen is studied using Kirchhoff approximation (KA) method. The scattering fields can be considered as field radiations from equivalent current sources assumed by closing the aperture of the hole. The resulting scattering patterns are compared with those of other method to confirm the validity of the approximation. Effect of the screen thickness on the transmitted fields has also been discussed.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Multifunctional Low Frequency RFID Coil Antenna for Embedded Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a miniaturized embedded RFID system has been proposed for smart pill-bottle to minimize the drug abuse. The pill-bottle will consist of a miniaturized RFID reader with on-board rechargeable battery. Hence, the reader has to fulfill two purposes: 1) read ID of the RFID access card, and 2) charging of the battery. A single coil antenna is proposed to perform the dual functions in order to miniaturize the embedded design. In this near field application, RFID band of 125/138 kHz is used. Primarily three different design topologies are explored to select the most suitable one for the application. Here we investigate the miniaturization of coil systems using high inductance coils.

articleTitle: An 18:1 Bandwidth Bio-Matched Antenna Covering the MedRadio, ISM, and WMTS Bands
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Our previous work has introduced a modeling framework for custom designs of Bio-Matched Antennas (BMAs): ultra-wideband, wearable, into-body antennas constructed from the combination of dielectric and water. In this paper, we use our modeling framework to design a novel BMA with 18:1 bandwidth that covers the 0.38 - 7 GHz range. This is the first BMA that covers the MedRadio, ISM, and WMTS bands. The antenna is fabricated using stereolithographic 3D printing and measured upon a tissue-emulating phantom. To ensure repeatable fabrication, we also present measurements of the electrical properties of the cured 3D printing material.

articleTitle: An Analytical Solution of the Electric Field Radiated by a Dipole Over a Layered Half-Space
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the Sommerfeld half-space problem is revisited and an analytical solution of the scattered electric fields excited by a vertical electric dipole (VED) above a layered half-space is proposed. The traditional solution is associated with the Sommerfeld-type integral, which is difficult to evaluate due to the oscillatory and slowly decaying integrand. The scattered electric fields are obtained from the intermediate Hertz potential decomposed into two integrals, and a rigorous closed-form solution in the near and far field regions is presented for each term. A numerical evaluation of the solution for different impedance half-planes, i.e., seawater, wet earth, dry earth and lake water, validates the accuracy of the proposed solution at various frequencies and distances from the antenna.

articleTitle: A Miniature and High-Efficiency Rectenna in ISM 868 MHz Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact three-dimensional (3D) configuration rectenna with high efficiency is presented. Its dimensions are 56 mm ×32 mm ×10 mm that is only 0.0004 of cubic wavelength at the operating frequency (865 MHz). This rectenna uses a miniaturized 3D folded dipole antenna with a maximum gain of +1.54 dBi at 865 MHz. The rectenna is optimized to operate at a low power level with high efficiency (71.6% max). This one can harvest a dc voltage greater than 1 V from illuminating radiofrequency power densities greater than 1.6 μWcm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Active Nonreciprocal Phase Shifter for Versatile Phased-Array Antennas and Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A nonreciprocal phase shifter for phased-array antenna and metasurface applications is presented. The proposed structure is designed for 2.4 GHz. The unit cells are consisting of Wilkinson power divider, gain block and reciprocal phase shifters. Scattering parameters and phase response are simulated and validated with ADS and CST. Simulation results follow well with theoretical assumptions.

articleTitle: A Frequency Reconfigurable Cavity Antenna Based on Polarization Standing Waves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable cavity antenna is proposed with continuous tuning in the X-band. The frequency tuning of the antenna is achieved by simple rotation of one end wall of the circular waveguide cavity, forming the antenna. The cavity supports a polarization standing wave resonance, made possible by utilizing anisotropic handedness preserving mirrors at the end walls of the cavity. These mirrors are based on dielectric ridge gratings with a metal back. The antenna shows to have a directional pattern, with high simulated efficiency (>80%), and >6.5dBi peak realized gain throughout the tuning range. The design provides ease in continuous tuning by simple rotation of one part, harnessing the unique feature of polarization standing waves.

articleTitle: Tracking seeds with tiny RFID chips and peel antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a method to detect and track the location and distribution of the seeds using RFID technology. The tiny RFID chip stick in the fruit can make the fruit's peel perform as the antenna which enables itself to be detected. It retains fruits' appearance and composition and makes the fruit look and smell similar with the original fruit to the animals. With the cut peel, the detection range can be improved significantly, which allows it applicable over a large area.

articleTitle: Concept of a Self-Phased Metasurface Pixel/Cell in Non-Reflective Mode
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A transmission-type Huygens's metasurface allows electromagnetic waves to be both transmitted and manipulated with negligible reflection. This can be achieved by properly designing electric and magnetic resonances. In this paper, we present concept of a self-phased metasurface pixel/cell that offers a reconfigurable transmissive phase. The tunable phase can be realized by using constituent material as the substrate supporting the metasurface. As the constituent material permittivity changes, the resonance wavelength of metasurface also changes, which results in a phase change. The proposed unit cell design consists of three layers of a metallic ring surrounding a metallic patch, all are integrated in a constituent material used as substrates. Simulation results show that the designed unit cell can achieve over 180 degrees of tunable phase with insertion loss of less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Prism-based Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain Analysis of Frequency Selective Surfaces in Lossy Water
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Planar periodic structures are widely utilized in microwave applications. The prism-based Discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method is optimal to cope with the modeling challenges associated with these planar structures. In this work, we modified the prism based DGTD to take lossy materials into account. A ring-shaped frequency selective surface (FSS) is studied as a representative numerical example. When submerged into water, the operating frequency of the FSS is lowered dramatically. We test the algorithm with distilled and tap water of different conductivity. Results of both examples compare well with references of commercial software, which validates the accuracy of the modified DGTD algorithm.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning-based Inverse Modelling with CMA-ES as Applied to the Design of A Wideband High-isolation Septum Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design method for electromagnetic (EM) devices based on inverse modelling using deep neural networks (DNNs) and evolutionary algorithms, which is suitable for generating new designs for complex EM devices with many design parameters and multiple objectives at a reduced computational cost. This method has been successfully applied to the design of a W-band septum polarizer, achieving a high isolation> 40 dB over 15.8% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Fully-Passive and Wireless Recording of Neural Activity in Freely Moving Animals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A unique system, namely the wireless neurosensing system (WiNS) is tested, for the first time, in a freely moving animal. WiNS was designed to sense neural signals in a battery-free manner, without using complex electronics, and by integrating the key components: (a) implant and external interrogator, (b) neural probes, and (c) demodulation circuit. In this paper, a set of in vivo experiments are carried out to demonstrate recovery of neural signals associated with transitions among states of awareness, and while alternating between resting and walking, i.e. in a freely moving rat. These first ever results were made possible by (a) newly developed low-impedance neural probes to closely match the impedance of WiNS and (b) realization of a new custom 3D printed cap. The collected signals provide concrete proof of this technology's pertinent role in neuroscience.

articleTitle: Fluidically Scanned Two-Dimensional (2-D) Meta-Fluidic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a fluidically scanned 2-dimensional meta-fluidic antenna. The proposed antenna consists of a source antenna and a bi-layered metasurface which acts as partially reflecting surface (PRS) as a superstrate. The top-layer metasurface composed of a 4× 4 square-ring element array on the top side of a thin dielectric substrate and 3-D printed fluidic channels inside the dielectric polylactic acid substrate for fluid movement as the bottom layer. It is demonstrated that proposed simple configuration generates a broadside beam that can be pointed to discrete azimuthal directions, whereas continuous elevation scanning of ±25° is also attained simultaneously for each azimuthal direction by controlling the programmable water injection inside the channels. Antenna achieved a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 2.41-2.65 GHz, and a radiation gain of 5.7 dBi demonstrated across the operating bandwidth. To validate the concept, an antenna prototype was fabricated, and far-field measurements were performed. The simulation and measurement results showed good agreement and confirmed the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Differential Stacked Reduced Surface-Wave Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A differential stacked reduced surface-wave microstrip antenna is proposed. A design principle is summarized to ensure the antenna that can reduce surface-wave excitation at least for the thin substrate. Based on the proposed principle, the differential stacked reduced surface-wave microstrip antenna is designed and fabricated. Measured results show that the lateral radiation level of the E-plane radiation pattern of the differential stacked reduced surface-wave microstrip antenna can be decreased to −40 dB.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal transmission based on self-induced nonlinear effects in bifacial dielectric metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The breaking of Lorentz reciprocity law is a nontrivial task, since it usually requires bulky magnets or complicated time-modulation dynamic techniques to be accomplished. We present a simple and compact design of a nonlinear bifacial dielectric metasurface to achieve strong self-induced passive nonreciprocal transmission without the use of external biases. It is composed of two passive silicon-based metasurfaces exhibiting Fano and Lorentzian resonances embedded in an ultrathin glass substrate. Highly asymmetric field enhancement is achieved that leads to strong nonreciprocity at low excitation intensities. Moreover, a cascade design is presented to further improve the insertion loss and broaden the nonreciprocal intensity range. The proposed structure is ideal for free space optics applications, can operate under both incident polarizations, and require very low input excitation power to reach the nonreciprocal regime, which can lead to the design of new nanophotonic-based all-optical diodes, isolators, circulators, and ultrathin protective layers for sensitive optical components.

articleTitle: Wave Scattering by Thin Dielectric and Lossy Materials Using the MoM Technique
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article is dedicated to the electromagnetic scattering of a finite volume of material. The volume has the shape of a thin plate and is excited by a plane wave. It is assumed that the plate is sufficiently thin compared to the wavelength of the incident wave so that the surface currents on the side edges of the plate can be ignored. Thus the plate can be viewed as an open surface, and coupled integral equations of the electric and magnetic type are derived for the equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents induced on the top and bottom of the plate. Appropriate boundary conditions are then used to solve the obtained integral equations in order to determine the radar cross section of the thin material plates.

articleTitle: A Compressible Cavity-Backed E-Textile Antenna for Body-Centric Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Presented here is the design and implementation of a light-weight wearable E-textile antenna for body-centric radios at 2.6 GHz. The antenna consists of a bracket-shaped slot, which is supported by a textile cavity on the back so that unidirectional radiation is achieved. A 50-Ω coaxial cable with SMA connector is utilized to feed the antenna. The inner conductor of the coax is extended to connect to the top wall and the outer conductor is soldered to the bottom wall of the cavity. The designed antenna was fabricated in-house using flexible fabric. The antenna gain measured in anechoic chamber at the resonance frequency of 2.62 GHz is better than 6.5 dB. The front-to-back ratio (FTBR) of nearly 15 dB and the reflection coefficient of lower than -20 dB are obtained.

articleTitle: Active Excitation Tuning for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an actively tuned balun to enable Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) antennas to achieve greater isolation. Specifically, for the first time, we propose placing an active chip into the balun feed to control the amplitude and phase of the current density. Nearly perfect balance of the feed currents enables STAR antennas to maintain strong isolation despite fabrication imperfections and unpredictable environmental reflections. Measurements demonstrate 42 dB isolation across a 250 MHz bandwidth, representing an 11 dB boost. This is the best reported transmit-receive isolation improvement to date. Notably, the balun was tuned across 1.68-1.93 GHz. A prototype was fabricated and measurements show good comparison with simulation.

articleTitle: High Isolation Log-Periodic Dipole Array System for Wideband Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study proposes a differentially driven log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) system with high isolation between reception and transmission ports for wideband full-duplex applications. The antenna system is comprised of two pairs of conventional log-periodic dipole arrays operating in the X-band from 8 GHz to 12 GHz. The simulation results show high isolation S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> <; -60 dB through the entire X-band while the measured results reach S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> <; -50 dB in a reflective lab room. The system is able to cover 360° direction with reasonable gain values, high efficiency, and good impedance matching.

articleTitle: Microwave Transmission of Pressure Sensor Signal Through Explosive Fireballs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we use microwaves for wirelessly transmitting the pressure signal delivered by sensors placed inside high explosive fireballs. It is demonstrated that the modulation of a microwave carrier frequency by pressure signal may be transmitted through fireballs without significant distortion, spectral filtering and attenuation of pressure signal. For experimental validation purpose, we show that the proposed wireless measurement of the pressure variation inside fireballs is in very good agreement with that obtained from a wired transmission, even if aluminized explosives create fireballs.

articleTitle: Circular-Polarization Discriminator Based on Cascaded Multilayer Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact circular-polarization discriminator is presented in this paper. The proposed structure is composed of three simple layers, which are connected by air spacers. The first and third layers act as circular polarisers (CPs), and the second one is a linear polarizer (LP). By combing the three layers together, the right-handed circularly-polarized wave (RHCPW) can be reflected, while the left-handed circularly-polarized wave (LHCPW) can be transmitted through the proposed structure. Within the operating band, the insertion loss is lower than 2.5 dB. Finally, the proposed design is validated by both simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: A Wideband Light Weight L-Probe Fed U-Slot Patch Antenna Array for VHF Ice Sounding
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband light weight U-slot patch antenna array with wide L-probe feed for ultra-wideband radar to sound and image ice is developed. A prototype of 1×4 element array is fabricated and tested to verify the concept. To achieve wideband impedance matching, we used a wide flat L-probe feed along with the mutual coupling between antenna array elements. The antenna array operates over 170 MHz - 325 MHz frequency band (67% impedance bandwidth). More than 11 dBi broadside gain is obtained over the desired frequency band.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Multilayer Energy Harvesting Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient dual-band energy harvesting surface (EHS) array is presented using two stacked-layer of cross-dipole elements for efficient harvesting at two frequency bands for multiple polarizations. The proposed EHS array introduces the concept of stacked surfaces that can be directly integrated and matched with rectification circuitries. Each layer of the EHS array is dedicated to harvesting at a particular frequency band with its own directly matched rectifying circuity allowing better AC to DC matching and harvesting efficiency at each frequency band. The simulation results of the dual-band EHS energy harvesting array show overall radiation to AC harvesting efficiencies of 95% and 93%, respectively, at various polarization angles at the desired operating frequencies of 2.7 GHz and 3.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Fabry-Pérot cavity antenna generating multi frequency overlapping apertures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband planar Fabry-Pérot cavity (FPC) antenna formed by an electrically thick partially reflective surface (PRS) with overlapping radiating apertures operating at different frequencies is investigated. Recent techniques for FPC wideband operation allow the reuse of the same FPC at multiple frequencies, where each frequency has its own feed. The distance between two adjacent feeds is in the order of 1.2 wavelength.

articleTitle: Multi-Mode Cavity-Backed Slot Ring Antenna for Multi-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a multi-mode approach for designing multi-band cavity-backed slot antennas. The approach is based on the analysis of the fundamental and first higher-order mode of a slot ring structure. In addition, cavity modes can be introduced by adding a floating reflector underneath the slot at a small distance of around one-eleventh wavelength, which is much less than the conventional requirement for quarter-wavelength separation distance. The first higher-order mode of the slot can be controlled by placing, at particular locations, one or more capacitors inside the slot. Simulated IEEE gains of the designed antennas are around 9 dBi over the entire frequency band of 900 MHz-3 GHz. Prototypes and measurements will be further detailed.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Nanoscale Arbitrary Meta-element Robustness
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Optical metasurface designs often suffer performance degradations originating from the fabrication process due to manufacturing uncertainties. Therefore, a critical need exists for designs which incorporate robustness, but this is typically intractable during optimization due to the large number of function evaluations required. Nevertheless, by augmenting the process with a deep learning intermediate step, the speed of function evaluations can be greatly accelerated, enabling robustness to be directly optimized during the inverse design process rather than as an a posteriori step applied after the fact. A deep learning assisted robustness framework is introduced for application to nanophotonic meta-element design.

articleTitle: A Novel G-Band E-plane Waveguide to Microstrip Transition for Sub-Millimeter-Wave/THz Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design of a novel G-band (140-220 GHz) waveguide to microstrip transition using an extended longitudinal E-Plane probe is presented in this paper. Proposed design with a wide operating band and low-loss is obtained through systematic parametric studies and optimization using HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator). The optimized transition has a comb like structure which enables it to have broadband characteristics. The low-complexity, low-profile transition is realized on a Quartz substrate of dielectric constant 3.8 and currently under experimental investigations.

articleTitle: Active Incoherent Millimeter-Wave Imaging of Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Active incoherent millimeter-wave (AIM) imaging is a recently developed technique that utilizes the transmission of noise waveforms and a sparse receiving array to form imagery. By cross-correlating the received signal pairwise, the receiving array samples the scene in the spatial frequency domain. Thus, the image can be reconstructed using an inverse Fourier transform from a sufficient set of spatial frequency samples. This technique enables the use of incoherent signals that are unlikely to interfere with other systems and a sparse receiving array, minimizing millimeter-wave hardware compared to phased arrays and focal-plane imagers. In this paper we demonstrate the first measurements of dielectric objects using AIM imaging. Using three 37 GHz noise transmitters and a Y-shaped 16-element receiving array, we demonstrate two-dimensional image reconstruction of two dielectric objects in a laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable Beam Scanning Reflectarray using Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electronically tunable reflectarray (RA) is designed using a frequency selective surface (FSS) in the Ku-Band. The design consists of two layers. At the top layer, multiple smaller sized patches are used as the radiating element while a circular slotted patch is used as an FSS at the bottom layer. The element is a square of length 10mm (0.43λ at 13.1 GHz). A surface mount varactor diode is attached at the top layer geometry. A biasing network is considered to isolate the RF signal from DC. The element provides a maximum phase tuning range of 270° with an amplitude loss under 3 dB. For a proof of concept, a 7 × 7 reconfigurable RA is designed for the center-fed method and its performance is evaluated for H-plane scanning. A stacked patch is used as a feed. The proposed reconfigurable RA provides electronic beam scanning ability within ±30° (@ 13.1 GHz).

articleTitle: Antenna Miniaturization and Adaptive Aperture Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This Paper presents the pioneering contributions of Pedram Mousavi and Mojgan Daneshmand to antenna engineering, during their graduate programs at University of Manitoba. Their research covered two different aspects of antenna theory and design, but effort is made here to combine them under a unified topic of antenna “miniaturization and adaptive aperture antennas”. As such, the term miniaturization is meant to represent the miniaturization of the antenna geometry, for an isolated element, and total hardware miniaturization, for a large complex system of reflector antennas and phased arrays.

articleTitle: Microwave measurement technology of optical signal based on the helical antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an optical signal microwave measurement technique based on the resonance performance of a helical antenna is proposed. The helical antenna loaded with a cadmium sulfide (CdS) photoresistor is used as the core detection sensor. When the CdS photoresistor is irradiated, the resistance loaded on the helical antenna changes, which causes the microwave resonance performance to change accordingly. Therefore, according to the measurement of the microwave resonance, the optical signal can be successfully detected. In this experiment, the light source is a power tunable signal source with a working wavelength of 480nm. The minimum detection power is 2.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>W, and the photosensitivity is R=0.034dB/nW.

articleTitle: Low-Sidelobe Robust Adaptive Digital Beamforming Under Single Snapshot
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new low-sidelobe robust adaptive digital beamforming (ADBF) method is presented. ADBF is known to degrade severely when underlying assumptions are violated in practical application, the high sidelobe level also introduces interferences which have rapid time-varying properties. The proposed method generates a pseudo sample covariance matrix under single snapshot, estimates the direction of arrival (DOA) by ESPRIT and computes the optimal low-sidelobe quiescent weights with an additional special constraints. Under single snapshot, this approach adaptively nulls the interferences, fixes the steering direction error and suppresses the sidelobe to an acceptable level whether signals are coherent or not.

articleTitle: Radiation Efficiency of Reduced Surface-Wave Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The surface-wave fields of the reduced surface-wave microstrip patch antenna based on the integral equation of fields method are calculated. The surface-wave loss is compared with that of conventional circular patch antenna. Comparison result shows that, if the substrate is thin electrically, the surface-wave loss of the reduced surface-wave microstrip patch antenna is negligible.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband and Wide-Angle Scanning Dual-Polarization Array with Compact Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an ultra-wideband dual-polarization tightly-coupled array with an integrated feeding structure and a wide-angle scanning superstrate layer. This antenna is fed by a simple microstrip-to-slotline structure, which can significantly reduce the complexity and the cost. The superstrate layer consists of two frequency selective surfaces (FSSs), which can efficiently improve the scanning angle. A small notch is cut on the dipole antenna. Then, the dual-polarization array can be obtained by embedding one polarization printed circuit board (PCB) into another polarization PCB. Finally, the dual-polarization tightly-coupled dipole array (TCDA) with 16 ×16 elements is proposed, which has a bandwidth of 3.6:1 (1.22-4.4 GHz) with and can scan its beams to ±70°, ±60°, and ±70° in the E, H, and D planes, respectively. The proposed array has advantages of ultra-wideband, wide scanning range, and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: Generation of Free-Space Cylindrical Bessel Beams of Arbitrary Integer/Non-Integer Orders
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a method to generate arbitrary free-space Bessel beams and particularly Non-Integer Cylindrical-Vectorial Bessel Beams (NI-CV-BBs). This method follows from a novel and insightful mathematical representation of NI-CV-BBs. It consists in distributing sources with prescribed conical angular spectrum and azimuthal phase distribution along a circle perpendicular to the axis of the desired beam. This construction is numerically demonstrated and we shall present at the conference an experimental realization of it in the form of a pair of cascaded inhomogeneous wave-plate metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Theoretical Explanation and Prediction of Branches in Permittivity from S-parameter Values
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the field of electromagnetism, knowing the permittivity of a material can be useful. When using the scattering parameters to identify the permittivity of materials, branch discontinuities may be an issue. If they occur, branches of some systems could be neglected. This paper analyzes a theoretical solution for permittivity from the scattering parameters, particularly related to metamaterials, and shows that these branches are due to the use of the argument of an exponential function. Analyzing this exponential function can provide a unique and accurate prediction method of when branches will occur.

articleTitle: Prototyping an S-Band Conformal Line Array Antenna on a Partial Wing Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design, prototyping, and testing of an S-Band conformal array on a partial wing surface. The array elements are series fed microstrip patch antennas fabricated entirely through additive manufacturing (AM) technology using a combination of fused deposition modeling and thermal spray. A robust material set of ULTEM 9085 and copper alloy is used for a good balance of mechanical/environmental robustness and RF performance, while also offering a viable path forward for a future fielded design. The focus of this paper is on AM multi-material fabrication, fundamental print settings and material characterization, and antenna testing. AM characterization coupons are utilized to improve the accuracy of the RF antenna model, which showed excellent agreement with the prototype measurements.

articleTitle: Measurements of All-Dielectric Compound Metaoptics for Wavefront Transformation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reflectionless and lossless metasurfaces can manipulate the propagation of electromagnetic waves by applying a phase discontinuity to a wavefront. While phase-only control is sufficient to perform simple refractive functions, more advanced applications such as establishing custom antenna apertures, forming custom optical beam-splitters, and projecting complex-valued holograms require manipulation of both the phase and amplitude of a wave. Here, we show that a pair of lossless metasurfaces arranged along a common axis (forming a compound metaoptic) can implement phase and amplitude control without loss. We report measurements of compound metaoptics at near-infrared wavelengths, demonstrating a beam-splitter with a custom 4:1 intensity ratio between two output beams.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multibeam Conformal X-Band Patch Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a procedure for designing and testing a conformal array of microstrip radiators. The design procedure for a rectangular patch antenna at 9 GHz is briefly discussed. Next, a total of three patch antennas are designed on the same substrate, separated by a distance of roughly twice the radiation center frequency wavelength. The planar array is then bent to a specified radius to create a conformal array, and its beam pattern is predicted using an analytical model originally developed for open waveguide radiators. Lastly, the array is placed onto a 3D printed structure and excited by the corporate feed microstrip beamforming network.

articleTitle: Accurate and Stable Method for Solving Maxwell's Equations in Non-Conformal Mixed Tetrahedron and Brick Meshes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The solution of many real-world engineering problems can be made more flexible and efficient if objects can be separately meshed independent of each other. In this paper, we develop a method to solve Maxwell's equations in such a setting where non-conformal tetrahedron and brick meshes coexist. Using this method, the tetrahedron mesh can be used to discretize arbitrarily shaped objects, and embedded in the background brick mesh. A brick mesh can also be embedded in the background tetrahedron mesh. The meshes can be generated independent of each other and their interface does not need to share nodes and edges in common. The proposed method in time domain is free of matrix solution across the entire mixed meshes. An interface scheme is also developed to stitch two different meshes and thereby matrix systems accurately, while ensuring the time-domain stability. The method is equally applicable in frequency domain. Numerical experiments in non-conformal mixed meshes validate its effectiveness, accuracy, and flexibility.

articleTitle: Hight-Gain Circulary Polarised Patch Antenna Array At 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact, high gain, and circularly polarized patch antenna array design is proposed. The proposed structure is destined for the 5G wireless communications systems operating at 28 GHz band. The proposed antenna structure uses a loaded dielectric hemisphere Lens to focalize electromagnetic energy and enhance the gain. Simulation results shows that the antenna design covers about 0.5 GHz of bandwidth while delivering high gain of 15.3 dBi and an axial-ratio bandwidth of 0.35 GHz.

articleTitle: Floating-Potential Boundary Conditions using Discontinuous Galerkin Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Isolated conductors appear in various electrostatic problems. In simulations, an equipotential condition with a floating (undefined) potential value is enforced on the surface of an isolated conductor. In this work, a numerical scheme making use of the discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method is proposed to model such conductors in electrostatic simulations. A floating-potential boundary condition, which involves the equipotential condition together with a total charge condition, is “weakly” enforced on the conductor surface through the numerical flux. Compared to adaptations of the finite element method used for modeling conductors, the proposed method is more accurate, capable of imposing nonzero charge conditions, and simpler to implement. Numerical results, which demonstrate the accuracy and applicability of the proposed method, are provided.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Metasurface for High-Gain Radiation and Low RCS by Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
