abstract: In this work, an anisotropic metasurface (MS) is proposed for independent wave manipulation of radiation and scattering, which realizes high gain radiation and low radar cross section (RCS) by the excitation of spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP). The presented MS consists of anisotropic unit cells, which exhibit reflected mode and transmitted mode for x and y polarization, respectively. Besides, x-polarized reflection phase and y-polarized transmission phase can be independently changed in a wide range by varying structural parameters of the unit cell. By integrating with a conventional microstrip antenna, the proposed MS realizes y-polarized high-gain radiation of 15.3 dB, gain enhancement of 8.84 dB, and RCS reduction of more than 10 dB from 22 to 26GHz by the excited SSPPs in the simulation.

articleTitle: Phase-Only Synthesis Methods for General Beam-forming Reflective Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two methods for synthesizing the phase profile of a reflective metasurface are presented based on Woodward-Lawson (WL) method and amplitude-to-phase mapping techniques. Using a simple square loop resonator based unit cell at 60 GHz, WL method is full-wave verified to approximate the desired far-field beam patterns. To improve the synthesis performance, a direct complex amplitude-to-phase mapping, is further presented which closely approximates any arbitrary pattern characteristics using phase-only modulated metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Biconical Antenna with Integrated Balun Fabricated in Additive Manufacturing Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design and manufacturing of a biconical antenna with integrated balun for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The antenna is composed by a Duncan-Minerva balun that feeds a vertically polarized biconical radiating element. The fabrication of the item has been fully realized in Additive Manufacturing (AM) technology to simplify the assembly and reduce the weight. The applied technique has been the Direct Metal Laser Sintering (DMLS). The radiating element works from 200 MHz to 800 MHz ensuring good reflection coefficient and desired omnidirectional patterns. Simulation and measurement results show very close correspondence validating the design.

articleTitle: On the Difference between the Nyström Method and Point-Matching Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the integral equation approach for solving electromagnetic (EM) problems, the Nyström Method (NM) and Point-Matching Method (PMM) could be the two alternative or competitive methods to the widely-applied method of moments (MoM). The NM has been increasingly applied to solve various EM problems in recent years, but it is thought of as the same as the PMM by some researchers. We clarify their similarity and difference and propose a hybrid scheme by combining their advantages. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and merit of the scheme.

articleTitle: Investigation of MIMO Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency in Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Based on the investigations of the recent research efforts for Single-Input Single-Output(SISO), Multiple-Input Single-Output(MISO), and Multiple-Input Multiple-Output(MIMO) Wireless Power Transfer(WPT) systems, we present simple approximate solutions for Tx sources and Rx loads to achieve maximum efficiency in practical environments. In comparison with Genetic Algorithm(GA) and maximum Rayleigh quotient method, the maximum efficiency using this method gives some discrepancies but can be conveniently applied in practice for somewhat rough estimation of the system.

articleTitle: Microwave Sensor of Integrated CSRR Cells for Typing Detection in Synthetic Blood
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates the potential of an improved microwave planar sensor operating in the centimeter-band 1 - 6 GHz for ABO-Rh blood typing applications. The sensor integrates three cells of complementary split ring resonators (CSRRs) on a thin layer of an FR4 dielectric substrate. A rectangular plexiglass-made channel is appropriately incorporated on top of the CSRRs region to hold the blood samples for measurements. The proposed sensor has shown to be reliable for differentiating various types of synthetic bloods as evidenced by the in-lab measurements using a convenient VNA setup.

articleTitle: A Regularized Electric Flux Volume Integral Equation for Brain Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Volume integral equations for modeling biological tissues in the frequency domain typically suffer from ill-conditioning for high dielectric contrasts and low frequencies. These conditioning breakdowns severely compromise the accuracy and applicability of these models and render them impractical despite their numerous advantages. In this work, we present an electric flux volume integral equation (D-VIE) free from these shortcomings when computed on biologically compatible simply connected objects. This new formulation leverages on careful spectral analysis to obtain volume quasi-Helmholtz projectors capable of curing both sources of ill-conditioning. In particular, the normalization of the projectors by the material permittivity allows for an inhomogeneous re-scaling of the equation which stabilises the high contrast breakdown together with the low-frequency breakdown. Numerical results show the applicability of this new formulation in realistic brain imaging.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Ka-Band Leaky-Wave Antenna Using Ridged Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel miniaturized leaky-wave antenna fabricated on ridged half-mode substrate integrated waveguide technology is proposed in this paper for operation at a 5G millimeter-wave band. This paper investigates the performance of ridged half-mode SIW in its near cutoff region, and presents the simulated results. The proposed antenna achieves greater than 70% miniaturization over a reference HMSIW design while maintaining comparable gain and performance.

articleTitle: Wireless High Sensitivity Low-Profile Permittivity Sensor Using Resonant Absorbing Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A layered passive periodic resonant structure is proposed as a sensor where a thin layer of material under test is combined with a resonant absorbing surface to provide a highly-sensitive permittivity measurement (1.46 GHz/εr). Using an interrogating antenna, this measurement is completed by wirelessly tracking the frequency shifts in the absorption peak of the proposed sensor. A prototype of the sensor is fabricated on a low-cost FR-4 substrate with an overall dimension of 65 mm ×65 mm ×2.61 mm. An experiment is performed where air, poly-ether-imide (PEI), and polytetrafiuoroethylene (PTFE) samples are detected with corresponding resonance frequencies of 9.91 GHz, 8.55 GHz, and 8.30 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Green's Functions for Source and Field Points on a Faceted Convex Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) solution for mutual coupling is applied to a faceted conducting convex surface to predict the asymptotic Green's functions for electric and magnetic fields at a field point due to infinitesimal electric and magnetic currents at a source point, both points being on the surface. A quadratic surface mapping is used to introduce surface curvature to triangular facets. A previously developed geodesic ray tracing algorithm is applied to identify geodesic ray paths between source and field points on a faceted convex surface. The geometrical parameters extracted from the surface are used to apply the UTD solution to predict the asymptotic Green's functions. The results of the application of UTD to a faceted convex surface is validated with those of the analytical UTD solution for a circular cylinder and a sphere. This approach is applicable to arbitrary faceted convex surfaces.

articleTitle: A Novel Planar Dual CP MIMO Antenna With Polarization Diversity and High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a low cost planar two-port circularly polarized MIMO patch antenna with the polarization diversity is presented. Three grounded stubs and a mirrored F defected ground slot are used to achieve simultaneous matching and isolation between the two patch and offset feeding for circular polarization. The proposed antenna covering 2.5-2.55 GHz is fabricated and measured. Its measured performance show that and axial ratio for the whole band. Its radiation patterns and gain are also measured and an agreement with the simulation result has been achieved.

articleTitle: Unified Current Mapping Framework for Mixed Finite Element Particle in Cell Methods
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: There has been significant recent effort to improve analysis of plasma physics particle in cell methods that use finite element methods for transient electromagnetic analysis. The challenge with any of these formulations is the mapping the charges and currents on the grid consistently so that charge is conserved as the particle distribution evolves in time. This work analyzes this challenge by determining the spatial and temporal requirements needed to satisfy the governing equations, and presents a unified approach for source representation on both primal and dual grids are presented. It is shown that the proposed approach leads to charge conserving scheme when combined with an appropriate time integration methods.

articleTitle: Radiating Discontinuity in Leaky-Wave Antenna: A Role in Complex Propagation Constant Engineering
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the role of radiating discontinuity (RD) in engineering or reshaping complex propagation constant, i.e., attenuation and phase constants of leaky-wave antennas is explored and presented. To be more specific, the attenuation constant of the leaky mode is related to the real part of the RD's impedance/admittance while the phase constant can be manipulated by the imaginary part of that parameter. As a result, leaky-wave antennas possessing either stable radiation performance or alternatively rapid beam-scanning characteristics can be realized by engineering the RD. Both are separately examined and demonstrated in this work by practical examples.

articleTitle: Generation and Control of Bessel Beam with a Reconfigurable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Bessel beam, known to have an amplitude that follows a Bessel function of the first kind has attracted considerable attention these last decades, especially due to their propriety of being non-diffractive beam over short distances. In this paper, we propose to generate and control Bessel beams by using a reconfigurable metasurface. This structure allows both to reconfigure the operating frequency and to change the spatial position of the generated Bessel beam. Both numerical simulations and experimental measurements are performed at microwave frequencies to validate the concept.

articleTitle: Time-Average Behaviors of Indoor Propagation Channels on Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates the three-dimensional spatial distribution of incident waves within an indoor environment over commonly used wireless bands such as GSM900, GSM1800, IMT2000 and WiFi 2.4 GHz. Unlike previous works, the proposed approach derives the time-average behavior of the channels from the received powers coming from common existing RF transmitters. It is seen that the 3D-spatial envelopes of the channels over wireless bands are Gaussian-type only for downlinks.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Antenna With Broadside and Conical Radiation Patterns for NB-IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact single-fed dual-band dual-mode antenna with different polarization and radiation patterns is proposed in this paper. By simply removing one feed of a differential shorted patch antenna (DSPA)., both the even and odd coupled modes can be excited in the original structure. As a result., the proposed antenna exhibits two operating band with horizontal-polarized broadside radiation and vertical-polarized conical radiation patterns., respectively. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed antenna is a good antenna candidate in Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communication systems for narrowband Internet of things (NB-IoT) applications.

articleTitle: A Parasitic Loaded Series Array for Intelligent Transportation Systems in C-band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a series-fed array antenna suitable for vehicular communications in C-band is presented. The array, printed on a commercial substrate, is optimized for obtaining the maximum gain in the radio channels assigned to the Intelligent Transportation Systems. Moreover, its compactness allows for an easy integration with already existing systems. Measurements confirm simulations results, with a maximum gain of 9.00 dB at 5.8GHz and 8.75 dB at 5.9GHz, as well as a reasonable gain exceeding 3.00 dB up to 6.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Agile Antenna using PIN Diodes and SPDT Switches
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new design of a reconfigurable antenna is proposed. The antenna structure is using two PIN diodes for switching between two radiation patterns (directional and bidirectional) and a SPDT switch to achieve good impedance matching. The simulated results show a good impedance matching, with S11 below -10 dB using the SPDT switch configuration. In addition, the far-field directivity for both configurations is around 5 dB.

articleTitle: Multi-mode OAM parabolic antenna with dual feeds
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A double-feed OAM parabolic antenna is proposed, consisting of a parabolic antenna, which is designed to reflect the OAM beams onto its surface, a low mode feed which generates vortex waves with l=1,2, and a high mode feed which generates OAM beams with l=3,4. This principle of getting high gain vortex wave is described and verified by simulation. From the results we get, the OAM antenna gains of the four modes are all above 24.7dBi.

articleTitle: 700 MHz Quad Port Helical Antenna Array for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Quad helical antenna is designed for Multiple Inputs Multiple Outputs (MIMO) application in the 700 MHz Europe 2020 allocated band for wireless communications. The quad printed helical antenna with four collocated independent ports has S11<; -20dB 13% band width in 694 MHz - 790 MHz band. We present the element and a staggered column array with simulation and measured results of radiation patterns, and s-parameters for the single stand-alone quad antenna and in the array. The staggered array is designed and fabricated. Measured results and field tests will be presented.

articleTitle: A Highly Efficient, Multi-beam, Wide Scan Angle Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Some of the challenges in the design of multi-beam antennas is achieving good beam performance at wide angles, high cross over levels between adjacent beams, all while a high efficiency is maintained. Planar antenna, while very attractive because of their low-profile character, have difficulties achieving most of the above-mentioned goals. Reflectors, even the toroidal type, have very limited scanning capabilities. The closest antenna type that can get close to meet these goals is the Luneburg lens, widely known for years. The present paper presents a multi-beam antenna concept based on a special variation of the Luneburg lens. The unique features of this concept are the following: 1. Complete coverage of a solid angle with a radius of 60°. 2. Constant separation between adjacent beams. 3. A 40% reduction in weight with respect to the traditional Luneburg Lens.

articleTitle: Optically Invisible Touch Sensor Panel Integrated Antenna: Concept and Demonstration at mmWave Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a first-of-its-kind optically invisible phased-array antenna which can be integrated on the OLED touch screen panel for future beamforming devices. Denotes as TSPIA, the proposed concept is exemplified and studies in the form of a 1×4 phased-array antenna for millimeter-wave 5G NR cellular handsets. The fabricated prototype exhibits 3-dB beam scanning range of ±40° at 28 GHz while fully functioning as conventional touch sensor arrays.

articleTitle: Advanced Base Station Concept for Wireless Connectivity in Rural Areas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we discuss an advanced base station system with smart algorithms operating on its multiple directional antenna arrays to provide seamless full-directional wireless connectivity and present its simulation result for 5G using Matlab. The system has six-sectors for communication and a scanning array for user discovery. Based on angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation, optimized beamforming algorithm is employed to establish communication link between respective sector with optimized beams and the identified users. This system modifies the physical layer without affecting other layers and can be installed on the existing infrastructure. All the standards for WiFi, LTE and 5G radios are kept intact. The initial results of simulation show that continued connectivity and tracking with high data rate in multiuser LTE and 5G environment can be achieved.

articleTitle: Liquid Metal-based Tunable Coaxial Antenna for Microwave Ablation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a liquid metal tunable antenna for microwave ablation that aims to maintain the optimal impedance matching among different organs of treatment. Tuning was achieved by a pneumatic-driven physical displacement of liquid metal plug inside a dielectric tube interconnecting with the coaxial cable. Simulations were performed at the operating frequency of 2.45 GHz for the tunable coaxial monopole antenna inserted into models of liver, bone, inflated and deflated lung tissue. We demonstrated that with minor tuning of monopole length, the optimal impedance matching can be achieved among a wide range of dielectric property variations.

articleTitle: Pixel-Based Optimization of Touch Sensing Electrodes for Integration with 5G Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conventional capacitive touch sensor panels (TSPs) have densely packed sensing electrodes that substantially reflect electromagnetic (EM) waves impinging on them especially in S and C-bands. There is a strong interaction between the antenna element placed underneath and the electrodes, distorting the antenna's radiation pattern. Thus, we propose a systematic strategy that optimizes the shapes of the sensing electrodes to configure transmission pass-bands at will for a normally incident plane wave. Finally, the optimized TSP is integrated with a dipole antenna operating at 4 GHz (5G n77-band) to validate our proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Embedded CPW-Mode Diplexer Using Multiconductor Transmission-Line Metamaterial Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A via-fenced coplanar-waveguide-mode diplexer is presented, the output filters of which consist of multiple cascaded unit cells designed via multiconductor transmission-line metamaterial techniques. The diplexer exhibits relatively wide bands (0-3.6 GHz and 6.2-9.5 GHz), with a region of high reflection in between the two bands. The metamaterial unit cells are entirely embedded into the host transmission line, and make use of rigorous equivalent-circuit models to possess inherent rejection of the microstrip- and coupled-slotline-like modes.

articleTitle: Extraction of Geometrical Parameters From Faceted Convex Surfaces for Creeping Wave Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: It is proposed to extract the geometrical parameters required by the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) solutions from a faceted convex surface, accurately. The accuracy of extraction is demonstrated compared to the actual values.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Coupling Compact MIMO Antenna Based on Partially Overlapped Microstrip Patch
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-port compact and low-coupled microstrip multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is realized by partially overlapping two patches that work at mode TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>, respectively. Because of the effects of counteraction of the induced electromagnetic fields, a very low mutual coupling of -32 dB can be achieved when the two patches are partially overlapped with the distance between the centers of them equaling to 175 λλ is the free space wavelength at 6.5 GHz). The proposed MIMO antenna realizes compact and high isolation properties simultaneously, with no additional structure inserted between the antenna elements.

articleTitle: Low-Profile True-Time Delay Based Electronically Reconfigurable Leaky-wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a low-profile leaky-wave antenna is proposed that combines the full-space beam-scanning capabilities of transmitarrays and the low-profile nature of leaky-wave antennas. A 1D slice of a center-fed radial array comprising 2564-elements (of height .5\lambda$ at 19.5 GHz) with a true-time delay phase-shifting mechanism is presented. The array generates a directive beam and is steerable to an arbitrary angle. In addition to reduction in profile, the demonstration shows minimal beam-squint effects with a 1 dB gain bandwidth of 2.25% operating at the K-band, a characteristic not easily attained in large reconfigurable apertures.

articleTitle: Scan-Multiplying Lens suitable for use with Small Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here, we outline the development of a lens like structure that allows a single planar phased array antenna to provide hemispherical coverage. The device employs an inhomogeneous dielectric dome and complex element phase excitations to achieve the goal.

articleTitle: Enhanced Circular Bull's Eye Antenna with Dielectric Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Circular Bull's Eye antenna consists of circular waveguide surrounded by conducting flange with circular grooves radially placed about one wavelength from each other is presented at the V-band (48-72 GHz). An extra corrugation is added at the flange edge to reduce the edge diffraction. Besides, a dielectric superstrate of quarter wavelength thickness is placed at λ0/2 on top of the waveguide aperture to enhance further the radiation characteristics. As such, a directivity better than 18 dBi is achieved.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Arrays with Reconfigurable Metamaterials for Bandwidth Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Tighly Coupled Dipole Arrays (TCDA) are ultra wideband conformal antennas of low profile. Contiguous bandwidth greater than 10:1 have been reported that reach the Bode-Fano limit. In this paper, we present an active approach to further increase the bandwidth of TCDAs using tunable Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) and Artificial Electromagnetic Conductors (AMC). Preliminary results led to a dual-polarized Active TCDA (A-TCDA) that covers the entire UHF band (0.2-2.8GHz).

articleTitle: Aperture-Coupled Liquid Metal Tunable Dipole
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A frequency-tunable planar antenna that uses parallel, variable-length, liquid-metal dipole filaments is presented. The liquid-metal dipoles are contained in thin cavities embedded in a silicon-based polymer and are aperture-coupled by a feed structure beneath. A prototype of the antenna with nominal frequency of 3.5 GHz is fabricated and measured to demonstrate 730 MHz of continuous tuning with a peak realized gain of 4.50 dBi and back radiation below -3.93 dBi. The antenna is constructed on a 40mm × 50mm Rogers 5880 (ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 2.2, tanδ == 0.0009) laminate sheet with thickness 0.51 mm.

articleTitle: Low Side-lobe, RCS Reduction Microstrip Antenna Array for 24 GHz Vehicle Millimetre Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: During the vehicle millimeter-wave radar application, the envelope signal would be continuously reflected between the bumper and radar, which causes the misjudgment in the direction of arrival (DoA). Thereby it is essential to improve the resolution through scattering the reflected envelope signal. Assuming the bumper installed in front of the radar, then the key of resolution enhancement resides in the backward scattering, or to say, the monostatic radar cross-section (RCS) reduction. This paper presents a hollow substrate with square unit cells, which form an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) combining with the grounded substrate. Notably based on the array, we shaped the empty part for RCS reduction, also for low side-lobe.

articleTitle: Adaptation of a Microwave Ablation System for Wireless Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An emerging technique for medical telemetry using implantable medical devices is 3D printing antennas constructed of a biocompatible polymer directly into the body. In this work, we demonstrate the use of a 10 GHz floating sleeve dipole antenna, designed for the ablation of tumors, for heating and solidifying biopolymer materials. Experiments in egg white and the proposed biopolymer indicate a sustained heating area of 1 cm can be produced. In addition, solidification of the biopolymer is achieved by applying 15 W for 15 min.

articleTitle: Broadband Pentadent Monopole Antenna with Uniform Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a broadband pentadent monopole antenna is presented. The pentadent monopole antenna consists of five arms: main monopole antenna and two side monopoles with parasitic arms attached to each of them. The side monopoles and parasitic arms resonate at higher frequencies, which are responsible for wide impedance bandwidth and less variation in radiation pattern. The 10 dB impedance matching bandwidth is from 1.326-4.628 GHz (110%) and the antenna has uniform radiation pattern over the bandwidth. The size of the fabricated antenna is 73.5mm × 62mm ( 0.32λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.27λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> corresponds to lowest frequency of the impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Dual-Polarized Antenna for Wideband Full-Duplex Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new four-port dual-polarized antenna for in-band full duplex (IBFD) operation is presented offering high inter-port isolation. The antenna consists of four H-shape slots, stacked patches for wide bandwidth, and two 180° hybrid couplers. The multilayer antenna is well matched from about 2.2 to 2.4 GHz and provides high isolation, and with the addition of external hybrid couplers, the simulated coupling between the ports is below 60 dB. When compared to other types of similar hybrid coupler and antenna systems, the proposed configuration provides a higher isolation bandwidth (10%) and higher gain. As reported in the paper, simulation and measurement results are in good agreement and suggest that maximum realized gain values of 7.8 dBi are possible with cross-polarization levels of 30 dB or lower. To the best knowledge of the authors' no similar antenna system has been previously reported in the literature with similar operating bandwidths and isolation values in the S-band which can enable new data link possibilities for future IBFD wireless networks.

articleTitle: Synthetic Aperture Interferometric Imaging for noncooperative leack detection from shielded structures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes the application of Synthetic Aperture Interferometric Imaging to the detection of electromagnetic leakage from shielded equipment and buildings. By conducting laboratory experiments, we demonstrate the efficiency of this technique for the accurate detection and location of electromagnetic leakage from a metallic cavity with faulty faradization and adjustable quality factor.

articleTitle: Dual-Band and High-Efficiency Reflective Polarization Converter Based on Strip Grating
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A structure acting as a linear polarization reflective rotator that can convert x- or y-polarized electromagnetic waves to cross-polarized waves in two bands is proposed. The unit cell consists of a metallic strip grating with 45° from the x-axis in the middle of the dual-layer substrate, and a bottom ground. The simulation shows the polarization conversion ratio of over 98% in the frequency range from 5.7 to 12.44 GHz and 23.75 to 30.65 GHz with fractional bandwidths of 74.3% and 25.4%. The reason of dual-band polarization-converting function is explained by the equivalent circuit model of two orthogonal components. The fullwave simulation and equivalent circuit model results are all in agreement with the entire frequency regions.

articleTitle: Range and DOA Estimation of Micro-Doppler Target Using A LFMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The range and DOA estimation of a micro-Doppler target is verified using a linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) radar. The signal processing algorithms are implemented by DSP. The target range results of two radars are compared, and the consistency is high. The test results indicate that the DOA error is less than 1 degree, and the range error is less than 0.25 m.

articleTitle: Manipulating the Power Propagation Direction in Parallel-Plate Waveguide by Reconfigurable Huygens Source
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes a method to manipulate the power propagation direction in the parallel-plate waveguide based on a reconfigurable Huygens source. The Huygens source consists of one electric dipole and two magnetic dipoles. The magnitudes and phases of the two magnetic dipoles could control their synthesized magnetic-dipole vector, and thereby leads to the reconfigurability. The proposed reconfigurable Huygens source is then used to feed a parallel-plate waveguide (PPW), where the power propagation direction could be manipulated in the horizontal plane. This reconfigurable Huygens source may pave an effective way in the development of new multi-functional radio frequency (RF) circuits and antennas in the future.

articleTitle: Beam Manipulation Using Characteristic Mode Analysis for Switchable Beam Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The operating mechanisms of a planar patch antenna with a parasitic strip is analyzed in this paper. The patch antenna uses a thin parasitic strip to realize beam deflection, which facilitates switchable beam. The beam deflection effect of the parasitic strip can be explained by using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). Specifically, the parasitic strip introduces a new mode that interacts with a fundamental broadside mode to generate the beam deflection. This insight provides a practical way to manipulate the resulting beam. As an example, it is used to increase the deflection angle by enhancing the new mode.

articleTitle: On the Phase Shift of a Microstrip Transmission Line Loaded with Magneto-Responsive Conducting Micro-Particles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work demonstrates a novel loading method for a printed microstrip transmission line using variable conductive particle manipulation controlled by magnetic fields. The conductive particle loading showed that the propagation characteristics of the transmission line could be changed, or tuned in the 2 GHz to 3 GHz band. The work presented in this paper is to provide an understanding of the particles' reaction to a measurable magnetic field density and the effect the particles have on the transmission lines propagation characteristics.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Printed Bow-Tie Antenna for Passive RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized printed Bow-tie antenna with meandered shape for passive tag Radio Frequency Identifications (RFID) applications. The proposed antenna has size reduction about 85% compared to a conventional bow-tie antenna. The antenna has a bandwidth (900-930MHz) covering North America band. This meandered bow-tie antenna has a shape as a dipole antenna. In addition, an RFID chip is used with this antenna and represented by its equivalent lumped element. Using HFSS software, the proposed antenna is designed and optimized, and good performances are achieved in terms of impedance matching and compactness.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Inspired Meandered Leaky-Wave Antenna with Fast Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar frequency-scanned antenna is presented, which uses meandered one-dimensional loaded transmission-line unit cells. This topology allows for significant control over scan range within a fixed bandwidth, including through broadside. Designs for the unit cell and the corresponding antenna are shown along with full-wave simulation results that demonstrate up to 88° of scan range through a 10% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Lightweight Deployable L-Band Patch Antenna Array for Ice Sounding
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-lightweight L-band patch antenna array is designed for the high sensitivity ground-based ice-sounding radar system. The antenna array achieves a realized gain of 29 dBi, which is benefit from the 2.88 m×1.44 m large aperture size. Despite its large size, the overall weight of the array including power dividers, cables and mechanical structures is only 36 kg and the thickness is less than 2 cm. The modulated design enables easy transportation to polar regions. For low-profile and wideband performance, U-slot air-substrate patch is used as single antenna element. The 16×8 large array operates from 1.17 to 1.48 GHz with a bandwidth of 310 MHz. Also, the antenna array is combined to 8 channels for the radar system, each channel can handle 2 kW peak power with customized power divider design. The antenna array was deployed in Antarctica in 2019 field season.

articleTitle: Reducing Beam Aberrations of Mechanical Scanning Transmit-array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: There is a new demand for high gain antennas capable of achieving wide-angle beam steering in the microwave and millimeter wave (mmW) regimes. This work focuses on transmit-array (TA) antennas that steer the beam using only in-plane displacement of the TA or feed. We showed in previous works that., for some applications., this solution can be a viable alternative to the more costly electronic beam steering of phased arrays. However., it is necessary to balance the trade-offs between several factors such as gain., beam aberrations., antenna size., maximum scanning angle and the complexity of the mechanical steering system. This communication surveys different techniques that we developed to improve the overall scanning performance of these antennas.

articleTitle: Thin Film Enabled Engineered Substrate for Miniaturized Antennas with Improved Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel engineered substrate enabled by patterned Permalloy (Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>, Py) thin films for the development of miniaturized antenna with improved bandwidth. The perspective substrate is implemented with multiple layers of 100 nm thick Py thin film patterns embedded on arbitrary microwave substrate, and each Py layer consists of an array of Py patterns with a dimension of 15μm×40μm and 5 μm gaps among them to suppress the magnetic loss. An equivalent permeability of 2.398 is achieved for engineered substrate embedding with 10 layers of Py thin films. A simple patch antenna has been implemented on the engineered substrate to demonstrate the efficacy of designing miniaturized antenna with improved bandwidth, compared to antenna on regular substrate, results show that the developed antenna on engineered substrate has a size reduction of 47.3% and an improved bandwidth of 49.6%.

articleTitle: Study on the Trend of the Sparsity of Phased Antenna Array Versus Steering Range
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Up to now, the sparse optimization has been widely used to reduce the active elements in antenna arrays for broadside radiation pattern. This work extends it to the synthesis of sparse phased array in order to achieve desired scanned pattern with as few elements as possible for 2-D beam steering. The performances of the sparse array and full array (uniformly spaced array with equidistance of 0.5λ) located in the same aperture are compared to explore the cost of saving elements. Meanwhile, the trend of the array sparsity versus steering range is investigated and further verified by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Stub-Based 6–18 GHz UWB Filter with Very Steep Rolloff for Radar Measurement Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass microstrip filter with short circuited stubs in order to transmit the signals within the range of 6-18 GHz, suitable for radar measurement Systems. The proposed filter is designed based on the seventh order Chebyshev method which enables the feasibility of the design. It also takes advantage of cascading techniques to provide a UWB response with extremely sharp rolloff. The final design shows a 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 110%, a passband insertion loss (IL) of less than 2 dB, group delay flatness of 0.2 ns, and a very steep roll-off (20 dB rejection level per 0.5 GHz).

articleTitle: Split-Ring Resonator Excited by a U-Shaped Transmission Line for Material Characterization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel microwave sensor for material characterization. The sensor is based on a split-ring resonator excited by the microstrip line technology. The sensor is a U-shaped two-port transmission line surrounding the split-ring resonator. Two-aluminum bars are added vertically on the resonator's gap to enhance the resonator's total capacitance, hence, the sensitivity. Compared to the normal transmission line, the U-shaped helps to increase the coupling between the microstrip line and the resonator. The design presents high sensitivity for low and high dielectric materials.

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Beam-Steerable Reflectarray with Independent Beam Control at X- and Ku-Bands
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reconfigurable reflectarrays (RAs) have attracted significant interest as affordable and relatively low-complexity beam scanning antennas for radar and satellite communication applications. We present a dual-band, beam-steerable RA capable of independent beam control at X and Ku bands based on a 1-bit polarization-rotating unit cell (PRUC). Two static versions of the RAs with different beam scanning scenarios are simulated, fabricated and measured. Good beam steering performance with independent beam control at each band is achieved.

articleTitle: A Two-Element Array Design of Dual-Band Quasi-Yagi Antenna With Reflector
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band Quasi-Yagi antenna and its planar and virtual array variations have been studied, and results are presented in this paper. The antenna operates at dual-band, and it contains a loop and a dipole geometry, which results in two different radiation characteristics. The array with a 1×2 element is proposed with two input ports and the virtual array is designed by using a copper plate reflector under the antenna structure. The gain and matching properties of the antenna have been studied to improve by modifying the antenna into a two-element array and the virtual array with a reflector element. The ECC (envelope correlation coefficient) graph is also presented and shows that the two input design antenna is a good candidate for a multiple-input system. Both numerical and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: A computer-aided design mobile phone model for antenna simulation benchmarking
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Computational electromagnetics tools are increasingly being adopted for the design and development of complex antenna systems. A minimum understanding of the numerical method implemented in a given computational tool is important to ensure meaningful simulation results. To help potential users-expert as well as non-expert-perform electromagnetic simulations of antennas with confidence, a draft recommended practice for computational electromagnetics applied to modeling and simulation of antennas is being developed. The recommended practice will define the concepts, techniques, benchmark models, validation procedures, uncertainties and limitations of computational electromagnetics techniques and tools used for modeling and simulation of antennas in free space. Herein a computer-aided design of a mobile phone model is proposed as an antenna simulation benchmark problem.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for the Synthesis of Planar Thinned Arrays with Sidelobes Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: By combining convex programming (CP) and genetic algorithms (GA), a hybrid method for the synthesis of excitations and locations of planar thinned arrays in order to minimize the side lobe level (SLL) is proposed and discussed in this paper. The approach takes definite advantage from the convexity of the problem with respect to excitation variables, and exploits a GA procedure as far as location variables are concerned. Through a suitable nesting of two optimization procedures, the overall problem can be formulated as a global optimization problem. Moreover, the method is very easy to implement, and it can reach the lowest SLL under the constraint of main lobe and limited number of array elements. Numerical results are conducted to validate the flexibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Feeding Structure for Wide-bandwidth Dual-polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cloverleaf-shaped wide-bandwidth dual-polarized antenna with novel balun is developed for passive radar systems in this paper. The antenna is designed to cover X and Ku bands (8 - 18 GHz), obtaining an impedance bandwidth of about 77%. The antenna gain is above 9 dBi over the operating frequency range. By using the printed-circuit-board technology, the radiating elements and feeding structure are conveniently fabricated and assembled with ease.

articleTitle: $4\times 4$ LTE MIMO Antenna Performance for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the last few years, MIMO (Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output) Cellular Antenna communication and high data streaming, have been developed and integrated into several vehicles lines by Automotive OEMs. The performance of Cellular Communication systems, in terms of uplink/downlink throughput is influenced by dynamic network factors such as Network traffic, time of day, network size, and location/environment. And, more recently 4×4 MIMO Cellular Communication are being developed for automotive applications to support 4G LTE Advanced Communication and subsequently 5G New Radio (NR) in an Over the Air (OTA) chamber Environment. This paper demonstrates MIMO Cellular Antenna performance OTA Chamber for 4×4 automotive Antenna system for various modulation schemes.

articleTitle: A New Application to the Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method for the Surface Plasmons
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Nowadays, there are lots of research on surface plasmons (SPs) due to a series of novel electromagnetic characteristics, such as remarkable near field enhancement effect, high sensitivity to dielectric environment. However, there are still great challenges for electromagnetic algorithms and commercial softwares to realize high precision and efficiency electromagnetic modeling for the SPs devices. It is necessary to deal with the complicated electromagnetic response mechanism of the metal materials in the SPs devices. Especially, the multiscale model has an important effect on time schemes. Although the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method has many advantages now, the explicit time scheme is constrained by the stability condition due to small size of fine meshes. Therefore, we propose three methods to improve present drawbacks of the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method in this paper. Firstly, we introduce the Generalized Nonlocal Optical Response (GNOR) mode into the DGTD method, then a new explicit time scheme by combining the Lawson method with a low-storage Runge-Kutta (LSRK) is used, finally, non-conformal region decomposition is used to realize the efficient electromagnetic modeling of the SPs device. Some numerical results show that the methods are feasible.

articleTitle: Sharply Defined UWB Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An UWB rectangular dielectric resonant antenna with sharply defined edge characteristic has been presented. In this design, the modified U -shaped feed structure is introduced to effectively widen the bandwidth of the dielectric antenna, and partial ground plane with rectangular slot is used for better impedance matching. As a result, the working frequency covering the UWB commercial frequency band requirements is obtained. Moreover, edge filtering characteristic for impedance bandwidth is achieved by loading a metal stub on the side of the antenna to enhance the selectivity of the antenna to the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Single-Source SIE for TE Electromagnetic Analysis of Penetrable Objects
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new single-source surface integral equation (SIE) is proposed to analyze the TE scattering by penetrable objects. In the SIE, a surface equivalent electric current density is derived through applying the equivalence theorem on the boundaries of penetrable objects and enforcing that tangential electric fields in the original and equivalent objects equal to each other. Compared with other dual source counterparts, which use both the electric and magnetic current densities, the proposed formulation only requires a single electric current source. At last, a numerical example validates its accuracy of the proposed formulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Microwave Absorber for Reduction of Radar Cross Section
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Nowadays, radar cross section (RCS) reduction is becoming more and more important in the military and civilian fields. In the work, we put forward a novel method to reduce RCS of the object by using the microwave absorber. The bandwidth of our absorber design reaches 14.63 GHz, from 3.37 GHz to 18 GHz. Additionally, the minimum reflection loss is -14.42 dB at 5.14 GHz and the total thickness is 3 mm. When our design is put on a PEC cylinder, it also has a good performance both for horizontally illumination and vertically polarized illumination. In a word, our absorber design is an effective way to achieve RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Design of a Electro-mechanically Tunable Low-Loss Mm-wave Phase-shifting Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a novel electro-mechanically tunable reflection phase-shifting metasurface at millimetre-wave frequencies is presented. In this paper, an unconventional phase-shifting approach with a variable air cavity between a periodic surface and a ground plane is presented, that provides enhanced reflection phase-shifting bandwidth in both TE and TM polarizations. Simulations have been carried out using CST Microwave Studio to evaluate the reflection response and the tunability of the proposed metasurface. Simulations demonstrate a continuous 180° phase shift with an operating frequency band from 45 GHz to 65 GHz with extremely low reflection losses.

articleTitle: Closed-Form Design of Optimum Linear Arrays Based on Raised-Cosine Beampattern
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Linear arrays forming pencil beams with slowly decaying sidelobes make a good trade-off among excitation dynamic range ratio, beam efficiency, directivity, sidelobe level, and beamwidth. Popular arrays with such sidelobe behavior are Taylor, Gauss, Gegenbauer, and second-kind Chebyshev. In this paper, we propose a closed-form method for the design of pencil-beam arrays with a prescribed sidelobe level. The method exploits the leastsquares approximation of a raised cosine function in the azimuth domain, thus bringing the beampattern with slowly decaying sidelobes. For common numbers of excitation coefficients and sidelobe levels, the proposed arrays simultaneously exhibit the optimum beamwidth, dynamic range ratio, and directivity.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna Coupled Infrared Antimonide Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Dielectric Resonator Antenna Coupled Infrared Antimonide Photodetector (DRACAD) is presented. The large capture area of the DRA feeds incident radiation to the subwavelength dimension detector. The reduced dimension of the detector reduces the Noise Equivalent Power (NEP). The large capture area of the DRA increases the captured signal. The combination leads to high Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR). The DRACAD is designed using a Genetic Algorithm Optimization to obtain dimensions which maximize the absorbed infrared radiation with the smallest possible detector. The plasmonic metals are modeled as effective lossy sheet impedances. Absorption spectrum simulations between 8-12μm wavelengths show the DRACAD absorbs nearly 73% of the incident light at 9μm after all metal losses are accounted for.

articleTitle: Ultra-low Power Beamforming Wideband OFDM Signal with Active GRIN Lens at 19 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an active GRIN lens with a flat active frequency selective surface (FSS) for ultralow-power beamforming. The active FSS unit cell consists of an I-shaped metallic patch, a varactor diode, and bias lines to control the voltage across the diode. A five-layer FSS unit cell provides the phase range of 360° at 19 GHz. We fabricated the active gradient-index (GRIN) lens with 32×32 FSS unit cells, 5λ0×5λ0 at 19 GHz. The lens provides the ultralow-power beamforming in the ±40° range. Power consumption for single beamforming is approximately 5.2 μW. The 3-dB gain bandwidth of broadside beam is 15.8%. A 0.8-GHz OFDM signal was successfully steered with the lens. Measured average error vector magnitude (EVM) is about 10%.

articleTitle: A 2.45-GHz Frugal Dumbbell-Shaped Rectenna Built on Recyclable Substrates
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Biodegradable materials have amassed attention for frugal green electronics applications to better assist underserved communities. In this paper, we design a frugal radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting system as a low-cost power supply for low-power on-body sensors. The system involves a loaded dumbbell antenna integrated with a single diode rectifier. The dumbbell antenna is outfitted with loaded rings and a ground plane spaced A/4 away (viz. 2.45GHz). Indeed, both were fabricated using cardboard substrate and copper tape as a conductor. The measurements suggested that the rectenna exhibited an excellent RF performance as well as a good RF-to-DC conversion. That is, excellent S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>of less than -20 dB and a realized gain of 9 dBi and 15μW for 25μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> RF power density, which is the equivalent of a figure-of-merit (EFOM) of 11.7 dB. This design is very attractive due to the fact it can be used in rural area and the materials used to assemble the device can be later recycled for other purposes.

articleTitle: A Novel Low Loss E-Plane Substrate Integrated Waveguide Narrow Wall Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel low loss E-plane Substrate Integrated Waveguide narrow wall slot antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna operating frequency is centered at 18GHz and is built by soldering four printed circuit boards together as well as two copper sheets, one on the bottom that is solid and one on the top with slots cut in it. A waveguide has both vertical and horizontal current, copper strips are used for the horizontal current and plated vias are used for the vertical current. A short is placed at the end using the same method to create a standing wave.

articleTitle: Distributed Array Transmitter Spatial Coherence in Active Incoherent Millimeter-Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present measurements and analysis of the transmit pattern spatial coherence in active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging systems. Incoherent microwave and millimeter-wave imaging systems have recently attracted research interest due to their ability to generate imagery with reduced hardware requirements compared to coherent systems like phased arrays. Unlike traditional coherent systems and computational imaging where the knowledge of transmit radiation is very important, a newly-developed active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging does not require explicit knowledge of the transmit waveform, provided that the spatial coherence between points in the scene is sufficiently low. In this paper, we introduce a simple measurement to quantify the spatial coherence of waveform impinging on the scene. We present the basic theory and experimental results of the transmission of two noise transmitters.

articleTitle: Design Challenges of High Gain Broadband Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents challenges associated with the design of compact high gain broadband monopole antennas. In this article, we shall present various techniques that can be adopted to improve the gain and bandwidth performance of the monopole antenna. We have surveyed various techniques used to design miniaturized high gain broadband monopole antennas and analyzed each based on some figure of merit with the aim of identifying areas of improvement for each technique.

articleTitle: Lens antenna with a beam focused in azimuth and a sectorial beam in elevation in W band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As part of the development of a millimeter radar system for safety-related applications, a lens antenna operating at 94GHz was designed, simulated and measured. In order to satisfy the application, its radiation pattern had to be focused in azimuth plane with constraints on side-lobe level and sectorial in elevation plane while being simple to fabricate and robust. A horn antenna with a radiation pattern limiting the level of the side lobes was also developed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetically-Coupled Loops Based On Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A preliminary numerical magnetic field study of a wireless power transfer system composed of two interconnected source loops is addressed in this paper. The key feature of this study is to propose a new configuration capable of maintaining a uniform magnetic field density between the two loops. Furthermore, it has been shown that the Theory of Characteristic Modes is a helpful tool for investigating the near field of the magnetically-coupled loops.

articleTitle: Geometrical Optics Ray Tracing in a Thick Anisotropic Slab
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Geometrical optics (GO) analysis of an infinitely extended thick anisotropic slab is presented. At the point where a ray trace in the anisotropic medium is performed, half-space coefficients for an isotropic-anisotropic interface are determined and field contributions from different orders of reflection and refraction are evaluated.

articleTitle: 40-65 GHz Dual-beam Dual-Band Tunable Microstrip CRLH Leaky-wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a composite right/left-handed (CRLH) dual-beam microstrip leaky-wave antenna (MLWA) with tunable operating region for V-band radiation coverage. Primarily, the symmetrical side-by-side dual-beam is obtained by the wideband excitation for second higher order mode within 52.5-65 GHz, and also realizes a pair of back to back half-modes generating two symmetrical side beams in E-plane with enhanced gain over 40-52 GHz with appropriate placement of metallic via holes. Mode switching is performed electronically by incorporating PIN diodes and proper biasing network. Finally, incorporating half-sinusoidal interdigital slot variations and periodically placed switching diodes enables composite right/left-handed media having frequency beam steering from backward-broadside-forward quadrant. Leaky bands in microstrip higher order modes were analyzed by dispersion characteristics, and the proposed antenna achieved -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 29.2%, scanning range in H-plane from -65° to +69.7°, and peak gain of 18.7 dBi for the unbiased state; and 28%, -78° to +69.6° and 18 dBi, respectively for the biased state. The average side lobe level and minimum cross polar level are obtained as 13.5 dB and 23 dB, respectively. The fabricated prototype responses closely matched theoretical predictions, verifying the proposed concept.

articleTitle: A Wideband MIMO Antenna with Fixed and Reconfigurable Band Notch Characteristics for UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a miniaturized ultrawideband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)/diversity antenna with fixed and reconfigurable band-stop/notch functionality is presented. The proposed MIMO elements exhibit an impedance match <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert < -10\ \text{dB}$</tex>, for the frequency band of 3.1 – 12 GHz. Enhanced isolation of above 20 dB is obtained between antenna elements by using circular slotted decoupling structure. To achieve reconfigurable WLAN (5.5 GHz) band notch characteristics, PIN-Diodes are inserted in horizontal stubs at ground plane. Fixed band notch is achieved for interference mitigation at downlink X-band satellite (7.5 GHz). Moreover, the simulated as well as measured results are in desired limits.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic radiation pressure at the liquid-vapour interface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conflicting formalisms for dielectric electromagnetic momentum and stress are implemented in a simulation engine to simulate radiation pressure on a nanometric single-component multiphase fluid. Non-relativistic deformations of the liquid-vapour interface, simulated using the pseudopotential Lattice-Boltzmann-method, are distinct for each formalism. These distinct deformations suggest optical pressure on liquids and gases may be used to empirically validate a single electrodynamic theory to describe light momentum in dielectrics.

articleTitle: A New Array Formation Method for Millimeter-wave Transverse Slot Scanning Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new array formation method for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) transverse slot scanning array antenna is proposed, which can effectively solve the grating lobes problem caused by the traditional array formation method. To verify the array formation method, a mm-wave scanning array antenna at 30GHz is designed, which consists of a traditional substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) 4 × 4 Butler Matrix (BM) feed network and 16 transverse slot elements. The distance between adjacent transverse slot elements is equal to half waveguide wavelength, and the transverse slot array antenna uses the metal cylinder matching method to improve the effective bandwidth of the array antenna, a -10dB impedance bandwidth (BW) of scanning array antenna from 28.9 to 31.04 GHz is simulated. The peak broadside gain of the array antenna is 13.7dB. This type of transverse slot scanning array antenna will have many applications in the future 5G mm-wave band.

articleTitle: Fully Printed and Electrically Small Folded Dipole with Inherent Matching
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A highly miniaturized fully printed folded dipole antenna suitable for narrowband applications has been designed. The input impedance of the antenna was engineered by varying the loading reactances in order to achieve inherent matching with respect to a given source impedance. Additionally, compared to a discrete lumped implementation, the printed topology allows realization of slightly larger bandwidth, however at the expense of radiation efficiency. The designed miniaturized antenna was fabricated and validated using measurements.

articleTitle: Amplitude and Phase Discretization Influence on Performance of Complex Amplitude Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Complex amplitude holography can be applied to calculate complete electromagnetic field information in the holographic plane, including amplitude and phase, so as to achieve high-precision image reconstruction. Complex amplitude metasurfaces, as ultra-thin and ultra-flat electromagnetic wave regulation elements, have opened a new path for the physical implementation of holograms. However, due to coupling between meta-atoms and manufacturing tolerance, it is impractical to accurately encode holographic metasurfaces. The solution is to reduce the number of different meta-atoms by discretizing amplitude and phase on the holographic plane. Here, we analyze and compare the imaging quality of different complex amplitude holographic metasurfaces in various discretization strategies. Numerical results indicate that reasonable discretization process can simplify the metasurfaces design and achieve well-performing image reconstruction.

articleTitle: Calibration and Synchronization of Software-Defined-Radio Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Software-defined radio (SDR) arrays require synchronization of separate SDR devices. This paper presents experimental results for an SDR array calibration procedure with automated phase and amplitude calibration of both transmitter and receiver chains, permitting coherent operation of a duplex SDR array.

articleTitle: Experimental Rician $K$-factor characterization in a laboratory environment at the 25 to 40 GHz frequency band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, an analysis of the Rician K-factor in a laboratory environment from 25 to 40 GHz has been carried out. The variation of the estimated K-factor has been assessed in frequency from a channel measurements campaign in both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-LOS (NLOS) conditions. Mean values of the K-factor ranging from 0.48 to 3.43 dB for LOS conditions, and from -5.54 to -0.56 dB for NLOS conditions, have been derived. The results reported here enable us to get insight into the propagation channel characteristics and can be of interest to evaluate the performance of fifth-generation (5G) networks in laboratory environments.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive and Transparent FSS for Flexible Electronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a polarization-insensitive, dual-band FSS reflector with a 45° maximum stable incident angle. A novel design, which evolved from fractal cross dipoles, is presented for GSM bands shielding. Due to the quadruple symmetry structure, the response of the proposed FSS is consistent for both TE and TM incident waves. A prototype, realized through a custom silver nanowires based transparent ink on a flexible PET sheet, demonstrates over 80% optical transparency. Simulations and measurements are in agreement, showing good reflection performance from 0.71 to 1.25 GHz and from 1.73 to 2.16 GHz. The printed FSS is a good candidate for various shielding applications in flexible transparent electronics.

articleTitle: A bifunctional reflector based on the chiral metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurfaces have attracted considerable attention due to their powerful abilities in electromagnetic wave manipulation and their easy fabrication. However, metasurface for circularly polarized waves with spin selective absorption characteristics has been less discussed. In this paper, an asymmetric chiral resonator lacking the mirror symmetry plane is studied, which presents different reflection properties for left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) and right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) waves. According to the theory of Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase, a bifunctional reflector based on the chiral unit is designed, which converts incident RHCP waves into vortex waves without changing handedness, while it absorbs incident LHCP waves. Full wave simulations are performed to validate the bifunctional performances of the metasurface. Such chiral metasurface paves the way to spin selective modulation of wavefronts, and present broad application prospects in the field of planar electromagnetic devices and communications.

articleTitle: Using Evanescent Plane Waves as Free Parameters in Array Design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A generalized Poisson summation formula produces an explicit expression for the surface current on a plane that radiates a set of preselected plane waves. When only a finite number of plane waves are specified, the surface current is a continuous function. If an infinite number of plane waves are specified, the surface current can degenerate into a discrete set of line sources. In such situations, the expression for the surface current determines both the location and strength of the line sources that radiate the infinite set of plane waves. One can specify both propagating and evanescent plane waves. The evanescent plane waves can be used as free parameters to reduce the imaginary power.

articleTitle: Characteristic Modes of Circular Conducting Plate with Zernike Polynomials as Entire-Domain Basis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper studies the use of entire-domain basis functions constructed with the Zernike polynomials to evaluate the characteristic modes of a circular conducting plate. Some new mathematical relations of the Zernike polynomials are discovered, which allows the generalized impedance matrix to be obtained in a completely analytical manner without the need of meshing or numerical integrations. This new approach is stable and efficient, and its validity is verified by comparing to the results produced by the common RWG sub-domain basis functions.

articleTitle: A Dual-Axis Interferometric Radar for Instantaneous 2D Angular Velocity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A complex correlation interferometric radar utilizing two orthogonal baselines to simultaneously measure the angular velocity of a moving target in two dimensions is presented. Measurements were conducted using a 40.5 GHz continuous-wave radar achieving an accuracy of 0.55 to 2.55%.

articleTitle: A Chipless RFID Tag Antenna Based on Surface Acoustic Wave
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio frequency identification (RFID) technique is a kind of wireless automatic identification technology. This technique has several advantages, i.e., long reading distance and large information storage. We propose a Chipless RFID tag using surface acoustic wave (SAW) to read and store the information. The tag features small size, high flexibility, strong radiation resistance, high consistency, repeatability, as well as high temperature stability. The simulation results by COMSOL verify the good performance of the tag antenna.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Dually Polarized Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband dually polarized transmitarray of tightly coupled dipoles is presented. The array exhibits an operational bandwidth of 6.2:1 for broadside, maintaining active <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 3$</tex>. Tightly coupled dipoles are used both as receiving and transmitting elements. To introduce the required phase shift at the transmitarray's elements, delay lines are used connecting the receiving and transmitting elements. The delay lines cut through a common perforated ground plane placed between the receive and transmit elements.

articleTitle: Dumbbell and Double elliptical printed slot antennas for wideband applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband dumbbell shape slot antenna in the frequency range of 5.21-8.46 GHz and double elliptical shape slot in the frequency range of 4.49-8.7 GHz are designed. Dumbbell slot provides 47.5% bandwidth (BW) for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤ -10 dB and maximum gain of 3.2 dBi at 6.56 GHz and double elliptical slot provides 63.8% BW for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤ -10 dB with maximum gain of 6.8 dBi at 5.1 GHz. Dumbbell Slot has dimensions of 0.52λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×1.17λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and double elliptical has dimensions of 0.38λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.88λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at 5.8 GHz. The designed antennas are fabricated and simulated results are validated with measured results.

articleTitle: Depolarization of a V-band (72 GHz) Circularly Polarized Beacon Signal Due to Tropospheric Weather Events
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present depolarization effects of various hydrometeors at the V-band (72 GHz) in Albuquerque, New Mexico during the 2018-2019 time period. The correlation between rain rate and the degradation of the cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) is calculated. The average XPD will first be found using clear sky cases and then deviations from that value will be calculated using cases where precipitous hydrometeors were present. The preliminary results presented here will contribute to an increased understanding of depolarization effects at extremely high frequencies (EHF, 30-300 GHz).

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a compact Double Ridged Horn Antenna for Ultra-Wide band Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microwave Imaging (MWI) is an emerging and noninvasive technique that offers a promising alternative method of breast screening. A new Double Ridged Horn (DRH) antenna to be used in an MWI system for the detection of breast cancer is presented.
