The developed DRH antenna is smaller than 30% of the traditional DRH antennas and has good performances suitable for MWI system.

articleTitle: Passband Tunable Frequency Selective Surface for a Pulsed Radiator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a preliminary design for a high-power, tunable resonant radiator. The device is composed of an Impulse Radiating Antenna integrated with a tunable Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) in the UHF band. By changing the separation between the components of the unit cells, a passband FSS with a tunability of around 300 MHz is obtained. The device can be used as a source for IEMI/EMC testing.

articleTitle: Error Analysis of 3D Simplex Interpolation Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The three-dimensional (3D) simplex interpolation method, which only uses the same shape and size of tetrahedrons for all points, is proposed. The maximum and root-means-square (RMS) errors are analyzed for the proposed simplex, traditional simplex and Lagrange interpolations. The interpolation regions are chosen basing on the smallest interpolation error or simpler numerical implementation. Numerical results verified that the proposed simplex interpolation makes the interpolation simple, easy to be implemented, and more efficient.

articleTitle: Conformal loop antenna for an active drug delivery device operating at 900 MHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Drug delivery devices have been widely considered for the treatment of chronic ailments as they can provide physicians the capability of controlling key therapy indexes. An active device consists of a RF system that can be triggered wirelessly to release drug formulations from the device. In this paper, a conformal loop antenna is designed around the outer wall of a reservoir. The device structure and placement of antenna are also elucidated. The CST Gustav voxel human body model is used to perform numerical study of the antenna to investigate its performance for implantable applications. According to the simulation results, the proposed conformal antenna has shown reflection coefficient of -19.68 dB at the desired frequency of 900 MHz. The concept of electro-thermal process for disintegrating the reservoir membrane is also discussed.

articleTitle: Dual-band Four-beam Generator Base on 2-bit Reflective Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The coding metasurface has received widespread attention in recent years. It links the traditional electromagnetic phase metasurface with digital signals, and realizes a powerful electromagnetic wave manipulation ability. In this work, a dual-band 2-bit reflective coding metasurface is designed. For a design example, a dual-band four-beam generator is implemented by giving a proper encoding to the proposed metasurface through the signal processing algorithm. The four-beam generator is fed by horn antenna and the simulation results are in consistent with the design goals. This work can be applied to the future wireless communication.

articleTitle: TETRA Coverage Assessment by Using Position Messages
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the coverage of a TETRA network was assessed using information from the system itself. Geolocation information is continuously being sent from the mobile devices operating in the network. We show how a collection of this data can be used for characterizing the coverage over a geographical area which presents high orographic complexity.

articleTitle: Throughput Enhancement of $2\times 2$ MIMO system Using a Novel Wideband Neutralization Line
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel wideband decoupling technique is proposed in this paper to improve the performance of a 2×2 multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) system. To achieve wideband decoupling, a stepped neutralization line is employed in conjunction with specially engineered ground plane to enhance the isolation between the two monopole antennas. The throughput of the proposed coupled and decoupled antennas is measured in a MIMO system and it is found that the proposed decoupling technique helps to increase the throughput of the decoupled antenna in comparison with the coupled antenna. The proposed antenna can be used for 5G (3.3-4.2 GHz, 4.4-5GHz), WLAN (3.6 GHz, 5.1-5.8 GHz), LTE (3.4-3.8 GHz, 5.15-5.925 GHz) and WiMAX (4.9-5.8 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Band Gap and Absorption Properties of High-Impedance Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) and absorption properties of high impedance structure (HIS) have been analyzed. These properties have been derived by using surface impedance method and transient resonance methods. The analysis is carried out in the ANSYS HFSS software 19.0. For HIS with vias radius of 0.01 mm and 0.05 mm, the overlapping of absorption band and EBG are obtained as 1.16 GHz and 1.25 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: SIW Antenna for 5G In-Band Full Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip fed, double differential antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology for In-Band Full Duplex communication at 28 GHz. Using higher order TE201 mode of the SIW cavity and differential port excitations, the proposed antenna achieves a self-interference cancellation of better than -77 dB over a 210 MHz bandwidth and a high gain of 8.2 dBi. Occupying a miniaturized size of 7.56 ×7.56 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the antenna features a radiation efficiency of 77% and front to back ratio of 19 dB.

articleTitle: Electromagetic Wave Scattering by Metal Structured Surface with an Infinite Periodic Array of Subwavelength Rectangular Grooves Partially Filled with an Optically Plasma Induced Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the author theoretically investigates electromagnetic plane wave scattering by perfect electric conductor (PEC) structured surface with an infinite periodic array of subwavelength rectangular grooves partially filled with an optically plasma induced semiconductor with very narrow array periodicity, using classical mode matching technique. The author theoretically discusses about the electromagnetic wave absorption characteristic caused by the interaction between photo-induced plasma and the surface plasmon-like wave on the PEC structured surface for application to radar cross section reduction.

articleTitle: THz Leaky-Wave Antenna Beam Steering With Low Loss Dynamic Tuning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Piezo-Electric Actuator (PEA) based electromechanically tunable Partially Reflective Surface (PRS) is proposed for high efficiency terahertz (THz) antenna beam steering. A phase shift of about 40° is achieved the by varying the mechanical separation between the PRS metasurface and ground layer. A high gain (18dBi) Leaky-Wave Antenna (LWA) is designed at 280 GHz band with 18<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> beam steering. The presented phase shifting technique offers an extremely low loss solution for antenna beam steering at THz frequencies.

articleTitle: Spatial Image Segmentation for Breast Cancer Detection in Terahertz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a new spatial image segmentation algorithm for breast cancer detection in terahertz (THz) images of freshly excised human tumors. Region classifications of fresh tissue with 3 or more regions, such as cancer, fat, and collagen, remain a challenge for cancer detection. We propose to tackle this problem by exploiting the spatial correlation among neighboring pixels in THz images, that is, pixels that are close to each other are more likely to belong to the same region. The spatial correlation among pixels is modeled by using Markov random fields (MRF). A Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with expectation maximization (EM) is then used to represent the statistical distributions of the THz images in both the frequency and spatial domain. Experiment results demonstrated that the proposed spatial image segmentation algorithm outperforms existing algorithms that do not consider spatial information.

articleTitle: Compact Wide-Band Dual-Polarized Rectangular Slot Antenna for mm-Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact size, wide-band, and dual-polarized rectangular slot antenna for 5G mobile phones is proposed. A rectangular slot and two feeding structures are used to realize wide bandwidth and dual polarization. Vertical polarization (V-pol) mode is excited by a coplanar waveguide (CPW), and horizontal polarization (H-pol) mode is excited by a microstrip line. It has -10 dB impedance bandwidths of 14.3 GHz (26.2-40.5 GHz) for V-pol and 14.0 GHz (26.0-40.0 GHz) for H-pol. The maximum gains of V-pol in 28 GHz and 39 GHz are 4.47 dBi and 3.79 dBi, respectively. Similarly, the maximum gains of H-pol are 3.51 dBi and 3.89 dBi, respectively. It has cross polarization level better than 20 dB. The characteristic of the antenna verified through measurements and simulations shows that this rectangular slot antenna design has the advantages of compact size, wide bandwidth, and dual polarization.

articleTitle: Explicit Solution of Time Domain Scalar Potential Surface Integral Equations for Penetrable Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An explicit time marching scheme is developed to solve a system of time domain surface integral equations enforced on homogeneous penetrable objects for scalar potential and its normal derivative. This system is cast in the form of an ordinary differential equation (ODE) and unknowns are expanded using high-order nodal functions. Inserting these expansions into the ODE and applying point-testing (Nyström method) yield a system in time-dependent coefficients of the unknown expansions. This system is integrated in time using a predictor-corrector algorithm to yield the expansion coefficients. The resulting explicit time marching scheme uses the same time step size as its implicit counterpart without sacrificing the stability of the solution and is almost three times faster for low frequency excitations.

articleTitle: Co-polarized Retrodirective Array with Active Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Four-arm spirals are proposed for use in an active Van Atta array configuration with co-polarized simultaneous transmit and receive in mind. Retrodirective behavior is observed out to 60° at the analysis frequency with active circuit gain possible up to a limit, related to the transmit-receive coupling. Additionally, retrodirection generally increases at a faster rate than specular reflection as circuit gain is increased.

articleTitle: Disposable Microwave Sensor for Real-time Monitoring and Content Sensing of Droplets in Microfluidic Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel chemical sensor with zero power consumption is presented for real-time, non-contact, and noninvasive droplet characterization within the microchannel. The proposed microwave-microfluidic device demonstrates the capability of performing droplet detection as well as sensing of an individual droplet content. The platform is based on a chipless flexible microwave resonator tag coupled to a reader for introducing a technique to reduce the dependency of the coupling to the distance. The performance of the microwave-microfluidic sensor has been validated when mineral oil is used as the continuous phase. The sensor demonstrates highly selective identification results when deionized water and acetone are used to generate droplets required to be detected.

articleTitle: A Beam-steerable Slotted Waveguide Antenna With Tunable Impedance Walls
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we describe the design and development of a novel beam-steerable slotted waveguide antenna which simplifies the process of phase-shifting between consecutive array elements by using impedance walls on the two sides of a waveguide. The leaky-wave antenna is capable of steering the beam from 17<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> to 73<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> by changing the voltage from 11 Volts to 2.8 Volts. The voltage changes the capacitance of varactors located on the two side-impedance walls from 0.2 pF to 0.5 pF. The waveguide slotted antenna is 420 mm long and has 36 loaded H-shaped slots. The antenna operates at 9.2 GHz. It has a maximum gain of 15.5 dB and its half-power beamwidth is 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of 3D Metamaterial Unit Cells for Broadband and Wide Field of View RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The framework of coding metasurfaces provides a method to achieve RCS reduction via phase-based scattering using the concepts of interfering PEC and PMC scatterers. Typically, coding metasurface unit cells are designed and fabricated as planar structures, and, as a result, the achievable field of view is limited. However, by extending the unit cell design to three dimensions, which can be realized with the aid of additive manufacturing, it is possible to design coding metasurfaces for wide field of view (FOV) and broadband RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Tunable Broadband Terahertz Metamaterial Absorbers Based on VO2
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a vanadium dioxide (VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) based broadband THz metamaterial absorber is presented. We verify by full-wave simulations the broadband absorptivity of the proposed absorber dramatically varies as a function of the VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>'s THz electrical conductivity which experiences a three orders of magnitude increase during an insulator-to-metal transition (IMT). The proposed metamaterial absorbers are capable offering strong modulation of THz radiation over a broad frequency band.

articleTitle: Gegenbauer Arrays with Minimum Dynamic Range Ratio and Maximum Beam Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Abstracf-Antenna arrays based on Gegenbauer polynomials are a generalization of Chebyshev and Legendre arrays. The generalization is characterized by an adjustable polynomial's parameter. This parameter allows the optimum design of Gegenbauer arrays. For a given sidelobe level, the Gegenbauer arrays with minimum beamwidth and maximum directivity have already been developed. In this paper, we present the design of the Gegenbauer arrays with minimum dynamic range ratio and maximum beam efficiency. The former design is based on a simple search, whereas the latter is given in a closed form.

articleTitle: Capacitive Cloaking Technique for Antenna Elements in Multi-Band Array Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A capacitance-based interference mitigation technique for multi-band dual-polarized base station antenna arrays is presented for microwave frequencies. Improved radiation characteristics such as gain, front-to-back ratio, and cross polarization discrimination can be achieved through utilization of this design technique. Simulation results utilizing this versatile technique applied to dipoles operating from 0.698-0.894 GHz and 1.695-2.180 GHz, and dipole feed stems operating from 1.695-2.700 GHz are demonstrated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 1.7$</tex> in two different array environments.

articleTitle: On the Design on Triple-band Flexible Antenna for Modern Wireless Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of triple-band flexible antenna for modern wireless application including, but not limited to, WiMAX, WLAN, RFID, and 5G application. The design of the antenna is printed on Vinyl flexible substrate of 4.4 dielectric constant and 0.47mm of thickness. The bandwidth of the antenna is extended as follow: band1 extends from 2.38GHz to 2.6GHz, band2 extends from 2.9GHz to 3.34GHz and band3 expands from 4.9GHz to 5.04GHz. The antenna possesses considerable realized gain of around ldB in each bandwidth. The triple-band antenna is suitable for future compact slim wireless devices where miniaturized size and reasonable performance are required.

articleTitle: Design of Unintuitive Antenna Geometries Using Additive Manufacturing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using 3D printing, it is possible to create antenna geometries which are not practically feasible through traditional subtractive manufacturing techniques. There are numerous possible ways to design these geometries, such as body of revolution or extrusion methods. With the aid of multiobjective optimization, these structures can be designed for various goals. Examples include wide bandwidth, high gain, strong circular polarization, and compact size. Additionally, 3D printed antennas can offer reduced cost and weight without compromising these performance goals.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Polarized Log-Periodic Antenna with Embedded Balun Impedance Transformer
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a wideband, over-2-octave bandwidth dual-polarized, unidirectional, log-periodic antenna with integrated impedance transformer balun is presented. The aim is to demonstrate a low-cost configuration for spectrum sensing over wide field-of-view as well as other applications such as communications and direction finding. Therefore, 3d printing was considered and important structural changes within the antenna structure, such as the use of rebars, are made to ensure reliable fabrication while maintaining good electrical performance. An impedance transforming balun is integrated in the booms of the two sets of arms to achieve match to 50 ohms. The antenna is silver painted and unidirectional performance with stable radiation patterns is achieved.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of MACKEY with improved operation on metal
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A meta-surface inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), which operates in a free space and on a metal plate, is proposed herein. The improved operation on metal is proposed to occur via change in the substrate vertical width W.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging System for In-Line Security Assessment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The accidental foreign bodies contamination is still a major issue for food manufacturing industries. The continuous growth of automation along production lines together with the increasing attention of the customers towards food products quality, improved the industries care aiming to avoid complaints and ensure the best possible quality. As a matter of fact, several technologies are employed, but they lack in detecting certain class of contaminants, such as low-density plastics or small glass fragments that could turn into a severe threat, in particular for children. This work proposes a microwave imaging system in order to overcome these limitation in employed technologies. The design and characterization are reported in this paper; the simulations are addressed to the realization of a system prototype.

articleTitle: Design of a Microstrip Rectenna for WLAN Wireless Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microstrip rectenna for WLAN wireless energy harvesting is proposed in this paper. The rectenna is composed of a microstrip antenna and a rectifier. The operating frequency of the receiving microstrip antenna is from 2.418GHz to 2.458GHz which the reflection coefficient is below -10dB. The circuit of rectifier is based on single stage double voltage rectifying structure. The working bandwidth of the rectifier is 40MHz. When the input power is -15dBm and the load resistance is 4KΩ, the output voltage of the rectenna at 2.44GHz is 0.11V.

articleTitle: RFID Tag Antenna Design for ARC Specs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we explain how to design a UHF RFID tag antenna for ARC requirements, which are industry tag certification specifications. We focus on a 50 mm×30 mm tag design that passes specs A through I. We explain how to model tag performance on complicated items that are part of ARC specs (such as jeans), and present modeling and simulation results which are in good agreement with measured data.

articleTitle: An Interdigitated Structure-Based, Electrically Small Dipole Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband, electrically small dipole antenna with stable radiation performance is presented. Inspired by recently reported metasurface antennas, a coax-fed dipole antenna with periodic patches acting as near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) elements is first developed. It exhibits operating mechanisms identical to those of the metasurface antennas and, thus, realizes a wide bandwidth and stable radiation patterns across it. Introducing interdigitated structures into the NFRP elements, an electrically small version is realized. A 14.4%, −10-dB fractional impedance bandwidth is achieved along with a stable realized gain, ∼ 1.5 dBi, over it. The antenna has potential applications in future wideband space-limited systems.

articleTitle: Non-Foster Self-Oscillating Huygens Radiator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A recently proposed concept of a self-oscillating non-Foster antenna is extended to a Huygens radiator. The system is comprised of two orthogonal pairs of electric and magnetic near-field parasitic radiators, each of which is driven by a small electric dipole. The input ports of the driving dipoles are connected to a floating negative impedance converter, thus forming a broadly-tunable and nearly perfectly matched self-oscillating system. The developed concept is verified with a series of full-wave/circuit theory (CST/ADS) co-simulations. Obtained results reveal self-oscillations that can be tuned within a 1: 1.5 frequency range, with familiar cardioid radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Four-Element Polarization-Reconfigurable MIMO Antenna using Fluidics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A four-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array with circular polarization reconfigurability (CPR) is proposed for the 2400 MHz band. It achieves CPR using 8 fluidic circuits that can be driven by a single fluidic switch. The antenna element is a square patch loaded at the corners with short circuited λ/4 stubs. Fluidic loading of the stubs provides asymmetric loads at the corners for CPR. The −10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW), minimum isolation, axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) are 100 MHz, 13.5 dB, and, 12 MHz for both left-handed (LH) and right-handed (RH) CP modes. The worst case ECC is ≤ 0.27 showing good MIMO performance.

articleTitle: A New Design Technique for Broadband Bull's Eye Antennas at low THz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a planar corrugated antenna (Bull's Eye) for operation around at low THz is proposed. The feeding mechanism is a tapered waveguide aperture, which offers a broadband matching performance. A novel design technique of gain bandwidth enhancement is proposed, which exploits the depth qualities of the corrugated unit cells. Simulated results of the novel antenna show a peak realized gain of 19.8 dBi at 292 GHz and 3-dB bandwidth of 8.9%.

articleTitle: Low Cost Millimetre-Wave Scale Model RCS Characterisation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel, low cost, high accuracy, high frequency radar cross section characterization method using commercially available, off-the-shelf hardware working in the millimeter-wave frequency range of 77-81GHz. Our approach demonstrates a number of key advantages over traditional methods at only a fraction of the cost. We also present a comparison of the monostatic RCS results of two wind turbine designs, and demonstrate good agreement between our simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: A Switchable Circular Polarizer based on Active Metasurface at 30 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a switchable circular polarizer based on varactor-loaded metasurface is proposed. With an incident wave of 45° linear polarization (LP) plane wave, the polarization of the transmission wave through this polarizer can be switched between left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) and right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) by controlling the bias voltage of the varactors. Simulation results show that the designed circular polarizer exhibits transmission loss better than -1 dB, and phase error within ±5° in frequency band 29.4 - 30.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Imaging of Walking Human Behind the Wall Using Impulse Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the imaging of walking human behind the wall utilizing UWB pulsed radar technique. Using the pulsed radar, the range profile of waking human behind the wall is provided for tracking a walking human. A series of image processing, such as time-gating, matched filtering, and envelope detection, is applied and therefore the 3D image is successfully reconstructed.

articleTitle: A Vibration Resistant GNSS Antenna with Reduced Size and Weight for Wideband Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a low profile, lightweight and wideband GNSS antenna implementation whose structural design is strengthened to withstand the vibration arisen from space launch vehicles. The proposed antenna mainly aims to meet all functional and physical requirements to cover the frequency bands of all known navigation satellite constellations (1.164-1.610 GHz) with minimized weight in a limited volume on the satellite platform. In accordance with this purpose, a right-hand circularly polarized crossed bowtie dipole antenna is designed, fabricated and measured. Although miniaturization of antennas is known to decrease operational bandwidth, the measurement results showing a good agreement with the simulation results indicate that the presented antenna covers all GNSS frequency bands with a satisfactory performance. The manufactured antenna is also exposed to vibration tests and the measured functional performance of the antenna after test is quite consistent with initial state.

articleTitle: Remote Antenna Impedance Measurement
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Due to the comparable size of the feeding cable to the original device and the induced current on the outer surface of the cable, the electrically small antenna (ESA) input impedance measurement using a network analyzer is a debatable technique. A remote impedance measurement technique is therefore implemented using an electrostatic discharge (ESD) to excite the ESA and remotely measure the ESA's terminated impulse response to three standard loads, short - open - matched load. The ESA's input impedance is evaluated based on three corresponding impulse responses, treating the measurement system as a three-port network and incorporating the advantage of microwave network analysis and the impulse responses resulting from the derived complex natural resonances (CNRs). To confirm the proposed technique, the input impedance of different antennas is directly measured via a network analyzer as well as a remote measurement technique, and the results are compared.

articleTitle: 3D Trajectories of Multiple Untagged Flying Insects from Millimetre-wave Beamscanning Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report the tracking of untagged flying insects using a millimetre-wave Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave radar. Flight trajectories were derived with a Multiple Input Multiple Output radar front-end and a mechanical beamscanning. In contrast to existing approaches, such as the harmonic radar, our novel method does not require a transponder or tag on the insects, provides 3D flight trajectories, and enables to track multiple individuals simultaneously. For illustration purpose, we reconstructed the 3D flight trajectories of two untagged bumblebees flying in a big outside tent.

articleTitle: SDR-based Psuedo-Doppler AoA Estimation for Low Duty Cycle Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Pseudo-Doppler (PD) is a powerful technique for Angle of Arrival (AoA) estimation for single-channel systems. In the application of collared animal tracking considered within, the VHF transmitting beacon is enabled for a very low duty cycle such as 2 percent. This low duty cycle presents several unique design challenges that are addressed in the revised PD algorithm. PD is then implemented using the LimeMini-SDR for a four-element antenna array. The resulting system delivers accurate AoA estimates for duty cycles approaching 1 percent.

articleTitle: Electronically Controlled Unit Cell for Single Layer Reconfigurable Reflect-array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ahstract-A novel varactor loaded unit cell for reconfigurable single-layer reflectarray antenna is proposed in this work. The unit cell consists of a varactor loaded conducting pattern printed on the substrate over a ground plane. The phase of the reflected wave is varied by changing voltage across the varactor diode. By tuning varactor diode between 0.02 pF to 0.25 pF we can achieve the phase agility of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}$</tex> at the design frequency of 11 GHz. Despite single layer, the unit cell shows excellent characteristics in terms of phase range, figure of merit, reflection loss, and bandwidth. The proposed unit cell has a unique and novel geometry which attributes to its excellent radiation characteristics. The designed unit-cell structure is a good candidate for low cost and low profile reconfigurable reflectarray antenna designs.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Broadband High-Gain Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna Using Novel Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual broadband antenna with circular polarization (CP) for small satellite application is proposed. A new slotted metasurface with dual band characteristic is introduced. Further, by perturbing the patch radiator with two slits, a dual band CP radiation is realized at 5 GHz and 5.9 GHz with a small frequency ratio of 1:1.18. The measured axial ratio bandwidths (ARBW) are 8.6% and 2.3% at lower and upper band, respectively. The measured gain is 6.3±0.9 dBi and 6.1±0.6 dBi in the lower and upper band respectively. The measured results are consistent with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Modeling of Volume Scattering in Bicontinuous Random Medium for Remote Sensing of Terrestrial Snow from 4 to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we study the snow aggregation and its effects on the frequency dependence of snow volume scattering from C to Ku band (4-18GHz) with the bicontinuous model. The snow microstructures are modeled by the bicontinuous model. The snow size distribution and aggregation are quantified by the bicontinuous correlation function which then gives the spectral density of snow. The phase matrix of snow is derived from the volume integral equation based on the Born approximation (BA). The phase matrix is proportional to the spectral density of snow. Finally, the scattering coefficients are expressed in terms of the phase matrix. The results show that snow with more aggregation has faster decay spectral density leading to a weaker frequency dependence than that of Rayleigh scattering from C to Ku band. The scattering coefficients computed with BA, and the numerical solution of Maxwell equation in 3D (NMM3D) gives similar frequency dependence of ~2.6 power. In addition, scattering coefficients of BA and NMM3D are also in good agreement from X to Ku band.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Antena With Bandpass Filtering Response
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel dual circularly polarized filtering antenna by seamlessly integrating a substrate integrated waveguide dual-mode filter with a dual-port patch antenna is proposed in this paper. Owing to the characteristics of the dual-mode cavity, different circular polarization (RHCP and LHCP) could be achieved by switching between the different feeding ports of antenna. This developed antenna exhibits a simulated impendence bandwidth of 4% and an axial ratio bandwidth of 2% at 5 GHz. In addition, a bandpass filtering response is achieved resulting from a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102/201</sub> dual mode operation. The antenna prototype is fabricated and tested. The measured results are in good agreement with simulation.

articleTitle: Multifocal Reflectarray with Optimized Aperture Phase
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for optimization of aperture phase of a dual-polarized multifocal single reflectarray antenna is presented based on the multi-objective Brainstorm optimization. It is tested for aperture optimization in two different schemes. The results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively optimize large antenna array.

articleTitle: A Metasurface for Boardband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a checkerboard metasurface is designed to achieve the radar cross section (RCS) reduction within a wide frequency band. The basic meta-atoms are printed on a substrate plane with two choices of layer thickness, and destructive interference are obtained by adjusting the geometry parameters of the meta-atoms. The combination of multiple layer thicknesses increases the range of the phase cancellation and improves the ability to control the electromagnetic waves of the planar target. Based on the optimized multielement phase cancellation (OMEPC), the designed metasurface can realize a 10 dB RCS reduction in a wideband from 4.8 to 19.6 GHz with a ratio bandwidth ( fH/fL) of 4.08:1 under normal incidence for both polarizations. In addition, a 10 dB RCS reduction performance can be preserved under wide-angle oblique incidences under TM wave. The estimated and simulated results are in good agreement and prove that the proposed metasurface can realize wideband cancellation interference in its style sheet. This work is a verification to prove that the increase of layer thickness can expand the bandwidth for RCS reduction apparently compared with a single layer.

articleTitle: A 30 GHz SIW based $4\mathrm{x}4$ Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 4×4 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) butler matrix is designed at 30 GHz. The design of 90° hybrid coupler and crossover which are the components of the butler matrix are discussed using theory of short slot couplers. The butler matrix is simulated and experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Employing EBG in Wireless Inter-chip Communication Links: Design and Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates the use of Electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures in wireless inter-chip communication links, EBG structures can be used to package open microstrip line baluns to suppress their radiation, and consequently enhance the overall wireless inter-chip link budget.

articleTitle: A Planar Pattern-reconfigurable Antenna for IEEE 802.11ax Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: IEEE 802.11ax systems will appear in the market soon and bring significant advancements to existing WLAN technologies. To further enhance their system performance, this paper proposes a planar reconfigurable antenna inspired by the Yagi-Uda structure. It is capable of beam steering by utilizing a switched pixel structure to change the antenna current distribution. Combined with system channel state information the antenna beam direction can be steered towards an active user in order to maximize the gain and therefore improve channel throughput. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth from 4.6 to 6.0 GHz (26.4%) and achieves a 300°scanning beamwidth with realized gain up to 9.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of Neural-Network-Based Mutual Coupling Compensators for Printed Planar Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a methodology to compensate the effect of mutual coupling in planar antenna array arrangements using a novel electromagnetic machine learning (ML) technique. The electromagnetic behavior of the array elements and their mutual coupling interactions are described via the antenna current Green's function (ACGF). A ML artificial neural network (ANN) procedure is then applied and combined with the ACGF to optimize array ports and mitigate for mutual coupling effects.

articleTitle: Broadband VLF/LF Transmission from an Electrically-Small Structure via Time-Varying Antenna Properties
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: High-speed time-varying electromagnetic systems have recently been able to achieve feats that would otherwise be impossible with conventional steady-state solutions. Broadband electrically-small antennas and nonmagnetic unilateral networks are two such systems that have come to fruition through time-varying electronics. Here, we present work aimed at combining these two capabilities in order to effectively radiate wideband VLF/LF signals from a nonreciprocal electrically-small transmitter. We discuss the theory of operation and detailed FDTD simulations that serve to validate the concept. We also explore preliminary results from a low-power prototype as well as improvements to said prototype made by moving from GaAs to GaN technology. Finally, we demonstrate a successful communication link between the time-varying transmitter and a newly designed VLF/ LF electric field receiver.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network with Active Element Pattern Technique for Finite Periodic Array Design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an artificial neural network model based on the transfer function is proposed for parametric modeling of finite periodic arrays. The active element pattern-technique, which takes the effects of the mutual coupling into account, is applied to the array analysis. A linear periodic phased array consisting of U-shaped slot elements is utilized to confirm the validity of the proposed model. The results demonstrate that the model is practical and efficient in array design.

articleTitle: An Approximate Direct Inverse as a Preconditioner for Ill-conditioned Problems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper implemented an approximate direct inverse for the surface integral equation including multilevel fast-multipole method. We apply it as a preconditioner to two examples suffering convergence problem with an iterative solver.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Patch Array for 5G Smart City Enviroment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the increasing demand for high speed wireless data access, the 5th generation mobile networks promise a revolution in the way we connect; with faster data transfer and the capacity to support a higher density of users. In the presented work, a capacitive edge-coupled patch antenna array is designed and simulated to operate at 28GHz. Back to back printed microstrip feeding network technology is used to achieve compact, low-loss and cost-effective millimeter-wave antenna array. Both connectivity and signal coverage with installed street light poles and near-by cellular towers are investigated.

articleTitle: Vegetation Effects for Remote Sensing of Soil Moisture Using NMM3D Full-wave Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The transmission of microwave through vegetation layer has been studied by the Radiative Transfer Equations (RTE) and Distorted Born Approximation (DBA) model, both of which assume a uniformly random distribution of the scatterers in vegetation. In this paper, a hybrid method is developed for the Numerical Maxwell Model of 3D (NMM3D) full-wave simulation of vegetation field consisting of many plants. A geometry setup is used to include the plant structure and gaps. Using the Huygens's principle and vector cylindrical wave expansions, the T-matrix of single plant is extracted based on the near field solutions from Ansys High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). The final scattered field is calculated using Foldy-Lax multiple scattering equations. The convergence of the T-matrix is tested and the hybrid method is verified with HFSS for the case of 4 wheat. The transmissivity of wheat at L-band calculated from the hybrid method is significantly higher than that of RTE/DBA.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-polarization UHF RFID Reader Antenna for Near-field Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel multi-polarized UHF RFID reader antenna for near-field applications is presented. Based on capacitive coupling and standing-wave structure, the antenna is designed and fabricated by microstrip lines. By designing the number of units that consists of an antenna, the interrogated area can be adjusted flexibly and easily. In the interrogated area, the antenna can generate uniform and multi-polarization electric field distributions to detect arbitrarily oriented linearly polarized tags in the horizontal plane. The measured results show that the antenna achieves impedance matching from 893 to 935 MHz.

articleTitle: An Approximation to the Exponentiated Weibull Phase Probability Density Function
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An approximation to the probability density function (PDF) of the exponentiated Weibull phase distribution is proposed. PDF curves and average absolute error, between exact and approximate phase PDFs, are presented. A speed up of two orders of magnitude in the time spent to compute the phase PDF is obtained.

articleTitle: Nonlinear and Amplification Response with Asymmetric Graphene-based Coherent Perfect Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work reports a novel asymmetric bifacial graphene metasurface design exhibiting broadband coherent perfect absorption (CPA) at low terahertz (THz) frequencies. Nonlinear CPA performance without resorting to optical nonlinearities, as well as amplification are demonstrated based on wave interference phenomena taking place in this subwavelength structure. The proposed design is composed of two graphene square patch arrays with different dimensions stacked over an ultrathin dielectric substrate. Asymmetric reflection in a broad frequency range is obtained that leads to the presented broadband and nonlinear CPA response and amplifying performance. The proposed ultrathin broadband CPA device is expected to be an important component to several new on-chip THz communication devices, such as sensors, coherent detectors, all-optical modulators, and small-signal amplifiers.

articleTitle: Low-Noise Impedance Matching Technique for Small Antennas Based on a Parametric Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low noise impedance matching technique for electrically small antennas is presented. To increase the bandwidth, the Bode-Fano theorem is applied to a magnetic electrically small antenna as a High-Q resonator. For prescribed bandwidth, the Bode-Fano theorem reveals the maximum received signal level leading to improve the overall noise figure. At the same time, an up-converter parametric amplifier as an active component is integrated into the structure to compensate for the mismatch loss introduced by the Bode-Fano theorem while maintaining a low-noise performance.

articleTitle: Development of an equivalent circuit model approach to the design of dense arrays of electrically small antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We model a linear EZ antenna array for HPEM applications. Equivalent circuit models of the single element EZ antenna and two element array antenna are presented, relating antenna performance and field coupling to physical parameters. This fully parameterized circuit model can be used to load the transmission line or waveguide feed and design a particular aperture field configuration, which can then be synthesized through the physical model.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultrawideband Printed Monopole Antenna Using Hexagonal CSRR at UHF-Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an ultrawideband microstrip monopole antenna operating at UHF frequency band is proposed. The proposed monopole antenna is composed of semi-circular shaped radiator fed by an 50 ohm transmission line. In order to enhance broadband characteristics of the antenna, ground plane beneath the transmission line is etched with three different equilateral hexagonal complementary split ring resonators. The proposed antenna has a broad return loss bandwidth starting from 300 MHz up to 1210 MHz where VSWR is less than 2. Omni-directional pattern with average 2.5 dBi gain and 85% total efficiency is achieved along whole frequency band.

articleTitle: Extraction of Knitted RFID Antenna Design Parameter from Transmission Line Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The seamless integration of knitted antennas into electronic devices requires accurate knowledge of the electrical properties of the conductive fabrics at high frequencies. This paper shows a new method of extracting sheet resistance of knitted conductive fabric from S-parameter measurements of two-port transmission lines. The extracted sheet resistance parameter is then used to simulate knitted antennas.

articleTitle: A 21.6-45 GHz Low-Profile Wideband Slot Antenna Array for 5G Wireless
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile 21.6-45 GHz printed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> antenna array with high gain and efficiency is presented. Such antenna array is composed of an in-phase 1:4 power divider and four slot antenna elements. Each antenna element fed by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \Omega$</tex> microstrip input/output (I/O) port consists of a C-shaped slotline and two ring slots with embedded defected ground structure (DGS). Multiple resonances are introduced by the proposed structure to achieve a wide operation bandwidth. To verify the mechanism mentioned above, a wideband slot antenna array is implemented and fabricated with a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$28\times 40\times 0.254\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The measured result exhibits a 70.3% impedance bandwidth operating from 21.6 to 45 GHz. With such high performance, the proposed wideband antenna array can be a good candidate for 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: Solution of Coupled Hydrodynamic and Volume Integral Equations for Analyzing Electromagnetic Interactions on Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coupled system of hydrodynamic and volume integral equations is solved for analyzing electromagnetic wave interactions with non-local dispersion effects on nanostructures. The proposed scheme discretizes the scatterer into a mesh of tetrahedral elements and expands (unknown) electric flux and hydrodynamic current using Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson basis functions defined on this mesh. Inserting these expansions into the coupled equations and applying Galerkin testing yield a matrix system. An iterative scheme is used to solve this matrix system for unknown expansion coefficients. Numerical results show additional resonance peaks in the scattering cross section spectrum of nanospheres, which can be explained by non-local dispersion effects accounted for by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Influence of Dielectric Overlay Dimensions on Performance of Miniaturized ESPAR Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the influence of dielectric overlay size on miniaturized ESPAR antenna performance has been investigated. The dielectric overlay's main function is antenna's size reduction but it can also be used to modify its radiation pattern. This creates the possibility of easy adopting antenna parameters to different applications by swapping used overlay. In particular, the lowering of antenna's main beam elevation direction has been considered. By using selected alternative overlay one can obtain a 20° lower beam. The design was confirmed by realization and measurements.

Author Keywords: electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Four-Sector Cube Antenna for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work suggests a compact switched-beam cube antenna system at 5.8GHz (C-band) for the Internet of Things (IoT) devices, such as automated robots. The antenna consists of four right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) arrays that are activated, one at a time, by a reconfigurable feeding network centered between them. The antenna configuration forms a 3D cube that can be easily mounted on each robot device. An 8.4 dBic directional beam switches between four consecutive 90° degree sectors, in order to detect possible communication links or to avoid interferences. The antenna has its feeding network surrounded by the four arrays in order to minimize the required area and to result in a compact 45×45×45mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> cube antenna system.

articleTitle: π-Impedance Matching Circuit for Wireless Power Transfer Systems under Dynamic Load and Transfer Distance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In recent years, wireless charging has become a trend because it is convenient and safe. However, its efficiency can deteriorate when the distance between coils or the load varies. In this paper, an automatic π - impedance matching method is proposed to obtain higher efficiency under dynamic-coupling or varied-load condition. The simulation results show that the efficiency can remain higher than 85% in varying transfer distances when coupling coefficient is over 0.3. For varied-load, the efficiency is higher than 80% when the load is over 20 ohm and reach around 88% as the load increases at the 6.78-MHz operating frequency.

articleTitle: A Multi-Functional Metasurface for Polarization Transformation Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multifunctional metasurface performing both linear-linear (cross) and linear-circular polarization conversion is proposed and analyzed. The unit cell of the metasurface comprises of double head umbrella shape. The cross polarization conversion is achieved in two frequency bands of 7.5-7.99 GHz and 14.1-24 GHz. The polarization conversion efficiency is more than 90% over both frequency bands. The metasurface achieves circular polarization conversion within the frequency ranges of 7.15-7.3 GHz, 8.5-12.06 GHz and 27.6-30.85 GHz. Moreover, the proposed metasurface is angularly stable against oblique incidences of upto 45°. The proposed multifunctional structure is suitable for many applications like satellite communications, tracking and navigation systems.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Wideband Circular Polarized Square Antenna With Ground Slot and Partial Feed
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized printed monopole antenna with coplanar waveguide feeding is proposed in this letter. The antenna consists of a square patch which dig two triangles diagonally and a slot cut on ground. In this way, antenna excite circular polarized wave and enhance 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth respectively. In addition, by means of shifting feeding line towards left edge, the impedance bandwidth has achieved great improvement. Overall size of the designed antenna is 60×60×1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. As simulation results, the proposed antenna can provide a wide impedance bandwidth of 62% (1.52-2.88 GHz) and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 53% (1.55-2.66 GHz) respectively. Which are useful for wireless communication.

articleTitle: Low profile Vertically Polarized Endfire Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this letter, a low profile vertically polarized end-fire antenna applying spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) transmission and radiation structure is introduced. It realizes wide end-fire radiation beam and could work in multiple frequency bands.

articleTitle: Radial Line Slot Array Antenna High Power Thermal Vacuum Testing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Radial Line Slot Array (RLSA) High Gain Antenna will be used on NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission for its primary science downlink. Thermal balance tests were performed in Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) on a Qualification Model (QM) to verify the electrical, structural, and thermal performance. Four cases of varying temperatures and RF power levels were considered. Return loss measurements were used to monitor any changes in real-time.

articleTitle: A Wideband Miniaturized Tapered Slot Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coplanar Vivaldi antenna featuring miniaturized size, wide bandwidth and high gain is presented. The miniaturization is achieved by introducing slots in the main radiating part that results in a small width of 16 mm that is 60% smaller than a standard Vivaldi operating at the same frequency. Fabricated on a RO4350B laminate, the antenna occupies 110×16 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and has a bandwidth of 5 GHz (7.5 to 12.5 GHz). The measured gain is 10 dBi gain with a radiation efficiency of 87% making it suitable for remote sensing and phased array applications.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Curvy Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Antenna With Controllable Bandwidth for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for improving gain in spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) antenna including guiding and radiating parts is proposed. This method is based on using a curvy tapering area instead of linear one to matched the antenna to the air. The obtained results show that realized gain can be improved approximately 3 dBi by this method. Furthermore, by using corrugated unit cells and stubs an undesired frequency band can be rejected. Since the antenna works at 27.2-28.2 GHz, it can be used for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of a 2.5-D 2-Bit Reconfigurable Transmitarray Element for 5G mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a novel reconfigurable transmitarray (RTA) element with 2-bit phase resolution is proposed. The 2.5-D receiver-transmitter transmitarray structure is adopted. In addition to the 1-bit current reversible dipole, it fully utilizes the longitudinal space for housing an additional 90° digital phase shifter based on a quadrature hybrid coupler with two PIN diodes. Full wave simulations under normal and oblique incidence show that the transmission insertion losses for four phase states are 1.1-1.2 dB at 26 GHz, with a 3-dB transmission bandwidth of 18.3%. The RTA element is able to generate stable performance under large incident angles, which makes it suitable for two-dimensional wide-angle beam scanning. The proposed element design has good 2-bit phase tuning capability. The simple structure with only two metallic layers and four PIN diodes effectively reduces the cost. It is believed to have great potentials for future 5G millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Estimating the Variance of SAR in a 3D Human Head Model Using Stochastic FDTD
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the variance of specific absorption rate (SAR) in a 3-D anatomical model of the human head is estimated using the stochastic finite difference time domain (S-FDTD) method. A half wave dipole antenna is placed in the near field of the ear at 835 MHz. The conductivity and permittivity of the head tissues are presumed to be varying randomly. The obtained results show that these statistical variations can significantly vary the magnitude of SAR.

articleTitle: Spread Spectrum Techniques with Channel Coding for Wideband Secured Communication Links
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) radios provide avenues for interference immunity using spread spectrum (SS) techniques. Doing so, provides a processing gain of 21 dB, allowing for successful retrieval of signals propagated below the noise floor. In addition, by applying advanced channel coding an additional coding gain of 9 dB can be achieved. In this paper, we are exploiting SS techniques with channel coding to maximize gain in wireless communication links. Bit error rate (BER) performance is presented for multiple channel coding approaches.

articleTitle: Design of Switched Antenna Arrays for a 28 GHz Propagation Channel Sounder
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A channel sounder is an advanced measurement system to estimate the behavior of wireless propagation channels. In this paper, we present the antenna array design for a 28GHz massive multiple-input multiple-output system, capable of measuring 256×128 dual-polarized channels, including dynamic properties of angular, delay, Doppler, and polarization parameters, respectively. Unique in comparison to other designs at 28 GHz, our approach is based on a switched, dual polarized patch antenna array architectures at both transmit and receive link ends. The interactions between the switch circuitry and the elements is analyzed and the measured radiation characteristics are compared to the simulated counterparts.

articleTitle: A Passive Harmonic Tag Using Nested Dual-Band Patch Antennas for Harmonic Doppler Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new harmonic tag based on a dual-band patch antenna designed for detecting harmonic Doppler signals is presented. The antenna structure is made from a patch antenna and parasitic antenna ring surrounded by a grounded ring. The tag is designed to receive a 2.5 GHz continuous-wave signal and using a nonlinear component retransmit the received signal at the second harmonic frequency (5 GHz), the Doppler shift of which can be detected for moving target measurements in cluttered environments. The patch design is used to achieve higher gain than common dipole-based harmonic tags can earn. We present simulation results of the antenna performance, and show measured reception of the scattered fundamental and generated harmonic signals. The proposed design would be suitable for applications ranging from home health care to internet of things (IoT) among other applications.

articleTitle: Indoor radio triangulation using only RSSI data
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper outlines an approach for indoor radio triangulation using only RSSI data. The method employs the incoherent reception of the transmission from a radio of unknown location by several identical indoor radios. These radios also communicate with one another, and the data are used to create an indoor propagation model. The resulting propagation model together with the received signals from the hidden radio is used to triangulate its position.

articleTitle: Active Cloaking Without A Priori Incident Field Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Active scattering-cancellation cloaking employs an array of antennas to cancel out an object's scattering. Although promising in terms of versatility and performance, the past dependence on a priori knowledge of the incident field represents a major barrier to practical implementation. This work addresses this obstacle by presenting the initial development of a field estimator, enabling determination of the incident field from total field measurements near the target. Accordingly, simulated total field values are used to configure a cloak to hide a quasi-2D, conductive, circular target against impinging plane waves of various amplitudes and directions. Scattering cross-section simulations validate good performance matching between estimator based and known field cloak configurations.

articleTitle: Angular Scan Enhancement of Antenna Arrays Using Two Lenses
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We discuss angular scan enhancement of antenna arrays with lenses. A condition on two lenses to behave as enhancers is given. It is shown that the two-lens scan enhancer can be placed much closer to the source array than the single-lens device.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wideband Printed Circularly Polarized Antenna Fed by PGW
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband planar circularly polarized antenna based on the differential excitation of an asymmetrical spiral antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed feeding method of the spiral antenna is an appropriate alternative to the complex balun circuits used in conventional spiral antennas. The simulation results show that the CP antenna covers the 46.84 % -15 dB impedance bandwidth and 36.19% 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth with the peak realized gain of 6.7 dBi. The presented antenna inherits the low profile characteristic and is capable of integration with planar structure.

articleTitle: High Gain $4\times 4$ SIW Passive Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high gain Ka-band 4×4 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) passive phased array antenna (PAA). A 4×4 SIW-based PAA consists of four SIW phase shifters for the beamforming network and SIW-series fed network to increase the gain of PAA. The simulated results show a continuous beam scanning range from -30° to +30° covering the whole operating band of 29-31 GHz. The maximum simulated gain is 15.2 dBi at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Circularly-Polarized Beam-Steerable Reflectarray for Satellite Applications in the Ku band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents the design of a dual-band reconfigurable circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray (RA) antenna for satellite communication in the Ku bands. Simultaneous and independent control is provided over the downlink and uplink beams at frequency bands of [10.8 - 11.8] GHz and [13.8 - 15] GHz, respectively. The unit cell is composed of two circular rings, each loaded using four varactor diodes, for operating in the two bands. The rings are symmetrically loaded in the vertical and horizontal directions to provide an isotropic response suitable for CP applications, and enable a phase range of more than 300°as the capacitive loading varies. Here, the response of the unit cell is studied through fullwave simulations and quasi-optical (QO) measurements, and a fabricated prototype of the RA is presented.

articleTitle: A Multiresolution Hybrid Technique for Large-Scale Multiple Buried Targets Profiling
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient hybrid inverse scattering technique for dealing with large-scale half-space GPR scenarios, is proposed. First, an initialization step using a fast and simple Diffraction Tomography (DT) method has been utilized to roughly detect the objects' borders and reduce the size of the investigation domain (ID). Then, an iterative multi-scale approach (IMSA) is applied that starts with coarse meshes, and then successively zooms inside the regions where the objects are located. In each step, the inversion procedure is performed by the stochastic optimization method of Covariance Matrix Adaption Evolutionary Strategy (CMA-ES) which is a robust technique for nonlinear problems. Furthermore, multi frequency data are used in each inversion process, to more effectively alleviate the problem's ill-posedness. The presented results show the reliability and efficiency of this technique in dealing with multiple buried targets. Moreover, comparison with a standard IMSA approach, reveals that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms it.

articleTitle: A Low-Frequency Motionless Magnetic Antenna Based on Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new method is introduced for generating electromagnetic waves. In this proposed method, a permanent magnet is used as a flux source and its stored magnetic energy is then modulated by altering the reluctance of the surrounding material through time-varying electric current. This approach uses the nonlinear B-H curve of magnetic material to saturate and desaturate the magnet's surrounding environment resulting in a time-varying magnetic field.

articleTitle: Evaluation of LTE-R System Performance with Pantograph-Catenary Arc Interference
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The pantograph-catenary arc interference is a key interference source impacting the performance of LTE-R system deployed in 450-470MHz, so the interference effects on LTE-R system performance should be evaluated. In this paper, the pantograph-catenary arc interference signal characteristics in time domain and frequency domain are modeled. A measurement system are built in laboratory to evaluate the effects of interference on the performance of LTE-R system. Based on the measurement results, a base station deployment strategy of the LTE-R system is proposed to solve pantograph-catenary arc interference problem.

articleTitle: Particle in Cell Finite Element Validation and Verification Methods
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Particle in cell codes are used extensively to understand plasma physics and to design devices that exploit these physics. More recent needs (say novel table top accelerators) have given impetus to development of the next generation plasma physics codes that have better fidelity. But despite this need, it is difficult to validate any code. For fully three dimensional simulations, there are no analytical solutions. One typically reduces the problem to the simplest 1-D problem and draw conclusions. Furthermore, the literature is sparse with respect to detail so as to be reproducible. This paper seeks present a set of problems (with multiple points of comparison) that can serve as a benchmark for all PIC codes.

articleTitle: A Wideband High-Gain Planar Corrugated Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a wideband high-gain corrugated antenna is investigated in this paper. Two planar substrate layers are used for shaping the corrugations and it is shown that significant enhancement can be achieved in the 3dB gain-bandwidth of the corrugated antenna. Based on the surface susceptance of the corrugated structure, the corrugated structure can be designed by adjusting the resonance frequency of the antenna using just one unit-cell of the structure. Also, a parametric study shows that the widths of the corrugations can be adjusted for having a large 3dB gain bandwidth. The results show that a high gain of 16.8 dBi is achieved along with a wide 3 dB gain-bandwidth of 11.5% at the center frequency of 11.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband Printed Quasi - Yagi Antenna with Simple Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new configuration of broadband printed quasi-Yagi antenna (PQYA) with monopole elements has been proposed. The proposed monopole element PQYA has a measured impedance bandwidth (BW) of 47.6%, a flat gain of 3.6-4.1 dBi, and the maximum front-to-back (F/B) ratio of 22.7 dB. It has a compact size of 76 ×86mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a simulated efficiency of 83%. The performance comparison of the proposed PQYA with the conventional dipole element PQYA is also presented. The dipole element PQYA designed for the same frequency band has measured impedance BW of 20.3%, increasing gain from 2.96-4.74 dBi, and the maximum F/B ratio of 20.6 dB. It has an overall size of 95×82mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a simulated efficiency of 79%. The novelty of proposed PQYA is, its simple MS line feed and flat gain with relatively small size in comparison with the dipole element PQYA having a large size, lower BW, and increasing gain.

articleTitle: Wideband Excitation and Matching of Fundamental Chassis Mode Using Inductive Coupling Element
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: It is known that the fundamental radiation mode of a mobile terminal chassis enables wideband coverage below 1 GHz. However, in theory, the bandwidth of this chassis mode extends infinitely beyond 1 GHz. In this paper, we investigate the use of inductive coupling element (ICE) to significantly increase the antenna bandwidth obtainable from the fundamental mode. Using characteristic mode analysis, a dual-ICE configuration is proposed and optimized to excite the fundamental mode, giving a simulated impedance bandwidth of nearly 1000%.

articleTitle: Broadband Compact Microstrip Antenna Loaded with Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband compact microstrip antenna that loaded with the metasurface is presented. The metasurface that consists of 3×3 double-face patches is applied above the conventional patch antenna to generate two resonant modes, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</sub> mode. Thus, bandwidth enhancement of the patch antenna can be achieved by properly exciting two modes of the metasurface simultaneously. The simple coaxial feeding method is used to excite the antenna in this paper. The results show that wide bandwidth of 28%, stable radiation pattern with wide beamwidth within the operating bandwidth and average gain of 8dBi can be achieved.

articleTitle: Using Highly Confined Fields to Develop Biosensors for Glucose Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes and demonstrates the significance of highly confined fields to develop biosensors for glucose measurements. Generating highly confined fields with concentrated energies at a particular point helps in enhancing the sensitivity of the sensing region of the biosensor. Due to the reduction in losses which can be incurred by radiation through air, the proposed principle can be helpful in designing highly sensitive sensors for glucose monitoring. The concept has been further demonstrated here using a biosensor design.

articleTitle: A Wideband Patch Antenna for 5G
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wide bandwidth requirement is one of the main challenging issues in 5G antenna technology. To satisfy this, a stacked low-profile patch antenna is proposed. The design has been optimized via an optimization tool based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) integrated with the finite integration technique (FIT).
