publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design method for the split-block manufacturing technique of the septum polarizer is proposed. By reasonably adjusting the splitting position of the septum polarizer, the negative influence on the circularly polarized (CP) performance caused by the misalignment and welding will be effectively reduced. Two split-block models of the septum polarizer are built for comparison and the effects of the misalignment and welding are analyzed for both of the two models. Finally, the septum polarizer is designed, machined, and welded with minimal impact on the CP performance. A conical horn antenna is connected with the septum polarizer. Good agreement can be found between the simulated and measured results, which confirms that the manufacturing technique is worth considering.

articleTitle: Monopulse Antenna in SIW Technology for Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Series-fed slot arrays using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology are reported in which the sum and difference patterns are steered to a desired beam angle in the far-field. Applications include radar, localization, and new target detection algorithms where beam steering designs are of interest. In the paper, the design methodology and steering approach for two antenna prototypes is discussed. Initially, simulations and measurements of a single-element antenna for monopulse are described. This planar SIW antenna is matched to 50-Ω and is defined by two-sided, microstrip end-launch feeding. A series-fed array of slots is realized defining a total antenna structure which employs sub-arrays and with two input ports for each sub-array element. Concepts are extended to a 4-port structure, defining a new monopulse array, which offers sum pattern control along with null steering for the monopulse pattern. The simulations and measurements show proof of concept for the developed monopulse antennas at 24 GHz. The design approach is also applicable to other planar antennas and arrays which operate at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies where pattern maximum and null steering for the sum and difference patterns is of interest.

articleTitle: A Broadband Frequency-Selective Rasorber with Double-Sided Absorption Bands
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband Frequency Selective Rasorber (FSR) with 2.5D FSS structure is proposed. The proposed FSR presents a wideband transmission window between two absorption bands. The FSR consists of a lossless periodic surface and a lossy periodic surface separated by an air layer. The lossy surface is realized by inserting a strip-type Parallel LC (P-LC) of via structure into the center of a dipole loaded with lumped-resistors. The lossless layer is a broadband bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) consisting of two metal patches surfaces and separated by a thin layer. An equivalent circuit model (ECM) is proposed to analyze operating principle of the FSR. The fractional bandwidth for reflection less than -10 dB is about 70% and a transmission bandwidth with insertion loss of -3 dB is about 22%. The FSR perform stable frequency response from 0 to 30 degrees.

articleTitle: Spacetime-Modulated Metasurface Camouflaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a hybrid space-modulated and time-modulated, or spacetime-modulated, camouflaging metasurface. Such a metasurface is implemented in the form of spacetime-alternating PEC and PMC cells. It is demonstrated to exhibit superior camouflaging performance as a result of the combined spreading of the temporal and spatial spectra of the incoming wave.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Reconfigurable Pixel Antenna for Millimeter Wave Bands
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The performance of a reconfigurable pixel antenna operating at 27 GHz is investigated in this paper. With different states of hardwired connection, the proposed pixel antenna can achieve a beam scanning range of 240° in the azimuth plane with 6.6-8.9 dBi realized gain. When all hardwired connections are replaced by PIN diode switching, the scanning range and realized gain reduce to 120° and 4.5-7.5 dBi respectively. The antenna efficiency is also decreased to around 65% from over 90%. It is concluded that, more efficient RF switches should be studied for use in in future millimeter-wave reconfigurable pixel antennas.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Nets for DOA Estimation With Random Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ensemble deep neural net framework is introduced to process nonuniform antenna arrays with unknown relative positions. The architecture is composed of two successive learning stages, the first one is a multilayered perceptron model and is used to interpolate the randomly sampled signals and estimate the corresponding uniformly sampled equivalent of the incoming signal. The second layer is an Long Short Term Memory network which learns the mapping of the incoming signal to its source location. The architecture allows for the model to learn the complex nonlinear functions required for mapping the arbitrarily sampled incoming space-time field to a virtual uniformly sampled field one and subsequently map it to the direction of the source. The structure has been trained and tested with independently generated sample sets, with results competitive with other algorithms that need the information about the sensor position.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Hybrid PICA Terahertz Antenna for High-Resolution Biomedical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the utility of a hybrid perovskite material, methyl-ammonium lead iodide (chemical formula, CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) in the design of a terahertz (THz) antenna. The proposed planar inverted cone antenna (PICA) operates in the frequency range of 0.6 - 2.4 THz. Full wave electromagnetic simulations show that antennas fabricated using a combination of the perovskite material and gold improve the antenna performance, and can be used for imaging in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: New Hybrid Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a simple and low-cost method to increase the bandwidth of a slot-fed rectangular dielectric resonator antenna. In this method, two parallel rectangular metallic strips are added to the two parallel flat sides of the DRA which are normal to the feeding slot. The metallic strips form a parallel-plate waveguide resonator and create two extra resonances resulting in a wider bandwidth. The efficiency of the method is evaluated by computer simulations. It is shown that a bandwidth enhancement of 40% is achieved for a rectangular DRA at the center frequency of 4.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Elliptical Metasurface Cloaks for Decoupling and Cloaking of Microstrip Monopole Antennas at 28 GHz and 39 GHz for 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to curtail mutual coupling between two closely spaced microstrip monopole antennas operating at frequencies 28 GHz and 39 GHz, the concept of electromagnetic cloaking is applied by utilizing elliptical metasurfaces. In this paper, we show that by enveloping the monopole antennas with the specifically engineered metasurface cloaks, not only is there a significant reduction in the mutual electromagnetic interaction but also restoration in the radiation patterns are observed, as if the antennas were completely isolated from each other. The decoupling effect is seen in the reduction of mutual S-parameters. This enables the antennas to radiate independently even though they are placed in a very close proximity.

articleTitle: Coded Intelligent Surface Design for Generalized Beamspace Modulation in Massive MIMO Communications Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems have been proposed to support high rates in next-generation 5G and 6G wireless networks. Recently, index modulation (IM) techniques have attracted significant interest for their potential to meet strict energy efficiency (EE) and spectral efficiency (SE) requirements of these networks. As a form of an low-cost IM for uplink scenarios with mobile stations (MS), the generalized beamspace modulation (GBM) exploits lens antenna arrays for achieving substantially increased data rates with a very small number of radio-frequency chains. However, realizing low-cost and low-form factor antennas with versatile beamforming capabilities remains a challenge. In this paper, we propose reconfigurable metasurface (R-MTS) design to implement GBM for wireless communications. Our full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate system feasibility to deploy arbitrary beam steering achieved with much lower hardware footprint than the lens arrays.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz $2\times 2$ Antenna Array with 10 Beams Using Passive Beamforming Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a 2×2 series fed antenna array working at 28 GHz with beam switching capability is proposed. The presented antenna design is suitable for 5G user equipments and high data rates applications with low cost, complexity, and size. The size of the antenna is 37. 2×37.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including the ground plane and it produces 10 different switched beams by using only two simple 3dB/90° couplers that create the required amplitudes and phase excitations for the antenna elements. The antenna design is implemented on 0.203 mm thick low-loss ( tan δ = 0.0027) Rogers 4003C substrate and it has a measured impedance bandwidth of 0.5 GHz for one of the ports. The antenna has an average realized gain of 9 dBi and at least 10 dB side lobe level (SLL) for all beams. The antenna is designed and simulated using HFSS and fabricated using regular PCB processing.

articleTitle: Analysis and Synthesis of Cylindrical Omega-Bianisotropic Metasurfaces with Mode Expansion
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple technique for the analysis and synthesis of cylindrical omega-bianisotropic metasurfaces (O-BMSs) is presented and numerically verified. The fields everywhere and the spatially varying surface-parameters of the O-BMS are decomposed into orthogonal cylindrical modes with the discrete Fourier transform. In the Fourier domain, the bianisotropic sheet transition conditions, which relate fields on both sides of the O-BMS, are written into a system of equations, which can be solved to obtain the transmitted and reflected fields of any arbitrary O-BMS, given the incident field as well as the surface-parameters. Conversely, one can easily invert these relations to synthesize the required surface-parameters for the O-BMS, given the desired incident, transmitted and reflected fields.

articleTitle: Bio-inspired Butterfly-shaped Patch Antenna Array for 2.4 GHz WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a bio-inspired butterfly-shaped patch antenna array, generated by polar transformations, covering the wireless local area network (WLAN) band at 2.4 GHz (2.400-2.483 GHz), with similar and dissimilar elements is presented in this paper. The dissimilar bio-inspired antenna presented a bandwidth of 96MHz covering the IEEE802.11b, g band, maximum gain of 8.64dBi, concentrated half power beamwidth of 52 degrees and front-to-back ratio of 15.21dB.

articleTitle: Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion from Impedance Loading of Single-Port Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic theory of antenna scattering has been previously applied to the minimization/maximization of radar signatures, and has been eventually used for designing antenna sensors for passive wireless sensing systems, in which the antenna backscattering mode is controlled by loading impedances. To mitigate the clutter and reduce polarization mismatch in such wireless systems, this paper investigates the linear-to-circular conversion of electric field from loading single-port patch antennas by passive impedance.

articleTitle: A Beam Squinted Linearly Polarised Radial Line Slot Array Antenna with Improved Return Loss Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an investigation to improve the poor return loss performance of linearly polarised radial line slot array (RLSA) antenna. The problem was tackled by applying the beam squinting technique. The antenna consists of radiating surface with a circular cavity and supports outward-travelling electromagnetic waves. The antenna is excited via a rear mounted modified disk-ended dielectric coated SMA connector. The simulation results show that the return loss performance has improved significantly over the entire frequency band with a return loss bandwidth of 52.5%. The far-field result indicates that the antenna has achieved a peak directivity of 24.7 dBi at 17 GHz with a beam squinted angle of 18° and a side lobe level of -10 dB.

articleTitle: A Modified Top-loaded Monopole Antenna with Trapezoidal Plates Element Arranged in Y-shape
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile wideband antenna composed of trapezoidal plates element arranged in Y-shape, a circular element and three short elements. The characteristics of the proposed antenna are analyzed through simulation. The results demonstrate that the proposed antenna offers a low-profile and wideband performance. The height and the relative bandwidth of the proposed antenna are 0.035λ and 48.0%, respectively. In addition, its radiation patterns are omnidirectional.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Properties of Millimeter- and THz Wave Scattering from Common Rough Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple numerical approach is presented to estimate rough surface scattering. We measure the roughness parameters of rough surfaces and then import them into a 2D model to compute the scattered fields under various surface illuminations. The validity of this approach is demonstrated by comparing the simulation results with measurements. Besides, we use the 2D model to simulate rough surfaces of a wide range of roughness parameters and perform a qualitative analysis on the scattering patterns. We show that, for most common building materials of moderate roughness, increasing the root-mean-square height of the rough surface reduces the maximum reflection and increases diffuse scattering. On the other hand, increasing the correlation length of the rough surface will lead to lower maximum reflection and diffuse scattering.

articleTitle: Hybrid Computer Simulation Of Automotive Radar Systems in High Multipath Environments
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The electromagnetic modeling of automotive radar in various traffic scenarios and in complex high multipath environments like highways and urban areas poses enormous computational challenges that cannot be addressed using conventional simulation approaches. In this paper, we describe a hybrid methodology that combines several full-wave and asymptotic numerical techniques within a unified framework that enables near-real-time dynamical simulation of an automotive radar system in a multipath physical channel, where the positions and orientations of the radar and target(s) can change dynamically as a function of time.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of On-Chip Antenna at 60 GHz Using an Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless data communication within and between CMOS chips at 60GHz is very attractive for short range wireless transmission. The objective of the work is to enhance antenna gain and improve the radiation efficiency with the use of the Jerusalem-Cross Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) to mitigate the effects of the silicon and improve data transmission within and between chips. The Yagi is optimized for an endfire radiation in the plane of the chip. Its performance is studied when it is placed in the center of the chip and along the edge, with the AMC layer extending only below the feed system and then compared when it extends over the entire chip. The results show that the AMC layer improves the gain by 2.5 dB and radiation efficiency by a few percent. All simulations are performed using ANSYS HFSS.

articleTitle: Dipole Antenna Using Mantle Cloak For Reducing Monostatic RCS at Close Frequency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dipole antenna using mantle cloak for reducing monostatic RCS at a close frequency with the operating frequency of the antenna. By adjusting the length of the dipole antenna and the surface reactance of mantle cloak, it confirms that the monostatic RCS can be reduced and antenna characteristics can be maintained simultaneously.

articleTitle: Using Augmented Lagrangian Methods to Design Electromagnetic Surfaces with Far Field Constraints
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a method to synthesize passive and lossless electromagnetic surfaces, such as metasurfaces, by synthesizing their macroscopic surface parameters (namely their surface impedance) using optimization. A relaxation of this non-convex problem using the alternating direction method of multipliers is shown. An example where the surface impedance is optimized to satisfy a given sidelobe level and main beam level is then presented. Further directions for this work are proposed.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-band Omnidirectional Planar Microstrip Antenna using Gielis Curves
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band omnidirectional planar microstrip antennas are designed using Gielis curves. Gielis curve profiles are used to create antenna prototypes with different patch section lengths to obtain a dual-band. The antenna characteristics of the antenna such as return loss, realized gain and radiation pattern are simulated and are compared with the measured results of the fabricated prototype. The designed antennas have a peak realized gain varying between 1 dB about 4 dB over the two bands.

articleTitle: Electronic Wound Monitoring Using Fabric-Integrated Data Modulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a cost-efficient smart textile electronic (textronic) for wound healing assessment. This assessment is done by reflection of the modulated wound-data to the interrogator. The RF modulation of the data is done by a textile-based voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) that takes the electric signal provided by electrochemical sensing of the uric acid found in the wound fluid. The assessment was done based on a threshold found to be 0.4 mM respect to which the severity or restoration of the damage wound is evaluated. The average sensitivity of this system is 44.67 MHz/mM and the maximum power consumption 0.38 mW. It uses low-cost materials and it is easy to manufacture and use by any patient or medical professional.

articleTitle: Flexible 16-Antenna System for Microwave Breast Screening: NB vs. UWB Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We here present a comparison of a narrowband (NB) and an ultrawideband (UWB) system in the microwave frequency range for early breast cancer detection. We describe key elements of the UWB and the NB systems, including the use of the same 16-antenna array and breast-tissue phantoms, as well as highlighting main differences. First, we compare their transmitting output power and then assess their suitability for breast cancer detection using a phantom measurement. The NB results are promising, showing sufficiently high-power levels.

articleTitle: On the Specific Absorption Rate Behavior of Square-wave Modulated Signals Exposures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we investigate the Specific Absorption Rate behavior of exposures from square-wave modulated signals in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) band. In particular, we demonstrated, through multiphysics numerical simulations, the SAR deposition equivalency between continuous-wave and square-wave modulated signals carrying the same average power. We show that the thermal diffusivity of the biological sample plays an important role in the derivation of the SAR equivalency: in this paper a biological sample with a low thermal diffusivity, as representative of human tissues, has been considered. These results can pave the way for novel and more simple methodologies to assess the safety of electromagnetic instrumentation employing modulated signals.

articleTitle: Low Cost All Metal Additively Manufactured Wideband Antenna Array Modules
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a modular, end-fire, dual-polarized ultra-wideband scalable array (MEDUSA) realized exclusively with titanium direct metal laser sintering (DMLS) to achieve a connector-less phased array antenna module. The radiator is based on a variation of conventional tapered slot antennas (i.e. Vivaldi) to achieve an all metal fully-monolithic element consisting of RF coaxial interface, balun, and free-space transformer. A very low-cost array module is achieved by adapting the design uniquely to the fabrication process in order to eliminate nearly all post-processing. A finite 8x8 array covering 7-21 GHz has been prototyped and measured to demonstrate agreement with predicted results.

articleTitle: Microwave Radar-based In-Well Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This contribution presents an FMCW radar-based in-well sensing concept. The radar works at 24 GHz and is mounted on an overmoded waveguide like tube, measuring 76 mm in diameter. In order to reduce wall losses and to increase the achievable measuring distance of the radar, an optimized TE11-TE01 mode converter is used. The applicability of the radar-based in-well sensing is demonstrated on a 500 m test rig, build up of single elements measuring 12 m. Here, each joint can clearly be identified within the range measurement using 200 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Fast Solutions of Multiscale Electromagnetic Problems Using Potential Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a full-wave electromagnetics solver to analyze multiscale scattering problems. The developed solver employs potential integral equations, which include both the electric current and the normal component of the magnetic vector potential as unknowns. These formulations are able to circumvent the low-frequency breakdown and related inaccuracy issues encountered when using electric- and magnetic-field integral equations. To analyze multiscale electromagnetic problems involving highly nonuniform discretizations, we solve the obtained matrix equations iteratively by employing a broadband multilevel fast multipole algorithm with incomplete-leaf tree structures. Accuracy and efficiency of the implementation are demonstrated on conical electromagnetic scattering problems.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Reductions in a Planar Hexagonal Scanning Array with Large Element Spacing
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new single-layer, dual-mode circular microstrip patch antenna with self-nulling capabilities is utilized as an antenna element in a seven-element hexagonal scanning phased array with a 1.25λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> element spacing to facilitate grating lobe reductions for medium scan angles. For the scan angles up to ±40°, it will be shown that the utilization of such dual-mode antenna elements leads to grating lobe reductions to well below -25 dB.

articleTitle: Multi/Wide Band Printed Quad Helical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A technique is proposed for designing multiband and/or wide band printed quadrifilar helical antennas. The technique uses microstrip line tuning section in the vicinity of the feeding ports. This section contains an elongated body and a tail member extending away from the body. Geometry of the tail member is selected for modifying the radiating element impedance and broadening the resonance bandwidth. A four port antenna is designed for operating in wide band (24%, ) or in 3 frequency bands, with one of the bands being more than 24% : 1.88-2.12GHz, 2.3-2.4GHz and 3.4-3.8GHz (E-UTRA 39, 40, and 42& 43, respectively).

articleTitle: A Low-Cost High-Performance Dual-Band Diaphragm Circular Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band dielectric-diaphragm circular polarizer with simple structure and good performance is presented, which can effectively improve the return loss and bandwidth characteristics through innovation in its structure. Simulation and experiment results show that the circular polarizer can decompose an incident linearly polarized wave into two components whose phase difference ranges from 85° to 95° and amplitudes are equal in dual frequency bands of 19.6-21.2GHz and 29.4-31.0GHz. Simulated return loss is better than -30dB, while the experiment one is below -10dB. By cascading the polarizer with a corrugated horn antenna, simulation results of axial ratio are less than 2dB at the center frequencies of the dual band, i.e., 20.4GHz and 30.2GHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable 4-Arm Spiral Antenna for Dual Polarization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 4-arm spiral antennas have a wide bandwidth and circular polarization when operating in mode 1 (fundamental mode). Switching to mode 3 (to obtain opposite circular polarization) dramatically reduces the antenna bandwidth compared to mode 1. In this work we reduce the arm sizes of the spiral (for example with RF switches) to increase the bandwidth of mode 3 at the higher mode 1 frequencies. In this way the antenna has the same wide bandwidth for both polarizations (modes).

articleTitle: A New Pattern and Polarization Diversity MIMO Antenna for Handheld Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A four-dipole multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna having pattern and polarization diversity for handheld terminals is presented and analyzed. The patterns are complementary, and they point at 0°, 90° 180°, and 270° directions in the azimuth plane with the help of adjacent parasitic elements. The elements are arranged orthogonally to obtain polarization diversity while achieving effective diversity gain of 15.8 dB at 1% outage probability. The influence of a battery and LCD on the antenna performance is also studied.

articleTitle: Investigation of Driver EMF Exposure From 4G/5G Automotive Glass Mounted Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The goal of this paper is to study the human exposure to electromagnetic fields due to vehicle-mounted on glass antennas. A novel multi-band planar antenna is designed and optimized using Invasive Weed Optimization. The design includes a multi-band 4G/5G antenna operating in the frequency band [600 MHz-5000 MHz]. Numerical simulations show a reflection coefficient below -10 dB at all the operating frequency bands. Additionally, we investigated various antenna placements including the front and rear glasses of the vehicle. The effect of the antenna radiation on the driver is discussed for different antenna locations in terms of electric field strength. The asymptotic method is applied for the simulation of the whole model, considering the huge electrical size of the car at frequencies up to 5 GHz. Electric field results show that the most convenient antenna placement is at the car backlite. These results are within the electric field exposure limits provided by the FCC.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Frequency-Tunable Varactor-Loaded Dual-Band Shorted Multi-Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by an L-probe with a Thick Dielectric Substrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized frequency-tunable varactor-loaded dual-band shorted multi-ring microstrip antenna (MR-MSA) fed by an L-probe with a thick dielectric substrate. The frequency-tunable MR-MSA consists of multiple ring patch elements arranged concentrically and a feeding L-probe arranged on a dielectric substrate. Two varactor diodes are mounted on each ring patch and resonant frequencies of the ring patches can be controlled electronically by the DC bias voltages applied to the varactor diodes independently. In order to miniaturize the ring patches, a varactor-loaded shorted MR-MSA has been proposed. By using via holes added at the center of the ring patch, the patch area of the MR-MSA can be reduced by a quarter in comparison with the original one. In this paper, a miniaturized varactor-loaded frequency-tunable dual-band MR-MSA with a thick dielectric substrate is proposed. Measured gain of the prototype MR-MSA with a thick substrate of 3.6 mm thickness is improved by approximately 5 dB in comparison with that with a thin substrate although the fractional frequency-tunable ranges of the two bands are almost unchanged.

articleTitle: Time-modulated Patch Antennas with Nonreciprocal Polarization Handedness
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose the concept and design of a time-modulated antenna able to exhibit nonreciprocal polarization handedness during transmission and reception (for instance, the antenna radiates right-handed circularly polarized waves but receives left-handed circularly polarized waves) by exploiting the photonic Aharonov-Bohm effect. To demonstrate our approach, we combine a patch antenna fed from four symmetrical sides with an appropriate low-frequency modulation scheme to control orthogonal currents. We show that it is simultaneously possible to (i) obtain very high frequency conversion efficiency; (ii) independently tailor the phase of radiated fields that have orthogonal polarization with the phase of certain modulation signals, thus implementing any polarization state of the Poincaré sphere; and (iii) achieve nonreciprocity at the polarization level with a single antenna element. We envision that the proposed time-modulated device may find exciting applications in the next generation of sensing, radar, and communication systems.

articleTitle: Combining Leak feeder cable and Antenna to support Mobile network in underground mine environment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports the measurements of a hybrid radiating LTE base-station (BS) based on Software Defined Radio (SDR) platform. The hybrid radiating elements consisted of a hybrid architecture of 2 antennas and a Leaky Feeder (LF) cable to support LTE technology operating in Frequency Division Duplex (FDD) on 850Mhz radio band. All the measurements were made in a former underground gold mine. The used LF cable aimed to enhance the radio signal propagation, particularly in Non-Line Of Sight (NLOS) areas where signal propagation has difficulty to reach the destination. Also, LF cable avoided increasing the number of deployed BSs to deal with NLOS areas and reduced the transmission power of the mobile user equipment (UE) without losing the quality of service(QoS).

articleTitle: A Wideband CP Resonant Cavity Antenna with a Self-Complimentary Partially Reflective Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents wideband gain enhancement of a circularly-polarized (CP) resonant cavity antenna (RCA) by using a broadband single-layer partially reflective surface (PRS). The significant effect of self-complimentary PRS structure on the antenna bandwidth is demonstrated. The antenna is fabricated and measured and the results show a reasonable agreement between the simulation and measurement. The results show that an AR and impedance bandwidths of 20.3% and 33.6% are obtained, respectively. The antenna gain is more than 10.5 dBic over the 3-dB gain bandwidth from 5.4 to 7.2 GHz, with a peak gain of 13.5 dBic.

articleTitle: 4-port MIMO CDR Antenna based with a Defected Ground Structure for 5G mm-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a 4-port Multi-Input-Multi-Output (MIMO) Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna (CDRA) based, at 28 GHz band for 5G communications system is proposed. A single CDRA is mounted on a compact size substrate of 20×20×1.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and excited with four microstrip feedlines. The proposed antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 27.0428.56 GHz. A Defected Ground Structure has been etched on the ground plan to obtain lower isolation levels. As a result, a maximum isolation enhancement of 15 dB is achieved in the operating band. Moreover, an acceptable gain from 4.5-7dBi along with the operational band with a maximum Envelope Correlation coefficient (ECC) of 0.005, which makes this antenna design a competitive candidate for a MIMO 5G cellular communications at the 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Diffuse Field Cross-Correlation in a Reverberantion Chamber
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The cross-correlation between diffuse field at two receiving antennas is very nearly equal to the direct response of one antenna to an impulse applied at the other one. Exploiting the diffuse wave field generated by rotation of a mechanical mode stirrer inside a reverberation chamber (RC) excited by a single transmitting antenna, we outline the convergence of the cross-correlation toward the impulse response between the two receiving antennas. The laboratory demonstration shows that it is possible to characterize passively the coupling between two antennas in an RC.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Transmitarrays via Convex Relaxation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A mathematical approach for the phase-only synthesis of transmitarray antennas based on iterative convex optimization is presented. Using semidefinite relaxation techniques, the proposed framework is suitable for a wide range of beam shaping applications. The synthesis of a pencil-beam pattern with reduced sidelobe levels and limited gain loss is illustrated. The pattern distortion due to the quantization of the optimal phase distribution is investigated to provide realistic design guidelines.

articleTitle: 3D Antenna in Package Design: Maximizing Radiation Pattern Isotropicity and CP Coverage
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Near-isotropic radiation pattern and maximum CP coverage in the radiation sphere are desirable features for antennas, particularly for modern applications such as Internet of Things. In this work, we derive conditions through a combination of three dipole model and particle swarm optimization to achieve near isotropic radiation pattern and maximum CP coverage, simultaneously. Based on the developed theoretical model, a 3D antenna-in-package design provides 98% isotropicity in the radiation pattern and a CP coverage of 22.6% over the entire radiation sphere.

articleTitle: Development of Dielectric Measurement Techniques for Arctic Oil Spill Studies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present results of dielectric measurements in support of oil spill studies in the Arctic. We created a cavity resonator that operates in the C-band and used a commercially available dielectric probe method to perform measurements on several candidate substances. Results showed good agreement between the techniques, giving confidence in the validity of the results.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Metasurface Using Combined Neural Network and Transfer Function
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an inverse-design network that combined neural network is proposed. Compared with traditional inverse network, the proposed network can achieve higher accuracy and efficiency. A reflective metasurface is used as an example to confirm the validity of this method.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Dual-Band Slot Antenna with Self-Scalable Pattern for Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-fed dual-band antenna operating in both X-band (9.8 GHz) and Ka-band (33GHz) is presented in this paper. A unique feature of the proposed antenna is to deploy a self-scalable pattern capable of working in an array environment without exhibiting full grating lobes in visible region. The principle of operation is based on the first and third resonance modes of a narrow slot antenna coupled to three parasitic dipoles. The second resonance mode is suppressed by even-symmetry feeding which also acts as reflector in the third resonance, thus improving the front-to-back ratio (by 7.5 dB) in this work.

articleTitle: Tri-band Multi-Constellation GNSS Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates a Tri band Multi-Constellation GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) Antenna solution for automotive applications. A single GNSS receive antenna that can be used in all global markets and support Tri-band operation is highly desirable for automotive applications. GNSS includes GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, and Beidou satellite constellations Each of these constellations use different bandwidths and carrier frequencies, thus making it is a challenge to design a single antenna solution to support global application. In this paper, a single Tri band multi-constellation patch antenna is designed, and simulation results are utilized to show the antenna design's capabilities.

articleTitle: A Tri-Band Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna for WiFi Applications in S- and C-band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a circular polarized disc patch antenna for tri-band operation. The design is based on the combination of two mechanisms: modal degeneration applied to a circular patch, and gap-coupling with parasitic elements, resulting in a first mode of operation at 2.42 GHz and two additional mode at 5.00GHz and 5.30GHz. The frequencies of operations as well as the circular polarization attained makes the proposed device suitable for WiFi application in both S-band and C-band.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Circuit with High RF-to-DC Conversion Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an energy harvesting circuit for high efficiency performance. The proposed circuit consists of an RLC shunt resonance circuit integrated to a RF antenna. The resonance circuit is used to (i) selectively pick the desired signal whose output is fed to a Cockcroft-Walton voltage multiplier circuit; and (ii) match the impedance of the antenna with the Cockcroft-Walton voltage multiplier circuit for optimum power (DC) transfer. The proposed circuit exhibits an efficiency of 68% for an input power of 200 μW.

articleTitle: Electronic Steerable Slotted Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel electronic beam-steering leaky-wave antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is realized on a substrate integrated waveguide. The beam-steering is achieved using modified longitudinal slots. Sweeping the bias voltage causes the variation in phase constant which leads to the beam scanning. The length, width, and height of the antenna are 95 mm, 23 mm, and 0.3 mm, respectively. Sweeping the capacitance of varactor from 200fF to 500fF leads to 27° scanning range at 27.8 GHz. Low profile and electronic beam-steering capability of the proposed antenna make it a suitable candidate for integrating into the 5G networks.

articleTitle: Hedgehog Waveguide Phase Adjustment of Dual Left/Right-Hand Circularly-Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual Left/right-hand circularly-polarized (LH/RH CP) antenna implemented using hedgehog waveguide is investigated and developed at 60-GHz. The hedgehog waveguide is employed as the host guiding structure to create a frequency-independent phase difference between the two orthogonal modes at the antenna aperture in order to obtain a wideband axial-ratio at the 60-GHz band from 57 to 64 GHz. The proposed technique provides a pure circularly-polarized (CP) operation over the entire operating frequency range through the frequency-independent triangular-shaped slot and phase adjustment using the hedgehog waveguide.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small Antenna in Package Design with Embedded Electronics for RPW Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The tracking and detection of Red Palm Weevils (RPWs) are highly desirable for efficient pest control. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking system is a good option for real-time monitoring, however, for mounting the system on the insect, it must be miniaturized, particularly the antenna part. In this paper, we propose an electrically small inverted F antenna which is realized on the BLE system package, qualifying it as an antenna in package (AiP) design. The antenna has been designed with the embedded electronics and has a highly compact size of 0.05λ × 0.05λ × 0.025λ. It is very well matched at 2.48 GHz with 17 MHz bandwidth. It demonstrates a maximum detection range of 300 meters.

articleTitle: Mitigating Quantization Lobes in Reconfigurable Reflective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a method for the reduction of quantization lobes in single/multi-bit reconfigurable reflective surfaces (e.g. reflectarrays and large intelligent surfaces). As such, we introduce random physical phase delays on each antenna element of the reflective surface, thus randomizing quantization errors, decreasing the level of the undesired quantization lobes. In this work, we explain our method and present results of a proof-of-concept 275 GHz linear 1-bit reconfigurable reflective surface. Finally, leveraging the proposed method, we achieve a reduction of quantization lobes up to 10 dB for single-bit configurations.

articleTitle: Tunable Triple-Band Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Mobile Phone
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the new design technique of the triple-band antenna for the sub-6 GHz 5G mobile phone is proposed. The new proposed patterns are designed into a metal clearance area with the pre-existing 4G antennas in order to cover the additional sub-6 GHz bands. In the proposed design, and the tunable inductor is placed between the legacy antenna and the proposed patterns to cover the wide frequency range in the sub-6GHz bands through the frequency switching without loss of the pre-existing 4G antennas. Consequently, the proposed antenna operates in triple-band (0.9 GHz, 2.5 GHz for the legacy band, 3.3 - 5.0 GHz for the sub-6 GHz) and the simulated and measured radiation efficiency is over 50% in whole target frequency bands. The proposed design technique can contribute to various mobile phones which need to add the new 5G band without the additional space.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed Dish Antenna With Integrated Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design and fabrication of a fully 3D printed dish antenna with integrated feeding. As opposed to traditional dish antennas where the dish, feeding antenna, and cables are separate components, a fully 3D printed dish antenna incorporates all these elements in one integrated structure. The designed 3D printed dish antenna operates at 28 GHz with 28.5 dBi of gain and features a integrated horn antenna feed, which is built directly onto the surface of the dish, and an integrated waveguide connector for connections for external RF connections. The introduction of 3D printable dish antenna structures with integrated feeding and connectors, grants users an extremely low cost and simple to manufacture antenna for applications which requires high gain and ease of deployment.

articleTitle: Compact Cavity-Backed Discone Array for Conformal Omnidirectional Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact shallow cavity-backed discone array for conformal omnidirectional vertically polarized antenna applications is investigated. The antenna described consists of four discone antennas arranged in a ring array in a circular contoured conical cavity covered with a radome. The individual discone antennas are fed with coaxial transmission lines. This paper describes the antenna design and electromagnetic simulations of the antenna array. Good omnidirectional realized gain radiation patterns are demonstrated over the 960 MHz to 1215 MHz Tactical Air Navigation System (TACAN) band, an approximate 23% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Multi-layer Metallic Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An innovative deep-learning based design approach for multi-layer metallic metasurfaces has been presented in this paper. By leveraging the strength of deep-learning networks, the higher order degree of freedom for metasurface design is unlocked. The structure and performance of the proposed deep neural network (DNN) are discussed. It is demonstrated that it can predict the possible amplitude and phase coverage of metasurface unit-cells under consideration. The physical insight derived from the proposed DNN can be utilized towards achieving a more time efficient and accurate metasurface design.

articleTitle: An Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel meter-wave antenna array using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) group is presented. The array is composed of UAVs, and each UAV bears a meter-wave antenna element. The UAV-borne array has advantages on reducing the influence of multipath effect, obtaining high gain and high mobility, etc. In order to suppress the grating lobe caused by large element spacing, dual- or multi- layer planar arrays can be built through flight trajectory control of UAVs.

articleTitle: Parity-time symmetry sensor circuits based on shunt and series RLC circuits
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present two types of second -order Parity-time (PT) symmetry circuits based on shunt and series RLC tanks. The physical meaning of the effective PT-symmetry Hamiltonian of two circuits are given. In addition, the input impedance of two circuits are derived, especially at exceptional point (EP). We find the input impedance of the two circuits has the opposite trend in terms of amplitude and phase. Based on the input impedance characteristics, for the sensing application, configurations are proposed with the depletion of reflected power at EPs, either of which can be chosen depending on sensor types.

articleTitle: Simple Dipole Scatter for Filling a Shadow Region
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For ever-increasing demand for communication capacity, carrier frequencies are increasing, but this brings greater shadowing which compromises the radio coverage. For example, mmWave signals are severely attenuated in the simplest of non-line-of-sight scenarios - around the corner of a building. We present a simple corner modification comprising a fixed scattering dipole to improve the coverage in the shadow region of the corner diffraction. Simulations are used to thoroughly investigate the scenario, and our numerical experiments are validated with physical experiments. For the vertical polarization, a signal level increase of well over ten dB in the shadow region is demonstrated using a single half-wavelength dipole scatterer.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Band WIFI Antenna with Frequency-Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-band WIFI antenna with frequency-reconfigurability by utilizing a capacitor. The higher band is mainly contributed by a monopole and the lower band is jointly inspired by the monopole and the capacity loaded floating branch. The dual-band antenna without lumped capacity has 112 MHz (2.374 GHz-2.486 GHz) and 1.026 GHz (4.678 GHz-5.704 GHz) -10 dB ( |S11|) bandwidth, for low and high bands, respectively. By introducing a tunable capacity, low-band frequency could be reconfigured and the antenna size can be further reduced. The measured radiation efficiency for the low-and high-band is above 70% and 90%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel GNSS Repeater Architecture for Indoor Positioning Systems in ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For indoor positioning using customary Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) receivers, the use of GNSS repeaters can be considered. However, regulations and provisions limit the use of GNSS repeaters. In order to circumvent these limitations, we propose a novel repeater architecture that transmits the Global Positioning System (GPS) signals in 433 MHz ISM band by frequency down-conversion. In addition, a receiver front end is proposed to upconvert GPS signals back to 1575.42 MHz, which allows any off-the-shelf GPS receiver to be used for indoor positioning. Measurement results with the RF hardware show that when the GPS signals are downconverted and then upconverted back to its original frequency, GPS signal fidelity and positioning accuracy are preserved.

articleTitle: UWB Propagation Characteristics of Human-to-Robot Communication in Automated Collaborative Warehouse
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Propagation of UWB Gaussian signal in a model of automated collaborative warehouse is analyzed using ray tracing method. The transmitting antenna is placed on the human body while the received power profiles in warehouse containing empty racks and racks filled with different loads are calculated. This gives rise to estimation of safe communication range between humans and robots.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of a Microstrip Patch Antenna on an EBG Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Performance of a microstrip patch antenna over a high impedance electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure made of small shorted patches is investigated. An extensive simulation study is conducted to show that the EBG substrate can increase the impedance bandwidth by as much as 27 % and the gain by 6 dB, while reducing cross polarization by 11 dB.

articleTitle: High Gain Circularly Polarized Antenna Loaded With Dual-Band AMC structure for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band circularly polarized (CP) printed monopole antenna backed with a 3×3 artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) array is presented for wireless body area network (WBAN) applications. The antenna is composed of a rectangular monopole and an asymmetric ground plane. By introducing the C-shaped ring, CP radiation could be achieved. To reduce the backward scattering wave towards the human body and achieve enhancements to gain and SAR, the monopole antenna is set above a conventional square loop geometry representing the Artificial Magnetic Conductor design. The proposed antenna operates at dual-band resonance frequencies at 3.5 GHz, for WiMAX wireless applications, and at 5.5 GHz for the ISM Band. It exhibits good gain and SAR at a separation of 15mm from the human body model. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed AMC integrated antenna has an average gain of 5.6 dBi in lower band, 5.15 dBi in upper band, and front-to-back ratio of 10.83 dB and 9.34 dB, when placed on the phantom. The proposed design is suitable for WBAN applications.

articleTitle: Concept of Integrating 4G LTE and Millimeter-wave 5G Antennas within Zero-Bezel Cellular Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a packaging technology of integrating 4G long-term evolution (LTE) and millimeter-wave (mmWave) 5G antennas for zero-bezel cellular devices. To verify the feasibility of the proposed technology, both antenna types are designed and coherently integrated into the cellular device prototype. The fabricated 2×2 4G LTE MIMO prototype exhibits total system efficiencies of more than 50% over the entire LTE spectrum (699–960 MHz and 1710–2690 MHz). The over-the-air evaluation of the fabricated mm Wave 5G phased array AoD module confirms 3-dB beam scanning range of more than ± 25° with an estimated maximum EIRP of 14.14 dBm at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Verification of an Electromagnetic Inversion Metasurface Design Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper summarizes, extends, and synthetically evaluates a method for metasurface design which uses electromagnetic inversion. After the inversion algorithm determines a homogenized surface susceptibility model to implement a desired power pattern, the susceptibility distribution is converted to a three-layer admittance sheet topology. Lastly, full-wave commercial software is used to simulate and verify the performance of a metasurface designed and implemented using the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: RF System Development for Sensor and Wireless Communication Applications Inside a Circular Pipe
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a wireless RF communication system, for propagation inside a circular metallic pipe is presented. A PCB antenna which is operational at 2.4 GHz is employed for the transceiver. Some lab measurements and simulations are reported, considering a 2 m length of metal pipe which is analyzed as an overmoded metallic waveguide. The reflection coefficients show that the antennas can be operational inside the pipe and the insertion losses were approximately 1 dB between the transceivers. The simulation results are in agreement with the measurements. Also included in the RF system are two software-defined radios, positioned at both ends of the pipe, for data communications. Also some extra attenuation was included in the system as well as additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) to test the system limits in terms of power and the bit error rate (BER), respectively.

articleTitle: Open-Source 4G Experimental Setup
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we show how to set up a cellular LTE network for wireless experimentation and measurement, relying on commodity hardware and open-source software. We first deploy a complete LTE network on a single laptop and an SDR hardware. Then, we use it to evaluate the reception performance of a commercial smartphone. In the end, we propose a calibration technique which allows using a smartphone as a wireless power measurement tool by reducing the root-mean-square error of the RSSI, with respect to a reference power measured with a specialized spectrum analyzer, from 6.4 dBm to 2.4 dBm.

articleTitle: 2D Stacked Magnetic Pendulum Arrays for Efficient ULF Transmission
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel mechanical antenna called 2D stacked Magnetic Pendulum Array (MPA) is proposed for efficient generation and transmission of Ultra Low Frequency (ULF) radiation. 55 magnets are stacked in 11 rows with 5 magnets in each row. The array is enclosed in a solenoid which provides the excitation. The experimental demonstration is performed at a resonance frequency of 727 Hz and a quality (Q) factor of 94 is achieved. Moreover, measured results show 18 dB improvement in the transmission efficiency of the MPA compared to the efficiency of a single solenoid of same dimensions.

articleTitle: A Low-Storage PML Implementation within a High-order Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The perfectly matched layer (PML) is one of the most popular domain truncation techniques used by wave equation solvers. PML implementations often use smooth-varying attenuation coefficients to achieve desired levels of accuracy and efficiency by reducing numerical reflection and PML thickness, respectively. For a discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) scheme, this approach requires storing a different mass matrix for every mesh element, and therefore significantly increases the memory footprint. In this work, an efficient implementation of PML, which makes use of weight-adjusted approximation to account for smooth-varying attenuation coefficients, is developed. The proposed scheme results in a DGTD scheme with a small memory footprint while maintaining the high-order accuracy of the solution using a thin PML.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Simulation for Chipless RFID Orientation Sensor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents an application of the Monte Carlo method for the evaluation of a chipless RFID orientation sensor in presence of noise. The working principle of the sensor is presented and an analytical model is derived. The sensitivity of the sensor to distance is put in evidence both with uncertainty propagation of the first order approximation of the model and by Monte Carlo Simulation. The Monte Carlo approach is applied successfully even for the nonlinear parts of the model contrary to the first order approach.

articleTitle: Monostatic Radar Cross Section Simulation of Small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles in UHF Band
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper studies the monostatic radar cross section (RCS) simulation of a popular Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), DJI Phantom 2 Vision Plus in UHF band. The RCS (σ) is evaluated when the plane wave is horizontally and vertically polarized. First, for a constant θ(θ = 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>) and a varying φ(0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> ≤ φ ≤ 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>), the results show that σhh is higher than the other polarizations, its highest value is found when φ = 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> or φ = 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>, meaning when the excitation is in front of the center of the blades. Second, for constant φ(φ = 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>) and a varying θ(0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> ≤ θ ≤ 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>), in this case also, σhh is higher than the other polarizations, its values are quite constant around -17dBsm with 2dBsm more when looking from the bottom or from the top (-15dBsm). These results give us an idea about the optimal position of the radar to get the highest value of the RCS of the drone.

articleTitle: Finite State Markov Modeling of Wideband Vehicular Channel
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Finite State Markov Channel (FSMC) has been commonly adopted in wireless communication system optimization and protocol design, as it provides a simple mathematical processing for the performance analysis. While the literature about FSMC modeling in time domain are abundant, FSMC models describing channel fading in frequency domain are few and lack the support of measurements. In this paper, we develop an FSMC model for the vehicular channel based on real field measurements obtained from Beijing-Tianjin highway scenario. We discuss the varieties of the steady state probability and temporary skip probability in different locations. The conclusion of this paper can be used in the future FSMC modeling in frequency domain.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Dual-polarized 5G Antenna for Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized antenna covering both 28- and 39-GHz bands for 5G mobile communications. The design consists of two discrete elements - a folded dipole and a folded monopole, which generate two orthogonal polarizations. Parasitic elements are used to realize the higher-band operation. The entire structure is designed on an ultra-thin four-layer laminate and is intended to be incorporated along the edges of smartphones to enable 5G operation. The folded dipole features 6.2 GHz (22.1 %) bandwidth in the 28-GHz band and 2.3 GHz (5.9%) in the 39-GHz band; the folded monopole has 6.8 GHz (24.3%) and 2.2 GHz (5.9%) bandwidth in the two aforementioned bands, respectively. The simulated peak gain of the folded dipole and monopole are both 5.5 dBi in the 28-GHz band, and 5.6 dBi and 3.7 dBi respectively in the 39-GHz band. The overall dimensions of the antenna are 6.75 mm × 5 mm.

articleTitle: Shared-Aperture Enabled Integration of Sub-6 GHz and Millimeter-Wave Antennas for Future Multi-Functional Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose and present a unit cell for developing a compact five-layer, dual-band scalable antenna array operating in both sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave (mmW). This high-gain and broadband antenna makes use of a shared-aperture concept comprising of a perforated patch stacked with a square loop antenna working in 3.6~3.9 GHz as well as a 3×3 antenna array operating in 25.2~30.4 GHz for dual-band operations. Theoretical and experimental results are presented to validate the proposed antenna scheme.
